Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Saṃyuttanikāyo

The Connected Discourses

Sagāthāvaggo

The Book with Verses

1. Devatāsaṃyuttaṃ

1. Connected Discourses with Deities

1. Naḷavaggo

1. The Chapter on the Reed

1. Oghataraṇasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Crossing the Flood

1. Evaṃ [T 1.0001][V 1.0001][P 1.0001][M 1.0001] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘kathaṃ nu tvaṃ, mārisa, oghamatarī’ti? ‘Appatiṭṭhaṃ khvāhaṃ, āvuso, anāyūhaṃ [V 1.0002] oghamatari’nti. ‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, mārisa, appatiṭṭhaṃ anāyūhaṃ oghamatarī’ti? ‘Yadākhvāhaṃ, āvuso, santiṭṭhāmi tadāssu saṃsīdāmi[T 1.0002]; yadākhvāhaṃ, āvuso, āyūhāmi tadāssu nibbuyhāmi nivuyhāmi (syā. kaṃ. ka.). Evaṃ khvāhaṃ, āvuso, appatiṭṭhaṃ anāyūhaṃ oghamatari’”nti.

1. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then a certain deity, in the far advanced night, with surpassing radiance illuminating the entire Jeta's Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, that deity said this to the Blessed One: 'How, Venerable Sir, did you cross the flood?' 'By not halting, friend, and by not striving I crossed the flood.' 'But how is it, Venerable Sir, that by not halting and by not striving you crossed the flood?' 'When I halted, friend, then I sank; but when I strove, then I was swept away. Thus, friend, by not halting and by not striving I crossed the flood.'

“Cirassaṃ vata passāmi, brāhmaṇaṃ parinibbutaṃ;

Appatiṭṭhaṃ anāyūhaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ loke visattika”nti. –

“For long, indeed, I see a brahmin fully extinguished, who, by not halting and not striving, has crossed over the world’s attachments.”

Idamavoca [M 1.0002] sā devatā. Samanuñño satthā ahosi. Atha kho sā devatā – “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

This the deity said. The Teacher approved. Then that deity, knowing, 'The Teacher has approved of me,' paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to the right, and vanished right there.

2. Nimokkhasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Release

2. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 1.0002]. Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

2. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain deity, as the night was far advanced, with surpassing radiance lighting up the entire Jetavana, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, that deity said to the Blessed One:

“Jānāsi no tvaṃ, mārisa, sattānaṃ nimokkhaṃ pamokkhaṃ viveka”nti?

“Do you know, Venerable Sir, the release, the complete release, and the seclusion of beings?”

“Jānāmi khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sattānaṃ nimokkhaṃ pamokkhaṃ viveka”nti.

“I know, friend, the release, the complete release, and the seclusion of beings.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, mārisa, jānāsi sattānaṃ nimokkhaṃ pamokkhaṃ viveka”nti?

“But how, Venerable Sir, do you know the release, the complete release, and the seclusion of beings?”

“Nandībhavaparikkhayā [T 1.0003] nandibhavaparikkhayā (syā. kaṃ.), saññāviññāṇasaṅkhayā, vedanānaṃ nirodhā upasamā – evaṃ khvāhaṃ, āvuso, jānāmi sattānaṃ nimokkhaṃ pamokkhaṃ viveka”nti.

“Through the destruction of delight in existence, through the destruction of perception and consciousness, and through the cessation and appeasement of feelings—thus, friend, I know the release, the complete release, and the seclusion of beings.”

3. Upanīyasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Being Led On

3. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0003]. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

3. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Upanīyati jīvitamappamāyu,

Jarūpanītassa na santi tāṇā;

Etaṃ bhayaṃ maraṇe pekkhamāno,

Puññāni kayirātha sukhāvahānī”ti.

“Life is led on, the life-span is short; for one led on by old age, there are no shelters. Seeing this fear in death, one should perform meritorious deeds that bring happiness.”

“Upanīyati jīvitamappamāyu,

Jarūpanītassa na santi tāṇā;

Etaṃ bhayaṃ maraṇe pekkhamāno,

Lokāmisaṃ pajahe santipekkho”ti.

“Life is led on, the life-span is short; for one led on by old age, there are no shelters. Seeing this fear in death, one who seeks peace should abandon worldly bait.”

4. Accentisuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Passing Away

4. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 1.0003]. Ekamantaṃ [T 1.0004][P 1.0003] ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

4. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo,

Vayoguṇā anupubbaṃ jahanti;

Etaṃ bhayaṃ maraṇe pekkhamāno,

Puññāni kayirātha sukhāvahānī”ti.

“Times pass, nights go by; the stages of life are successively left behind. Seeing this fear in death, one should perform meritorious deeds that bring happiness.”

“Accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo,

Vayoguṇā anupubbaṃ jahanti;

Etaṃ bhayaṃ maraṇe pekkhamāno,

Lokāmisaṃ pajahe santipekkho”ti.

“Times pass, nights go by; the stages of life are successively left behind. Seeing this fear in death, one who seeks peace should abandon worldly bait.”

5. Katichindasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on How Many to Cut Off

5. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0004]. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

5. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Kati chinde kati jahe, kati cuttari bhāvaye;

Kati saṅgātigo bhikkhu, oghatiṇṇoti vuccatī”ti.

“How many should one cut off? How many abandon? How many more should one cultivate? Having overcome how many attachments is a bhikkhu called ‘one who has crossed the flood’?”

“Pañca chinde pañca jahe, pañca cuttari bhāvaye;

Pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu, oghatiṇṇoti vuccatī”ti.

“One should cut off five, abandon five, and cultivate five more. A bhikkhu who has overcome five attachments is called ‘one who has crossed the flood’.”

6. Jāgarasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Wakefulness

6. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ [T 1.0005] ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

6. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Kati jāgarataṃ suttā, kati suttesu jāgarā;

Katibhi katīhi (sī.) rajamādeti, katibhi katīhi (sī.) parisujjhatī”ti.

“For those who are awake, how many things are asleep? In those who are asleep, how many are awake? By how many does one acquire dust? By how many is one purified?”

“Pañca jāgarataṃ suttā, pañca suttesu jāgarā;

Pañcabhi pañcahi (sī.) rajamādeti, pañcabhi pañcahi (sī.) parisujjhatī”ti.

“For those who are awake, five things are asleep. In those who are asleep, five are awake. By five one acquires dust. By five one is purified.”

7. Appaṭividitasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on What Is Not Penetrated

7. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 1.0004]. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0004] ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

7. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Yesaṃ dhammā appaṭividitā, paravādesu nīyare niyyare (ka.);

Suttā te nappabujjhanti, kālo tesaṃ pabujjhitu”nti.

“Those for whom the Dhammas are not penetrated are led by the doctrines of others. They are asleep and do not awaken. It is time for them to awaken.”

“Yesaṃ dhammā suppaṭividitā, paravādesu na nīyare;

Te sambuddhā sammadaññā, caranti visame sama”nti.

“Those for whom the Dhammas are well penetrated are not led by the doctrines of others. They, the fully enlightened ones, having rightly known, fare evenly amidst the uneven.”

8. Susammuṭṭhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on What Is Thoroughly Forgotten

8. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

8. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity spoke this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Yesaṃ [T 1.0006] dhammā susammuṭṭhā, paravādesu nīyare;

Suttā te nappabujjhanti, kālo tesaṃ pabujjhitu”nti.

“For those for whom the truths are thoroughly forgotten, they are led into the doctrines of others. Asleep, they do not awaken. It is time for them to awaken.”

“Yesaṃ [V 1.0005] dhammā asammuṭṭhā, paravādesu na nīyare;

Te sambuddhā sammadaññā, caranti visame sama”nti.

“For those for whom the truths are not forgotten, they are not led into the doctrines of others. Perfectly enlightened, having known rightly, they walk evenly amidst the uneven.”

9. Mānakāmasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on One Who Desires Conceit

9. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

9. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the Blessed One's presence:

“Na mānakāmassa damo idhatthi,

Na monamatthi asamāhitassa;

Eko araññe viharaṃ pamatto,

Na maccudheyyassa tareyya pāra”nti.

“For one who desires conceit, there is no taming here, nor is there wisdom for one who is unconcentrated. Dwelling alone in the forest, heedless, one cannot cross to the far shore of Death’s domain.”

“Mānaṃ pahāya susamāhitatto,

Sucetaso sabbadhi vippamutto;

Eko araññe viharaṃ appamatto,

Sa maccudheyyassa tareyya pāra”nti.

“Having abandoned conceit, well-concentrated, with a virtuous mind, everywhere released; dwelling alone in the forest, heedful, that one can cross to the far shore of Death’s domain.”

10. Araññasuttaṃ

10. The Sutta on the Forest

10. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0006][M 1.0005]. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0005] ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

10. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Araññe [T 1.0007] viharantānaṃ, santānaṃ brahmacārinaṃ;

Ekabhattaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ, kena vaṇṇo pasīdatī”ti.

“For those dwelling in the forest, the pacified ones, who live the holy life, eating but a single meal—for what reason is their complexion so clear?”

“Atītaṃ nānusocanti, nappajappanti nāgataṃ;

Paccuppannena yāpenti, tena vaṇṇo pasīdati”.

“They do not grieve for the past, nor do they long for the future. They sustain themselves with what is present; for that reason their complexion is clear.”

“Anāgatappajappāya, atītassānusocanā;

Etena bālā sussanti, naḷova harito luto”ti.

“Through longing for the future and grieving for the past, fools wither away, like a green reed that has been cut.”

Naḷavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Reed Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Oghaṃ nimokkhaṃ upaneyyaṃ, accenti katichindi ca;

Jāgaraṃ appaṭividitā, susammuṭṭhā mānakāminā;

Araññe dasamo vutto, vaggo tena pavuccati.

Ogha, Nimokkha, Upaneyya, Accenti, and Katicchindi; Jāgara, Appaṭividitā, Susammuṭṭhā, Mānakāmi; and Arañña is said to be the tenth. Thus is the chapter proclaimed.

2. Nandanavaggo

2. The Nandana Chapter

1. Nandanasuttaṃ

1. The Sutta on Nandana

11. Evaṃ [T 1.0008] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa [V 1.0007] ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

11. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks!” “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatarā tāvatiṃsakāyikā devatā nandane vane accharāsaṅghaparivutā dibbehi pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricāriyamānā paricāriyamānā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

“Once in the past, monks, a certain deity of the Tāvatiṃsa realm, in the Nandana Grove, surrounded by a host of celestial nymphs, furnished and endowed with the five divine strands of sensual pleasure, was being attended upon. On that occasion, that deity recited this verse:”

“Na [M 1.0006] te sukhaṃ pajānanti, ye na passanti nandanaṃ;

Āvāsaṃ naradevānaṃ, tidasānaṃ yasassina”nti.

“They do not know happiness, those who do not see Nandana, the abode of the god-men, of the thirty glorious ones.”

“Evaṃ [P 1.0006] vutte, bhikkhave, aññatarā devatā taṃ devataṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi –

“When this was said, monks, a certain deity replied to that deity with a verse:”

“Na tvaṃ bāle pajānāsi, yathā arahataṃ vaco;

Aniccā sabbasaṅkhārā sabbe saṅkhārā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho”ti.

“You foolish one, you do not know the word of the Arahants as it is: ‘All conditioned phenomena are impermanent, having the nature to arise and pass away. Having arisen, they cease; their pacification is happiness.’”

2. Nandatisuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on Delighting

12. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ [T 1.0009] ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

12. At Sāvatthī. Standing in a suitable place, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Nandati puttehi puttimā,

Gomā gomiko (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) gohi tatheva nandati;

Upadhīhi [V 1.0008] narassa nandanā,

Na hi so nandati yo nirūpadhī”ti.

“One who has sons delights in his sons; likewise, one with cattle delights in his cattle. For a person, delight comes from the substrates of existence. Indeed, one who is without substrates does not delight.”

“Socati puttehi puttimā,

Gomā gohi tatheva socati;

Upadhīhi narassa socanā,

Na hi so socati yo nirūpadhī”ti.

“One who has sons grieves on account of his sons; likewise, one with cattle grieves on account of his cattle. For a person, grief comes from the substrates of existence. Indeed, one who is without substrates does not grieve.”

3. Natthiputtasamasuttaṃ

3. The Sutta on ‘None Equal to a Son’

13. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

13. At Sāvatthī. Standing in a suitable place, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Natthi puttasamaṃ pemaṃ, natthi gosamitaṃ dhanaṃ;

Natthi sūriyasamā suriyasamā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ābhā, samuddaparamā sarā”ti.

“There is no love equal to a son; there is no wealth equal to cattle. There is no light equal to the sun; no lake is greater than the ocean.”

“Natthi attasamaṃ pemaṃ, natthi dhaññasamaṃ dhanaṃ;

Natthi paññāsamā ābhā, vuṭṭhi ve paramā sarā”ti.

“There is no love equal to oneself; there is no wealth equal to grain. There is no light equal to wisdom; indeed, rain is the foremost lake.”

4. Khattiyasuttaṃ

4. The Sutta on the Khattiya

14. “Khattiyo [T 1.0010][M 1.0007] dvipadaṃ seṭṭho, balībaddo balivaddo (sī. pī.), balibaddo (syā. kaṃ. ka.) catuppadaṃ.

14. “The khattiya is the best of bipeds; the bull is the best of quadrupeds.

Komārī seṭṭhā bhariyānaṃ, yo ca puttāna pubbajo”ti.

A maiden is the best of wives, and of sons, the one who is firstborn.”

“Sambuddho dvipadaṃ seṭṭho, ājānīyo catuppadaṃ;

Sussūsā seṭṭhā bhariyānaṃ, yo ca puttānamassavo”ti.

“The Perfectly Enlightened One is the best of bipeds; a thoroughbred is the best of quadrupeds. An attentive wife is the best of wives, and of sons, the one who is obedient.”

5. Saṇamānasuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on the Sound

15. “Ṭhite [P 1.0007] majjhanhike majjhantike (sabbattha) kāle, sannisīvesu pakkhisu.

15. “When the time of midday is established, and the birds have settled,

Saṇateva brahāraññaṃ mahāraññaṃ (ka. sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.), taṃ bhayaṃ paṭibhāti ma”nti.

The great forest seems to resound; that fear appears to me.”

“Ṭhite majjhanhike kāle, sannisīvesu pakkhisu;

Saṇateva brahāraññaṃ, sā rati paṭibhāti ma”nti.

“When the time of midday is established, and the birds have settled, the great forest seems to resound; that delight appears to me.”

6. Niddātandīsuttaṃ

6. The Sutta on Drowsiness and Lethargy

16. “Niddā [V 1.0009] tandī vijambhitā tandi vijambhikā (sī. pī.), aratī bhattasammado.

16. “Drowsiness, lethargy, yawning, discontent, and stupor from food—

Etena nappakāsati, ariyamaggo idha pāṇina”nti.

Because of these, the noble path is not made manifest here for beings.”

“Niddaṃ tandiṃ vijambhitaṃ, aratiṃ bhattasammadaṃ;

Vīriyena viriyena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) naṃ paṇāmetvā, ariyamaggo visujjhatī”ti.

“Drowsiness, lethargy, yawning, discontent, and stupor from food—having dispelled these with energy, the noble path is purified.”

7. Dukkarasuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on What is Difficult

17. “Dukkaraṃ [T 1.0011] duttitikkhañca, abyattena ca sāmaññaṃ.

17. “For the unskilled, the ascetic life is difficult to practice and difficult to endure.

Bahūhi tattha sambādhā, yattha bālo visīdatī”ti.

There are many constraints wherein the fool sinks down.”

“Katihaṃ careyya sāmaññaṃ, cittaṃ ce na nivāraye;

Pade pade visīdeyya, saṅkappānaṃ vasānugo”ti.

“For how many days could one practice the ascetic life if one did not restrain the mind? Following the sway of one's intentions, one would sink down at every turn.”

“Kummova aṅgāni sake kapāle,

Samodahaṃ bhikkhu manovitakke;

Anissito aññamaheṭhayāno,

Parinibbuto nūpavadeyya kañcī”ti.

“Like a tortoise drawing its limbs into its own shell, so a bhikkhu should draw in the thoughts of his mind. Unreliant, not harming another, fully extinguished, he would not disparage anyone.”

8. Hirīsuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on Moral Shame

18. “Hirīnisedho [M 1.0008] puriso, koci lokasmiṃ vijjati.

18. “Is there any person in the world restrained by moral shame,

Yo nindaṃ apabodhati apabodheti (syā. kaṃ. ka.), asso bhadro kasāmivā”ti.

who awakens to blame, like a fine horse to the whip?”

“Hirīnisedhā tanuyā, ye caranti sadā satā;

Antaṃ dukkhassa pappuyya, caranti visame sama”nti.

“Few are they who, restrained by moral shame, fare on ever mindful. Having reached the end of suffering, they fare evenly amidst the uneven.”

9. Kuṭikāsuttaṃ

9. The Sutta on the Hut

19.

19.

“Kacci [V 1.0010][P 1.0008] te kuṭikā natthi, kacci natthi kulāvakā;

Kacci santānakā natthi, kacci muttosi bandhanā”ti.

“Pray, have you no hut? Pray, have you no nest? Pray, have you no web of progeny? Pray, are you freed from bonds?”

“Taggha me kuṭikā natthi, taggha natthi kulāvakā;

Taggha santānakā natthi, taggha muttomhi bandhanā”ti.

“Indeed, for me there is no hut; indeed, there is no nest. Indeed, for me there is no web of progeny; indeed, I am freed from bonds.”

“Kintāhaṃ [T 1.0012] kuṭikaṃ brūmi, kiṃ te brūmi kulāvakaṃ;

Kiṃ te santānakaṃ brūmi, kintāhaṃ brūmi bandhana”nti.

“What do I mean, speaking to you, by ‘hut’? What do I mean by ‘nest’? What do I mean by ‘web of progeny’? What do I mean by ‘bond’?”

“Mātaraṃ kuṭikaṃ brūsi, bhariyaṃ brūsi kulāvakaṃ;

Putte santānake brūsi, taṇhaṃ me brūsi bandhana”nti.

“Mother you call a hut, a wife you call a nest; children you call a web of progeny, craving you say to me is the bond.”

“Sāhu te kuṭikā natthi, sāhu natthi kulāvakā;

Sāhu santānakā natthi, sāhu muttosi bandhanā”ti.

“It is good you have no hut; it is good you have no nest. It is good you have no web of progeny; it is good you are freed from bonds.”

10. Samiddhisuttaṃ

10. The Sutta on Samiddhi

20. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati tapodārāme. Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya yena tapodā tenupasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṃ. Tapode gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsi gattāni pubbāpayamāno. Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ tapodaṃ obhāsetvā yena āyasmā samiddhi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vehāsaṃ ṭhitā āyasmantaṃ samiddhiṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

20. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagaha at the Tapodārāma. Then the Venerable Samiddhi, having risen in the last watch of the night, at dawn, went to the Tapodā hot springs to bathe his limbs. Having bathed his limbs in the Tapodā and emerged, he stood wearing a single robe, drying his limbs. Then a certain devatā, when the night was far advanced, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Tapodā, approached the Venerable Samiddhi. Having approached, standing in the air, she addressed the Venerable Samiddhi with a verse:

“Abhutvā [M 1.0009] bhikkhasi bhikkhu, na hi bhutvāna bhikkhasi;

Bhutvāna bhikkhu bhikkhassu, mā taṃ kālo upaccagā”ti.

“Without having enjoyed, monk, you go for alms; you should not go for alms without having first enjoyed. Having enjoyed, monk, then go for alms. Do not let the opportune time pass you by.”

“Kālaṃ [T 1.0013][V 1.0011][P 1.0009] vohaṃ na jānāmi, channo kālo na dissati;

Tasmā abhutvā bhikkhāmi, mā maṃ kālo upaccagā”ti.

“I do not know the time of death; the time is concealed, it is not seen. Therefore, without having enjoyed, I go for alms. May the time for striving not pass me by.”

Atha kho sā devatā pathaviyaṃ paṭhaviyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) patiṭṭhahitvā āyasmantaṃ samiddhiṃ etadavoca – “daharo tvaṃ bhikkhu, pabbajito susu kāḷakeso, bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato, paṭhamena vayasā, anikkīḷitāvī kāmesu. Bhuñja, bhikkhu, mānusake kāme; mā sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvī”ti.

Then that devatā, having established herself on the ground, said this to the Venerable Samiddhi: “You are young, monk, a tender youth with black hair, endowed with fine youth, in the first stage of life, not having sported in sensual pleasures. Enjoy human sensual pleasures, monk! Do not abandon what is visible here and now to pursue what is of the future.”

“Na khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvāmi. Kālikañca khvāhaṃ, āvuso, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṃ anudhāvāmi. Kālikā hi, āvuso, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā; ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṃ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī”ti.

“Indeed, friend, I do not abandon what is visible here and now to pursue what is of the future. Rather, friend, I abandon what is of the future to pursue what is visible here and now. For, friend, sensual pleasures of the future have been declared by the Blessed One to be of much suffering and much despair; the danger in them is great. This Dhamma is visible here and now, timeless, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be realized for oneself by the wise.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhu, kālikā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo? Kathaṃ sandiṭṭhiko ayaṃ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī”ti?

“And how, monk, have sensual pleasures of the future been declared by the Blessed One to be of much suffering and much despair, with great danger in them? And how is this Dhamma visible here and now, timeless, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be realized for oneself by the wise?”

“Ahaṃ kho, āvuso, navo acirapabbajito adhunāgato imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ. Na tāhaṃ na khvāhaṃ (sī. pī.) sakkomi vitthārena ācikkhituṃ. Ayaṃ so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho rājagahe viharati tapodārāme. Taṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ puccha. Yathā te bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāsī”ti.

“Friend, I am new, not long gone forth, recently come to this Dhamma and Discipline. I am not able to explain this in detail. But that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly and Fully Awakened One, is dwelling in Rājagaha at the Tapodārāma. Having approached the Blessed One, ask him about this matter. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so should you bear it in mind.”

“Na kho, bhikkhu, sukaro so bhagavā amhehi upasaṅkamituṃ[T 1.0014], aññāhi mahesakkhāhi devatāhi parivuto. Sace kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, taṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ puccheyyāsi, mayampi āgaccheyyāma dhammassavanāyā”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā samiddhi tassā devatāya paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0010] nisinno kho āyasmā samiddhi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

“Monk, it is not easy for us to approach the Blessed One, for he is surrounded by other devatās of great power. If you, monk, were to approach the Blessed One and ask about this matter, we too would come for the hearing of the Dhamma.” “Even so, friend,” the Venerable Samiddhi replied, assenting to that devatā. Then he went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Samiddhi said this to the Blessed One:

“Idhāhaṃ[V 1.0012][M 1.0010], bhante, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya yena tapodā tenupasaṅkamiṃ gattāni parisiñcituṃ. Tapode gattāni parisiñcitvā paccuttaritvā ekacīvaro aṭṭhāsiṃ gattāni pubbāpayamāno. Atha kho, bhante, aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ tapodaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vehāsaṃ ṭhitā imāya gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

“Venerable Sir, just now, having risen in the last watch of the night, at dawn, I went to the Tapodā hot springs to bathe my limbs. Having bathed my limbs in the Tapodā and emerged, I stood wearing a single robe, drying my limbs. Then, Venerable Sir, a certain devatā, when the night was far advanced, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Tapodā, approached me. Having approached, standing in the air, she addressed me with this verse:”

“Abhutvā bhikkhasi bhikkhu, na hi bhutvāna bhikkhasi;

Bhutvāna bhikkhu bhikkhassu, mā taṃ kālo upaccagā”ti.

“‘Without having enjoyed, monk, you go for alms; you should not go for alms without having first enjoyed. Having enjoyed, monk, then go for alms. Do not let the opportune time pass you by.’”

“Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhante, taṃ devataṃ gāthāya paccabhāsiṃ –

“When this was said, Venerable Sir, I replied to that devatā with a verse:”

“Kālaṃ vohaṃ na jānāmi, channo kālo na dissati;

Tasmā abhutvā bhikkhāmi, mā maṃ kālo upaccagā”ti.

“‘I do not know the time of death; the time is concealed, it is not seen. Therefore, without having enjoyed, I go for alms. May the time for striving not pass me by.’”

“Atha kho, bhante, sā devatā pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhahitvā maṃ etadavoca – ‘daharo [T 1.0015] tvaṃ, bhikkhu, pabbajito susu kāḷakeso, bhadrena yobbanena samannāgato, paṭhamena vayasā, anikkīḷitāvī kāmesu. Bhuñja, bhikkhu, mānusake kāme; mā sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvī’”ti.

“Then, Venerable Sir, that devatā, having established herself on the ground, said this to me: ‘You are young, monk, a tender youth with black hair, endowed with fine youth, in the first stage of life, not having sported in sensual pleasures. Enjoy human sensual pleasures, monk! Do not abandon what is visible here and now to pursue what is of the future.’”

“Evaṃ vuttāhaṃ, bhante, taṃ devataṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘na khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvāmi; kālikañca khvāhaṃ, āvuso, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṃ anudhāvāmi. Kālikā hi, āvuso, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā; ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṃ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’”ti.

When this was said, Venerable Sir, I said this to that deity: 'Indeed, friend, I do not abandon what is visible here and now to pursue what is subject to time; and indeed, friend, I abandon what is subject to time to pursue what is visible here and now. For, friend, sensual pleasures subject to time have been declared by the Blessed One as having much suffering, much distress; the danger in them is greater. This Dhamma is visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be individually realized by the wise.'

“Evaṃ vutte, bhante, sā devatā maṃ etadavoca – ‘kathañca, bhikkhu, kālikā kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā; ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo? Kathaṃ sandiṭṭhiko [P 1.0011] ayaṃ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti? Evaṃ vuttāhaṃ, bhante[V 1.0013], taṃ devataṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘ahaṃ kho, āvuso, navo acirapabbajito adhunāgato imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, na tāhaṃ sakkomi vitthārena ācikkhituṃ. Ayaṃ so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho rājagahe viharati tapodārāme. Taṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ puccha. Yathā te bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāsī’”ti.

When this was said, Venerable Sir, that deity said to me: 'And how, monk, have sensual pleasures subject to time been declared by the Blessed One as having much suffering, much distress, and the danger in them is greater? And how is this Dhamma visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be individually realized by the wise?' When this was said, Venerable Sir, I said to that deity: 'Friend, I am new, not long gone forth, and have only recently come to this Dhamma and Discipline. I am not able to explain this in detail. That Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is dwelling at Rājagaha in the Tapodārāma. Approach that Blessed One and ask about this matter. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so you should remember it.'

“Evaṃ [M 1.0011] vutte, bhante, sā devatā maṃ etadavoca – ‘na kho, bhikkhu, sukaro so bhagavā amhehi upasaṅkamituṃ, aññāhi mahesakkhāhi devatāhi parivuto. Sace kho, tvaṃ bhikkhu, taṃ bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ puccheyyāsi, mayampi āgaccheyyāma [T 1.0016] dhammassavanāyā’ti. Sace, bhante, tassā devatāya saccaṃ vacanaṃ, idheva sā devatā avidūre”ti.

When this was said, Venerable Sir, that deity said to me: 'Indeed, monk, it is not easy for us to approach the Blessed One, for he is surrounded by other deities of great power. But if you, monk, were to approach the Blessed One and ask about this matter, we too would come to hear the Dhamma.' If, Venerable Sir, that deity's words are true, that deity must be right here, not far away.

Evaṃ vutte, sā devatā āyasmantaṃ samiddhiṃ etadavoca – “puccha, bhikkhu, puccha, bhikkhu, yamahaṃ anuppattā”ti.

When this was said, that deity said this to the Venerable Samiddhi: 'Ask, monk, ask! I have arrived.'

Atha kho bhagavā taṃ devataṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One addressed that deity with verses:

“Akkheyyasaññino sattā, akkheyyasmiṃ patiṭṭhitā;

Akkheyyaṃ apariññāya, yogamāyanti maccuno.

“Beings who perceive in terms of the expressible, established in the expressible, not fully understanding the expressible, come under the yoke of Death.

“Akkheyyañca pariññāya, akkhātāraṃ na maññati;

Tañhi tassa na hotīti, yena naṃ vajjā na tassa atthi;

Sace vijānāsi vadehi yakkhā”ti yakkhīti (pī. ka.).

“And having fully understood the expressible, one does not conceive of an expounder, for that by which one might be described does not exist for him. If you understand, speak, O Yakkha.”

“Na khvāhaṃ, bhante, imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tathā bhāsatu yathāhaṃ imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ jāneyya”nti.

“Venerable Sir, I do not understand in detail the meaning of what the Blessed One has stated in brief. It would be good if the Blessed One would speak in such a way that I may understand in detail the meaning of what the Blessed One has stated in brief.”

“Samo [P 1.0012] visesī uda vā athavā (sī. pī.) nihīno,

Yo maññatī so vivadetha sopi vadetha (ka.) tena;

Tīsu [V 1.0014] vidhāsu avikampamāno,

Samo visesīti na tassa hoti;

Sace vijānāsi vadehi yakkhā”ti.

“Whoever conceives ‘I am equal,’ ‘I am superior,’ or ‘I am inferior,’ would dispute on that account. But for one unshaken in these three modes, the thought ‘I am equal’ or ‘I am superior’ does not arise. If you understand, speak, O Yakkha.”

“Imassāpi [T 1.0017] khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa na vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tathā bhāsatu yathāhaṃ imassa bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ jāneyya”nti.

“Venerable Sir, of this also I do not understand in detail the meaning of what the Blessed One has stated in brief. It would be good if the Blessed One would speak in such a way that I might understand in detail the meaning of what the Blessed One has stated in brief.”

“Pahāsi saṅkhaṃ na vimānamajjhagā, acchecchi acchejji (syā. kaṃ. ka.) taṇhaṃ idha nāmarūpe;

Taṃ chinnaganthaṃ anighaṃ nirāsaṃ, pariyesamānā nājjhagamuṃ;

Devā manussā idha vā huraṃ vā, saggesu vā sabbanivesanesu;

Sace vijānāsi vadehi yakkhā”ti.

“He has abandoned reckoning, has not resorted to conceit; he has cut off craving here in name-and-form. Him, with bonds cut, free from trouble, without longing—searching for him, they did not find him: gods and humans, here or beyond, in the heavens or in any abode. If you understand, speak, O Yakkha.”

“Imassa [M 1.0012] khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi –

“Venerable Sir, of this brief statement spoken by the Blessed One, I understand the meaning in detail thus:

“Pāpaṃ na kayirā vacasā manasā,

Kāyena vā kiñcana sabbaloke;

Kāme pahāya satimā sampajāno,

Dukkhaṃ na sevetha anatthasaṃhita”nti.

“Let one do no evil whatsoever by speech, mind, or body in all the world. Having abandoned sensual pleasures, mindful and clearly comprehending, one should not cultivate suffering that is unbeneficial.”

Nandanavaggo dutiyo.

The Nandana Chapter, the Second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Nandanā [T 1.0018] nandati ceva, natthiputtasamena ca;

Khattiyo saṇamāno ca, niddātandī ca dukkaraṃ;

Hirī kuṭikā navamo, dasamo vutto samiddhināti.

Nandana, Nandati, and Natthiputtasama; Khattiya, Saṇamāna, Niddātandī, and Dukkara; Hiri, Kuṭikā as the ninth, and the tenth is said to be Samiddhi.

3. Sattivaggo

3. The Chapter on the Spear

1. Sattisuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Spear

21. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0015][P 1.0013]. Ekamantaṃ [T 1.0019] ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

21. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho, ḍayhamānova ḍayhamāneva (sabbattha) matthake;

Kāmarāgappahānāya, sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.

“As though pierced by a spear, or as though one's head were on fire, a mindful bhikkhu should wander for the abandoning of sensual lust.”

“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho, ḍayhamānova matthake;

Sakkāyadiṭṭhippahānāya, sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.

“As though pierced by a spear, or as though one's head were on fire, a mindful bhikkhu should wander for the abandoning of identity-view.”

2. Phusatisuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Contact

22.

22.

“Nāphusantaṃ phusati ca, phusantañca tato phuse;

Tasmā phusantaṃ phusati, appaduṭṭhapadosina”nti.

“It does not touch one who is not touching, but it does touch one who is touching. Therefore, it touches the one who is touching, the one who harms the harmless.”

“Yo [M 1.0013] appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati,

Suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa;

Tameva bālaṃ pacceti pāpaṃ,

Sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṃva khitto”ti.

“Whoever harms a harmless man, a person who is pure and stainless, that evil returns to that very fool, like fine dust thrown against the wind.”

3. Jaṭāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Tangle

23.

23.

“Anto [T 1.0020] jaṭā bahi jaṭā, jaṭāya jaṭitā pajā;

Taṃ taṃ gotama pucchāmi, ko imaṃ vijaṭaye jaṭa”nti.

“A tangle within, a tangle without, this generation is entangled in a tangle. I ask you this, O Gotama: who can disentangle this tangle?”

“Sīle [V 1.0016] patiṭṭhāya naro sapañño, cittaṃ paññañca bhāvayaṃ;

Ātāpī nipako bhikkhu, so imaṃ vijaṭaye jaṭaṃ.

“A wise person, established in virtue, developing concentration and insight; an ardent and prudent bhikkhu, this one can disentangle this tangle.

“Yesaṃ rāgo ca doso ca, avijjā ca virājitā;

Khīṇāsavā arahanto, tesaṃ vijaṭitā jaṭā.

“For those in whom lust, hatred, and ignorance have faded away—the Arahants with taints destroyed—for them, the tangle is disentangled.

“Yattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhati;

Paṭighaṃ rūpasaññā ca, etthesā chijjate vijaṭe (ka.) jaṭā”ti.

“Wherein name-and-form cease without remainder, along with perception of resistance and perception of form; it is there this tangle is cut.”

4. Manonivāraṇasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Restraining the Mind

24. “Yato [P 1.0014] yato mano nivāraye,

24. “From whatever it may be that one would restrain the mind,

Na dukkhameti naṃ tato tato;

Sa sabbato mano nivāraye,

Sa sabbato dukkhā pamuccati”.

from that, suffering does not come to one. One should restrain the mind from everything; from all suffering, one is released.”

“Na sabbato mano nivāraye,

Na mano saṃyatattamāgataṃ;

Yato yato ca pāpakaṃ,

Tato tato mano nivāraye”ti.

“One should not restrain the mind from everything, nor the mind that has come to be restrained. From whatever evil may arise, from that one should restrain the mind.”

5. Arahantasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Arahant

25.

25.

“Yo hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ katāvī,

Khīṇāsavo antimadehadhārī;

Ahaṃ [T 1.0021] vadāmītipi so vadeyya,

Mamaṃ vadantītipi so vadeyyā”ti.

“The bhikkhu who is an Arahant, who has done what is to be done, whose taints are destroyed, bearing his final body—would he say, ‘I speak’? Would he say, ‘They speak of me’?”

“Yo [V 1.0017][M 1.0014] hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ katāvī,

Khīṇāsavo antimadehadhārī;

Ahaṃ vadāmītipi so vadeyya,

Mamaṃ vadantītipi so vadeyya;

Loke samaññaṃ kusalo viditvā,

Vohāramattena so sa (?) vohareyyā”ti.

“The bhikkhu who is an Arahant, who has done what is to be done, whose taints are destroyed, bearing his final body—he may say, ‘I speak,’ and he may say, ‘They speak of me.’ Skilled, having known the designations in the world, he would speak only by way of convention.”

“Yo hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ katāvī,

Khīṇāsavo antimadehadhārī;

Mānaṃ nu kho so upagamma bhikkhu,

Ahaṃ vadāmītipi so vadeyya;

Mamaṃ vadantītipi so vadeyyā”ti.

“The bhikkhu who is an Arahant, who has done what is to be done, whose taints are destroyed, bearing his final body—having resorted to conceit, would that bhikkhu say, ‘I speak’? Would he say, ‘They speak of me’?”

“Pahīnamānassa na santi ganthā,

Vidhūpitā mānaganthassa sabbe;

Sa vītivatto maññataṃ mānanaṃ (sī.), maññītaṃ (?) sumedho,

Ahaṃ [P 1.0015] vadāmītipi so vadeyya.

“For one with conceit abandoned, there are no bonds; all bonds of conceit have been shattered. That one of good wisdom has overcome conceiving; he may say, ‘I speak,’

“Mamaṃ vadantītipi so vadeyya;

Loke samaññaṃ kusalo viditvā;

Vohāramattena so vohareyyā”ti.

and he may say, ‘They speak of me.’ Skilled, having known the designations in the world, he would speak only by way of convention.”

6. Pajjotasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Radiance

26.

26.

“Kati [T 1.0022] lokasmiṃ pajjotā, yehi loko pakāsati pabhāsati (ka. sī.);

Bhagavantaṃ bhavantaṃ (ka.) puṭṭhumāgamma, kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya”nti.

“How many radiances are there in the world, by which the world is illuminated? Having come to ask the Blessed One, how may we know this?”

“Cattāro [V 1.0018] loke pajjotā, pañcamettha na vijjati;

Divā tapati ādicco, rattimābhāti candimā.

“There are four radiances in the world; a fifth is not found here. By day the sun shines; by night the moon gives light.

“Atha aggi divārattiṃ, tattha tattha pakāsati;

Sambuddho tapataṃ seṭṭho, esā ābhā anuttarā”ti.

“Then fire illuminates here and there, by day and by night. The Fully Enlightened One is the foremost of those that shine; this radiance is unsurpassed.”

7. Sarasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Streams

27.

27.

“Kuto [M 1.0015] sarā nivattanti, kattha vaṭṭaṃ na vattati;

Kattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhatī”ti.

“From where do the streams turn back? Where does the cycle not revolve? Where do name-and-form cease without remainder?”

“Yattha āpo ca pathavī, tejo vāyo na gādhati;

Ato sarā nivattanti, ettha vaṭṭaṃ na vattati;

Ettha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhatī”ti.

“Where water and earth, fire and air, find no footing; from there the streams turn back, here the cycle does not revolve. Here name-and-form cease without remainder.”

8. Mahaddhanasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Great Wealth

28.

28.

“Mahaddhanā mahābhogā, raṭṭhavantopi khattiyā;

Aññamaññābhigijjhanti, kāmesu analaṅkatā.

“Even kings, possessing great wealth, vast enjoyments, and ruling over kingdoms, covet one another, being insatiate in sensual pleasures.

“Tesu ussukkajātesu, bhavasotānusārisu;

Kedha taṇhaṃ rodhataṇhaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), gedhataṇhaṃ (ka.) pajahiṃsu pavāhiṃsu (syā. kaṃ. ka.), ke lokasmiṃ anussukā”ti.

“Among those in whom striving has arisen, who follow the stream of becoming—who have abandoned the craving of attachment? Who in the world are without striving?”

“Hitvā [T 1.0023] agāraṃ pabbajitā, hitvā puttaṃ pasuṃ viyaṃ;

Hitvā rāgañca dosañca, avijjañca virājiya;

Khīṇāsavā arahanto, te lokasmiṃ anussukā”ti.

“Having abandoned the home and gone forth; having abandoned beloved children and cattle; having abandoned lust and hatred, and become dispassionate towards ignorance; they, the Arahants whose taints are destroyed, are without striving in the world.”

9. Catucakkasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Four Wheels

29.

29.

“Catucakkaṃ [V 1.0019][P 1.0016] navadvāraṃ, puṇṇaṃ lobhena saṃyutaṃ;

Paṅkajātaṃ mahāvīra, kathaṃ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.

“O Great Hero, for this body with four wheels and nine doors, filled and bound by greed, born from mud—how will there be an escape?”

“Chetvā naddhiṃ varattañca, icchā lobhañca pāpakaṃ;

Samūlaṃ taṇhamabbuyha, evaṃ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.

“Having cut the strap and the thong, evil desire and greed, and having uprooted craving together with its root—thus will there be an escape.”

10. Eṇijaṅghasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Deer-Shanked One

30.

30.

“Eṇijaṅghaṃ kisaṃ vīraṃ, appāhāraṃ alolupaṃ;

Sīhaṃ vekacaraṃ nāgaṃ, kāmesu anapekkhinaṃ;

Upasaṅkamma pucchāma, kathaṃ dukkhā pamuccatī”ti.

“The one with shanks like a deer, lean, heroic, of little food, ungreedy; like a solitary lion, like a solitary elephant, unconcerned with sensual pleasures—having approached, we ask: How is one freed from suffering?”

“Pañca [M 1.0016] kāmaguṇā loke, manochaṭṭhā paveditā;

Ettha chandaṃ virājetvā, evaṃ dukkhā pamuccatī”ti.

“The five strands of sensual pleasure in the world, with mind as the sixth, have been declared. Having become dispassionate towards desire for these, thus one is freed from suffering.”

Sattivaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on the Spear.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Sattiyā phusati ceva, jaṭā manonivāraṇā;

Arahantena pajjoto, sarā mahaddhanena ca;

Catucakkena navamaṃ, eṇijaṅghena te dasāti.

The Spear, Touches, Matted Hair, Hindrance of Mind, the Arahant, Radiance, Streams, and Great Wealth; with Four Wheels as the ninth, and Deer-Shanked One—these are the ten.

4. Satullapakāyikavaggo

4. The Chapter on the Satullapakāyika Devas

1. Sabbhisuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Virtuous

31. Evaṃ [T 1.0024][V 1.0020] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0017] ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

31. Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī at Jeta’s Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍika’s park. Then, when the night was advanced, a number of devas of the Satullapakāyika group, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the whole of Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deva recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha krubbetha (ka.) santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, seyyo hoti na pāpiyo”ti.

“One should associate only with the virtuous; one should foster fellowship with the virtuous. Having understood the good Dhamma of the virtuous, one becomes better, not worse.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then, another deva recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, paññā labbhati paññaṃ labhati (syā. kaṃ.) nāññato”ti.

“One should associate only with the virtuous; one should foster fellowship with the virtuous. Having understood the good Dhamma of the virtuous, one obtains wisdom, and not from another.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then, another deva recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, sokamajjhe na socatī”ti.

“One should associate only with the virtuous; one should foster fellowship with the virtuous. Having understood the good Dhamma of the virtuous, one does not grieve in the midst of those who grieve.”

Atha [M 1.0017] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then, another deva recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sabbhireva [T 1.0025] samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, ñātimajjhe virocatī”ti.

“One should associate only with the virtuous; one should foster fellowship with the virtuous. Having understood the good Dhamma of the virtuous, one shines in the midst of one’s relatives.”

Atha [V 1.0021] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then, another deva recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, sattā gacchanti suggati”nti.

“One should associate only with the virtuous; one should foster fellowship with the virtuous. Having understood the good Dhamma of the virtuous, beings go to a good destination.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then, another deva recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, sattā tiṭṭhanti sātata”nti.

“One should associate only with the virtuous; one should foster fellowship with the virtuous. Having understood the good Dhamma of the virtuous, beings are established in happiness for a long time.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kassa nu kho, bhagavā, subhāsita”nti? Sabbāsaṃ vo subhāsitaṃ pariyāyena, api ca mamapi suṇātha –

Then, another deva said this to the Blessed One: “Whose speech, Blessed One, is well-spoken?” “All of your words are well-spoken in their own way. However, listen also to mine:

“Sabbhireva [P 1.0018] samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.

“One should associate only with the virtuous; one should foster fellowship with the virtuous. Having understood the good Dhamma of the virtuous, one is released from all suffering.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā tā devatāyo bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsūti.

The Blessed One said this. Delighted, those devas paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping their right side towards him, and vanished right there.

2. Maccharisuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Stinginess

32. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ [T 1.0026] gāthaṃ abhāsi –

32. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then, when the night was far advanced, a number of deities from the Satullapa group, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta's Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Maccherā [V 1.0022] ca pamādā ca, evaṃ dānaṃ na dīyati diyyati (ka.);

Puññaṃ ākaṅkhamānena, deyyaṃ hoti vijānatā”ti.

“Because of stinginess and negligence, a gift is thus not given. A gift should be given by one who desires merit and knows its fruit.”

Atha [M 1.0018] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then another deity recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Yasseva bhīto na dadāti maccharī, tadevādadato bhayaṃ;

Jighacchā ca pipāsā ca, yassa bhāyati maccharī;

Tameva bālaṃ phusati, asmiṃ loke paramhi ca.

“That which the miser fears when not giving is the very danger that comes to the non-giver. Hunger and thirst, which the miser fears, afflict that very fool in this world and in the next.

“Tasmā vineyya maccheraṃ, dajjā dānaṃ malābhibhū;

Puññāni paralokasmiṃ, patiṭṭhā honti pāṇina”nti.

“Therefore, having removed stinginess, one who has overcome that stain should give a gift. Merits are the support for beings in the next world.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then another deity recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Te matesu na mīyanti, panthānaṃva sahabbajaṃ;

Appasmiṃ ye pavecchanti, esa dhammo sanantano.

“Those who give from what little they have, like fellow travelers on a journey, are not dead among the dead. This is the eternal law.

“Appasmeke pavecchanti, bahuneke na dicchare;

Appasmā dakkhiṇā dinnā, sahassena samaṃ mitā”ti.

“Some give from a little, while others with much do not give. A donation given from a little is measured as equal to a thousand.”

Atha [P 1.0019] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then another deity recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Duddadaṃ dadamānānaṃ, dukkaraṃ kamma kubbataṃ;

Asanto nānukubbanti, sataṃ dhammo duranvayo durannayo (sī.).

“They give what is hard to give and do the deed that is hard to do. The unvirtuous do not emulate them; the Dhamma of the good is hard to follow.

“Tasmā [T 1.0027] satañca asataṃ asatañca (sī. syā. kaṃ.), nānā hoti ito gati;

Asanto nirayaṃ yanti, santo saggaparāyanā”ti.

“Therefore, from here the destination of the good and the unvirtuous is different. The unvirtuous go to hell; the good have heaven as their destination.”

Atha [V 1.0023] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike etadavoca – “kassa nu kho, bhagavā, subhāsita”nti?

Then another deity said this to the Blessed One: “Whose speech, Blessed One, is well-spoken?”

“Sabbāsaṃ vo subhāsitaṃ pariyāyena; api ca mamapi suṇātha –

“All of your speeches are, in their own way, well-spoken. However, listen also to mine:

“Dhammaṃ care yopi samuñjakaṃ care,

Dārañca posaṃ dadamappakasmiṃ;

Sataṃ sahassānaṃ sahassayāginaṃ,

Kalampi nāgghanti tathāvidhassa te”ti.

“One who practices the Dhamma, even if living by gleaning, supporting a wife and giving from little—the sacrifices of one hundred thousand who each offer a thousand are not worth even a fraction of such a one.”

Atha [M 1.0019] kho aparā devatā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then another deity addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Kenesa yañño vipulo mahaggato,

Samena dinnassa na agghameti;

Kathaṃ idaṃ padaṃ katthaci sīhaḷapotthake natthi sataṃ sahassānaṃ sahassayāginaṃ,

Kalampi nāgghanti tathāvidhassa te”ti.

“For what reason does this vast and great sacrifice not equal the worth of a gift given righteously? How is it that the sacrifices of one hundred thousand who each offer a thousand are not worth even a fraction of such a one?”

“Dadanti heke visame niviṭṭhā,

Chetvā vadhitvā atha socayitvā;

Sā [T 1.0028] dakkhiṇā assumukhā sadaṇḍā,

Samena dinnassa na agghameti.

“Some give while established in unrighteousness; having struck and killed, and then having caused sorrow. Such a donation, given with tear-filled faces and with force, does not equal the worth of a gift given righteously.

“Evaṃ sataṃ sahassānaṃ sahassayāginaṃ;

Kalampi nāgghanti tathāvidhassa te”ti.

“Thus, the sacrifices of one hundred thousand who each offer a thousand are not worth even a fraction of such a one.”

3. Sādhusuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on What is Good

33. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 1.0020]. Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā [V 1.0024] abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

33. At Sāvatthī. Then, when the night was far advanced, many radiant deities of the Satullapa group, having exceedingly pleasing complexions, illuminating the entire Jeta's Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, paid homage to the Blessed One, and stood in a suitable place, one deity uttered this inspired utterance in the Blessed One's presence:

“Sādhu kho, mārisa, dānaṃ;

Maccherā ca pamādā ca, evaṃ dānaṃ na dīyati;

Puññaṃ ākaṅkhamānena, deyyaṃ hoti vijānatā”ti.

“Venerable Sir, giving is indeed good. Because of stinginess and negligence, a gift is thus not given. A gift should be given by one who desires merit and knows its fruit.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then another deity uttered this inspired utterance in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Sādhu kho, mārisa, dānaṃ;

Api ca appakasmimpi sāhu dānaṃ”.

“Venerable Sir, giving is indeed good; moreover, giving even a little is good.”

“Appasmeke pavecchanti, bahuneke na dicchare;

Appasmā dakkhiṇā dinnā, sahassena samaṃ mitā”ti.

“Some give from what is little, while others with much do not give. A donation given from what is little is measured as equal to a thousand.”

Atha [M 1.0020] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then another deity uttered this inspired utterance in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Sādhu kho, mārisa, dānaṃ; appakasmimpi sāhu dānaṃ;

Api ca saddhāyapi sāhu dānaṃ”.

“Venerable Sir, giving is indeed good; giving even a little is good; moreover, a gift given with faith is also good.”

“Dānañca yuddhañca samānamāhu,

Appāpi santā bahuke jinanti;

Appampi ce saddahāno dadāti,

Teneva so hoti sukhī paratthā”ti.

“Giving and battle, they say, are the same; even a few who are virtuous conquer many. If one, being faithful, gives even a little, by that alone one is happy in the next life.”

Atha [T 1.0029] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then another deity uttered this inspired utterance in the Blessed One's presence:

“Sādhu [V 1.0025] kho, mārisa, dānaṃ; appakasmimpi sāhu dānaṃ;

Saddhāyapi [P 1.0021] sāhu dānaṃ; api ca dhammaladdhassāpi sāhu dānaṃ”.

“Venerable Sir, giving is indeed good; giving even a little is good; a gift given with faith is good; moreover, a gift from righteously gained wealth is also good.”

“Yo dhammaladdhassa dadāti dānaṃ,

Uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatassa jantu;

Atikkamma so vetaraṇiṃ yamassa,

Dibbāni ṭhānāni upeti macco”ti.

“Whatever being gives a gift from wealth acquired through effort and energy to one who has righteously attained the Dhamma, that mortal, having crossed over Yama's Vetaraṇī, reaches the divine abodes.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then another deity uttered this inspired utterance in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Sādhu kho, mārisa, dānaṃ; appakasmimpi sāhu dānaṃ;

Saddhāyapi sāhu dānaṃ; dhammaladdhassāpi sāhu dānaṃ;

Api [T 1.0030] ca viceyya dānampi sāhu dānaṃ”.

“Venerable Sir, giving is good; giving even a little is good; a gift given with faith is good; a gift from righteously gained wealth is good; moreover, a gift given with discernment is also good.”

“Viceyya dānaṃ sugatappasatthaṃ,

Ye dakkhiṇeyyā idha jīvaloke;

Etesu dinnāni mahapphalāni,

Bījāni vuttāni yathā sukhette”ti.

“Giving with discernment is praised by the Sugata. Those who are worthy of offerings in this living world—gifts given to them are of great fruit, just as seeds sown in a good field.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then another deity uttered this inspired utterance in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Sādhu kho, mārisa, dānaṃ; appakasmimpi sāhu dānaṃ;

Saddhāyapi sāhu dānaṃ; dhammaladdhassāpi sāhu dānaṃ;

Viceyya dānampi sāhu dānaṃ; api ca pāṇesupi sādhu saṃyamo”.

“Venerable Sir, giving is good; giving even a little is good; a gift given with faith is good; a gift from righteously gained wealth is good; a gift given with discernment is good; moreover, restraint towards living beings is also good.”

“Yo [M 1.0021] pāṇabhūtāni pāṇabhūtesu (sī. pī.) aheṭhayaṃ caraṃ,

Parūpavādā na karonti pāpaṃ;

Bhīruṃ [V 1.0026] pasaṃsanti na hi tattha sūraṃ,

Bhayā hi santo na karonti pāpa”nti.

“One who fares along without harming living beings, and does no evil for fear of others’ reproach—they praise the timid in this matter, not the brave. Indeed, the good do not commit evil out of such fear.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kassa [P 1.0022] nu kho, bhagavā, subhāsita”nti?

Then another deity said this to the Blessed One: “Whose speech, Blessed One, is well-spoken?”

“Sabbāsaṃ vo subhāsitaṃ pariyāyena, api ca mamapi suṇātha –

“The speech of all of you is well-spoken in its own way; moreover, you should also listen to my speech:

“Saddhā hi dānaṃ bahudhā pasatthaṃ,

Dānā ca kho dhammapadaṃva seyyo;

Pubbe [T 1.0031] ca hi pubbatare ca santo,

Nibbānamevajjhagamuṃ sapaññā”ti.

“Giving with faith is indeed praised in many ways, but the principle of Dhamma is more excellent than giving. For in the past, and even before that, the good ones endowed with wisdom attained Nibbāna itself.”

4. Nasantisuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on ‘There Are Not’

34. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

34. At one time the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then, late at night, many radiant deities of the Satullapa group, illuminating the entire Jeta's Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Na santi kāmā manujesu niccā,

Santīdha kamanīyāni yesu kāmesu (ka.) baddho;

Yesu pamatto apunāgamanaṃ,

Anāgantā puriso maccudheyyā”ti.

“Permanent sensual pleasures do not exist among humans; here there are desirable things. A person bound and heedless in regard to these is unable to go to the state of non-return from the dominion of Death.”

“Chandajaṃ aghaṃ chandajaṃ dukkhaṃ;

Chandavinayā aghavinayo;

Aghavinayā dukkhavinayo”ti.

“Affliction is born of desire; suffering is born of desire. Through the disciplining of desire, affliction is disciplined. Through the disciplining of affliction, suffering is disciplined.”

“Na [V 1.0027] te kāmā yāni citrāni loke,

Saṅkapparāgo [T 1.0032] purisassa kāmo;

Tiṭṭhanti citrāni tatheva loke,

Athettha dhīrā vinayanti chandaṃ.

“Those things of beauty in the world are not sensual pleasures; lust born of thought is a person's sensual pleasure. Beautiful things remain just as they are in the world, but the wise discipline their desire for them.”

“Kodhaṃ [M 1.0022][P 1.0023] jahe vippajaheyya mānaṃ,

Saṃyojanaṃ sabbamatikkameyya;

Taṃ nāmarūpasmimasajjamānaṃ,

Akiñcanaṃ nānupatanti dukkhā.

“One should abandon anger, renounce pride, and overcome all fetters. For one who does not cling to name-and-form, possessing nothing, sufferings do not befall.”

“Pahāsi saṅkhaṃ na vimānamajjhagā na ca mānamajjhagā (ka. sī.), na vimānamāgā (syā. kaṃ.),

Acchecchi taṇhaṃ idha nāmarūpe;

Taṃ chinnaganthaṃ anighaṃ nirāsaṃ,

Pariyesamānā nājjhagamuṃ;

Devā manussā idha vā huraṃ vā,

Saggesu vā sabbanivesanesū”ti.

“He has abandoned classifications, has not come to conceit; he has cut off craving here for name-and-form. Him, with bonds cut, untroubled, without longing—searching for him, they did not find him, neither gods nor humans, here or hereafter, in the heavens or in any abodes.”

“Taṃ ce hi nāddakkhuṃ tathāvimuttaṃ (iccāyasmā mogharājā),

Devā manussā idha vā huraṃ vā;

Naruttamaṃ atthacaraṃ narānaṃ,

Ye taṃ namassanti pasaṃsiyā te”ti.

(Venerable Mogharāja said:) “Regarding him, thus liberated, whom gods and humans did not find here or elsewhere—that highest of men who acts for the welfare of humans—are those who pay homage to him praiseworthy?”

“Pasaṃsiyā tepi bhavanti bhikkhū (mogharājāti bhagavā),

Ye taṃ namassanti tathāvimuttaṃ;

Aññāya [T 1.0033] dhammaṃ vicikicchaṃ pahāya,

Saṅgātigā tepi bhavanti bhikkhū”ti.

(The Blessed One said to Mogharāja:) “Those monks who pay homage to him who is thus liberated are also praiseworthy. Having understood the Dhamma and abandoned doubt, those monks also go beyond attachment.”

5. Ujjhānasaññisuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Perception of Disparagement

35. Ekaṃ [V 1.0028] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho sambahulā ujjhānasaññikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā vehāsaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Vehāsaṃ [P 1.0024] ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

35. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then, late in the night, several deities with the perception of disparagement, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they stood in the air. Standing in the air, one deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Aññathā santamattānaṃ, aññathā yo pavedaye;

Nikacca kitavasseva, bhuttaṃ theyyena tassa taṃ.

“He who, being one way, presents himself as another—what he partakes of is taken by theft, like a cunning cheat’s deception.”

“Yañhi kayirā tañhi vade, yaṃ na kayirā na taṃ vade;

Akarontaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ, parijānanti paṇḍitā”ti.

“One should speak of what one does; one should not speak of what one does not do. The wise recognize one who speaks but does not act.”

“Na yidaṃ bhāsitamattena, ekantasavanena vā;

Anukkamitave sakkā, yāyaṃ paṭipadā daḷhā;

Yāya dhīrā pamuccanti, jhāyino mārabandhanā.

“Not by mere speech, nor by extensive hearing, can one follow this firm path by which the wise, being meditators, are freed from Māra’s bonds.”

“Na [M 1.0023] ve dhīrā pakubbanti, viditvā lokapariyāyaṃ;

Aññāya nibbutā dhīrā, tiṇṇā loke visattika”nti.

“Indeed, the wise do not act improperly, having understood the course of the world. The wise, having realized, are extinguished, having crossed over worldly clinging.”

Atha [T 1.0034] kho tā devatāyo pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhahitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “accayo no, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ yathābālā yathāmūḷhā yathāakusalā (sabbattha), yā mayaṃ bhagavantaṃ āsādetabbaṃ amaññimhā. Tāsaṃ no, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā sitaṃ pātvākāsi. Atha kho tā devatāyo bhiyyosomattāya ujjhāyantiyo vehāsaṃ abbhuggañchuṃ. Ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then those deities, having settled on the earth, bowed their heads at the Blessed One’s feet and said this: “Venerable Sir, a transgression has overcome us, according to our foolishness, our delusion, our unskillfulness, in that we presumed to offend the Blessed One. Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One accept our transgression as a transgression, for the sake of restraint in the future.” Then the Blessed One made a smile manifest. Then those deities, disparaging even more, ascended into the air. One deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Accayaṃ [V 1.0029] desayantīnaṃ, yo ce na paṭigaṇhati;

Kopantaro dosagaru, sa veraṃ paṭimuñcatī”ti.

“If one does not accept the transgression of those who confess it, being one with anger within, holding hatred as important, that one binds enmity to himself.”

“Accayo ce na vijjetha, nocidhāpagataṃ nocīdha apahataṃ (syā. kaṃ.), nocidhāpakataṃ (?) siyā;

Verāni na ca sammeyyuṃ, kenīdha verāni ca sammeyyuṃ, tenidha (sī.) kusalo siyā”ti.

“If transgression did not exist, there would be no fault here. And if enmities were not pacified, by what means would one be skillful here?”

“Kassaccayā na vijjanti, kassa natthi apāgataṃ;

Ko na sammohamāpādi, ko ca dhīro kodha dhīro (syā. kaṃ.) sadā sato”ti.

“For whom do transgressions not exist? For whom is there no fault? Who has not fallen into confusion? And who is the wise one, always mindful?”

“Tathāgatassa [P 1.0025] buddhassa, sabbabhūtānukampino;

Tassaccayā na vijjanti, tassa natthi apāgataṃ;

So na sammohamāpādi, sova sodha (syā. kaṃ.) dhīro sadā sato”ti.

“For the Tathāgata, the Buddha, compassionate towards all beings, for him transgressions do not exist; for him there is no fault. He has not fallen into confusion; he alone is the wise one, always mindful.”

“Accayaṃ desayantīnaṃ, yo ce na paṭigaṇhati;

Kopantaro [T 1.0035] dosagaru, sa veraṃ paṭimuñcati;

Taṃ veraṃ nābhinandāmi, paṭiggaṇhāmi voccaya”nti.

“If one does not accept the transgression of those who confess it, being one with anger within, holding hatred as important, that one binds enmity to himself. I do not delight in that enmity; I accept your transgression.”

6. Saddhāsuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Faith

36. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho sambahulā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ [M 1.0024] obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

36. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then, when the night was advanced, a multitude of Satullapakāyika deities, of surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Saddhā dutiyā purisassa hoti,

No ce assaddhiyaṃ avatiṭṭhati;

Yaso [V 1.0030] ca kittī ca tatvassa hoti,

Saggañca so gacchati sarīraṃ vihāyā”ti.

“Faith is a person’s companion; if one does not stand in faithlessness, then for that person there is fame and renown. Having abandoned the body, one goes to heaven.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then another deity recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Kodhaṃ jahe vippajaheyya mānaṃ,

Saṃyojanaṃ sabbamatikkameyya;

Taṃ nāmarūpasmimasajjamānaṃ,

Akiñcanaṃ nānupatanti saṅgā”ti.

“One should abandon anger, one should renounce conceit; one should overcome every fetter. To him, not attached to name-and-form, who is without impediment, attachments do not befall.”

“Pamādamanuyuñjanti[T 1.0036], bālā dummedhino janā;

Appamādañca medhāvī, dhanaṃ seṭṭhaṃva rakkhati.

Foolish, unwise people engage in negligence; but the wise one guards diligence as one would a supreme treasure.

“Mā pamādamanuyuñjetha, mā kāmarati santhavaṃ;

Appamatto hi jhāyanto, pappoti paramaṃ sukha”nti.

Do not engage in negligence, nor in intimacy with sensual pleasure. For the heedful one, meditating, attains supreme bliss.

7. Samayasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Assembly

37. Evaṃ [P 1.0026] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi; dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca. Atha kho catunnaṃ suddhāvāsakāyikānaṃ devatānaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi; dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca. Yaṃnūna mayampi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike paccekaṃ gāthaṃ paccekagāthaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhāseyyāmā”ti.

37. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Wood, together with a great assembly of bhikkhus, five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants. And deities from the ten world-systems had for the most part assembled to see the Blessed One and the assembly of bhikkhus. Then this thought occurred to four deities of the Pure Abodes: “This Blessed One is dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Wood, together with a great assembly of bhikkhus, five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants. And deities from the ten world-systems have for the most part assembled to see the Blessed One and the assembly of bhikkhus. What if we were to approach the Blessed One and, having approached, each recite a verse in his presence?”

Atha [M 1.0025] kho tā devatā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ [V 1.0031] vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya. Evameva – suddhāvāsesu devesu antarahitā bhagavato purato pāturahesuṃ. Atha kho tā devatā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ [T 1.0037] gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then those deities—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—even so, they vanished from the Pure Abodes and appeared before the Blessed One. Then those deities, having paid homage to the Blessed One, stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Mahāsamayo pavanasmiṃ, devakāyā samāgatā;

Āgatamha imaṃ dhammasamayaṃ, dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅgha”nti.

“A great assembly is in the forest; the hosts of deities have assembled. We have come to this Dhamma-assembly to see the unconquered Saṅgha.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Tatra bhikkhavo samādahaṃsu, cittamattano ujukaṃ akaṃsu ujukamakaṃsu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.);

Sārathīva nettāni gahetvā, indriyāni rakkhanti paṇḍitā”ti.

“There the bhikkhus have concentrated themselves, they have made their own minds straight. Like a charioteer holding the reins, the wise ones guard their faculties.”

Atha [P 1.0027] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Chetvā khīlaṃ chetvā palighaṃ, indakhīlaṃ ūhacca manejā;

Te caranti suddhā vimalā, cakkhumatā sudantā susunāgā”ti.

“Having cut the stake, having cut the cross-bar, having uprooted the threshold-post, being without agitation, they wander pure and stainless, endowed with vision, well-tamed, young noble ones.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Ye keci buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatāse, na te gamissanti apāyabhūmiṃ;

Pahāya mānusaṃ dehaṃ, devakāyaṃ paripūressantī”ti.

“Whoever has gone to the Buddha for refuge, they will not go to the plane of misery. Having abandoned the human body, they will fill the host of devas.”

8. Sakalikasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Stone Splinter

38. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati maddakucchismiṃ [T 1.0038] migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavato pādo sakalikāya sakkhalikāya (ka.) khato hoti. Bhusā sudaṃ bhagavato vedanā vattanti sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā tippā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā; tā sudaṃ bhagavā sato sampajāno [V 1.0032] adhivāseti avihaññamāno. Atha kho bhagavā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññāpetvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappeti pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno.

38. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi Deer Park. Now at that time, the Blessed One’s foot had been injured by a stone splinter. Indeed, severe feelings arose in the Blessed One—bodily feelings that were painful, intense, harsh, sharp, unpleasant, and disagreeable. But the Blessed One endured them, mindful and clearly comprehending, without being distressed. Then the Blessed One, having folded his outer robe into four, lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, placing one foot slightly over the other, mindful and clearly comprehending.

Atha [M 1.0026] kho sattasatā satullapakāyikā devatāyo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ maddakucchiṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “nāgo [P 1.0028] vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; nāgavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.

Then, when the night was far advanced, seven hundred devas of the Satullapa group, with surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire Maddakucchi, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deva uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One: “Truly, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is a great elephant! And with the fortitude of a great elephant, he endures the arisen bodily feelings—painful, intense, harsh, sharp, unpleasant, and disagreeable—mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “sīho vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; sīhavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.

Then another deva uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One: “Truly, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is a lion! And with the fortitude of a lion, he endures the arisen bodily feelings—painful, intense, harsh, sharp, unpleasant, and disagreeable—mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed.”

Atha [T 1.0039] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “ājānīyo vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; ājānīyavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.

Then another deva uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One: “Truly, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is a thoroughbred! And with the fortitude of a thoroughbred, he endures the arisen bodily feelings—painful, intense, harsh, sharp, unpleasant, and disagreeable—mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “nisabho vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; nisabhavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.

Then another deva uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One: “Truly, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is a bull! And with the fortitude of a bull, he endures the arisen bodily feelings—painful, intense, harsh, sharp, unpleasant, and disagreeable—mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “dhorayho vata, bho, samaṇo gotamo; dhorayhavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.

Then another deva uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One: “Truly, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is a beast of burden! And with the fortitude of a beast of burden, he endures the arisen bodily feelings—painful, intense, harsh, sharp, unpleasant, and disagreeable—mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “danto vata, bho, samaṇo [V 1.0033] gotamo; dantavatā ca samuppannā sārīrikā vedanā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno”ti.

Then another deva uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One: “Truly, sirs, the ascetic Gotama is tamed! And by virtue of being tamed, he endures the arisen bodily feelings—painful, intense, harsh, sharp, unpleasant, and disagreeable—mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “passa samādhiṃ subhāvitaṃ cittañca suvimuttaṃ, na cābhinataṃ na [T 1.0040] cāpanataṃ na [M 1.0027] ca sasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagataṃ sasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritavataṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sasaṅkhāraniggayhavārivāvataṃ (ka.). Yo evarūpaṃ purisanāgaṃ purisasīhaṃ purisaājānīyaṃ [P 1.0029] purisanisabhaṃ purisadhorayhaṃ purisadantaṃ atikkamitabbaṃ maññeyya kimaññatra adassanā”ti.

Then another deva uttered this inspired utterance in the presence of the Blessed One: “Behold the well-developed concentration and the mind so perfectly freed—not inclined towards, nor inclined away, nor restrained by forceful suppression. Whoever would think to transgress against such a man—a great nāga among men, a lion among men, a thoroughbred among men, a bull among men, a beast of burden among men, a tamed one among men—what else could it be but lack of vision?”

“Pañcavedā sataṃ samaṃ, tapassī brāhmaṇā caraṃ;

Cittañca nesaṃ na sammā vimuttaṃ, hīnattharūpā na pāraṅgamā te.

“Brahmins, masters of the five Vedas, practicing as ascetics for a hundred years—yet their minds are not rightly freed. They are of inferior nature; they do not go to the further shore.”

“Taṇhādhipannā vatasīlabaddhā, lūkhaṃ tapaṃ vassasataṃ carantā;

Cittañca nesaṃ na sammā vimuttaṃ, hīnattharūpā na pāraṅgamā te.

“Those overcome by craving, bound by vows and observances, practicing harsh austerity for a hundred years—yet their minds are not rightly freed. They are of inferior nature; they do not go to the further shore.”

“Na mānakāmassa damo idhatthi, na monamatthi asamāhitassa;

Eko araññe viharaṃ pamatto, na maccudheyyassa tareyya pāra”nti.

“For one who desires conceit, there is no taming here; for one who is unconcentrated, there is no wisdom. Dwelling alone in the forest, heedless, one cannot cross to the further shore of Death’s domain.”

“Mānaṃ pahāya susamāhitatto, sucetaso sabbadhi vippamutto;

Eko araññe viharamappamatto, sa maccudheyyassa tareyya pāra”nti.

“Having abandoned conceit, well-concentrated, with a pure mind, everywhere freed; dwelling alone in the forest, heedful, one can cross to the further shore of Death’s domain.”

9. Paṭhamapajjunnadhītusuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on the Daughter of Pajjunna

39. Evaṃ [T 1.0041] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Atha kho kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ mahāvanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

39. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, at the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Then Kokanadā, the daughter of Pajjunna, late in the night, with surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire Great Wood, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, she paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, that deity Kokanadā, the daughter of Pajjunna, recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Vesāliyaṃ [V 1.0034] vane viharantaṃ, aggaṃ sattassa sambuddhaṃ;

Kokanadāhamasmi [P 1.0030] abhivande, kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā.

“To the one dwelling in the wood at Vesālī, the foremost of beings, the Perfectly Enlightened One, I, Kokanadā, pay homage—Kokanadā, the daughter of Pajjunna.

“Sutameva pure āsi, dhammo cakkhumatānubuddho;

Sāhaṃ dāni sakkhi jānāmi, munino desayato sugatassa.

“Formerly, it was only heard by me that the Dhamma was awakened to by the One with Vision. But now I know it for myself as a witness, from the Sage, the Well-Gone One, as he teaches.
