“Ye keci ariyaṃ dhammaṃ, vigarahantā caranti dummedhā;

Upenti roruvaṃ ghoraṃ, cirarattaṃ dukkhaṃ anubhavanti.

“Whatever foolish ones conduct themselves disparaging the Noble Dhamma, they go to the dreadful Roruva hell and experience suffering for a long time.

“Ye ca kho ariye dhamme, khantiyā upasamena upetā;

Pahāya mānusaṃ dehaṃ, devakāya paripūressantī”ti.

“But those who, in regard to the Noble Dhamma, are endowed with patience and tranquility, having abandoned the human body, will go to fill the host of devas.”

10. Dutiyapajjunnadhītusuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on the Daughter of Pajjunna

40. Evaṃ [M 1.0028] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Atha kho cūḷakokanadā cullakokanadā (sī. syā. kaṃ.) pajjunnassa dhītā [T 1.0042] abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ mahāvanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā cūḷakokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

40. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, at the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Then, late in the night, Cūḷakokanadā, daughter of Pajjunna, of surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire Great Wood, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, she paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, that deity Cūḷakokanadā, daughter of Pajjunna, recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Idhāgamā vijjupabhāsavaṇṇā, kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā;

Buddhañca dhammañca namassamānā, gāthācimā atthavatī abhāsi.

“With radiance like a flash of lightning, Kokanadā, daughter of Pajjunna, came here. Wishing to pay homage to the Buddha and the Dhamma, she spoke these meaningful verses.

“Bahunāpi [P 1.0031] kho taṃ vibhajeyyaṃ, pariyāyena tādiso dhammo;

Saṃkhittamatthaṃ saṃkhittamattaṃ (ka.) lapayissāmi, yāvatā me manasā pariyattaṃ.

“I could indeed analyze that by many methods, for such is the nature of the Dhamma. I will state the meaning in brief, to the extent that it has been mastered by my mind.

“Pāpaṃ na kayirā vacasā manasā,

Kāyena vā kiñcana sabbaloke;

Kāme [V 1.0035] pahāya satimā sampajāno,

Dukkhaṃ na sevetha anatthasaṃhita”nti.

“One should do no evil whatsoever by body, speech, or mind in all the world. Having abandoned sensual pleasures, mindful and clearly comprehending, one should not cultivate suffering that is not connected with benefit.”

Satullapakāyikavaggo catuttho.

The Satullapakāyika Chapter is the fourth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Sabbhimaccharinā sādhu, na santujjhānasaññino;

Saddhā samayo sakalikaṃ, ubho pajjunnadhītaroti.

Sabbhi, Macchariya, Sādhu, Na Santi, and Ujjhānasaññī; Saddhā, Samayo, Sakalika, and the two on Pajjunna's Daughter.

5. Ādittavaggo

5. The Chapter on the Blazing

1. Ādittasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Blazing

41. Evaṃ [T 1.0043] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya [M 1.0029] rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

41. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then, a certain deity, when the night was far advanced, with surpassing radiance illuminating the entire Jeta's Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, that deity recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Ādittasmiṃ agārasmiṃ, yaṃ nīharati bhājanaṃ;

Taṃ tassa hoti atthāya, no ca yaṃ tattha ḍayhati.

“When a house is blazing, whatever possession one carries out, that is for one's benefit, and not that which is burned therein.

“Evaṃ ādittako loko, jarāya maraṇena ca;

Nīharetheva dānena, dinnaṃ hoti sunīhataṃ.

“Likewise, the world is ablaze with aging and death. One should carry forth from it by means of giving; what is given is well carried forth.

“Dinnaṃ [V 1.0036][P 1.0032] sukhaphalaṃ hoti, nādinnaṃ hoti taṃ tathā;

Corā haranti rājāno, aggi ḍahati nassati.

“What is given has pleasant fruit; what is not given is not so. Thieves and kings carry it away; fire burns it, it is lost.

“Atha [T 1.0044] antena jahati, sarīraṃ sapariggahaṃ;

Etadaññāya medhāvī, bhuñjetha ca dadetha ca;

Datvā ca bhutvā ca yathānubhāvaṃ;

Anindito saggamupeti ṭhāna”nti.

“Then, in the end, one abandons the body along with one's possessions. Knowing this, a wise person should both enjoy and give. Having given and enjoyed according to one's means, blameless, one goes to the heavenly abode.”

2. Kiṃdadasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on What is Given

42.

42.

“Kiṃdado balado hoti, kiṃdado hoti vaṇṇado;

Kiṃdado sukhado hoti, kiṃdado hoti cakkhudo;

Ko ca sabbadado hoti, taṃ me akkhāhi pucchito”ti.

“The giver of what is a giver of strength? The giver of what is a giver of beauty? The giver of what is a giver of happiness? The giver of what is a giver of sight? And who is a giver of all? Being asked, declare that to me.”

“Annado balado hoti, vatthado hoti vaṇṇado;

Yānado sukhado hoti, dīpado hoti cakkhudo.

“The giver of food is a giver of strength; the giver of cloth is a giver of beauty; the giver of a vehicle is a giver of happiness; the giver of a lamp is a giver of sight.

“So ca sabbadado hoti, yo dadāti upassayaṃ;

Amataṃ dado ca so hoti, yo dhammamanusāsatī”ti.

“And he is a giver of all who gives a dwelling place; and he is a giver of the Deathless who instructs in the Dhamma.”

3. Annasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Food

43.

43.

“Annamevābhinandanti, ubhaye devamānusā;

Atha ko nāma so yakkho, yaṃ annaṃ nābhinandatī”ti.

“Both gods and humans delight only in food. Then what, indeed, is that yakkha who does not delight in food?”

“Ye [M 1.0030] naṃ dadanti saddhāya, vippasannena cetasā;

Tameva annaṃ bhajati, asmiṃ loke paramhi ca.

“Those who give it with faith, with a confident mind—that very food attends them in this world and in the next.

“Tasmā [T 1.0045][V 1.0037] vineyya maccheraṃ, dajjā dānaṃ malābhibhū;

Puññāni paralokasmiṃ, patiṭṭhā honti pāṇina”nti.

“Therefore, having removed stinginess, having overcome that stain, one should give a gift. Merits are a support for beings in the next world.”

4. Ekamūlasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the One Root

44.

44.

“Ekamūlaṃ dvirāvaṭṭaṃ, timalaṃ pañcapattharaṃ;

Samuddaṃ dvādasāvaṭṭaṃ, pātālaṃ atarī isī”ti.

“The sage has crossed the one-rooted, two-turning, three-stained, five-spread, twelve-whirlpooled ocean, the abyss.”

5. Anomasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Peerless One

45.

45.

“Anomanāmaṃ [P 1.0033] nipuṇatthadassiṃ, paññādadaṃ kāmālaye asattaṃ;

Taṃ passatha sabbaviduṃ sumedhaṃ, ariye pathe kamamānaṃ mahesi”nti.

“Behold him of peerless name, who sees subtle meanings, who bestows wisdom, unattached in the abode of sensual pleasures; the all-knowing, the greatly wise, the great sage treading the Noble Path.”

6. Accharāsuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Celestial Nymphs

46.

46.

“Accharāgaṇasaṅghuṭṭhaṃ, pisācagaṇasevitaṃ;

Vanantaṃ mohanaṃ nāma, kathaṃ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.

“Resounding with hosts of celestial nymphs, frequented by hosts of spirits—that forest named ‘Bewilderment,’ how will there be a passing beyond?”

“Ujuko nāma so maggo, abhayā nāma sā disā;

Ratho akūjano nāma, dhammacakkehi saṃyuto.

“That path is named ‘Straight,’ that direction is named ‘Fearless.’ The chariot is named ‘Soundless,’ fitted with wheels of Dhamma.

“Hirī tassa apālambo, satyassa parivāraṇaṃ;

Dhammāhaṃ sārathiṃ brūmi, sammādiṭṭhipurejavaṃ.

“Moral shame is its back-rest, mindfulness its protective screen. I declare the Dhamma to be the charioteer, with right view as the forerunner.

“Yassa etādisaṃ yānaṃ, itthiyā purisassa vā;

Sa ve etena yānena, nibbānasseva santike”ti.

“For whatever woman or man has such a vehicle, they indeed, by means of that vehicle, are in the very presence of Nibbāna.”

7. Vanaropasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Planting Groves

47.

47.

“Kesaṃ [T 1.0046][V 1.0038] divā ca ratto ca, sadā puññaṃ pavaḍḍhati;

Dhammaṭṭhā sīlasampannā, ke janā saggagāmino”ti.

“For whom does merit always increase, by day and by night? Which people, established in Dhamma and accomplished in virtue, are goers to the heavenly world?”

“Ārāmaropā vanaropā, ye janā setukārakā;

Papañca udapānañca, ye dadanti upassayaṃ.

“Those people who are planters of parks and planters of groves, who are builders of bridges; and those who provide water-stands, wells, and resting places.

“Tesaṃ [M 1.0031] divā ca ratto ca, sadā puññaṃ pavaḍḍhati;

Dhammaṭṭhā sīlasampannā, te janā saggagāmino”ti.

“For them, merit always increases, by day and by night. Established in Dhamma, accomplished in virtue, those people are goers to the heavenly world.”

8. Jetavanasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Jetavana

48.

48.

“Idañhi taṃ jetavanaṃ, isisaṅghanisevitaṃ;

Āvutthaṃ āvuṭṭhaṃ (ka.) dhammarājena, pītisañjananaṃ mama.

“This is that Jetavana, frequented by the assembly of sages, inhabited by the King of Dhamma, a generator of joy for me.

“Kammaṃ [P 1.0034] vijjā ca dhammo ca, sīlaṃ jīvitamuttamaṃ;

Etena maccā sujjhanti, na gottena dhanena vā.

“Action, knowledge, and Dhamma, virtue and the supreme life—by these are mortals purified, not by lineage or by wealth.

“Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso, sampassaṃ atthamattano;

Yoniso vicine dhammaṃ, evaṃ tattha visujjhati.

“Therefore, a wise person, seeing their own true welfare, should judiciously investigate the Dhamma; in this way, one is purified therein.

“Sāriputtova paññāya, sīlena upasamena ca;

Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu, etāvaparamo siyā”ti.

“Sāriputta is supreme in wisdom, virtue, and tranquility. Even a monk who has gone to the far shore would be supreme only to this extent.”

9. Maccharisuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Stinginess

49.

49.

“Yedha [V 1.0039] maccharino loke, kadariyā paribhāsakā;

Aññesaṃ dadamānānaṃ, antarāyakarā narā.

“Those people here in the world who are stingy, miserly, and abusive, who create obstacles for others who are giving—

“Kīdiso [T 1.0047] tesaṃ vipāko, samparāyo ca kīdiso;

Bhagavantaṃ puṭṭhumāgamma, kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya”nti.

“What is their result, and what is their future state? Having come to ask the Blessed One, how may we know this?”

“Yedha maccharino loke, kadariyā paribhāsakā;

Aññesaṃ dadamānānaṃ, antarāyakarā narā.

“Those people here in the world who are stingy, miserly, and abusive, who create obstacles for others who are giving,

“Nirayaṃ tiracchānayoniṃ, yamalokaṃ upapajjare;

Sace enti manussattaṃ, dalidde jāyare kule.

“They arise in hell, the animal realm, or the world of Yama. If they come to the human state, they are born into a poor family.

“Coḷaṃ piṇḍo ratī khiḍḍā, yattha kicchena labbhati;

Parato āsīsare āsiṃsare (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bālā, tampi tesaṃ na labbhati;

Diṭṭhe dhammesa vipāko, samparāye samparāyo (syā. kaṃ. pī.) ca duggatī”ti.

“Where clothing, almsfood, pleasure, and sport are obtained with difficulty. Fools, they hope for things from others, but even that they do not get. This is the result in the present life, and in the next, a woeful state.”

“Itihetaṃ vijānāma, aññaṃ pucchāma gotama;

Yedha laddhā manussattaṃ, vadaññū vītamaccharā.

“Thus we understand this. We ask another question, Gotama: Those here who, having attained the human state, are generous and free from stinginess—

“Buddhe [M 1.0032] pasannā dhamme ca, saṅghe ca tibbagāravā;

Kīdiso tesaṃ vipāko, samparāyo ca kīdiso;

Bhagavantaṃ puṭṭhumāgamma, kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya”nti.

“Who have confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, and have intense reverence—what is their result, and what is their future state? Having come to ask the Blessed One, how may we know this?”

“Yedha laddhā manussattaṃ, vadaññū vītamaccharā;

Buddhe pasannā dhamme ca, saṅghe ca tibbagāravā;

Ete saggā sagge (sī. syā. kaṃ.) pakāsanti, yattha te upapajjare.

“Those here who, having attained the human state, are generous and free from stinginess, who have confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha, and have intense reverence—they illuminate the heavens wherever they arise.

“Sace [V 1.0040][P 1.0035] enti manussattaṃ, aḍḍhe ājāyare kule;

Coḷaṃ piṇḍo ratī khiḍḍā, yatthākicchena labbhati.

“If they come to the human state, they are born into an affluent family, where clothing, almsfood, pleasure, and sport are obtained without difficulty.

“Parasambhatesu [T 1.0048] bhogesu, vasavattīva modare;

Diṭṭhe dhammesa vipāko, samparāye ca suggatī”ti.

“They rejoice in wealth accumulated by others, wielding mastery over it. This is the result in the present life, and in the next, a happy state.”

10. Ghaṭīkārasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Ghaṭīkāra

50.

50.

“Avihaṃ upapannāse, vimuttā satta bhikkhavo;

Rāgadosaparikkhīṇā, tiṇṇā loke visattika”nti.

“Seven bhikkhus, reborn in the Aviha realm, are liberated; with passion and aversion exhausted, they have crossed over attachment in the world.”

“Ke ca te ataruṃ paṅkaṃ saṅgaṃ (sī. syā.), maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ;

Ke hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upaccagu”nti.

“And who are they who crossed over the mire, the realm of Death so difficult to cross? Who, having abandoned the human body, have transcended to the divine state?”

“Upako palagaṇḍo ca, pukkusāti ca te tayo;

Bhaddiyo khaṇḍadevo ca, bāhuraggi ca siṅgiyo bahudantī ca piṅgayo (sī.);

Te hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upaccagu”nti.

“Upaka and Palagaṇḍa, and Pukkusāti, those three; and Bhaddiya and Khaṇḍadeva, Bāhuraggi and Siṅgiya; they, having abandoned the human body, have transcended to the divine state.”

“Kusalī bhāsasī tesaṃ, mārapāsappahāyinaṃ;

Kassa te dhammamaññāya, acchiduṃ bhavabandhana”nti.

“You speak well of them, of those who have abandoned the snare of Māra. Whose Dhamma having understood, did they sever the bond of existence?”

“Na aññatra bhagavatā, nāññatra tava sāsanā;

Yassa te dhammamaññāya, acchiduṃ bhavabandhanaṃ.

“Not apart from the Blessed One, not apart from your Dispensation; having understood his Dhamma, they severed the bond of existence.

“Yattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhati;

Taṃ te dhammaṃ idhaññāya, acchiduṃ bhavabandhana”nti.

“Where name-and-form ceases without remainder, having understood that Dhamma here, they severed the bond of existence.”

“Gambhīraṃ [V 1.0041] bhāsasī vācaṃ, dubbijānaṃ sudubbudhaṃ;

Kassa tvaṃ [T 1.0049] dhammamaññāya, vācaṃ bhāsasi īdisa”nti.

“You speak a profound utterance, difficult to know, very difficult to understand. Having understood whose Dhamma, do you speak such an utterance?”

“Kumbhakāro [M 1.0033] pure āsiṃ, vekaḷiṅge vehaḷiṅge (sī.), vebhaḷiṅge (syā. kaṃ.) ghaṭīkaro;

Mātāpettibharo āsiṃ, kassapassa upāsako.

“Formerly, in Vekaḷiṅga, I was a potter named Ghaṭikāra. I was a supporter of my mother and father, a lay disciple of the Buddha Kassapa.

“Virato [P 1.0036] methunā dhammā, brahmacārī nirāmiso;

Ahuvā te sagāmeyyo, ahuvā te pure sakhā.

“I abstained from the practice of sexual intercourse; I was a practitioner of the holy life, free from worldly desires. I was a fellow villager with you; I was your friend in the past.

“Sohamete pajānāmi, vimutte satta bhikkhavo;

Rāgadosaparikkhīṇe, tiṇṇe loke visattika”nti.

“Thus I know these seven bhikkhus who are liberated, with passion and aversion exhausted, who have crossed over attachment in the world.”

“Evametaṃ tadā āsi, yathā bhāsasi bhaggava;

Kumbhakāro pure āsi, vekaḷiṅge ghaṭīkaro;

Mātāpettibharo āsi, kassapassa upāsako.

“So it was then, Bhaggava, just as you say. Formerly, in Vekaḷiṅga, you were a potter named Ghaṭikāra. You were a supporter of your mother and father, a lay disciple of the Buddha Kassapa.”

“Virato methunā dhammā, brahmacārī nirāmiso;

Ahuvā me sagāmeyyo, ahuvā me pure sakhā”ti.

“You abstained from the practice of sexual intercourse; you were a practitioner of the holy life, free from worldly desires. You were a fellow villager with me; you were my friend in the past.”

“Evametaṃ purāṇānaṃ, sahāyānaṃ ahu saṅgamo;

Ubhinnaṃ bhāvitattānaṃ, sarīrantimadhārina”nti.

“Thus was this meeting of old friends, of both who had developed themselves, bearing their final bodies.”

Ādittavaggo pañcamo.

The Āditta Chapter, the Fifth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Ādittaṃ kiṃdadaṃ annaṃ, ekamūlaanomiyaṃ;

Accharāvanaropajetaṃ, maccharena ghaṭīkaroti.

Āditta, Kiṃdada, Anna, Ekamūla, Anomiya, Accharā, Vanaropa, Jeta, Macchara, and Ghaṭikāra.

6. Jarāvaggo

6. The Chapter on Old Age

1. Jarāsuttaṃ

1. The Sutta on Old Age

51.

51.

“Kiṃsu [T 1.0050][V 1.0042] yāva jarā sādhu, kiṃsu sādhu patiṭṭhitaṃ;

Kiṃsu narānaṃ ratanaṃ, kiṃsu corehi dūhara”nti.

“What is good until old age? What is good when well-established? What is the jewel of human beings? What is hard for thieves to take?”

“Sīlaṃ yāva jarā sādhu, saddhā sādhu patiṭṭhitā;

Paññā narānaṃ ratanaṃ, puññaṃ corehi dūhara”nti.

“Virtue is good until old age; faith is good when well-established; wisdom is the jewel of human beings; merit is hard for thieves to take.”

2. Ajarasāsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Ageless

52.

52.

“Kiṃsu [M 1.0034] ajarasā sādhu, kiṃsu sādhu adhiṭṭhitaṃ;

Kiṃsu narānaṃ ratanaṃ, kiṃsu corehyahāriya”nti.

“What is good through being ageless? What is good when well-established? What is the jewel of humankind? What cannot be taken by thieves?”

“Sīlaṃ [P 1.0037] ajarasā sādhu, saddhā sādhu adhiṭṭhitā;

Paññā narānaṃ ratanaṃ, puññaṃ corehyahāriya”nti.

“Virtue is good through being ageless; faith is good when well-established; wisdom is the jewel of humankind; merit cannot be taken by thieves.”

3. Mittasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on a Friend

53.

53.

“Kiṃsu pavasato pathavato (pī. ka.) mittaṃ, kiṃsu mittaṃ sake ghare;

Kiṃ mittaṃ atthajātassa, kiṃ mittaṃ samparāyika”nti.

“What is the friend of one away from home? What is a friend in one's own house? What is the friend of one for whom a need has arisen? What is a friend in the life to come?”

“Sattho pavasato mittaṃ, mātā mittaṃ sake ghare;

Sahāyo [T 1.0051] atthajātassa, hoti mittaṃ punappunaṃ;

Sayaṃkatāni puññāni, taṃ mittaṃ samparāyika”nti.

“A caravan is the friend of one away from home; a mother is a friend in one's own house. A companion, for one for whom a need has arisen, is a friend again and again. The merits one has done oneself—that is a friend in the life to come.”

4. Vatthusuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on a Support

54.

54.

“Kiṃsu [V 1.0043] vatthu manussānaṃ, kiṃsūdha paramo sakhā;

Kiṃsu bhūtā upajīvanti, ye pāṇā pathavissitā”ti pathaviṃ sitāti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

“What is the support for humans? What here is the supreme companion? On what do they live, those beings who are dependent on the earth?”

“Puttā vatthu manussānaṃ, bhariyā ca bhariyāva (sī.), bhariyā (syā. kaṃ.) paramo sakhā;

Vuṭṭhiṃ bhūtā upajīvanti, ye pāṇā pathavissitā”ti.

“Sons are the support for humans; a wife is the supreme companion. On rain do they live, those beings who are dependent on the earth.”

5. Paṭhamajanasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on Generation

55.

55.

“Kiṃsu janeti purisaṃ, kiṃsu tassa vidhāvati;

Kiṃsu saṃsāramāpādi, kiṃsu tassa mahabbhaya”nti.

“What generates a person? What runs about for him? What enters saṃsāra? What is his great fear?”

“Taṇhā janeti purisaṃ, cittamassa vidhāvati;

Satto saṃsāramāpādi, dukkhamassa mahabbhaya”nti.

“Craving generates a person; his mind runs about. A being enters saṃsāra; suffering is his great fear.”

6. Dutiyajanasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Generation

56.

56.

“Kiṃsu [M 1.0035] janeti purisaṃ, kiṃsu tassa vidhāvati;

Kiṃsu saṃsāramāpādi, kismā na parimuccatī”ti.

“What generates a person? What runs about for him? What enters saṃsāra? From what is he not freed?”

“Taṇhā janeti purisaṃ, cittamassa vidhāvati;

Satto saṃsāramāpādi, dukkhā na parimuccatī”ti.

“Craving generates a person; his mind runs about. A being enters saṃsāra; from suffering he is not freed.”

7. Tatiyajanasuttaṃ

7. The Third Discourse on Generation

57.

57.

“Kiṃsu [P 1.0038] janeti purisaṃ, kiṃsu tassa vidhāvati;

Kiṃsu saṃsāramāpādi, kiṃsu tassa parāyana”nti.

“What generates a person? What runs about for him? What enters saṃsāra? What is his final resort?”

“Taṇhā [T 1.0052][V 1.0044] janeti purisaṃ, cittamassa vidhāvati;

Satto saṃsāramāpādi, kammaṃ tassa parāyana”nti.

“Craving generates a person; his mind runs about. A being enters saṃsāra; kamma is his final resort.”

8. Uppathasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Wrong Path

58.

58.

“Kiṃsu uppatho akkhāto, kiṃsu rattindivakkhayo;

Kiṃ malaṃ brahmacariyassa, kiṃ sinānamanodaka”nti.

“What is declared to be the wrong path? What is the wasting away of night and day? What is the stain of the holy life? What is the bath that is without water?”

“Rāgo uppatho akkhāto, vayo rattindivakkhayo;

Itthī malaṃ brahmacariyassa, etthāyaṃ sajjate pajā;

Tapo ca brahmacariyañca, taṃ sinānamanodaka”nti.

“Lust is declared to be the wrong path; age is the wasting away of night and day. A woman is the stain of the holy life; in her this generation is ensnared. Austerity and the holy life—this is the bath that is without water.”

9. Dutiyasuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse

59.

59.

“Kiṃsu dutiyā dutiyaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.) purisassa hoti, kiṃsu cenaṃ pasāsati;

Kissa cābhirato macco, sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.

“What is a person’s companion? And what instructs them? Delighting in what is a mortal freed from all suffering?”

“Saddhā dutiyā purisassa hoti, paññā cenaṃ pasāsati;

Nibbānābhirato macco, sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.

“Faith is a person’s companion; wisdom instructs them. A mortal delighting in Nibbāna is freed from all suffering.”

10. Kavisuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Poet

60.

60.

“Kiṃsu nidānaṃ gāthānaṃ, kiṃsu tāsaṃ viyañjanaṃ;

Kiṃsu sannissitā gāthā, kiṃsu gāthānamāsayo”ti.

“What is the origin of verses? What is their expression? On what do verses rely? What is the basis of verses?”

“Chando [M 1.0036] nidānaṃ gāthānaṃ, akkharā tāsaṃ viyañjanaṃ;

Nāmasannissitā gāthā, kavi gāthānamāsayo”ti.

“Meter is the origin of verses; letters are their expression. Verses rely on names; the poet is the basis of verses.”

Jarāvaggo chaṭṭho.

The Sixth Chapter on Old Age.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Jarā [T 1.0053][V 1.0045] ajarasā mittaṃ, vatthu tīṇi janāni ca;

Uppatho ca dutiyo ca, kavinā pūrito vaggoti.

Old Age, Undecaying, Friend, Support, the three on Generation, Wrong Path, Second, and with the Poet the chapter is completed.

7. Addhavaggo

7. The Chapter on Overcoming

1. Nāmasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Name

61.

61.

“Kiṃsu [T 1.0054][P 1.0039] sabbaṃ addhabhavi anvabhavi (sī.), kismā bhiyyo na vijjati;

Kissassu ekadhammassa, sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti vasamaddhagū (ka.).

“What has overcome all? What is it that nothing surpasses? Under the sway of what single phenomenon have all come?”

“Nāmaṃ sabbaṃ addhabhavi, nāmā bhiyyo na vijjati;

Nāmassa ekadhammassa, sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.

“Name has overcome all; nothing surpasses name. Under the sway of the single phenomenon, name, have all come.”

2. Cittasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Mind

62.

62.

“Kenassu nīyati loko, kenassu parikassati;

Kissassu ekadhammassa, sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.

“By what is the world led? By what is it drawn along? Under the sway of what single phenomenon have all come?”

“Cittena nīyati loko, cittena parikassati;

Cittassa ekadhammassa, sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.

“By the mind the world is led, by the mind it is drawn along. Under the sway of the single phenomenon, the mind, have all come.”

3. Taṇhāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Craving

63.

63.

“Kenassu nīyati loko, kenassu parikassati;

Kissassu ekadhammassa, sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.

“By what is the world led? By what is it drawn along? Under the sway of what single phenomenon have all come?”

“Taṇhāya [V 1.0046] nīyati loko, taṇhāya parikassati;

Taṇhāya ekadhammassa, sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti.

“By craving the world is led, by craving it is drawn along. Under the sway of the single phenomenon, craving, have all come.”

4. Saṃyojanasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Fetter

64.

64.

“Kiṃsu [T 1.0055][M 1.0037] saṃyojano loko, kiṃsu tassa vicāraṇaṃ;

Kissassu vippahānena, nibbānaṃ iti vuccatī”ti.

“What is the fetter of the world? What is its sphere of movement? By the abandoning of what is it called Nibbāna?”

“Nandīsaṃyojano nandisaṃyojano (sī. syā. kaṃ.) loko, vitakkassa vicāraṇaṃ;

Taṇhāya vippahānena, nibbānaṃ iti vuccatī”ti.

“Delight is the fetter of the world; thought is its sphere of movement. By the abandoning of craving, it is called Nibbāna.”

5. Bandhanasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Bond

65.

65.

“Kiṃsu sambandhano loko, kiṃsu tassa vicāraṇaṃ;

Kissassu vippahānena, sabbaṃ chindati bandhana”nti.

“What is the bond of the world? What is its sphere of movement? By the abandoning of what does one cut all bonds?”

“Nandīsambandhano [P 1.0040] loko, vitakkassa vicāraṇaṃ;

Taṇhāya vippahānena, sabbaṃ chindati bandhana”nti.

“Delight is the bond of the world; thought is its sphere of movement. By the abandoning of craving, one cuts all bonds.”

6. Attahatasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Being Struck

66.

66.

“Kenassubbhāhato loko, kenassu parivārito;

Kena sallena otiṇṇo, kissa dhūpāyito sadā”ti.

“By what is the world afflicted? By what is it surrounded? By what dart is it pierced? By what is it always ablaze?”

“Maccunābbhāhato loko, jarāya parivārito;

Taṇhāsallena otiṇṇo, icchādhūpāyito sadā”ti.

“By death the world is afflicted, by aging it is surrounded; by the dart of craving it is pierced, by desire it is always ablaze.”

7. Uḍḍitasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Being Pierced

67.

67.

“Kenassu [V 1.0047] uḍḍito loko, kenassu parivārito;

Kenassu pihito loko, kismiṃ loko patiṭṭhito”ti.

“By what is the world pierced? By what is it surrounded? By what is the world covered? In what is the world established?”

“Taṇhāya uḍḍito loko, jarāya parivārito;

Maccunā pihito loko, dukkhe loko patiṭṭhito”ti.

“By craving the world is pierced, by aging it is surrounded. By death the world is covered, in suffering the world is established.”

8. Pihitasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Being Covered

68.

68.

“Kenassu [T 1.0056] pihito loko, kismiṃ loko patiṭṭhito;

Kenassu uḍḍito loko, kenassu parivārito”ti.

“By what is the world covered? In what is the world established? By what is the world pierced? By what is it surrounded?”

“Maccunā [M 1.0038] pihito loko, dukkhe loko patiṭṭhito;

Taṇhāya uḍḍito loko, jarāya parivārito”ti.

“By death the world is covered, in suffering the world is established. By craving the world is pierced, by aging it is surrounded.”

9. Icchāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Desire

69.

69.

“Kenassu bajjhatī loko, kissa vinayāya muccati;

Kissassu vippahānena, sabbaṃ chindati bandhana”nti.

“By what is the world bound? By the subduing of what is it freed? By the abandoning of what does one cut all bonds?”

“Icchāya bajjhatī loko, icchāvinayāya muccati;

Icchāya vippahānena, sabbaṃ chindati bandhana”nti.

“By desire the world is bound; by the subduing of desire it is freed. By the abandoning of desire, one cuts all bonds.”

10. Lokasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the World

70.

70.

“Kismiṃ [P 1.0041] loko samuppanno, kismiṃ kubbati santhavaṃ;

Kissa loko upādāya, kismiṃ loko vihaññatī”ti.

“When what has arisen does the world arise? With what does it form intimacy? Depending on what does the world exist? In what is the world afflicted?”

“Chasu [V 1.0048] loko samuppanno, chasu kubbati santhavaṃ;

Channameva upādāya, chasu loko vihaññatī”ti.

“When the six have arisen, the world arises; with the six it forms intimacy. Depending only on the six it exists; in the six the world is afflicted.”

Addhavaggo anvavaggo (sī.) sattamo.

The Addha Chapter, the Seventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Nāmaṃ cittañca taṇhā ca, saṃyojanañca bandhanā;

Abbhāhatuḍḍito pihito, icchā lokena te dasāti.

Name, Mind, and Craving, Fetter and Bond, Struck, Pierced, Covered, Desire, and with the World—these are the ten.

8. Chetvāvaggo

8. The Chapter on Severing

1. Chetvāsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Severing

71. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ [T 1.0057] ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

71. The setting is Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, that devatā addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Kiṃsu chetvā jhatvā (sī.), ghatvā (syā. kaṃ.) evamuparipi sukhaṃ seti, kiṃsu chetvā na socati;

Kissassu ekadhammassa, vadhaṃ rocesi gotamā”ti.

“Having destroyed what, does one sleep happily? Having destroyed what, does one not grieve? The destruction of what one thing do you approve of, Gotama?”

“Kodhaṃ [M 1.0039] chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kodhaṃ chetvā na socati;

Kodhassa visamūlassa, madhuraggassa devate;

Vadhaṃ ariyā pasaṃsanti, tañhi chetvā na socatī”ti.

“Having destroyed anger, one sleeps happily; having destroyed anger, one does not grieve. O devatā, the noble ones praise the destruction of anger, with its poisoned root and sweet tip; for having destroyed it, one does not grieve.”

2. Rathasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Chariot

72.

72.

“Kiṃsu rathassa paññāṇaṃ, kiṃsu paññāṇamaggino;

Kiṃsu raṭṭhassa paññāṇaṃ, kiṃsu paññāṇamitthiyā”ti.

“What is the sign of a chariot? What is the sign of a fire? What is the sign of a kingdom? What is the sign of a woman?”

“Dhajo [V 1.0049][P 1.0042] rathassa paññāṇaṃ, dhūmo paññāṇamaggino;

Rājā raṭṭhassa paññāṇaṃ, bhattā paññāṇamitthiyā”ti.

“A banner is the sign of a chariot, smoke is the sign of a fire, a king is the sign of a kingdom, a husband is the sign of a woman.”

3. Vittasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Wealth

73.

73.

“Kiṃsūdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ, kiṃsu suciṇṇo sukhamāvahati;

Kiṃsu [T 1.0058] have sādutaraṃ sādhutaraṃ (ka.) rasānaṃ, kathaṃjīviṃ kiṃsujīviṃ (ka.) jīvitamāhu seṭṭha”nti.

“What, here in this world, is the best wealth for a man? What, when well-practiced, brings happiness? What, indeed, is the most excellent of flavors? One living in what way, do they say, has the best life?”

“Saddhīdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ, dhammo suciṇṇo sukhamāvahati;

Saccaṃ have sādutaraṃ rasānaṃ, paññājīviṃ jīvitamāhu seṭṭha”nti.

“Faith, here in this world, is the best wealth for a man; the Dhamma, when well-practiced, brings happiness. Truth, indeed, is the most excellent of flavors; one who lives by wisdom, they say, has the best life.”

4. Vuṭṭhisuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Rain

74.

74.

“Kiṃsu uppatataṃ seṭṭhaṃ, kiṃsu nipatataṃ varaṃ;

Kiṃsu pavajamānānaṃ, kiṃsu pavadataṃ vara”nti.

“What is best among things that rise up? What is excellent among things that fall down? What is best among those that travel by foot? Who is excellent among those who speak?”

“Bījaṃ uppatataṃ seṭṭhaṃ, vuṭṭhi nipatataṃ varā;

Gāvo pavajamānānaṃ, putto pavadataṃ varoti.

“A seed is best among things that rise up; rain is excellent among things that fall down. Cattle are best among those that travel by foot; a son is excellent among those who speak.”

“Vijjā uppatataṃ seṭṭhā, avijjā nipatataṃ varā;

Saṅgho pavajamānānaṃ, buddho pavadataṃ varo”ti.

“Knowledge is best among things that rise up; ignorance is excellent among things that fall down. The Saṅgha is excellent among those that travel by foot; the Buddha is excellent among those who speak.”

5. Bhītāsuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Fear

75.

75.

“Kiṃsūdha bhītā janatā anekā,

Maggo canekāyatanappavutto;

Pucchāmi taṃ gotama bhūripañña,

Kismiṃ ṭhito paralokaṃ na bhāye”ti.

“The path has been taught by you with many reasons, yet why are so many people here afraid? I ask you this, O Gotama of vast wisdom: established in what does one not fear the next world?”

“Vācaṃ [V 1.0050][M 1.0040] manañca paṇidhāya sammā,

Kāyena [T 1.0059] pāpāni akubbamāno;

Bavhannapānaṃ gharamāvasanto,

Saddho [P 1.0043] mudū saṃvibhāgī vadaññū;

Etesu dhammesu ṭhito catūsu,

Dhamme ṭhito paralokaṃ na bhāye”ti.

“Having rightly directed speech and mind, not doing evil deeds with the body; dwelling in a home with abundant food and drink, being faithful, gentle, one who shares, and skilled in speech—established in these four dhammas, established in the Dhamma, one does not fear the next world.”

6. Najīratisuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on What Does Not Decay

76.

76.

“Kiṃ jīrati kiṃ na jīrati, kiṃsu uppathoti vuccati;

Kiṃsu dhammānaṃ paripantho, kiṃsu rattindivakkhayo;

Kiṃ malaṃ brahmacariyassa, kiṃ sinānamanodakaṃ.

“What decays? What does not decay? What is called a wrong path? What is the obstacle to wholesome dhammas? What is the wasting away of night and day? What is the stain of the holy life? What is the cleansing without water?”

“Kati lokasmiṃ chiddāni, yattha vittaṃ cittaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) na tiṭṭhati;

Bhagavantaṃ puṭṭhumāgamma, kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya”nti.

“How many are the holes in the world, wherein wealth does not remain? Having come to ask the Blessed One, how might we know of that?”

“Rūpaṃ jīrati maccānaṃ, nāmagottaṃ na jīrati;

Rāgo uppathoti vuccati.

“The material form of mortals decays; name and clan do not decay. Lust is called a wrong path.”

“Lobho dhammānaṃ paripantho, vayo rattindivakkhayo;

Itthī malaṃ brahmacariyassa, etthāyaṃ sajjate pajā;

Tapo ca brahmacariyañca, taṃ sinānamanodakaṃ.

“Greed is the obstacle to wholesome dhammas; age is the wasting away of night and day. A woman is the stain of the holy life; to her these beings are attached. Both austerity and the holy life, that is the cleansing without water.”

“Cha lokasmiṃ chiddāni, yattha vittaṃ na tiṭṭhati;

Ālasyañca ālassañca (sī. pī.) pamādo ca, anuṭṭhānaṃ asaṃyamo;

Niddā tandī tandi (sī.) ca te chidde, sabbaso taṃ vivajjaye”ti.

“Six are the holes in the world wherein wealth does not remain: laziness and heedlessness, lack of exertion and lack of restraint, excessive sleep and lethargy. These are the holes; one should avoid them completely.”

7. Issariyasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Sovereignty

77.

77.

“Kiṃsu [T 1.0060][V 1.0051] issariyaṃ loke, kiṃsu bhaṇḍānamuttamaṃ;

Kiṃsu satthamalaṃ loke, kiṃsu lokasmimabbudaṃ.

“What is sovereignty in the world? What is the best of possessions? What is the stain of a weapon in the world? What is the calamity in the world?”

“Kiṃsu harantaṃ vārenti, haranto pana ko piyo;

Kiṃsu punappunāyantaṃ, abhinandanti paṇḍitā”ti.

“Whom do they prevent when he is carrying away? Who, then, is dear when carrying away? Whom do the wise delight in, who comes again and again?”

“Vaso [M 1.0041] issariyaṃ loke, itthī bhaṇḍānamuttamaṃ;

Kodho satthamalaṃ loke, corā lokasmimabbudā.

“Control is sovereignty in the world; a woman is the best of possessions; anger is the stain of a weapon in the world; thieves are the calamities in the world.”

“Coraṃ harantaṃ vārenti, haranto samaṇo piyo;

Samaṇaṃ punappunāyantaṃ, abhinandanti paṇḍitā”ti.

“They prevent a thief who is carrying things away; but the ascetic who carries things away is dear. The wise delight in the ascetic who comes again and again.”

8. Kāmasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Desire

78.

78.

“Kimatthakāmo [P 1.0044] na dade, kiṃ macco na pariccaje;

Kiṃsu muñceyya kalyāṇaṃ, pāpikaṃ na ca mocaye”ti.

“What should one who desires benefit not give? What should a mortal not abandon? What good thing should one utter, and what evil thing should one not utter?”

“Attānaṃ na dade poso, attānaṃ na pariccaje;

Vācaṃ muñceyya kalyāṇaṃ, pāpikañca na mocaye”ti.

“A person should not give oneself away, nor should one abandon oneself. One should utter good speech, and not utter evil speech.”

9. Pātheyyasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Provisions for the Journey

79.

79.

“Kiṃsu bandhati pātheyyaṃ, kiṃsu bhogānamāsayo;

Kiṃsu naraṃ parikassati, kiṃsu lokasmi dujjahaṃ;

Kismiṃ baddhā puthū sattā, pāsena sakuṇī yathā”ti.

“What binds up provisions for the journey? What is the foundation of wealth? What drags a person around? What in the world is hard to abandon? By what are many beings bound, like a bird by a snare?”

“Saddhā [T 1.0061][V 1.0052] bandhati pātheyyaṃ, sirī bhogānamāsayo;

Icchā naraṃ parikassati, icchā lokasmi dujjahā;

Icchābaddhā puthū sattā, pāsena sakuṇī yathā”ti.

“Faith binds up provisions for the journey; prosperity is the foundation of wealth. Craving drags a person around; craving in the world is hard to abandon. By craving are many beings bound, like a bird by a snare.”

10. Pajjotasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Light

80.

80.

“Kiṃsu lokasmi pajjoto, kiṃsu lokasmi jāgaro;

Kiṃsu kamme sajīvānaṃ, kimassa iriyāpatho.

“What is the light in the world? What is wakefulness in the world? For those who live by their work, what is their companion? What is their livelihood?”

“Kiṃsu alasaṃ analasañca kiṃ ālasyānālasyañca (ka.), mātā puttaṃva posati;

Kiṃ bhūtā upajīvanti, ye pāṇā pathavissitā”ti.

“What nourishes both the lazy and the diligent, just as a mother nourishes her son? On what do living beings who depend on the earth subsist?”

“Paññā lokasmi pajjoto, sati lokasmi jāgaro;

Gāvo kamme sajīvānaṃ, sītassa iriyāpatho.

“Wisdom is the light in the world; mindfulness is wakefulness in the world. Cattle are the companions for those who live by their work; ploughing is their livelihood.”

“Vuṭṭhi alasaṃ analasañca, mātā puttaṃva posati;

Vuṭṭhiṃ bhūtā upajīvanti, ye pāṇā pathavissitā”ti.

“Rain nourishes both the lazy and the diligent, just as a mother nourishes her son. Living beings who depend on the earth subsist on rain.”

11. Araṇasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Strifeless

81.

81.

“Kesūdha [M 1.0042] araṇā loke, kesaṃ vusitaṃ na nassati;

Kedha icchaṃ parijānanti, kesaṃ bhojissiyaṃ sadā.

“Who here in this world are the strifeless? Whose holy life does not perish? Who here fully understand craving? For whom is there always mastery?”

“Kiṃsu [P 1.0045] mātā pitā bhātā, vandanti naṃ patiṭṭhitaṃ;

Kiṃsu idha jātihīnaṃ, abhivādenti khattiyā”ti.

“Whom, when established, do mother, father, and brother venerate? Whom here, though of low birth, do nobles salute?”

“Samaṇīdha araṇā loke, samaṇānaṃ vusitaṃ na nassati;

Samaṇā icchaṃ parijānanti, samaṇānaṃ bhojissiyaṃ sadā.

“Ascetics here in this world are the strifeless; the holy life of ascetics does not perish. Ascetics fully understand craving; for ascetics there is always mastery.”

“Samaṇaṃ [T 1.0062][V 1.0053] mātā pitā bhātā, vandanti naṃ patiṭṭhitaṃ;

Samaṇīdha jātihīnaṃ, abhivādenti khattiyā”ti.

“Mother, father, and brother venerate the established ascetic; here nobles salute the ascetic even though of low birth.”

Chetvāvaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Chetvā Chapter, the Eighth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of its contents:

Chetvā rathañca cittañca, vuṭṭhi bhītā najīrati;

Issaraṃ kāmaṃ pātheyyaṃ, pajjoto araṇena cāti.

Chetvā, Ratha, Citta, Vuṭṭhi, Bhītā, Na Jīrati, Issara, Kāma, Pātheyya, Pajjota, and Araṇa.

Devatāsaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses with Devatās is concluded.

2. Devaputtasaṃyuttaṃ

2. The Connected Discourses with Devaputtas

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Paṭhamakassapasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on Kassapa

82. Evaṃ [T 1.0063][V 1.0054][P 1.0046][M 1.0043] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho kassapo devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho kassapo devaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhikkhuṃ bhagavā pakāsesi, no ca bhikkhuno anusāsa”nti. “Tena hi kassapa, taññevettha paṭibhātū”ti.

82. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then, when the night was far advanced, the devaputta Kassapa, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the devaputta Kassapa said this to the Blessed One: “The Blessed One proclaims the bhikkhu, but not the instruction for the bhikkhu.” “In that case, Kassapa, let it be you who speaks on this matter.”

“Subhāsitassa sikkhetha, samaṇūpāsanassa ca;

Ekāsanassa ca raho, cittavūpasamassa cā”ti.

“One should train in what is well-spoken, and in attending on ascetics; in sitting alone in seclusion, and in the calming of the mind.”

Idamavoca kassapo devaputto; samanuñño satthā ahosi. Atha kho kassapo devaputto “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

This is what the devaputta Kassapa said. The Teacher approved. Then the devaputta Kassapa, thinking, “The Teacher approves of me,” paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and vanished right there.

2. Dutiyakassapasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on Kassapa

83. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho kassapo devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

83. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, the devaputta Kassapa recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Bhikkhu [T 1.0064][V 1.0055] siyā jhāyī vimuttacitto,

Ākaṅkhe ce hadayassānupattiṃ;

Lokassa ñatvā udayabbayañca,

Sucetaso anissito tadānisaṃso”ti.

“Should a bhikkhu, meditative and with a liberated mind, aspire to the heart's attainment, he should, having known the arising and passing away of the world, be of pure mind, unattached; that is his benefit.”

3. Māghasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Māgha

84. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 1.0047]. Atha kho māgho devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi[M 1.0044]. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho māgho devaputto bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

84. At Sāvatthī. Then, when the night was far advanced, the devaputta Māgha, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the devaputta Māgha addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kiṃsu chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kiṃsu chetvā na socati;

Kissassu ekadhammassa, vadhaṃ rocesi gotamā”ti.

“Having cut off what does one dwell happily? Having cut off what does one not grieve? Of what one thing, Gotama, do you approve the destruction?”

“Kodhaṃ chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kodhaṃ chetvā na socati;

Kodhassa visamūlassa, madhuraggassa vatrabhū;

Vadhaṃ ariyā pasaṃsanti, tañhi chetvā na socatī”ti.

“Having cut off anger, one dwells happily; having cut off anger, one does not grieve. O subduer of Vatra, the noble ones praise the destruction of anger, with its poisoned root and sweet tip; for having cut that off, one does not grieve.”

4. Māgadhasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Māgadha

85. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho māgadho devaputto bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

85. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, the devaputta Māgadha addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kati [T 1.0065] lokasmiṃ pajjotā, yehi loko pakāsati;

Bhavantaṃ puṭṭhumāgamma, kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya”nti.

“How many are the lights in the world, by which the world is illuminated? We have come to ask you, Venerable Sir; how are we to know this?”

“Cattāro [V 1.0056] loke pajjotā, pañcamettha na vijjati;

Divā tapati ādicco, rattimābhāti candimā.

“There are four lights in the world; a fifth is not found here. The sun shines by day; the moon glows by night.

“Atha aggi divārattiṃ, tattha tattha pakāsati;

Sambuddho tapataṃ seṭṭho, esā ābhā anuttarā”ti.

“Then fire shines day and night, here and there. The Perfectly Enlightened One is the best of those that shine; this is the unsurpassed radiance.”

5. Dāmalisuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Dāmali

86. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho dāmali devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho dāmali devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

86. At Sāvatthī. Then, when the night was far advanced, the devaputta Dāmali, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the devaputta Dāmali recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Karaṇīyametaṃ brāhmaṇena, padhānaṃ akilāsunā;

Kāmānaṃ vippahānena, na tenāsīsate bhava”nti.

“This striving should be done by a brahmin who is unwearying; through the abandoning of sensual pleasures, he does not long for becoming.”

“Natthi kiccaṃ brāhmaṇassa (dāmalīti bhagavā),

Katakicco hi brāhmaṇo.

“There is no task for a brahmin, Dāmali,” said the Blessed One, “for a brahmin has done what was to be done.

“Yāva [M 1.0045] na gādhaṃ labhati nadīsu,

Āyūhati [P 1.0048] sabbagattebhi jantu;

Gādhañca laddhāna thale ṭhito yo,

Nāyūhatī [T 1.0066] pāragato hi sova soti (sī. pī. ka.), hoti (syā. kaṃ.), so (?).

“As long as a being does not find a footing in the rivers, it strives with all its limbs; but having found a footing and standing on dry land, it does not strive, for it has gone to the far shore.

“Esūpamā dāmali brāhmaṇassa,

Khīṇāsavassa nipakassa jhāyino;

Pappuyya jātimaraṇassa antaṃ,

Nāyūhatī pāragato hi so”ti hotīti (syā. kaṃ.).

“This is the simile, Dāmali, for the brahmin whose taints are destroyed, the prudent, the meditative one. Having reached the end of birth and death, he does not strive, for he has gone to the far shore.”

6. Kāmadasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Kāmada

87. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0057]. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho kāmado devaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dukkaraṃ bhagavā, sudukkaraṃ bhagavā”ti.

87. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, the devaputta Kāmada said this to the Blessed One: “It is difficult to do, Blessed One! It is very difficult to do, Blessed One!”

“Dukkaraṃ vāpi karonti (kāmadāti bhagavā),

Sekhā sīlasamāhitā;

Ṭhitattā anagāriyupetassa,

Tuṭṭhi hoti sukhāvahā”ti.

“The trainees, Kāmada,” said the Blessed One, “established in virtue and of steadfast nature, do even what is difficult. For one who has gone forth into homelessness, contentment brings happiness.”

“Dullabhā bhagavā yadidaṃ tuṭṭhī”ti.

“This contentment, Blessed One, is difficult to obtain.”

“Dullabhaṃ vāpi labhanti (kāmadāti bhagavā),

Cittavūpasame ratā;

Yesaṃ divā ca ratto ca,

Bhāvanāya rato mano”ti.

“They obtain even what is difficult to obtain, Kāmada,” said the Blessed One, “those whose minds delight in mental development day and night, who delight in the calming of the mind.”

“Dussamādahaṃ bhagavā yadidaṃ citta”nti.

“This mind, Blessed One, is difficult to compose.”

“Dussamādahaṃ vāpi samādahanti (kāmadāti bhagavā),

Indriyūpasame ratā;

Te chetvā maccuno jālaṃ,

Ariyā gacchanti kāmadā”ti.

“They compose even what is difficult to compose, Kāmada,” said the Blessed One, “those who delight in the calming of the faculties. Having cut the net of Death, Kāmada, the noble ones go forth.”

“Duggamo [M 1.0046] bhagavā visamo maggo”ti.

“The path is difficult to travel, Blessed One, an uneven path.”

“Duggame visame vāpi, ariyā gacchanti kāmada;

Anariyā visame magge, papatanti avaṃsirā;

Ariyānaṃ samo maggo, ariyā hi visame samā”ti.

“Even on a difficult and uneven path, Kāmada, the noble ones travel. The ignoble fall headlong on an uneven path. The path of the noble ones is even, for the noble ones are even amidst the uneven.”

7. Pañcālacaṇḍasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Pañcālacaṇḍa

88. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0058]. Ekamantaṃ [T 1.0067] ṭhito kho pañcālacaṇḍo devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

88. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, the devaputta Pañcālacaṇḍa recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sambādhe vata okāsaṃ, avindi bhūrimedhaso;

Yo jhānamabujjhi jhānamabudhā (ka. sī.), jhānamabuddhi (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) buddho, paṭilīnanisabho munī”ti.

“Indeed, in a constricted place, the one of great wisdom found an opening—the Buddha who understood jhāna, the sage, the chief among those who have withdrawn.”

“Sambādhe vāpi vindanti (pañcālacaṇḍāti bhagavā),

Dhammaṃ nibbānapattiyā;

Ye satiṃ paccalatthaṃsu,

Sammā te susamāhitā”ti.

“Even in a constricted place they find, O Pañcālacaṇḍa,” said the Blessed One, “the Dhamma for the attainment of Nibbāna. Those who have obtained mindfulness—they are rightly and well-composed.”

8. Tāyanasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Tāyana

89. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha [P 1.0049] kho tāyano devaputto purāṇatitthakaro abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho tāyano devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

89. At Sāvatthī. Then the devaputta Tāyana, a former sectarian teacher, when the night was far advanced, his surpassing radiance illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the devaputta Tāyana recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Chinda sotaṃ parakkamma, kāme panuda brāhmaṇa;

Nappahāya munī kāme, nekattamupapajjati.

“Strive and cut the stream, O brahmin, dispel sensual pleasures. Without abandoning sensual pleasures, a sage does not attain oneness.

“Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṃ, daḷhamenaṃ parakkame;

Sithilo hi paribbājo, bhiyyo ākirate rajaṃ.

“If one should do it, one should do it; one should strive at it firmly. For a lax ascetic scatters the dust all the more.

“Akataṃ [T 1.0068] dukkaṭaṃ dukkataṃ (sī. pī.) seyyo, pacchā tapati dukkaṭaṃ;

Katañca sukataṃ seyyo, yaṃ katvā nānutappati.

“Better is a misdeed not done; a misdeed torments one afterwards. Better is a good deed done, which, having been done, one does not regret.

“Kuso [V 1.0059][M 1.0047] yathā duggahito, hatthamevānukantati;

Sāmaññaṃ dupparāmaṭṭhaṃ, nirayāyūpakaḍḍhati.

“Just as kusa grass, wrongly grasped, cuts the hand, so the state of a monk, wrongly handled, drags one to hell.

“Yaṃ kiñci sithilaṃ kammaṃ, saṃkiliṭṭhañca yaṃ vataṃ;

Saṅkassaraṃ brahmacariyaṃ, na taṃ hoti mahapphala”nti.

“Whatever action is lax, and whatever vow is defiled, a holy life lived with reluctance—that is not of great fruit.”

Idamavoca tāyano devaputto; idaṃ vatvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

This is what the devaputta Tāyana said. Having said this, he paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and vanished right there.

Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi – “imaṃ, bhikkhave, rattiṃ tāyano nāma devaputto purāṇatitthakaro abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, tāyano devaputto mama santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then, when that night had passed, the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, this night the devaputta Tāyana, a former sectarian teacher, when the night was far advanced, his surpassing radiance illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached me. Having approached, he paid homage to me and stood to one side. Standing to one side, monks, the devaputta Tāyana recited these verses in my presence:

“Chinda sotaṃ parakkamma, kāme panuda brāhmaṇa;

Nappahāya munī kāme, nekattamupapajjati.

“‘Strive and cut the stream, O brahmin, dispel sensual pleasures. Without abandoning sensual pleasures, a sage does not attain oneness.

“Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṃ, daḷhamenaṃ parakkame;

Sithilo [P 1.0050] hi paribbājo, bhiyyo ākirate rajaṃ.

“‘If one should do it, one should do it; one should strive at it firmly. For a lax ascetic scatters the dust all the more.

“Akataṃ dukkaṭaṃ seyyo, pacchā tapati dukkaṭaṃ;

Katañca sukataṃ seyyo, yaṃ katvā nānutappati.

“‘Better is a misdeed not done; a misdeed torments one afterwards. Better is a good deed done, which, having been done, one does not regret.

“Kuso [T 1.0069] yathā duggahito, hatthamevānukantati;

Sāmaññaṃ dupparāmaṭṭhaṃ, nirayāyūpakaḍḍhati.

“‘Just as kusa grass, wrongly grasped, cuts the hand, so the state of a monk, wrongly handled, drags one to hell.

“Yaṃ [V 1.0060] kiñci sithilaṃ kammaṃ, saṃkiliṭṭhañca yaṃ vataṃ;

Saṅkassaraṃ brahmacariyaṃ, na taṃ hoti mahapphala”nti.

“‘Whatever action is lax, and whatever vow is defiled, a holy life lived with reluctance—that is not of great fruit.’”

“Idamavoca, bhikkhave, tāyano devaputto, idaṃ vatvā maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi. Uggaṇhātha, bhikkhave, tāyanagāthā; pariyāpuṇātha, bhikkhave, tāyanagāthā; dhāretha, bhikkhave, tāyanagāthā. Atthasaṃhitā, bhikkhave, tāyanagāthā ādibrahmacariyikā”ti.

“This is what the devaputta Tāyana said, monks. Having said this, he paid homage to me, circumambulated me respectfully, and vanished right there. Learn the verses of Tāyana, monks; master the verses of Tāyana, monks; remember the verses of Tāyana, monks. The verses of Tāyana are beneficial, monks, fundamental to the holy life.”

9. Candimasuttaṃ

9. 9. The Candimā Sutta

90. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 1.0048]. Tena kho pana samayena candimā devaputto rāhunā asurindena gahito hoti. Atha kho candimā devaputto bhagavantaṃ anussaramāno tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

90. At Sāvatthī. At that time, Candimā the devaputta was seized by Rāhu, lord of the asuras. Then Candimā the devaputta, recollecting the Blessed One, recited this verse at that time:

“Namo te buddha vīratthu, vippamuttosi sabbadhi;

Sambādhapaṭipannosmi, tassa me saraṇaṃ bhavā”ti.

“Homage to you, O Buddha, O Hero! You are liberated in every way. I have fallen into distress; be a refuge for me!”

Atha kho bhagavā candimaṃ devaputtaṃ ārabbha rāhuṃ asurindaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, on account of Candimā the devaputta, addressed Rāhu, lord of the asuras, with a verse:

“Tathāgataṃ arahantaṃ, candimā saraṇaṃ gato;

Rāhu candaṃ pamuñcassu, buddhā lokānukampakā”ti.

“Candimā has gone for refuge to the Tathāgata, the Arahant. Release Candimā, O Rāhu! The Buddhas are compassionate toward the world.”

Atha kho rāhu asurindo candimaṃ devaputtaṃ muñcitvā taramānarūpo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā saṃviggo [T 1.0070] lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho rāhuṃ asurindaṃ vepacitti asurindo gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then Rāhu, lord of the asuras, having released Candimā the devaputta, hurriedly approached Vepacitti, lord of the asuras. Having approached, terrified and with his hair standing on end, he stood to one side. To Rāhu, lord of the asuras, who was standing to one side, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, addressed him with a verse:

“Kiṃ nu santaramānova, rāhu candaṃ pamuñcasi;

Saṃviggarūpo āgamma, kiṃ nu bhītova tiṭṭhasī”ti.

“Why now, O Rāhu, as if in a great hurry, did you release Candimā? Having come here with a terrified appearance, why do you stand as if afraid?”

“Sattadhā [V 1.0061] me phale muddhā, jīvanto na sukhaṃ labhe;

Buddhagāthābhigītomhi, no ce muñceyya candima”nti.

“I was overwhelmed by the verse spoken by the Buddha. If I were not to release Candimā, my head would split into seven pieces; while living, I would find no happiness.”

10. Sūriyasuttaṃ

10. 10. The Sūriya Sutta

91. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena [P 1.0051] kho pana samayena sūriyo devaputto rāhunā asurindena gahito hoti. Atha kho sūriyo devaputto bhagavantaṃ anussaramāno tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

91. At Sāvatthī. At that time, Sūriya the devaputta was seized by Rāhu, lord of the asuras. Then Sūriya the devaputta, recollecting the Blessed One, recited this verse at that time:

“Namo te buddha vīratthu, vippamuttosi sabbadhi;

Sambādhapaṭipannosmi, tassa me saraṇaṃ bhavā”ti.

“Homage to you, O Buddha, O Hero! You are liberated in every way. I have fallen into distress; be a refuge for me!”

Atha kho bhagavā sūriyaṃ devaputtaṃ ārabbha rāhuṃ asurindaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, on account of Sūriya the devaputta, addressed Rāhu, lord of the asuras, with verses:

“Tathāgataṃ [M 1.0049] arahantaṃ, sūriyo saraṇaṃ gato;

Rāhu sūriyaṃ suriyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pamuñcassu, buddhā lokānukampakā.

“Sūriya has gone for refuge to the Tathāgata, the Arahant. Release Sūriya, O Rāhu! The Buddhas are compassionate toward the world.

“Yo andhakāre tamasi pabhaṅkaro,

Verocano maṇḍalī uggatejo;

Mā [T 1.0071] rāhu gilī caramantalikkhe,

Pajaṃ mamaṃ rāhu pamuñca sūriya”nti.

“That maker of light in the darkness and gloom, brilliant, orb-like, and of fierce power—do not swallow him, Rāhu, as he travels in the sky. O Rāhu, release my son, Sūriya!”

Atha kho rāhu asurindo sūriyaṃ devaputtaṃ muñcitvā taramānarūpo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho rāhuṃ asurindaṃ vepacitti asurindo gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then Rāhu, lord of the asuras, having released Sūriya the devaputta, hurriedly approached Vepacitti, lord of the asuras. Having approached, terrified and with his hair standing on end, he stood to one side. To Rāhu, lord of the asuras, who was standing to one side, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, addressed him with a verse:

“Kiṃ nu santaramānova, rāhu sūriyaṃ pamuñcasi;

Saṃviggarūpo āgamma, kiṃ nu bhītova tiṭṭhasī”ti.

“Why now, O Rāhu, as if in a great hurry, did you release Sūriya? Having come here with a terrified appearance, why do you stand as if afraid?”

“Sattadhā [V 1.0062] me phale muddhā, jīvanto na sukhaṃ labhe;

Buddhagāthābhigītomhi, no ce muñceyya sūriya”nti.

“I was overwhelmed by the verses spoken by the Buddha. If I were not to release Sūriya, my head would split into seven pieces; while living, I would find no happiness.”

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary:

Dve kassapā ca māgho ca, māgadho dāmali kāmado;

Pañcālacaṇḍo tāyano, candimasūriyena te dasāti.

The two Kassapas, Māgha, Māgadha, Dāmali, Kāmada, Pañcālacaṇḍa, Tāyana, and with Candimā and Sūriya—these are the ten.

2. Anāthapiṇḍikavaggo

2. 2. The Chapter on Anāthapiṇḍika

1. Candimasasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Candimasa

92. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 1.0072]. Atha kho candimaso candimāso (ka.) devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā [P 1.0052] tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi[M 1.0050]. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho candimaso devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

92. At Sāvatthī. Then, when the night was far advanced, the devaputta Candimasa, of exceedingly pleasing appearance, having illuminated the entire Jeta's Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the devaputta Candimasa recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Te hi sotthiṃ gamissanti, kacche vāmakase magā;

Jhānāni upasampajja, ekodi nipakā satā”ti.

“They indeed will reach a state of well-being, like deer in a mountain or river bend free from gadflies—those who, having perfected the jhānas, are concentrated, prudent, and mindful.”

“Te hi pāraṃ gamissanti, chetvā jālaṃva ambujo;

Jhānāni upasampajja, appamattā raṇañjahā”ti.

“They indeed will go to the far shore, having cut the net like a fish—those who, having perfected the jhānas, are diligent and have abandoned conflict.”

2. Veṇḍusuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Veṇḍu

93. Ekamantaṃ [V 1.0063] ṭhito kho veṇḍu veṇhu (sī.) devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

93. Standing to one side, the devaputta Veṇḍu recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sukhitāva te sukhitā vata te (sī. syā. kaṃ.) manujā, sugataṃ payirupāsiya;

Yuñjaṃ yujja (sī.), yuñja (syā. kaṃ. pī.) gotamasāsane, appamattā nu sikkhare”ti.

“Happy indeed are those people who attend upon the Well-farer; striving in Gotama’s teaching, being diligent, they train.”

“Ye [T 1.0073] me pavutte siṭṭhipade satthipade (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) (veṇḍūti bhagavā),

Anusikkhanti jhāyino;

Kāle te appamajjantā,

Na maccuvasagā siyu”nti.

(The Blessed One said to Veṇḍu:) “Those meditators who train in the rules of instruction proclaimed by me, being diligent at the proper time, they will not come under the sway of Death.”

3. Dīghalaṭṭhisuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Dīghalaṭṭhi

94. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho dīghalaṭṭhi devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ veḷuvanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho dīghalaṭṭhi devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

94. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Then, when the night was far advanced, the devaputta Dīghalaṭṭhi, of exceedingly pleasing appearance, having illuminated the entire Bamboo Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the devaputta Dīghalaṭṭhi recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Bhikkhu siyā jhāyī vimuttacitto,

Ākaṅkhe ce hadayassānupattiṃ;

Lokassa ñatvā udayabbayañca,

Sucetaso anissito tadānisaṃso”ti.

“If a bhikkhu should wish for the attainment of the heart's release, he should be a meditator with a liberated mind. Having known the arising and passing away of the world, being pure-minded and unattached, he would have that benefit.”

4. Nandanasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Nandana

95. Ekamantaṃ [M 1.0051] ṭhito kho nandano devaputto bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

95. Standing to one side, the devaputta Nandana addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Pucchāmi taṃ gotama bhūripañña,

Anāvaṭaṃ bhagavato ñāṇadassanaṃ;

Kathaṃvidhaṃ [T 1.0074][V 1.0064][P 1.0053] sīlavantaṃ vadanti,

Kathaṃvidhaṃ paññavantaṃ vadanti;

Kathaṃvidho dukkhamaticca iriyati,

Kathaṃvidhaṃ devatā pūjayantī”ti.

“I ask you, Gotama of vast wisdom, for the Blessed One’s knowledge and vision is unobstructed: What kind of person do they call virtuous? What kind of person do they call wise? What kind of person lives having overcome suffering? What kind of person do the devas revere?”

“Yo sīlavā paññavā bhāvitatto,

Samāhito jhānarato satīmā;

Sabbassa sokā vigatā pahīnā,

Khīṇāsavo antimadehadhārī.

“One who is virtuous, wise, with a developed self, composed, delighting in jhāna, and mindful; for whom all sorrows are gone and abandoned, whose taints are destroyed, who bears their final body.

“Tathāvidhaṃ sīlavantaṃ vadanti,

Tathāvidhaṃ paññavantaṃ vadanti;

Tathāvidho dukkhamaticca iriyati,

Tathāvidhaṃ devatā pūjayantī”ti.

“Such a one they call virtuous; such a one they call wise. Such a one lives, having overcome suffering; such a one the devas revere.”

5. Candanasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Candana

96. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho candano devaputto bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

96. Standing to one side, the devaputta Candana addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kathaṃsu kosudha (sī.) tarati oghaṃ, rattindivamatandito;

Appatiṭṭhe anālambe, ko gambhīre na sīdatī”ti.

“How does one cross the flood, unwearied day and night? With no standing place, with nothing to grasp, who does not sink in the deep?”

“Sabbadā sīlasampanno, paññavā susamāhito;

Āraddhavīriyo pahitatto, oghaṃ tarati duttaraṃ.

“One who is always endowed with virtue, wise, and well-concentrated, with aroused energy and a resolute mind, crosses the flood so difficult to cross.

“Virato [T 1.0075] kāmasaññāya, rūpasaṃyojanātigo;

Nandīrāgaparikkhīṇo, so gambhīre na sīdatī”ti.

“One who is detached from perception of sensual pleasure, who has gone beyond the fetter of form, and in whom delight-lust is exhausted—that one does not sink in the deep.”

6. Vāsudattasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Vāsudatta

97. Ekamantaṃ [V 1.0065][M 1.0052] ṭhito kho vāsudatto devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

97. Standing to one side, the devaputta Vāsudatta recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho, ḍayhamānova ḍayhamāneva (sabbattha) matthake;

Kāmarāgappahānāya, sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.

“As if struck by a spear, or as if one's head were on fire, a bhikkhu, being mindful, should wander for the abandoning of sensual lust.”

“Sattiyā viya omaṭṭho, ḍayhamānova matthake;

Sakkāyadiṭṭhippahānāya, sato bhikkhu paribbaje”ti.

“As if struck by a spear, or as if one's head were on fire, a bhikkhu, being mindful, should wander for the abandoning of identity-view.”

7. Subrahmasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Subrahmā

98. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho subrahmā devaputto bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

98. Standing to one side, the devaputta Subrahmā addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Niccaṃ utrastamidaṃ cittaṃ, niccaṃ ubbiggamidaṃ ubbiggidaṃ (mahāsatipaṭṭhānasuttavaṇṇanāyaṃ) mano;

Anuppannesu [P 1.0054] kicchesu kiccesu (bahūsu), atho uppatitesu ca;

Sace atthi anutrastaṃ, taṃ me akkhāhi pucchito”ti.

“This mind is always terrified, this mind is always anxious, on account of troubles not yet arisen and also those that have arisen. If there is that which is free from terror, being asked, please declare it to me.”

“Nāññatra bojjhā tapasā bojjhaṅgatapasā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), nāññatrindriyasaṃvarā;

Nāññatra sabbanissaggā, sotthiṃ passāmi pāṇina”nti.

“Other than from the factors of awakening and asceticism, other than from restraint of the sense faculties, other than from the relinquishing of all, I see no well-being for living beings.”

“Idamavoca…pe… tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.

This was said by the Blessed One... and so on... he vanished right there.

8. Kakudhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Kakudha

99. Evaṃ [T 1.0076] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sākete viharati añjanavane migadāye. Atha kho kakudho devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ añjanavanaṃ obhāsetvā [V 1.0066] yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho kakudho devaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “nandasi, samaṇā”ti? “Kiṃ laddhā, āvuso”ti? “Tena hi, samaṇa, socasī”ti? “Kiṃ jīyittha, āvuso”ti? “Tena hi, samaṇa, neva nandasi na ca neva (sī. syā. kaṃ.) socasī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti.

99. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāketa in the Añjana Grove, the deer park. Then, when the night was far advanced, the devaputta Kakudha, of surpassing splendor, illuminating the entire Añjana Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the devaputta Kakudha said this to the Blessed One: “Do you rejoice, ascetic?” “Having gained what, friend?” “Then, ascetic, do you grieve?” “What has perished, friend?” “Then, ascetic, do you neither rejoice nor grieve?” “So it is, friend.”

“Kacci [M 1.0053] tvaṃ anagho anigho (sabbattha) bhikkhu, kacci nandī nandi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) na vijjati;

Kacci taṃ ekamāsīnaṃ, aratī nābhikīratī”ti.

“Are you without distress, bhikkhu? Is there no delight found in you? When you are sitting alone, does discontent not assail you?”

“Anagho ve ahaṃ yakkha, atho nandī na vijjati;

Atho maṃ ekamāsīnaṃ, aratī nābhikīratī”ti.

“Indeed, yakkha, I am without distress, and no delight is found in me. Moreover, when I am sitting alone, discontent does not assail me.”

“Kathaṃ tvaṃ anagho bhikkhu, kathaṃ nandī na vijjati;

Kathaṃ taṃ ekamāsīnaṃ, aratī nābhikīratī”ti.

“How are you without distress, bhikkhu? How is there no delight found in you? How is it that when you are sitting alone, discontent does not assail you?”

“Aghajātassa ve nandī, nandījātassa ve aghaṃ;

Anandī anagho bhikkhu, evaṃ jānāhi āvuso”ti.

“For one in whom distress has arisen, friend, there is delight. For one in whom delight has arisen, there is distress. A bhikkhu without delight is without distress. Know this, friend.”

“Cirassaṃ vata passāmi, brāhmaṇaṃ parinibbutaṃ;

Anandiṃ anaghaṃ bhikkhuṃ, tiṇṇaṃ loke visattika”nti.

“After a long time, indeed, I see a brahmin fully serene, a bhikkhu without delight and without distress, who has crossed beyond attachment in the world.”

9. Uttarasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Uttara

100. Rājagahanidānaṃ[T 1.0077]. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho uttaro devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

100. The setting is Rājagaha. Standing to one side, the devaputta Uttara recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Upanīyati [P 1.0055] jīvitamappamāyu,

Jarūpanītassa na santi tāṇā;

Etaṃ [V 1.0067] bhayaṃ maraṇe pekkhamāno,

Puññāni kayirātha sukhāvahānī”ti.

“Life is led away; the lifespan is short. For one led away by aging, there are no shelters. Seeing this danger in death, one should perform meritorious deeds that bring happiness.”

“Upanīyati jīvitamappamāyu,

Jarūpanītassa na santi tāṇā;

Etaṃ bhayaṃ maraṇe pekkhamāno,

Lokāmisaṃ pajahe santipekkho”ti.

“Life is led away; the lifespan is short. For one led away by aging, there are no shelters. Seeing this danger in death, one aspiring for peace should relinquish the world’s bait.”

10. Anāthapiṇḍikasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse concerning Anāthapiṇḍika

101. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

101. Standing to one side, the devaputta Anāthapiṇḍika recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Idañhi taṃ jetavanaṃ, isisaṅghanisevitaṃ;

Āvutthaṃ dhammarājena, pītisañjananaṃ mama.

“This indeed is that Jetavana, frequented by the community of seers, dwelt in by the King of Dhamma; it generates joy in me.

“Kammaṃ [M 1.0054] vijjā ca dhammo ca, sīlaṃ jīvitamuttamaṃ;

Etena maccā sujjhanti, na gottena dhanena vā.

“Action, knowledge, and Dhamma, virtue and a supreme livelihood—by this are mortals purified, not by lineage or by wealth.

“Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso, sampassaṃ atthamattano;

Yoniso [T 1.0078][P 1.0056] vicine dhammaṃ, evaṃ tattha visujjhati.

“Therefore, a wise person, seeing their own welfare, should wisely investigate the Dhamma; thus they are purified therein.

“Sāriputtova paññāya, sīlena upasamena ca;

Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu, etāvaparamo siyā”ti.

“In wisdom, virtue, and tranquility, Sāriputta is indeed supreme. Whatever bhikkhu has gone to the far shore, he would have Sāriputta as his highest limit.”

Idamavoca anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto. Idaṃ vatvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

The devaputta Anāthapiṇḍika said this. Having said this, and having paid homage to the Blessed One and circumambulated him, he vanished right there.

Atha [V 1.0068] kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi – “imaṃ, bhikkhave, rattiṃ aññataro devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, so devaputto mama santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then, when that night had passed, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, tonight, when the night was far advanced, a certain devaputta of surpassing beauty, having illuminated the entire Jetavana, approached me. Having approached, he paid homage to me and stood to one side. Standing to one side, bhikkhus, that devaputta recited these verses in my presence:

“Idañhi taṃ jetavanaṃ, isisaṅghanisevitaṃ;

Āvutthaṃ dhammarājena, pītisañjananaṃ mama.

“‘This indeed is that Jetavana, frequented by the community of seers, dwelt in by the King of Dhamma; it generates joy in me.

“Kammaṃ vijjā ca dhammo ca, sīlaṃ jīvitamuttamaṃ;

Etena maccā sujjhanti, na gottena dhanena vā.

“‘Action, knowledge, and Dhamma, virtue and a supreme livelihood—by this are mortals purified, not by lineage or by wealth.

“Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso, sampassaṃ atthamattano;

Yoniso vicine dhammaṃ, evaṃ tattha visujjhati.

“‘Therefore, a wise person, seeing their own welfare, should wisely investigate the Dhamma; thus they are purified therein.

“Sāriputtova paññāya, sīlena upasamena ca;

Yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu, etāvaparamo siyā”ti.

“‘In wisdom, virtue, and tranquility, Sāriputta is indeed supreme. Whatever bhikkhu has gone to the far shore, he would have Sāriputta as his highest limit.’”

“Idamavoca, bhikkhave, so devaputto. Idaṃ vatvā maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.

“Bhikkhus, the devaputta said this. Having said this, and having paid homage to me and circumambulated me, he vanished right there.”

Evaṃ [T 1.0079] vutte, āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “so hi nūna, bhante, anāthapiṇḍiko devaputto bhavissati. Anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati āyasmante sāriputte abhippasanno ahosī”ti. “Sādhu [M 1.0055] sādhu, ānanda, yāvatakaṃ kho, ānanda, takkāya pattabbaṃ anuppattaṃ taṃ tayā. Anāthapiṇḍiko hi so, ānanda, devaputto”ti.

When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, that must surely be the devaputta Anāthapiṇḍika. The householder Anāthapiṇḍika was deeply devoted to the Venerable Sāriputta.” “Good, good, Ānanda! To the extent that one can reach by reasoning, Ānanda, you have reached. Indeed, Ānanda, that was the devaputta Anāthapiṇḍika.”

Anāthapiṇḍikavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter: Anāthapiṇḍika.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Candimaso [V 1.0069] candimāso (pī. ka.) ca veṇḍu veṇhu (sī. ka.) ca, dīghalaṭṭhi ca nandano;

Candano vāsudatto ca, subrahmā kakudhena ca;

Uttaro navamo vutto, dasamo anāthapiṇḍikoti.

Candimasa and Veṇḍu, Dīghalaṭṭhi and Nandana; Candana and Vāsudatta, Subrahmā and Kakudha; Uttara is declared the ninth, and Anāthapiṇḍika the tenth.

3. Nānātitthiyavaggo

3. The Chapter on Various Sectarians

1. Sivasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse concerning Siva

102. Evaṃ [T 1.0080] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho sivo devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho sivo devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

102. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then, when the night was far advanced, the devaputta Siva, of surpassing radiance, illuminating the entire Jeta's Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the devaputta Siva recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.

“One should associate only with the good; one should cultivate intimacy with the good. Having known the good Dhamma of the good, one becomes better, not worse.

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, paññā labbhati nāññato.

“One should associate only with the good; one should cultivate intimacy with the good. Having known the good Dhamma of the good, one obtains wisdom, not from another.

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, sokamajjhe na socati.

“One should associate only with the good; one should cultivate intimacy with the good. Having known the good Dhamma of the good, one does not grieve in the midst of the sorrowful.

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ [P 1.0057] saddhammamaññāya, ñātimajjhe virocati.

“One should associate only with the good; one should cultivate intimacy with the good. Having known the good Dhamma of the good, one shines in the midst of one's relatives.

“Sabbhireva [V 1.0070][M 1.0056] samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ [T 1.0081] saddhammamaññāya, sattā gacchanti suggatiṃ.

“One should associate only with the good; one should cultivate intimacy with the good. Having known the good Dhamma of the good, beings go to a good destination.

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, sattā tiṭṭhanti sātata”nti.

“One should associate only with the good; one should cultivate intimacy with the good. Having known the good Dhamma of the good, beings are established in happiness for a long time.”

Atha kho bhagavā sivaṃ devaputtaṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One replied to the devaputta Siva with a verse:

“Sabbhireva samāsetha, sabbhi kubbetha santhavaṃ;

Sataṃ saddhammamaññāya, sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.

“One should associate only with the good; one should cultivate intimacy with the good. Having known the good Dhamma of the good, one is freed from all suffering.”

2. Khemasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse concerning Khema

103. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho khemo devaputto bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

103. Standing to one side, the devaputta Khema recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Caranti bālā dummedhā, amitteneva attanā;

Karontā pāpakaṃ kammaṃ, yaṃ hoti kaṭukapphalaṃ.

“Fools of little wisdom wander about as their own enemy, doing evil kamma which has a bitter fruit.

“Na taṃ kammaṃ kataṃ sādhu, yaṃ katvā anutappati;

Yassa assumukho rodaṃ, vipākaṃ paṭisevati.

“That kamma is not well done, which, having been done, one later regrets; whose result one experiences weeping, with a tearful face.

“Tañca kammaṃ kataṃ sādhu, yaṃ katvā nānutappati;

Yassa patīto sumano, vipākaṃ paṭisevati.

“And that kamma is well done, which, having been done, one does not later regret; whose result one partakes of, delighted and glad of mind.

“Paṭikacceva paṭigacceva (sī.) taṃ kayirā, yaṃ jaññā hitamattano;

Na sākaṭikacintāya, mantā dhīro parakkame.

“Whatever one might know to be for one's own welfare, that one should do beforehand. A wise person should not strive with the slow thought of a carter.

“Yathā sākaṭiko maṭṭhaṃ panthaṃ (sī.), pasatthaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), samaṃ hitvā mahāpathaṃ;

Visamaṃ maggamāruyha, akkhacchinnova jhāyati.

“Just as a carter, having abandoned the smooth, even highway and taken to an uneven road, grieves with a broken axle;

“Evaṃ [T 1.0082][V 1.0071] dhammā apakkamma, adhammamanuvattiya;

Mando maccumukhaṃ patto, akkhacchinnova jhāyatī”ti.

“So too a foolish person, having departed from the Dhamma and followed the non-Dhamma, upon reaching the mouth of death, grieves just like one with a broken axle.”

3. Serīsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse concerning Serī

104. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho serī devaputto bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

104. Standing to one side, the devaputta Serī addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Annamevābhinandanti[M 1.0057], ubhaye devamānusā;

Atha ko nāma so yakkho, yaṃ annaṃ nābhinandatī”ti.

“Both gods and humans rejoice in food; now what is the name of that spirit who does not rejoice in food?”

“Ye naṃ dadanti saddhāya, vippasannena cetasā;

Tameva annaṃ bhajati, asmiṃ loke paramhi ca.

“Those who give that food with faith, with a serene mind, that very food follows them in this world and in the next.

“Tasmā vineyya maccheraṃ, dajjā dānaṃ malābhibhū;

Puññāni paralokasmiṃ, patiṭṭhā honti pāṇina”nti.

“Therefore, having removed stinginess, one should give a gift, having overcome that stain. Merits are the support for beings in the next world.”

“Acchariyaṃ[P 1.0058], bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāvasubhāsitamidaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā –

“Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Amazing, Venerable Sir! How well-spoken this is by the Blessed One:

“Ye naṃ dadanti saddhāya, vippasannena cetasā;

Tameva annaṃ bhajati, asmiṃ loke paramhi ca.

“Those who give that food with faith, with a serene mind, that very food follows them in this world and in the next.

“Tasmā vineyya maccheraṃ, dajjā dānaṃ malābhibhū;

Puññāni paralokasmiṃ, patiṭṭhā honti pāṇina”nti.

“Therefore, having removed stinginess, one should give a gift, having overcome that stain. Merits are the support for beings in the next world.”

“Bhūtapubbāhaṃ, bhante, sirī serī (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nāma rājā ahosiṃ dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, catūsu dvāresu dānaṃ dīyittha samaṇa-brāhmaṇa-kapaṇaddhika-vanibbakayācakānaṃ.
