Atha kho [T 1.0083] maṃ, bhante, itthāgāraṃ upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca itthāgārā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ (ka.) – ‘devassa kho devasseva kho (ka. sī.) dānaṃ dīyati; amhākaṃ dānaṃ na dīyati. Sādhu mayampi devaṃ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ khosmi dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Dānaṃ dassāmāti vadante kinti vadeyya’nti? So khvāhaṃ, bhante, paṭhamaṃ dvāraṃ itthāgārassa adāsiṃ. Tattha itthāgārassa dānaṃ dīyittha; mama dānaṃ paṭikkami.

“Formerly, Venerable Sir, I was a king named Seri, a giver, a lord of gifts, one who was accustomed to speaking on the virtues of giving. At my four gates, Venerable Sir, alms were given to ascetics, brahmins, the poor, travelers, beggars, and supplicants. Then, Venerable Sir, the royal women approached me and said this: ‘Alms are given by the king, but alms are not given by us. It would be good if we too, relying on the king, might give alms and make merit.’ Then, Venerable Sir, this thought occurred to me: ‘I am a giver, a lord of gifts, one who is accustomed to speaking on the virtues of giving. To those who say, “We will give alms,” what should I say?’ So, Venerable Sir, I gave the first gate to the royal women. There, alms were given by the royal women, and my own alms-giving subsided.

“Atha kho maṃ, bhante, khattiyā anuyantā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘devassa kho dānaṃ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṃ dīyati; amhākaṃ dānaṃ na dīyati. Sādhu mayampi devaṃ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti[V 1.0072]. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ khosmi dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Dānaṃ dassāmāti vadante kinti vadeyya’nti[M 1.0058]? So khvāhaṃ, bhante, dutiyaṃ dvāraṃ khattiyānaṃ anuyantānaṃ adāsiṃ. Tattha khattiyānaṃ anuyantānaṃ dānaṃ dīyittha, mama dānaṃ paṭikkami.

“Then, Venerable Sir, the attendant khattiyas approached me and said this: ‘Alms are given by the king, and alms are given by the royal women, but alms are not given by us. It would be good if we too, relying on the king, might give alms and make merit.’ Then, Venerable Sir, this thought occurred to me: ‘I am a giver, a lord of gifts, one who is accustomed to speaking on the virtues of giving. To those who say, “We will give alms,” what should I say?’ So, Venerable Sir, I gave the second gate to the attendant khattiyas. There, alms were given by the attendant khattiyas, and my own alms-giving subsided.

“Atha kho maṃ, bhante, balakāyo upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘devassa kho dānaṃ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṃ dīyati; khattiyānaṃ anuyantānaṃ dānaṃ dīyati; amhākaṃ dānaṃ na dīyati. Sādhu mayampi devaṃ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti. Tassa [P 1.0059] mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ khosmi dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Dānaṃ dassāmāti vadante [T 1.0084] kinti vadeyya’nti? So khvāhaṃ bhante, tatiyaṃ dvāraṃ balakāyassa adāsiṃ. Tattha balakāyassa dānaṃ dīyittha, mama dānaṃ paṭikkami.

“Then, Venerable Sir, the army approached me and said this: ‘Alms are given by the king, alms are given by the royal women, and alms are given by the attendant khattiyas, but alms are not given by us. It would be good if we too, relying on the king, might give alms and make merit.’ Then, Venerable Sir, this thought occurred to me: ‘I am a giver, a lord of gifts, one who is accustomed to speaking on the virtues of giving. To those who say, “We will give alms,” what should I say?’ So, Venerable Sir, I gave the third gate to the army. There, alms were given by the army, and my own alms-giving subsided.

“Atha kho maṃ, bhante, brāhmaṇagahapatikā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘devassa kho dānaṃ dīyati; itthāgārassa dānaṃ dīyati; khattiyānaṃ anuyantānaṃ dānaṃ dīyati; balakāyassa dānaṃ dīyati; amhākaṃ dānaṃ na dīyati. Sādhu mayampi devaṃ nissāya dānāni dadeyyāma, puññāni kareyyāmā’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ khosmi dāyako dānapati dānassa vaṇṇavādī. Dānaṃ dassāmāti vadante kinti vadeyya’nti? So khvāhaṃ, bhante, catutthaṃ dvāraṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ adāsiṃ. Tattha brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ dānaṃ dīyittha, mama dānaṃ paṭikkami.

“Then, Venerable Sir, the brahmins and householders approached me and said this: ‘Alms are given by the king, alms are given by the royal women, alms are given by the attendant khattiyas, and alms are given by the army, but alms are not given by us. It would be good if we too, relying on the king, might give alms and make merit.’ Then, Venerable Sir, this thought occurred to me: ‘I am a giver, a lord of gifts, one who is accustomed to speaking on the virtues of giving. To those who say, “We will give alms,” what should I say?’ So, Venerable Sir, I gave the fourth gate to the brahmins and householders. There, alms were given by the brahmins and householders, and my own alms-giving subsided.

“Atha kho maṃ, bhante, purisā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘na kho dāni devassa koci dānaṃ dīyatī’ti. Evaṃ vuttāhaṃ, bhante, te purise etadavocaṃ – ‘tena hi, bhaṇe, yo bāhiresu janapadesu āyo sañjāyati tato upaḍḍhaṃ antepure pavesetha, upaḍḍhaṃ tattheva dānaṃ detha samaṇa-brāhmaṇa-kapaṇaddhika-vanibbaka-yācakāna’nti[V 1.0073]. So khvāhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ dīgharattaṃ katānaṃ puññānaṃ evaṃ dīgharattaṃ katānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pariyantaṃ nādhigacchāmi – ettakaṃ puññanti vā ettako puññavipākoti vā ettakaṃ sagge ṭhātabbanti vāti. Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāvasubhāsitamidaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā –

“Then, Venerable Sir, some royal officials approached me and said this: ‘Now, Your Majesty, no alms are being given by you in any place.’ When this was said, Venerable Sir, I told those officials: ‘Well then, my good men, of the revenue that is collected in the outer provinces, bring half into the inner palace, and give the other half as alms right there to the ascetics, brahmins, the poor, travelers, beggars, and supplicants.’ So, Venerable Sir, for such a long time having made merit, for such a long time having done wholesome deeds, I cannot find a limit, thinking: ‘The merit is this much,’ or ‘The result of the merit is this much,’ or ‘One is to remain in heaven for this long.’ Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Amazing, Venerable Sir! How well-spoken this is by the Blessed One:

“Ye [T 1.0085] naṃ dadanti saddhāya, vippasannena cetasā;

Tameva annaṃ bhajati, asmiṃ loke paramhi ca.

“Those who give that food with faith, with a serene mind, that very food follows them in this world and in the next.

“Tasmā vineyya maccheraṃ, dajjā dānaṃ malābhibhū;

Puññāni paralokasmiṃ, patiṭṭhā honti pāṇina”nti.

“Therefore, having removed stinginess, one should give a gift, having overcome that stain. Merits are the support for beings in the next world.”

4. Ghaṭīkārasuttaṃ

4. The Ghaṭīkāra Sutta

105. Ekamantaṃ [M 1.0059][P 1.0060] ṭhito kho ghaṭīkāro devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

105. Standing to one side, the devaputta Ghaṭikāra recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Avihaṃ upapannāse, vimuttā satta bhikkhavo;

Rāgadosaparikkhīṇā, tiṇṇā loke visattika”nti.

“Seven bhikkhus, reborn in the Aviha realm, are liberated; their lust and hatred are exhausted; they have crossed over attachment in the world.”

“Ke ca te ataruṃ paṅkaṃ, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ;

Ke hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upaccagu”nti.

“And who are they who crossed the mire, the realm of Death so difficult to overcome? Who, having abandoned the human body, have overcome the divine yoke?”

“Upako palagaṇḍo phalagaṇḍo (ka.) ca, pukkusāti ca te tayo;

Bhaddiyo khaṇḍadevo ca, bāhuraggi ca saṅgiyo bāhudantī ca piṅgiyo (sī. syā.);

Te hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upaccagu”nti.

“Upaka, Palagaṇḍa, and Pukkusāti, those three; Bhaddiya, Khaṇḍadeva, Bāhuraggi, and Saṅgiya; they, having abandoned the human body, have overcome the divine yoke.”

“Kusalī bhāsasī tesaṃ, mārapāsappahāyinaṃ;

Kassa te dhammamaññāya, acchiduṃ bhavabandhana”nti.

“You speak well of them, of those who have abandoned Māra's snare. Whose Dhamma having understood, did they cut the bond of existence?”

“Na [V 1.0074] aññatra bhagavatā, nāññatra tava sāsanā;

Yassa te dhammamaññāya, acchiduṃ bhavabandhanaṃ.

“Not apart from the Blessed One, not apart from your teaching. It was by understanding your Dhamma that they cut the bond of existence.”

“Yattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhati;

Taṃ te dhammaṃ idhaññāya, acchiduṃ bhavabandhana”nti.

“Where name-and-form ceases without remainder—having understood that Dhamma here, they have cut the bond of existence.”

“Gambhīraṃ [T 1.0086] bhāsasī vācaṃ, dubbijānaṃ sudubbudhaṃ;

Kassa tvaṃ dhammamaññāya, vācaṃ bhāsasi īdisa”nti.

“You speak a profound utterance, difficult to know, very difficult to understand. Having understood whose Dhamma do you speak such an utterance?”

“Kumbhakāro pure āsiṃ, vekaḷiṅge ghaṭīkaro;

Mātāpettibharo āsiṃ, kassapassa upāsako.

“Formerly, I was a potter in Vekaḷiṅga named Ghaṭikāra; I was a supporter of my mother and father, a lay follower of Kassapa.

“Virato methunā dhammā, brahmacārī nirāmiso;

Ahuvā te sagāmeyyo, ahuvā te pure sakhā.

“I abstained from sexual intercourse, was a practitioner of the holy life, and was free from worldly things. I was from the same village as you; I was formerly a friend to you.

“Sohamete pajānāmi, vimutte satta bhikkhavo;

Rāgadosaparikkhīṇe, tiṇṇe loke visattika”nti.

“That I know these seven bhikkhus who are liberated, their lust and hatred exhausted, having crossed over attachment in the world.”

“Evametaṃ tadā āsi, yathā bhāsasi bhaggava;

Kumbhakāro pure āsi, vekaḷiṅge ghaṭīkaro.

“So it was then, Bhaggava, just as you say. Formerly, there was a potter in Vekaḷiṅga named Ghaṭikāra.

“Mātāpettibharo [M 1.0060] āsi, kassapassa upāsako;

Virato methunā dhammā, brahmacārī nirāmiso;

Ahuvā me sagāmeyyo, ahuvā me pure sakhā”ti.

“He was a supporter of his mother and father, a lay follower of Kassapa. He abstained from sexual intercourse, was a practitioner of the holy life, and was free from worldly things. He was from the same village as me; he was formerly a friend to me.”

“Evametaṃ purāṇānaṃ, sahāyānaṃ ahu saṅgamo;

Ubhinnaṃ bhāvitattānaṃ, sarīrantimadhārina”nti.

“Thus was this meeting of old friends, of both who had developed themselves, who were bearing their final bodies.”

5. Jantusuttaṃ

5. The Discourse with Jantu

106. Evaṃ [V 1.0075][P 1.0061] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ sambahulā bhikkhū, kosalesu viharanti himavantapasse araññakuṭikāya uddhatā unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā muṭṭhassatino asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā pākatindriyā.

106. Thus have I heard. On one occasion, a number of bhikkhus were dwelling among the Kosalans, in a forest hut on a slope of the Himalayas. They were restless, arrogant, fickle, harsh-spoken, of scattered speech, unmindful, not clearly comprehending, unconcentrated, with bewildered minds, and with their sense faculties unrestrained.

Atha kho [T 1.0087] jantu devaputto tadahuposathe pannarase yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the devaputta Jantu, on the fifteenth, which was the Uposatha day, approached those bhikkhus. Having approached, he addressed those bhikkhus with verses:

“Sukhajīvino pure āsuṃ, bhikkhū gotamasāvakā;

Anicchā piṇḍamesanā piṇḍamesānā (?), anicchā sayanāsanaṃ;

Loke aniccataṃ ñatvā, dukkhassantaṃ akaṃsu te.

“Formerly, the bhikkhus who were disciples of Gotama lived happily. Without desire they sought alms-food; without desire they sought lodging. Having known impermanence in the world, they made an end of suffering.

“Dupposaṃ katvā attānaṃ, gāme gāmaṇikā viya;

Bhutvā bhutvā nipajjanti, parāgāresu mucchitā.

“Having made themselves difficult to support, like village headmen in a village, having eaten and eaten, they lie down, infatuated in the houses of others.

“Saṅghassa añjaliṃ katvā, idhekacce vadāmahaṃ vandāmahaṃ (ka.);

Apaviddhā anāthā te, yathā petā tatheva te tatheva ca (sī.).

“Having paid reverence to the Saṅgha, I say this to some here: they are cast off, without refuge; they are just like the departed.

“Ye kho pamattā viharanti, te me sandhāya bhāsitaṃ;

Ye appamattā viharanti, namo tesaṃ karomaha”nti.

“This was spoken by me with reference to those who dwell heedlessly. To those who dwell heedfully, I pay homage.”

6. Rohitassasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse with Rohitassa

107. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho rohitasso devaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yattha nu kho, bhante, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na jiyyati na miyyati (syā. kaṃ. ka.) na cavati na upapajjati, sakkā nu kho so, bhante, gamanena lokassa [M 1.0061] anto ñātuṃ vā daṭṭhuṃ vā pāpuṇituṃ [V 1.0076] vā”ti? “Yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṃ taṃ gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ daṭṭheyyaṃ [T 1.0088] patteyyanti vadāmī”ti.

107. At Sāvatthī. Standing to one side, the devaputta Rohitassa said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, is it possible, by traveling, to know, to see, or to reach the end of the world where one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn?” “Friend, where one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn, I do not say that the end of the world is to be known, to be seen, or to be reached by traveling.”

“Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāvasubhāsitamidaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā – ‘yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṃ taṃ gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ daṭṭheyyaṃ patteyyanti vadāmī’ti.

“Marvelous, venerable sir! Amazing, venerable sir! How well spoken this is by the Blessed One, venerable sir: ‘Friend, where one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn, I do not say that the end of the world is to be known, to be seen, or to be reached by traveling.’”

“Bhūtapubbāhaṃ, bhante, rohitasso nāma isi ahosiṃ bhojaputto iddhimā vehāsaṅgamo. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evarūpo [P 1.0062] javo ahosi; seyyathāpi nāma daḷhadhammā daḷhadhammo (sabbattha) ṭīkā ca moggallānabyākaraṇaṃ ca oloketabbaṃ dhanuggaho susikkhito katahattho katayoggo katūpāsano lahukena asanena appakasireneva tiriyaṃ tālacchāyaṃ atipāteyya. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evarūpo padavītihāro ahosi; seyyathāpi nāma puratthimā samuddā pacchimo samuddo. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evarūpaṃ icchāgataṃ uppajji – ‘ahaṃ gamanena lokassa antaṃ pāpuṇissāmī’ti. So khvāhaṃ, bhante, evarūpena javena samannāgato evarūpena ca padavītihārena aññatreva asita-pīta-khāyita-sāyitā aññatra uccāra-passāvakammā aññatra niddākilamathapaṭivinodanā vassasatāyuko vassasatajīvī vassasataṃ gantvā appatvāva lokassa antaṃ antarāva kālaṅkato.

“In a former time, venerable sir, I was a seer named Rohitassa, a son of Bhoja, possessing psychic power and able to travel through the sky. My speed, venerable sir, was such that it was like a great archer—strong-bowed, well-trained, of steady hand, with practiced skill—who could easily shoot a light arrow across the shadow of a palm tree. My stride, venerable sir, was such that it was like the distance from the eastern ocean to the western ocean. To me, venerable sir, such a wish arose: ‘I will reach the end of the world by traveling.’ Endowed with such speed and with such a stride, venerable sir, I—except for eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting; except for defecating and urinating; and except for dispelling sleep and weariness—with a lifespan of a hundred years, living for a hundred years, traveled for a hundred years. But without reaching the end of the world, I died along the way.

“Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāvasubhāsitamidaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā – ‘yattha kho, āvuso, na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, nāhaṃ taṃ gamanena lokassa antaṃ ñāteyyaṃ daṭṭheyyaṃ patteyyanti vadāmī’”ti.

“Marvelous, venerable sir! Amazing, venerable sir! How well spoken this is by the Blessed One, venerable sir: ‘Friend, where one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn, I do not say that the end of the world is to be known, to be seen, or to be reached by traveling.’”

“Na kho [T 1.0089] panāhaṃ, āvuso, appatvā lokassa antaṃ dukkhassa antakiriyaṃ vadāmi. Api ca khvāhaṃ, āvuso, imasmiṃyeva byāmamatte kaḷevare sasaññimhi samanake lokañca paññapemi lokasamudayañca lokanirodhañca lokanirodhagāminiñca paṭipadanti.

“And yet, friend, I do not declare that an end of suffering is to be made without having reached the end of the world. But indeed, friend, it is in this very fathom-long body, with its perception and mind, that I make known the world, the origin of the world, the cessation of the world, and the path leading to the cessation of the world.

“Gamanena na pattabbo, lokassanto kudācanaṃ;

Na ca appatvā lokantaṃ, dukkhā atthi pamocanaṃ.

“The end of the world is never to be reached by traveling; and without reaching the end of the world, there is no release from suffering.

“Tasmā [V 1.0077][M 1.0062] have lokavidū sumedho,

Lokantagū vusitabrahmacariyo;

Lokassa antaṃ samitāvi ñatvā,

Nāsīsati lokamimaṃ parañcā”ti.

“Therefore, indeed, the wise one, a knower of the world, who has gone to the world’s end and lived the holy life; that tranquil one, having known the end of the world, does not yearn for this world or for the next.”

7. Nandasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse with Nanda

108. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho nando devaputto bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

108. Standing to one side, the devaputta Nanda recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo,

Vayoguṇā anupubbaṃ jahanti;

Etaṃ [T 1.0090][P 1.0063] bhayaṃ maraṇe pekkhamāno,

Puññāni kayirātha sukhāvahānī”ti.

“Periods of time pass, nights fly by, the stages of life are successively left behind; seeing this danger in death, one should perform meritorious deeds that bring happiness.”

“Accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo,

Vayoguṇā anupubbaṃ jahanti;

Etaṃ bhayaṃ maraṇe pekkhamāno,

Lokāmisaṃ pajahe santipekkho”ti.

“Periods of time pass, nights fly by, the stages of life are successively left behind; seeing this danger in death, one who longs for peace should abandon worldly allurements.”

8. Nandivisālasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse with Nandivisāla

109. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho nandivisālo devaputto bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

109. Standing to one side, the devaputta Nandivisāla addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Catucakkaṃ navadvāraṃ, puṇṇaṃ lobhena saṃyutaṃ;

Paṅkajātaṃ mahāvīra, kathaṃ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.

“O Great Hero, this body has four wheels and nine doors, is filled with impurities, and is bound by greed. It is born from mud. How can there be a journey forth from it?”

“Chetvā naddhiṃ varattañca, icchālobhañca pāpakaṃ;

Samūlaṃ taṇhamabbuyha, evaṃ yātrā bhavissatī”ti.

“Having cut the strap and the thong, and evil desire and greed; having uprooted craving with its root, thus will the journey forth be.”

9. Susimasuttaṃ

9. The Susima Sutta

110. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0078]. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “tuyhampi no, ānanda, sāriputto ruccatī”ti?

110. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. To the Venerable Ānanda, so seated, the Blessed One said this: “Ānanda, does Sāriputta also please you?”

“Kassa [M 1.0063] hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya? Paṇḍito, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto[T 1.0091]. Mahāpañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Puthupañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Hāsapañño hāsupañño (sī.), bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Javanapañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Tikkhapañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Nibbedhikapañño, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Appiccho, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Santuṭṭho, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Pavivitto, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Asaṃsaṭṭho, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Āraddhavīriyo, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Vattā, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Vacanakkhamo, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Codako, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Pāpagarahī, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?

“Venerable sir, to what person who is not foolish, not malicious, not deluded, and whose mind is not distorted, would the Venerable Sāriputta not be pleasing? The Venerable Sāriputta is wise, venerable sir. He is of great wisdom, venerable sir. He is of diverse wisdom, venerable sir. He is of joyful wisdom, venerable sir. He is of swift wisdom, venerable sir. He is of sharp wisdom, venerable sir. He is of penetrating wisdom, venerable sir. He is of few wishes, venerable sir. He is content, venerable sir. He is secluded, venerable sir. He is unassociated, venerable sir. He is of aroused energy, venerable sir. He is an admonisher, venerable sir. He is patient of exhortation, venerable sir. He is a reprover, venerable sir. He is a censurer of evil, venerable sir. To what person who is not foolish, not malicious, not deluded, and whose mind is not distorted, would the Venerable Sāriputta not be pleasing?”

“Evametaṃ[P 1.0064], ānanda, evametaṃ, ānanda! Kassa hi nāma, ānanda, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa sāriputto na rucceyya? Paṇḍito, ānanda, sāriputto. Mahāpañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Puthupañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Hāsapañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Javanapañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Tikkhapañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Nibbedhikapañño, ānanda, sāriputto. Appiccho, ānanda, sāriputto. Santuṭṭho, ānanda, sāriputto. Pavivitto, ānanda, sāriputto. Asaṃsaṭṭho, ānanda, sāriputto. Āraddhavīriyo, ānanda, sāriputto. Vattā, ānanda, sāriputto. Vacanakkhamo, ānanda, sāriputto[T 1.0092]. Codako, ānanda, sāriputto. Pāpagarahī, ānanda, sāriputto. Kassa hi nāma, ānanda, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?

“So it is, Ānanda, so it is! To what person, Ānanda, who is not foolish, not malicious, not deluded, and whose mind is not distorted, would Sāriputta not be pleasing? Sāriputta is wise, Ānanda. Sāriputta is of great wisdom, Ānanda. Sāriputta is of diverse wisdom, Ānanda. Sāriputta is of joyful wisdom, Ānanda. Sāriputta is of swift wisdom, Ānanda. Sāriputta is of sharp wisdom, Ānanda. Sāriputta is of penetrating wisdom, Ānanda. Sāriputta is of few wishes, Ānanda. Sāriputta is content, Ānanda. Sāriputta is secluded, Ānanda. Sāriputta is unassociated, Ānanda. Sāriputta is of aroused energy, Ānanda. Sāriputta is an admonisher, Ānanda. Sāriputta is patient of exhortation, Ānanda. Sāriputta is a reprover, Ānanda. Sāriputta is a censurer of evil, Ānanda. To what person, Ānanda, who is not foolish, not malicious, not deluded, and whose mind is not distorted, would Sāriputta not be pleasing?”

Atha kho susimo susīmo (sī.) devaputto āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne mahatiyā devaputtaparisāya [V 1.0079] parivuto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho susimo devaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

Then, while the virtues of the Venerable Sāriputta were being spoken of, the devaputta Susima, surrounded by a great assembly of devaputtas, went to the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he stood to one side. Standing there, the devaputta Susima said this to the Blessed One:

“Evametaṃ[M 1.0064], bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata. Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya? Paṇḍito, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Mahāpañño, bhante, puthupañño, bhante, hāsapañño, bhante, javanapañño, bhante, tikkhapañño, bhante, nibbedhikapañño, bhante, appiccho, bhante, santuṭṭho, bhante, pavivitto, bhante, asaṃsaṭṭho, bhante, āraddhavīriyo, bhante, vattā, bhante, vacanakkhamo, bhante, codako, bhante, pāpagarahī, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto. Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyya?

“So it is, Blessed One; so it is, Well-Farer! To what person, venerable sir, who is not foolish, not malicious, not deluded, and whose mind is not distorted, would the Venerable Sāriputta not be pleasing? The Venerable Sāriputta is wise, venerable sir. He is of great wisdom, venerable sir. He is of diverse wisdom, venerable sir. He is of joyful wisdom, venerable sir. He is of swift wisdom, venerable sir. He is of sharp wisdom, venerable sir. He is of penetrating wisdom, venerable sir. He is of few wishes, venerable sir. He is content, venerable sir. He is secluded, venerable sir. He is unassociated, venerable sir. He is of aroused energy, venerable sir. He is an admonisher, venerable sir. He is patient of exhortation, venerable sir. He is a reprover, venerable sir. He is a censurer of evil, venerable sir. To what person, venerable sir, who is not foolish, not malicious, not deluded, and whose mind is not distorted, would the Venerable Sāriputta not be pleasing?”

“Ahampi hi, bhante, yaññadeva devaputtaparisaṃ upasaṅkamiṃ, etadeva bahulaṃ saddaṃ suṇāmi – ‘paṇḍito āyasmā sāriputto; mahāpañño āyasmā, puthupañño āyasmā, hāsapañño āyasmā, javanapañño āyasmā, tikkhapañño āyasmā, nibbedhikapañño āyasmā, appiccho āyasmā, santuṭṭho āyasmā, pavivitto āyasmā, asaṃsaṭṭho āyasmā, āraddhavīriyo āyasmā, vattā āyasmā, vacanakkhamo āyasmā, codako āyasmā, pāpagarahī āyasmā sāriputto’ti[T 1.0093]. Kassa hi nāma, bhante, abālassa aduṭṭhassa amūḷhassa avipallatthacittassa āyasmā sāriputto na rucceyyā”ti?

“Indeed, venerable sir, whatever assembly of devaputtas I approach, I frequently hear this very declaration: ‘The Venerable Sāriputta is wise; the Venerable One is of great wisdom, of diverse wisdom, of joyful wisdom, of swift wisdom, of sharp wisdom, of penetrating wisdom. The Venerable One is of few wishes, content, secluded, unassociated, of aroused energy. The Venerable One is an admonisher, patient of exhortation, a reprover, a censurer of evil—the Venerable Sāriputta.’ To what person, venerable sir, who is not foolish, not malicious, not deluded, and whose mind is not distorted, would the Venerable Sāriputta not be pleasing?”

Atha kho susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṃseti.

Then, as the virtues of the Venerable Sāriputta were being spoken of, the assembly of devaputtas of the devaputta Susima, being pleased, delighted, and filled with rapture and happiness, displayed various radiant hues.

“Seyyathāpi nāma maṇi veḷuriyo subho jātimā aṭṭhaṃso suparikammakato paṇḍukambale nikkhitto bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṃ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā [P 1.0065] āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṃseti.

“Just as a beryl gem, beautiful, of excellent origin, eight-faceted, and well-polished, when placed on a paṇḍukambala blanket, shines, blazes, and radiates; even so, when the virtues of the Venerable Sāriputta were being spoken of, the assembly of devaputtas of the devaputta Susima, being pleased, delighted, and filled with rapture and happiness, displayed various radiant hues.”

“Seyyathāpi nāma nikkhaṃ jambonadaṃ dakkhakammāraputtaukkāmukhasukusalasampahaṭṭhaṃ paṇḍukambale [V 1.0080] nikkhittaṃ bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṃ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṃseti.

“Just as a Jambu-river gold ornament, skillfully smelted and finished at the mouth of a furnace by the son of a clever goldsmith, when placed on a reddish-yellow woolen blanket, shines, blazes, and radiates; even so, when the virtues of the Venerable Sāriputta were being spoken of, the assembly of devas of the deva Susima, being pleased, joyful, and filled with rapture and happiness, manifested a varied radiance of complexion.

“Seyyathāpi [M 1.0065] nāma saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ osadhitārakā bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṃ susimassa devaputtassa [T 1.0094] devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṃseti.

“Just as in the autumn season, in a clear, cloudless sky, the morning star at the time of dawn shines, blazes, and radiates; even so, when the virtues of the Venerable Sāriputta were being spoken of, the assembly of devas of the deva Susima, being pleased, joyful, and filled with rapture and happiness, manifested a varied radiance of complexion.

“Seyyathāpi nāma saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nabhaṃ abbhussakkamāno abbhussukkamāno (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), abbhuggamamāno (dī. ni. 2.258) sabbaṃ ākāsagataṃ tamagataṃ abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṃ susimassa devaputtassa devaputtaparisā āyasmato sāriputtassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanā pamuditā pītisomanassajātā uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṃseti.

“Just as in the autumn season, in a clear, cloudless sky, the sun, rising into the sky and dispelling all the mass of darkness that pervades the sky, shines, blazes, and radiates; even so, when the virtues of the Venerable Sāriputta were being spoken of, the assembly of devas of the deva Susima, being pleased, joyful, and filled with rapture and happiness, manifested a varied radiance of complexion.

Atha kho susimo devaputto āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then the deva Susima, concerning the Venerable Sāriputta, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Paṇḍitoti samaññāto, sāriputto akodhano;

Appiccho sorato danto, satthuvaṇṇābhato isī”ti.

“Known as ‘wise,’ Sāriputta is free from anger, of few desires, steadfast, and tamed; an accomplished sage, he has received the Teacher’s praise.”

Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ ārabbha susimaṃ devaputtaṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, concerning the Venerable Sāriputta, replied to the deva Susima with a verse:

“Paṇḍitoti samaññāto, sāriputto akodhano;

Appiccho sorato danto, kālaṃ kaṅkhati sudanto” kālaṃ kaṅkhati bhatako sudanto (sī.), kālaṃ kaṅkhati bhāvito sudanto (syā. kaṃ.), kālaṃ kaṅkhati bhatiko sudanto (pī.) ti.

“Known as ‘wise,’ Sāriputta is free from anger, of few desires, steadfast, and tamed; being well-tamed, he awaits his time.”

10. Nānātitthiyasāvakasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Disciples of Various Sectarians

111. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho sambahulā nānātitthiyasāvakā devaputtā [T 1.0095] asamo ca sahali sahalī (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ca nīko niṅko (sī. pī.), niko (syā. kaṃ.) ca ākoṭako ca vegabbhari ca veṭambarī ca (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) māṇavagāmiyo ca abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā [V 1.0081] kevalakappaṃ [P 1.0066] veḷuvanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā [M 1.0066] ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho asamo devaputto pūraṇaṃ kassapaṃ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

111. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, at the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Then, a number of devas who were disciples of various sectarian teachers—Asama and Sahali, Nīka and Ākoṭaka, Vegabbhari and Māṇavagāmiya—when the night was advanced, with their surpassing radiance, having illuminated the entire Bamboo Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the deva Asama, concerning Pūraṇa Kassapa, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Idha chinditamārite, hatajānīsu kassapo;

Na pāpaṃ samanupassati, puññaṃ vā pana attano;

Sa ve vissāsamācikkhi, satthā arahati mānana”nti.

“Here, in cutting and killing, in striking and loss of property, Kassapa sees no evil, nor does he see any merit for himself. He indeed has declared a basis for confidence; therefore, the Teacher is worthy of honor.”

Atha kho sahali devaputto makkhaliṃ gosālaṃ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then the deva Sahali, concerning Makkhali Gosāla, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Tapojigucchāya susaṃvutatto,

Vācaṃ pahāya kalahaṃ janena;

Samosavajjā virato saccavādī,

Na hi nūna tādisaṃ karoti na ha nuna tādī pakaroti (sī. syā. kaṃ.) pāpa”nti.

“Well-restrained through austerity and abhorrence, having abandoned speech and quarreling with people; impartial regarding what is blameworthy, abstinent, a speaker of truth. Surely such a one does no evil.”

Atha kho nīko devaputto nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ nāthaputtaṃ (sī.) ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then the deva Nīka, concerning the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Jegucchī [T 1.0096] nipako bhikkhu, cātuyāmasusaṃvuto;

Diṭṭhaṃ sutañca ācikkhaṃ, na hi nūna kibbisī siyā”ti.

“The bhikkhu who is scrupulous and prudent, well-restrained by the fourfold restraint, who declares what is seen and heard—surely he would not be a wrongdoer.”

Atha kho ākoṭako devaputto nānātitthiye ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then the deva Ākoṭaka, concerning the various sectarians, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Pakudhako kātiyāno nigaṇṭho,

Ye cāpime makkhalipūraṇāse;

Gaṇassa [V 1.0082] satthāro sāmaññappattā,

Na hi nūna te sappurisehi dūre”ti.

“Pakudha Kātiyāna and the Nigaṇṭha, and also these, Makkhali and Pūraṇa—they are teachers of schools, have attained the state of ascetics. Surely they are not far from true men.”

Atha kho vegabbhari devaputto ākoṭakaṃ devaputtaṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi –

Then the deva Vegabbhari replied to the deva Ākoṭaka in verse:

“Sahācaritena sahāravenāpi (ka. sī.), sagāravenāpi (pī.) chavo sigālo siṅgālo (ka.),

Na kotthuko sīhasamo kadāci;

Naggo musāvādī gaṇassa satthā,

Saṅkassarācāro na sataṃ sarikkho”ti.

“A wretched jackal, by imitating a lion’s behavior, is never the equal of a lion. Naked, a speaker of falsehoods, a teacher of a school, of contemptible conduct, he is not like the true ones.”

Atha [M 1.0067][P 1.0067] kho māro pāpimā begabbhariṃ devaputtaṃ anvāvisitvā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then Māra, the Evil One, having possessed the deva Vegabbhari, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Tapojigucchāya āyuttā, pālayaṃ pavivekiyaṃ;

Rūpe ca ye niviṭṭhāse, devalokābhinandino;

Te ve sammānusāsanti, paralokāya mātiyā”ti.

“Those who are devoted to austerity and abhorrence, guarding seclusion, and who are settled in form, delighting in the deva world—they indeed instruct well for the sake of the next world. Know this.”

Atha [T 1.0097] kho bhagavā, ‘māro ayaṃ pāpimā’ iti viditvā, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, having known, ‘This is Māra the Evil One,’ replied to Māra the Evil One in verse:

“Ye keci rūpā idha vā huraṃ vā,

Ye cantalikkhasmiṃ pabhāsavaṇṇā;

Sabbeva te te namucippasatthā,

Āmisaṃva macchānaṃ vadhāya khittā”ti.

“Whatever forms there are, whether here or elsewhere, and those in the sky of shining radiance—all of them, Namuci, are extolled by you. They are all cast out for the slaughter, like bait for the killing of fish.”

Atha kho māṇavagāmiyo devaputto bhagavantaṃ ārabbha bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then the deva Māṇavagāmiya, concerning the Blessed One, recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Vipulo [V 1.0083] rājagahīyānaṃ, giriseṭṭho pavuccati;

Seto himavataṃ seṭṭho, ādicco aghagāminaṃ.

“Among the mountains of Rājagaha, Vipula is called the best of mountains. Among the Himavant mountains, Seto is the best. Among those that move in the sky, the sun is the best.

“Samuddo udadhinaṃ seṭṭho, nakkhattānañca candimā nakkhattānaṃva candimā (ka.);

Sadevakassa lokassa, buddho aggo pavuccatī”ti.

“Among the waters, the ocean is the best. Among the stars, the moon is the best. In the world with its devas, the Buddha is called the foremost.”

Nānātitthiyavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on Various Sectarians, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Sivo khemo ca serī ca, ghaṭī jantu ca rohito;

Nando nandivisālo ca, susimo nānātitthiyena te dasāti.

Siva, Khema, and Seri, Ghaṭikāra, Jantu, and Rohita; Nanda and Nandivisāla, Susima; with the Nānātitthiya Sutta, they are ten.

Devaputtasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Devaputta Saṃyutta is concluded.

3. Kosalasaṃyuttaṃ

3. The Kosala Saṃyutta

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Daharasuttaṃ

1. The Sutta on the Young

112. Evaṃ [T 1.0098][V 1.0084][M 1.0068][P 1.0068] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhavampi no gotamo anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paṭijānātī”ti? “Yañhi taṃ, mahārāja, sammā vadamāno vadeyya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti, mameva mamaṃ (sabbattha) taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya. Ahañhi, mahārāja, anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho”ti.

112. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One, and having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded this conversation of greeting and remembrance, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Blessed One: “Does the venerable Gotama claim to have awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?” “Great king, if anyone, speaking rightly, were to say, ‘He has awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment,’ it is of me that one, speaking rightly, would say this. For I, great king, have awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.”

“Yepi te, bho gotama, samaṇabrāhmaṇā saṅghino gaṇino gaṇācariyā ñātā yasassino titthakarā sādhusammatā bahujanassa, seyyathidaṃ – pūraṇo kassapo, makkhali gosālo, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto, sañcayo belaṭṭhaputto, pakudho kaccāyano, ajito kesakambalo; tepi mayā [T 1.0099] ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paṭijānāthā’ti puṭṭhā samānā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti na paṭijānanti. Kiṃ pana bhavaṃ gotamo daharo ceva jātiyā navo ca pabbajjāyā”ti?

“Venerable Gotama, there are those ascetics and brahmins who are leaders of communities, heads of groups, teachers of groups, who are well-known, renowned, ford-makers, and regarded as virtuous by the manyfolk—namely, Pūraṇa Kassapa, Makkhali Gosāla, the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, Sañcaya Belaṭṭhaputta, Pakudha Kaccāyana, and Ajita Kesakambala. When asked by me, ‘Do you claim to have awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?’ they do not make such a claim. How then can the venerable Gotama, who is young in birth and new to the ordained life, do so?”

“Cattāro [P 1.0069] kho me, mahārāja, daharāti na uññātabbā, daharāti na paribhotabbā. Katame cattāro? Khattiyo kho, mahārāja, daharoti na uññātabbo, daharoti na paribhotabbo. Urago kho, mahārāja, daharoti na uññātabbo, daharoti na paribhotabbo. Aggi [V 1.0085] kho, mahārāja, daharoti na uññātabbo, daharoti na paribhotabbo. Bhikkhu, kho, mahārāja, daharoti na uññātabbo, daharoti na paribhotabbo. Ime kho, mahārāja, cattāro daharāti na uññātabbā, daharāti na paribhotabbā”ti.

“Great king, there are four who, because they are young, should not be looked down upon; who, because they are young, should not be scorned. What are the four? Great king, a khattiya, because he is young, should not be looked down upon; because he is young, should not be scorned. Great king, a snake, because it is young, should not be looked down upon; because it is young, should not be scorned. Great king, a fire, because it is young, should not be looked down upon; because it is young, should not be scorned. Great king, a bhikkhu, because he is young, should not be looked down upon; because he is young, should not be scorned. These, great king, are the four who, because they are young, should not be looked down upon; who, because they are young, should not be scorned.”

Idamavoca [M 1.0069] bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:

“Khattiyaṃ jātisampannaṃ, abhijātaṃ yasassinaṃ;

Daharoti nāvajāneyya, na naṃ paribhave naro.

“A person should not look down upon a khattiya endowed with high birth, of superior lineage, and renowned, thinking, ‘He is young’; one should not scorn him.

“Ṭhānañhi so manujindo, rajjaṃ laddhāna khattiyo;

So kuddho rājadaṇḍena, tasmiṃ pakkamate bhusaṃ;

Tasmā taṃ parivajjeyya, rakkhaṃ jīvitamattano.

“For that khattiya, a lord of men, having attained the kingdom, when angered, may strive mightily against that person with royal punishment. Therefore, one protecting one's own life should avoid him.

“Gāme vā yadi vā raññe, yattha passe bhujaṅgamaṃ;

Daharoti nāvajāneyya, na naṃ paribhave naro.

“Whether in a village or in the wilderness, wherever one might see a snake, a person should not look down upon it, thinking, ‘It is young’; one should not scorn it.

“Uccāvacehi [T 1.0100] vaṇṇehi, urago carati tejasī tejasā (sī. ka.), tejasi (pī. ka.);

So āsajja ḍaṃse bālaṃ, naraṃ nāriñca ekadā;

Tasmā taṃ parivajjeyya, rakkhaṃ jīvitamattano.

“The potent snake moves about with its diverse forms; having encountered a foolish man or woman, it might bite them at some time. Therefore, one protecting one's own life should avoid it.

“Pahūtabhakkhaṃ jālinaṃ, pāvakaṃ kaṇhavattaniṃ;

Daharoti nāvajāneyya, na naṃ paribhave naro.

“A person should not look down upon a fire that consumes much, is blazing, and has a black path, thinking, ‘It is small’; one should not scorn it.

“Laddhā hi so upādānaṃ, mahā hutvāna pāvako;

So āsajja ḍahe dahe bālaṃ, naraṃ nāriñca ekadā;

Tasmā taṃ parivajjeyya, rakkhaṃ jīvitamattano.

“For that fire, having obtained fuel, becomes great. Having encountered a foolish man or woman, it might burn them at some time. Therefore, one protecting one's own life should avoid it.

“Vanaṃ yadaggi ḍahati dahati (ka.), pāvako kaṇhavattanī;

Jāyanti tattha pārohā, ahorattānamaccaye.

“Whatever forest the fire with the black path burns, shoots grow there with the passing of days and nights.

“Yañca [V 1.0086] kho sīlasampanno, bhikkhu ḍahati tejasā;

Na tassa puttā pasavo, dāyādā vindare dhanaṃ;

Anapaccā adāyādā, tālāvatthū bhavanti te.

“But whomever a bhikkhu endowed with virtue burns with his potency, for that person there are no sons or livestock; heirs do not find their wealth. Without offspring, without heirs, they become like palmyra stumps.

“Tasmā [P 1.0070] hi paṇḍito poso, sampassaṃ atthamattano;

Bhujaṅgamaṃ pāvakañca, khattiyañca yasassinaṃ;

Bhikkhuñca sīlasampannaṃ, sammadeva samācare”ti.

“Therefore a wise person, seeing their own welfare, should conduct themselves rightly toward a snake, a fire, a renowned khattiya, and a bhikkhu endowed with virtue.”

Evaṃ vutte, rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi bhante, nikkujjitaṃ nikujjitaṃ (?) vā ukkujjeyya[M 1.0070], paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya[T 1.0101], andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! It is as if, venerable sir, one were to set upright what was overturned, or to reveal what was hidden, or to point out the path to one who was lost, or to hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms. In the very same way, the Dhamma has been clarified by the Blessed One in numerous ways. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.”

2. Purisasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on a Person

113. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kati nu kho, bhante, purisassa dhammā ajjhattaṃ uppajjamānā uppajjanti ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāyā”ti?

113. At Sāvatthī. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, how many qualities arising internally in a person, arise for his non-benefit, suffering, and uncomfortable living?”

“Tayo kho, mahārāja, purisassa dhammā ajjhattaṃ uppajjamānā uppajjanti ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāya. Katame tayo? Lobho kho, mahārāja, purisassa dhammo ajjhattaṃ uppajjamāno uppajjati ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāya. Doso kho, mahārāja, purisassa dhammo ajjhattaṃ uppajjamāno uppajjati ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāya. Moho kho, mahārāja, purisassa dhammo ajjhattaṃ uppajjamāno uppajjati ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāya[V 1.0087]. Ime kho, mahārāja, tayo purisassa dhammā ajjhattaṃ uppajjamānā uppajjanti ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāyā”ti. Idamavoca…pe…

“Great King, three qualities arising internally in a person, arise for his non-benefit, suffering, and uncomfortable living. What are the three? Greed, Great King, is a quality in a person that, arising internally, arises for his non-benefit, suffering, and uncomfortable living. Aversion, Great King, is a quality in a person that, arising internally, arises for his non-benefit, suffering, and uncomfortable living. Delusion, Great King, is a quality in a person that, arising internally, arises for his non-benefit, suffering, and uncomfortable living. These, Great King, are the three qualities in a person that, arising internally, arise for his non-benefit, suffering, and uncomfortable living.”

“Lobho [T 1.0102] doso ca moho ca, purisaṃ pāpacetasaṃ;

Hiṃsanti attasambhūtā, tacasāraṃva samphala”nti sapphalanti (syā. kaṃ.).

“Greed, aversion, and delusion, arisen from oneself, harm a person of wicked mind, just as its own fruit destroys the bamboo.”

3. Jarāmaraṇasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Aging and Death

114. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 1.0071]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atthi nu kho, bhante, jātassa aññatra jarāmaraṇā”ti? “Natthi kho, mahārāja, jātassa aññatra jarāmaraṇā. Yepi te, mahārāja, khattiyamahāsālā aḍḍhā mahaddhanā mahābhogā pahūtajātarūparajatā [M 1.0071] pahūtavittūpakaraṇā pahūtadhanadhaññā, tesampi jātānaṃ natthi aññatra jarāmaraṇā. Yepi te, mahārāja, brāhmaṇamahāsālā…pe… gahapatimahāsālā aḍḍhā mahaddhanā mahābhogā pahūtajātarūparajatā pahūtavittūpakaraṇā pahūtadhanadhaññā, tesampi jātānaṃ natthi aññatra jarāmaraṇā. Yepi te, mahārāja, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññāvimuttā, tesaṃ pāyaṃ kāyo bhedanadhammo nikkhepanadhammo”ti. Idamavoca…pe…

114. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, for one who is born, is there any escape from aging and death?” “There is no escape from aging and death, Great King, for one who is born. Even those great, wealthy khattiya families—affluent, with great wealth, with great possessions, with abundant gold and silver, with abundant assets and equipment, with abundant money and grain—for them too, being born, there is no escape from aging and death. Even those great, wealthy brahmin families… even those great, wealthy householder families—affluent, with great wealth, with great possessions, with abundant gold and silver, with abundant assets and equipment, with abundant money and grain—for them too, being born, there is no escape from aging and death. Even those bhikkhus, Great King, who are Arahants, whose corruptions are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own welfare, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and are rightly liberated by final knowledge—for them also, this body is of a nature to break up, of a nature to be laid down.”

“Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā,

Atho sarīrampi jaraṃ upeti;

Satañca dhammo na jaraṃ upeti,

Santo have sabbhi pavedayantī”ti.

“Well-adorned royal chariots indeed wear out, and so too the body approaches old age; but the Dhamma of the good does not approach old age; the good, indeed, make this known to the good.”

4. Piyasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Dear Self

115. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 1.0103]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [V 1.0088] – “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘kesaṃ nu kho piyo attā, kesaṃ appiyo attā’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘ye ca kho keci kāyena duccaritaṃ caranti, vācāya duccaritaṃ caranti, manasā duccaritaṃ caranti; tesaṃ appiyo attā’. Kiñcāpi te evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘piyo no attā’ti, atha kho tesaṃ appiyo attā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yañhi appiyo appiyassa [P 1.0072] kareyya, taṃ te attanāva attano karonti; tasmā tesaṃ appiyo attā. Ye ca kho keci kāyena sucaritaṃ caranti, vācāya sucaritaṃ caranti, manasā sucaritaṃ caranti; tesaṃ piyo attā. Kiñcāpi te evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘appiyo no attā’ti; atha kho tesaṃ piyo attā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yañhi piyo piyassa kareyya, taṃ te attanāva attano karonti; tasmā tesaṃ piyo attā”ti.

115. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, here, while I was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in my mind: “To whom is the self dear, and to whom is the self not dear?” Then, Venerable Sir, it occurred to me: “Those who engage in misconduct by body, speech, and mind—to them, the self is not dear.” Even if they were to say, “Our self is dear to us,” still, their self is not dear to them. For what reason? For what an enemy might do to an enemy, that they do to themselves by their own self. Therefore, their self is not dear to them. And those who engage in good conduct by body, speech, and mind—to them, the self is dear. Even if they were to say, “Our self is not dear to us,” still, their self is dear to them. For what reason? For what a friend might do for a friend, that they do to themselves by their own self. Therefore, their self is dear to them.'

“Evametaṃ, mahārāja, evametaṃ, mahārāja! Ye hi keci, mahārāja, kāyena duccaritaṃ caranti, vācāya duccaritaṃ caranti, manasā duccaritaṃ caranti; tesaṃ appiyo attā. Kiñcāpi te evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘piyo no attā’ti, atha kho tesaṃ appiyo attā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yañhi, mahārāja, appiyo appiyassa kareyya, taṃ te attanāva attano karonti; tasmā tesaṃ appiyo attā. Ye ca kho keci, mahārāja[T 1.0104], kāyena [M 1.0072] sucaritaṃ caranti, vācāya sucaritaṃ caranti, manasā sucaritaṃ caranti; tesaṃ piyo attā. Kiñcāpi te evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘appiyo no attā’ti; atha kho tesaṃ piyo attā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yañhi mahārāja, piyo piyassa kareyya, taṃ te attanāva attano karonti; tasmā tesaṃ piyo attā”ti. Idamavoca…pe…

“It is so, Great King! It is so, Great King! Indeed, Great King, those who engage in misconduct by body, speech, and mind—to them, the self is not dear. Even if they were to say, ‘Our self is dear to us,’ still, their self is not dear to them. For what reason? For what an enemy might do to an enemy, Great King, that they do to themselves by their own self. Therefore, their self is not dear to them. And indeed, Great King, those who engage in good conduct by body, speech, and mind—to them, the self is dear. Even if they were to say, ‘Our self is not dear to us,’ still, their self is dear to them. For what reason? For what a friend might do for a friend, Great King, that they do to themselves by their own self. Therefore, their self is dear to them.”

“Attānañce piyaṃ jaññā, na naṃ pāpena saṃyuje;

Na hi taṃ sulabhaṃ hoti, sukhaṃ dukkaṭakārinā.

“If one knows oneself to be dear, one should not associate that self with evil; for happiness is not easily obtained by one who does evil.”

“Antakenādhipannassa, jahato mānusaṃ bhavaṃ;

Kiñhi tassa sakaṃ hoti, kiñca ādāya gacchati;

Kiñcassa anugaṃ hoti, chāyāva anapāyinī anupāyinī (syā. kaṃ. ka.).

“For one overcome by the End-maker, while giving up the human state, what is truly one's own? What does one take when one goes? And what follows one, like a shadow that never departs?”

“Ubho [V 1.0089] puññañca pāpañca, yaṃ macco kurute idha;

Tañhi tassa sakaṃ hoti, tañca taṃva (?) ādāya gacchati;

Tañcassa taṃvassa (?) anugaṃ hoti, chāyāva anapāyinī.

“Both the merit and evil that a mortal does here, that is truly their own; that they take when they go. And that follows them, like a shadow that never departs.”

“Tasmā kareyya kalyāṇaṃ, nicayaṃ samparāyikaṃ;

Puññāni paralokasmiṃ, patiṭṭhā honti pāṇina”nti.

“Therefore, one should do good, as an accumulation for the future life. Merits are the foundation for beings in the next world.”

5. Attarakkhitasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Self-Protection

116. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko [T 1.0105] udapādi – ‘kesaṃ nu kho rakkhito attā, kesaṃ arakkhito attā’ti? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘ye kho keci kāyena duccaritaṃ caranti, vācāya duccaritaṃ caranti, manasā duccaritaṃ caranti; tesaṃ arakkhito attā. Kiñcāpi te hatthikāyo vā rakkheyya, assakāyo vā rakkheyya, rathakāyo vā rakkheyya, pattikāyo [P 1.0073] vā rakkheyya; atha kho tesaṃ arakkhito attā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Bāhirā hesā rakkhā, nesā rakkhā ajjhattikā; tasmā tesaṃ arakkhito attā. Ye ca kho keci kāyena sucaritaṃ caranti, vācāya sucaritaṃ caranti, manasā sucaritaṃ caranti; tesaṃ rakkhito attā. Kiñcāpi te neva hatthikāyo rakkheyya, na assakāyo rakkheyya, na rathakāyo rakkheyya[M 1.0073], na pattikāyo rakkheyya; atha kho tesaṃ rakkhito attā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ajjhattikā hesā rakkhā, nesā rakkhā bāhirā; tasmā tesaṃ rakkhito attā’”ti.

116. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, while I was alone in seclusion, a thought arose in my mind thus: 'For whom is the self protected, and for whom is the self unprotected?' Then, Venerable Sir, it occurred to me: 'Those who engage in misconduct by body, speech, and mind—for them the self is unprotected. Even if they were to be guarded by a corps of elephants, a corps of cavalry, a corps of chariots, or a corps of infantry, still for them the self is unprotected. For what reason? Because that is an external protection, not an internal protection. Therefore, for them the self is unprotected. But those who engage in good conduct by body, speech, and mind—for them the self is protected. Even if they were not to be guarded by a corps of elephants, a corps of cavalry, a corps of chariots, or a corps of infantry, still for them the self is protected. For what reason? Because that is an internal protection, not an external protection. Therefore, for them the self is protected.'"

“Evametaṃ, mahārāja, evametaṃ, mahārāja! Ye hi keci, mahārāja, kāyena duccaritaṃ caranti…pe… tesaṃ arakkhito attā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Bāhirā hesā, mahārāja, rakkhā, nesā rakkhā ajjhattikā; tasmā tesaṃ arakkhito attā. Ye ca kho keci, mahārāja, kāyena sucaritaṃ caranti, vācāya sucaritaṃ caranti, manasā sucaritaṃ caranti; tesaṃ rakkhito attā. Kiñcāpi te neva hatthikāyo rakkheyya, na assakāyo [T 1.0106] rakkheyya, na rathakāyo rakkheyya, na pattikāyo rakkheyya; atha kho tesaṃ rakkhito attā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ajjhattikā [V 1.0090] hesā, mahārāja, rakkhā, nesā rakkhā bāhirā; tasmā tesaṃ rakkhito attā”ti. Idamavoca…pe…

“So it is, Great King, so it is! Great King, for those who engage in misconduct by body... for them the self is unprotected. For what reason? Because that, Great King, is an external protection, not an internal protection. Therefore, for them the self is unprotected. And Great King, for those who engage in good conduct by body, speech, and mind—for them the self is protected. Even if they were not to be guarded by a corps of elephants, a corps of cavalry, a corps of chariots, or a corps of infantry, still for them the self is protected. For what reason? Because that, Great King, is an internal protection, not an external protection. Therefore, for them the self is protected.”

“Kāyena saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu vācāya saṃvaro;

Manasā saṃvaro sādhu, sādhu sabbattha saṃvaro;

Sabbattha saṃvuto lajjī, rakkhitoti pavuccatī”ti.

“Good is restraint by body, good is restraint by speech; good is restraint by mind, good is restraint in all things. One who is restrained in all things, who is conscientious, is said to be ‘protected’.”

6. Appakasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Few

117. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘appakā te sattā lokasmiṃ ye uḷāre uḷāre bhoge labhitvā na ceva majjanti, na ca pamajjanti, na ca kāmesu gedhaṃ āpajjanti, na ca sattesu vippaṭipajjanti. Atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā lokasmiṃ ye uḷāre uḷāre bhoge labhitvā majjanti ceva pamajjanti[P 1.0074], ca kāmesu ca gedhaṃ āpajjanti, sattesu ca vippaṭipajjantī’”ti.

117. At Sāvatthī. King Pasenadi of Kosala, having sat down to one side, said to the Blessed One: ‘Here, venerable sir, while I was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in my mind: “Few are those beings in the world who, having obtained great and abundant wealth, neither become intoxicated, nor heedless, nor fall into greed for sensual pleasures, nor transgress against other beings. But indeed, far more numerous are those beings in the world who, having obtained great and abundant wealth, become intoxicated and heedless, fall into greed for sensual pleasures, and transgress against other beings.”’”

“Evametaṃ, mahārāja, evametaṃ, mahārāja! Appakā te, mahārāja, sattā lokasmiṃ, ye uḷāre uḷāre bhoge labhitvā na ceva majjanti, na ca pamajjanti, na ca kāmesu gedhaṃ āpajjanti, na [T 1.0107] ca sattesu vippaṭipajjanti. Atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā lokasmiṃ, ye uḷāre uḷāre bhoge labhitvā [M 1.0074] majjanti ceva pamajjanti ca kāmesu ca gedhaṃ āpajjanti, sattesu ca vippaṭipajjantī”ti. Idamavoca…pe…

“So it is, great king, so it is, great king! Few are those beings in the world, great king, who, having obtained great and abundant wealth, neither become intoxicated, nor heedless, nor fall into greed for sensual pleasures, nor transgress against other beings. But indeed, far more numerous are those beings in the world who, having obtained great and abundant wealth, become intoxicated and heedless, fall into greed for sensual pleasures, and transgress against other beings.”

“Sārattā kāmabhogesu, giddhā kāmesu mucchitā;

Atisāraṃ na bujjhanti, migā kūṭaṃva oḍḍitaṃ;

Pacchāsaṃ kaṭukaṃ hoti, vipāko hissa pāpako”ti.

“Impassioned for sensual enjoyments, greedy and infatuated with sensual pleasures, they do not realize their transgression, like deer a trap that has been set. Afterwards, it becomes bitter for them, for its result is evil.”

7. Aḍḍakaraṇasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Court of Justice

118. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0091]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idhāhaṃ, bhante, aḍḍakaraṇe atthakaraṇe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nisinno passāmi khattiyamahāsālepi brāhmaṇamahāsālepi gahapatimahāsālepi aḍḍhe mahaddhane mahābhoge pahūtajātarūparajate pahūtavittūpakaraṇe pahūtadhanadhaññe kāmahetu kāmanidānaṃ kāmādhikaraṇaṃ sampajānamusā bhāsante. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘alaṃ dāni me aḍḍakaraṇena, bhadramukho dāni aḍḍakaraṇena paññāyissatī’”ti.

118. At Sāvatthī. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: ‘Here, venerable sir, while sitting in the court of justice, I see great warrior-nobles, great brahmins, and great householders—who are affluent, with great wealth, great possessions, abundant gold and silver, abundant resources and equipment, abundant wealth and grain—knowingly speaking falsehood for the sake of sensual pleasures, because of sensual pleasures, on account of sensual pleasures. Then, venerable sir, it occurred to me: “Enough now with judging for me! Let some fine fellow now be known for judging!”’”

“(Evametaṃ, mahārāja, evametaṃ mahārāja!) ( ) sī. pī. potthakesu natthi Yepi te, mahārāja, khattiyamahāsālā brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatimahāsālā aḍḍhā mahaddhanā mahābhogā pahūtajātarūparajatā pahūtavittūpakaraṇā [T 1.0108] pahūtadhanadhaññā kāmahetu kāmanidānaṃ kāmādhikaraṇaṃ sampajānamusā bhāsanti; tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā”ti. Idamavoca…pe…

“So it is, great king, so it is, great king! Those great warrior-nobles, great brahmins, and great householders who are affluent, with great wealth, great possessions, abundant gold and silver, abundant resources and equipment, abundant wealth and grain, and who knowingly speak falsehood for the sake of sensual pleasures, because of sensual pleasures, on account of sensual pleasures—for them, that will be for their long-term harm and suffering.”

“Sārattā kāmabhogesu, giddhā kāmesu mucchitā;

Atisāraṃ na bujjhanti, macchā khippaṃva oḍḍitaṃ;

Pacchāsaṃ kaṭukaṃ hoti, vipāko hissa pāpako”ti.

“Impassioned for sensual enjoyments, greedy and infatuated with sensual pleasures, they do not realize their transgression, like fish a fish-trap that has been set. Afterwards, it becomes bitter for them, for its result is evil.”

8. Mallikāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse with Mallikā

119. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 1.0075]. Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikāya deviyā saddhiṃ uparipāsādavaragato hoti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikaṃ deviṃ etadavoca – “atthi nu kho te, mallike, kocañño attanā piyataro”ti? “Natthi kho me, mahārāja, kocañño attanā piyataro. Tuyhaṃ pana, mahārāja, atthañño [M 1.0075] koci attanā piyataro”ti? “Mayhampi kho, mallike, natthañño koci attanā piyataro”ti.

119. At Sāvatthī. At that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala had gone up to the best upper palace terrace with Queen Mallikā. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to Queen Mallikā: “Mallikā, is there anyone else dearer to you than yourself?” “No, great king, there is no one else dearer to me than myself. But for you, great king, is there anyone else dearer to you than yourself?” “For me too, Mallikā, there is no one else dearer than myself.”

Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo pāsādā orohitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi [V 1.0092] kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idhāhaṃ, bhante, mallikāya deviyā saddhiṃ uparipāsādavaragato mallikaṃ deviṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘atthi nu kho te, mallike, kocañño [T 1.0109] attanā piyataro’ti? Evaṃ vutte, bhante, mallikā devī maṃ etadavoca – ‘natthi kho me, mahārāja, kocañño attanā piyataro. Tuyhaṃ pana, mahārāja, atthañño koci attanā piyataro’ti? Evaṃ vuttāhaṃ, bhante, mallikaṃ deviṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘mayhampi kho, mallike, natthañño koci attanā piyataro”ti.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, descending from the palace, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Blessed One: “Here, venerable sir, I had gone to the upper palace terrace with Queen Mallikā and said to her: ‘Mallikā, is there anyone dearer to you than yourself?’ When this was said, venerable sir, Queen Mallikā said to me: ‘No, great king, there is no one dearer to me than myself. But, great king, is there anyone dearer to you than yourself?’ When this was said, venerable sir, I said to Queen Mallikā: ‘For me too, Mallikā, there is no one dearer than myself.’”

Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then, the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion recited this verse:

“Sabbā disā anuparigamma cetasā,

Nevajjhagā piyataramattanā kvaci;

Evaṃ piyo puthu attā paresaṃ,

Tasmā na hiṃse paramattakāmo”ti.

“Having traversed all directions with the mind, one finds no one anywhere dearer than oneself. In the same way, the individual self is dear to others. Therefore, one who desires their own welfare should not harm another.”

9. Yaññasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Sacrifice

120. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena rañño pasenadissa kosalassa mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito hoti, pañca ca usabhasatāni pañca ca vacchatarasatāni pañca ca vacchatarisatāni pañca ca [P 1.0076] ajasatāni pañca ca urabbhasatāni thūṇūpanītāni honti yaññatthāya. Yepissa te honti dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā, tepi daṇḍatajjitā bhayatajjitā assumukhā rudamānā parikammāni karonti.

120. At Sāvatthī. At that time, a great sacrifice had been prepared for King Pasenadi of Kosala. Five hundred bulls, five hundred young bullocks, five hundred young heifers, five hundred goats, and five hundred rams had been led to the sacrificial post for the sacrifice. And those who were his slaves, messengers, or workers—they too, threatened by the rod, threatened by fear, with tearful faces and weeping, were performing the preparations.

Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya [T 1.0110] sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisiṃsu. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha, bhante, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito [M 1.0076] hoti, pañca ca usabhasatāni pañca ca vacchatarasatāni pañca ca vacchatarisatāni pañca ca ajasatāni pañca ca urabbhasatāni thūṇūpanītāni honti yaññatthāya[V 1.0093]. Yepissa te honti dāsāti vā pessāti vā kammakarāti vā, tepi daṇḍatajjitā bhayatajjitā assumukhā rudamānā parikammāni karontī”ti.

Then, many monks, having dressed in the morning and taken their bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms. Having wandered for alms in Sāvatthī and returned from their alms-round after the meal, they approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: “Here, venerable sir, a great sacrifice has been prepared for King Pasenadi of Kosala. Five hundred bulls, five hundred young bullocks, five hundred young heifers, five hundred goats, and five hundred rams have been led to the sacrificial post for the sacrifice. And those who are his slaves, messengers, or workers—they too, threatened by the rod, threatened by fear, with tearful faces and weeping, are performing the preparations.”

Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then, the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion recited these verses:

“Assamedhaṃ purisamedhaṃ, sammāpāsaṃ vājapeyyaṃ niraggaḷhaṃ;

Mahāyaññā mahārambhā vājapeyyuṃ; niraggaḷaṃ mahārambhā (ka.), na te honti mahapphalā.

“The horse sacrifice, the human sacrifice, the sammāpāsa sacrifice, the vājapeyya sacrifice, and the niraggaḷa sacrifice—these great sacrifices of great undertaking are not of great fruit.

“Ajeḷakā ca gāvo ca, vividhā yattha haññare;

Na taṃ sammaggatā yaññaṃ, upayanti mahesino.

“Where various goats, sheep, and cattle are slain, the great sages who have gone rightly do not approach that sacrifice.

“Ye ca yaññā nirārambhā, yajanti anukulaṃ sadā;

Ajeḷakā ca gāvo ca, vividhā nettha haññare;

Etaṃ [T 1.0111] sammaggatā yaññaṃ, upayanti mahesino.

“But those sacrifices without undertaking, traditionally performed, where no various goats, sheep, or cattle are slain—the great sages who have gone rightly approach that sacrifice.

“Etaṃ yajetha medhāvī, eso yañño mahapphalo;

Etañhi yajamānassa, seyyo hoti na pāpiyo;

Yañño ca vipulo hoti, pasīdanti ca devatā”ti.

“The wise should offer this sacrifice; this sacrifice is of great fruit. For the one who sacrifices thus, it is better, not worse. The sacrifice is abundant, and the deities are pleased.”

10. Bandhanasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Bondage

121. Tena kho pana samayena raññā pasenadinā kosalena mahājanakāyo bandhāpito hoti, appekacce rajjūhi appekacce andūhi appekacce saṅkhalikāhi.

121. Now at that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala had a great multitude of people bound; some with ropes, some with shackles, and some with chains.

Atha [P 1.0077] kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisiṃsu. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha, bhante, raññā pasenadinā kosalena mahājanakāyo [V 1.0094] bandhāpito, appekacce rajjūhi appekacce andūhi appekacce saṅkhalikāhī”ti.

Then, many monks, having dressed in the morning and taken their bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms. Having gone for alms in Sāvatthī and returned from the alms-round after the meal, they approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, here King Pasenadi of Kosala has had a great multitude of people bound; some with ropes, some with shackles, and some with chains.'

Atha [M 1.0077] kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered these verses:

“Na [T 1.0112] taṃ daḷhaṃ bandhanamāhu dhīrā,

Yadāyasaṃ dārujaṃ pabbajañca;

Sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu,

Puttesu dāresu ca yā apekkhā.

“The wise do not call that a strong bond which is made of iron, wood, or of fiber. But that passionate attachment to jeweled earrings, and the longing for children and wives—

“Etaṃ daḷhaṃ bandhanamāhu dhīrā,

Ohārinaṃ sithilaṃ duppamuñcaṃ;

Etampi chetvāna paribbajanti,

Anapekkhino kāmasukhaṃ pahāyā”ti.

“This, the wise call a strong bond—one that is dragging down, pliant, and hard to release. Having cut even this, they wander forth without longing, having abandoned the pleasure of sensual desires.”

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Daharo puriso jarā, piyaṃ attānarakkhito;

Appakā aḍḍakaraṇaṃ, mallikā yaññabandhananti.

Young, Man, Old Age, Dear, Self-Protected; Few, Making Half, Mallikā, Sacrifice, and Bondage.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Sattajaṭilasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Seven Matted-Hair Ascetics

122. Ekaṃ [T 1.0113] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bahidvārakoṭṭhake nisinno hoti. Atha [V 1.0095] kho rājā pasenadi kosalo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.

122. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park, Migāramātā’s Palace. Then, in the evening, the Blessed One rose from seclusion and sat by the outer gatehouse. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side.

Tena [P 1.0078] kho pana samayena satta ca jaṭilā satta ca nigaṇṭhā satta ca acelakā satta ca ekasāṭakā satta ca paribbājakā parūḷhakacchanakhalomā khārivividhamādāya khārividhaṃ ādāya (pī.) dī. ni. 1.280 tadaṭṭhakathāpi oloketabbā bhagavato avidūre atikkamanti. Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dakkhiṇajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ [M 1.0078] pathaviyaṃ nihantvā yena te satta ca jaṭilā satta ca nigaṇṭhā satta ca acelakā satta ca ekasāṭakā satta ca paribbājakā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ nāmaṃ sāvesi – “rājāhaṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo…pe… rājāhaṃ, bhante, pasenadi kosalo”ti.

At that time, seven matted-hair ascetics, seven Nigaṇṭhas, seven naked ascetics, seven single-robed ascetics, and seven wanderers—with overgrown armpit-hair, nails, and body-hair, carrying the various paraphernalia of ascetics—were passing by not far from the Blessed One. Then King Pasenadi of Kosala rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and extending his joined hands toward those seven matted-hair ascetics, seven Nigaṇṭhas, seven naked ascetics, seven single-robed ascetics, and seven wanderers, announced his name three times: 'Venerable sirs, I am King Pasenadi of Kosala… Venerable sirs, I am King Pasenadi of Kosala.'

Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo acirapakkantesu tesu [T 1.0114] sattasu ca jaṭilesu sattasu ca nigaṇṭhesu sattasu ca acelakesu sattasu ca ekasāṭakesu sattasu ca paribbājakesu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ye te, bhante, loke arahanto vā arahattamaggaṃ vā samāpannā ete tesaṃ aññatarā”ti.

Not long after those seven matted-hair ascetics, seven Nigaṇṭhas, seven naked ascetics, seven single-robed ascetics, and seven wanderers had departed, King Pasenadi of Kosala approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, of those in the world who are arahants or are entered upon the path to arahantship, are these some of them?'

“Dujjānaṃ kho etaṃ, mahārāja, tayā gihinā kāmabhoginā puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvasantena kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhontena mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhārayantena jātarūparajataṃ sādiyantena – ‘ime vā arahanto, ime vā arahattamaggaṃ samāpannā’”ti.

“Great king, it is difficult for you, a householder enjoying sensual pleasures, dwelling in a house crowded with children, enjoying Kāsi sandalwood, wearing garlands, perfumes, and cosmetics, delighting in gold and silver, to know: ‘These are arahants,’ or ‘These have entered upon the path to arahantship.’”

“Saṃvāsena kho, mahārāja, sīlaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṃ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena. Saṃvohārena kho, mahārāja, soceyyaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṃ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena. Āpadāsu kho, mahārāja, thāmo veditabbo. So ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṃ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena. Sākacchāya[P 1.0079], kho, mahārāja, paññā veditabbā. Sā ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṃ; manasikarotā, no [T 1.0115] amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā”ti.

“Great king, virtue is to be known by living together, and that over a long time, not a short time; by one who is attentive, not inattentive; by one who is wise, not unwise. Great king, purity is to be known through interaction, and that over a long time, not a short time; by one who is attentive, not inattentive; by one who is wise, not unwise. Great king, fortitude is to be known in adversity, and that over a long time, not a short time; by one who is attentive, not inattentive; by one who is wise, not unwise. Great king, wisdom is to be known by discussion, and that over a long time, not a short time; by one who is attentive, not inattentive; by one who is wise, not unwise.”

“Acchariyaṃ[V 1.0096], bhante, abbhutaṃ bhante! Yāva subhāsitamidaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā – ‘dujjānaṃ kho etaṃ, mahārāja, tayā gihinā kāmabhoginā puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvasantena kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhontena mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhārayantena jātarūparajataṃ sādiyantena – ime vā arahanto, ime vā arahattamaggaṃ samāpannā’ti. Saṃvāsena kho, mahārāja, sīlaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṃ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena. Saṃvohārena kho mahārāja[M 1.0079], soceyyaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṃ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena. Āpadāsu kho, mahārāja, thāmo veditabbo. So ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṃ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena. Sākacchāya kho, mahārāja, paññā veditabbā. Sā ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṃ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā”ti.

“Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Astonishing, Venerable Sir! How well this has been spoken by the Blessed One: ‘Great king, it is difficult for you, a householder enjoying sensual pleasures, dwelling in a house crowded with children, enjoying Kāsi sandalwood, wearing garlands, perfumes, and cosmetics, delighting in gold and silver, to know: “These are arahants,” or “These have entered upon the path to arahantship.” Great king, virtue is to be known by living together, and that over a long time, not a short time; by one who is attentive, not inattentive; by one who is wise, not unwise. Great king, purity is to be known through interaction, and that over a long time, not a short time; by one who is attentive, not inattentive; by one who is wise, not unwise. Great king, fortitude is to be known in adversity, and that over a long time, not a short time; by one who is attentive, not inattentive; by one who is wise, not unwise. Great king, wisdom is to be known by discussion, and that over a long time, not a short time; by one who is attentive, not inattentive; by one who is wise, not unwise.’”

“Ete, bhante, mama purisā carā ocarakā janapadaṃ ocaritvā āgacchanti. Tehi paṭhamaṃ ociṇṇaṃ ahaṃ pacchā osāpayissāmi oyāyissāmi (sī.), ohayissāmi (syā. kaṃ.). Idāni te, bhante, taṃ rajojallaṃ pavāhetvā sunhātā suvilittā kappitakesamassū odātavatthā odātavatthavasanā (sī.) pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricāressantī”ti.

“Venerable sir, these men of mine are spies, scouts who reconnoiter the countryside and then return. What they have first investigated, I will subsequently bring to a conclusion. Now, venerable sir, having washed off that dust and dirt, being well-bathed, well-anointed, with hair and beards trimmed, and wearing white garments, they will live in splendor, provided and endowed with the five strands of sensual pleasure.”

Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

Then, the Blessed One, having understood the significance of this matter, on that occasion recited these verses:

“Na vaṇṇarūpena naro sujāno,

Na vissase ittaradassanena;

Susaññatānañhi viyañjanena,

Asaññatā lokamimaṃ caranti.

“A person is not easily known by their appearance and form, nor should one place trust in a brief sighting. For in this world, the unrestrained move about in the guise of the well-restrained.”

“Patirūpako mattikākuṇḍalova,

Lohaḍḍhamāsova suvaṇṇachanno;

Caranti [T 1.0116] loke eke (sī. pī.) parivārachannā,

Anto asuddhā bahi sobhamānā”ti.

“Like a counterfeit earring made of clay, or a half-māsa of bronze covered with gold, they move about in the world concealed by their retinue—impure within, but shining externally.”

2. Pañcarājasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Five Kings

123. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0097]. Tena kho pana samayena pañcannaṃ rājūnaṃ pasenadipamukhānaṃ pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitānaṃ samaṅgībhūtānaṃ paricārayamānānaṃ ayamantarākathā udapādi – “kiṃ nu kho kāmānaṃ agga”nti? Tatrekacce tatreke (sī. pī.) evamāhaṃsu – “rūpā kāmānaṃ agga”nti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu [M 1.0080] – “saddā kāmānaṃ agga”nti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “gandhā kāmānaṃ agga”nti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “rasā kāmānaṃ agga”nti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu [P 1.0080] – “phoṭṭhabbā kāmānaṃ agga”nti. Yato kho te rājāno nāsakkhiṃsu aññamaññaṃ saññāpetuṃ.

123. At Sāvatthī.
