There I saw a great mountain, as high as the clouds, advancing and crushing all living beings to powder. Whatever is to be done by you, great king, do it.’ When such a great and terrible danger has arisen for you, great king, a cruel destruction of human life, with human existence being so difficult to obtain, what is there to be done?”

“Evarūpe me, bhante, mahati mahabbhaye samuppanne dāruṇe manussakkhaye dullabhe manussatte kimassa karaṇīyaṃ aññatra dhammacariyāya aññatra samacariyāya aññatra kusalakiriyāya aññatra puññakiriyāyā”ti?

“Venerable sir, when such a great and terrible danger has arisen for me, a cruel destruction of human life, with human existence being so difficult to obtain, what is there to be done other than practicing the Dhamma, other than righteous conduct, other than wholesome action, other than meritorious action?”

“Ārocemi kho te, mahārāja, paṭivedemi kho te, mahārāja, adhivattati kho taṃ, mahārāja, jarāmaraṇaṃ. Adhivattamāne ce te, mahārāja, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīya”nti? “Adhivattamāne ca me, bhante, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṃ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāya? Yāni tāni, bhante, raññaṃ khattiyānaṃ muddhāvasittānaṃ issariyamadamattānaṃ [M 1.0102] kāmagedhapariyuṭṭhitānaṃ janapadatthāvariyappattānaṃ mahantaṃ pathavimaṇḍalaṃ abhivijiya ajjhāvasantānaṃ hatthiyuddhāni bhavanti; tesampi, bhante, hatthiyuddhānaṃ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe. Yānipi tāni, bhante, raññaṃ khattiyānaṃ muddhāvasittānaṃ…pe… ajjhāvasantānaṃ assayuddhāni bhavanti…pe… rathayuddhāni bhavanti [T 1.0148] …pe… pattiyuddhāni bhavanti; tesampi[P 1.0102], bhante, pattiyuddhānaṃ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe. Santi kho pana, bhante, imasmiṃ rājakule mantino mahāmattā, ye pahonti yesaṃ honti (ka.) āgate paccatthike mantehi bhedayituṃ. Tesampi, bhante, mantayuddhānaṃ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe. Saṃvijjati kho pana, bhante, imasmiṃ rājakule pahūtaṃ hiraññasuvaṇṇaṃ bhūmigatañceva vehāsaṭṭhañca, yena mayaṃ pahoma āgate paccatthike dhanena upalāpetuṃ. Tesampi, bhante, dhanayuddhānaṃ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe. Adhivattamāne ca me, bhante, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṃ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāyā”ti?

“I declare to you, great king, I make it known to you, great king: aging and death are overwhelming you. When aging and death are overwhelming you, great king, what is there to be done?” “Venerable sir, when aging and death are overwhelming me, what is there to be done other than practicing the Dhamma, righteous conduct, wholesome action, and meritorious action? Venerable sir, there are the elephant battles of kings—anointed kṣatriyas, intoxicated with the pride of sovereignty, overcome by attachment to sensual pleasures, having attained stability in their country, and dwelling having conquered a great sphere of the earth; but for them, venerable sir, in those elephant battles, there is no recourse, no scope, when aging and death are overwhelming. Venerable sir, there are the cavalry battles… chariot battles… infantry battles of kings—anointed kṣatriyas… dwelling having conquered a great sphere of the earth; but for them, venerable sir, in those infantry battles, there is no recourse, no scope, when aging and death are overwhelming. Furthermore, venerable sir, in this royal family there are counselors and great ministers who are able to shatter approaching enemies with their strategies; but for them, venerable sir, in those battles of strategy, there is no recourse, no scope, when aging and death are overwhelming. Furthermore, venerable sir, in this royal family there is abundant gold and silver, both buried in the earth and stored in the air, with which we are able to entice approaching enemies; but for them, venerable sir, in those battles of wealth, there is no recourse, no scope, when aging and death are overwhelming. Venerable sir, when aging and death are overwhelming me, what is there to be done other than practicing the Dhamma, righteous conduct, wholesome action, and meritorious action?”

“Evametaṃ, mahārāja, evametaṃ, mahārāja! Adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṃ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāyā”ti? Idamavoca bhagavā…pe… satthā –

“So it is, great king, so it is! When aging and death are overwhelming, what is there to be done other than practicing the Dhamma, righteous conduct, wholesome action, and meritorious action?” This the Blessed One said… the Teacher:

“Yathāpi [V 1.0121] selā vipulā, nabhaṃ āhacca pabbatā;

Samantānupariyāyeyyuṃ, nippothento catuddisā.

“Just as massive, rocky mountains, reaching to the sky, might roll in from all around, from the four directions, crushing all to powder;

“Evaṃ jarā ca maccu ca, adhivattanti pāṇine pāṇino (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.);

Khattiye brāhmaṇe vesse, sudde caṇḍālapukkuse;

Na [T 1.0149] kiñci na kañci (?) parivajjeti, sabbamevābhimaddati.

So too do aging and death overwhelm living beings: kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, caṇḍālas, and pukkusas. They do not spare anything; they crush all.

“Na tattha hatthīnaṃ bhūmi, na rathānaṃ na pattiyā;

Na cāpi mantayuddhena, sakkā jetuṃ dhanena vā.

There, it is not the domain of elephants, nor of chariots, nor of infantry; nor is it possible to conquer by battles of strategy or by wealth.

“Tasmā hi paṇḍito poso, sampassaṃ atthamattano;

Buddhe dhamme ca saṅghe ca, dhīro saddhaṃ nivesaye.

Therefore, a wise and steadfast person, clearly seeing their own welfare, should establish faith in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha.

“Yo [M 1.0103] dhammaṃ cari dhammacārī (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kāyena, vācāya uda cetasā;

Idheva naṃ pasaṃsanti, pecca sagge pamodatī”ti.

One who practices the Dhamma by body, by speech, or by mind—they are praised right here in this life, and after death, they rejoice in heaven.”

Tatiyo vaggo.

The Third Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Puggalo ayyikā loko, issattaṃ issatthaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.) pabbatūpamā;

Desitaṃ buddhaseṭṭhena, imaṃ kosalapañcakanti.

Person, Grandmother, World, Archery, and Simile of the Mountain; this Kosala pentad was taught by the Best of Buddhas.

Kosalasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Kosala Saṃyutta is concluded.

4. Mārasaṃyuttaṃ

4. The Māra Saṃyutta

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Tapokammasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Practice of Austerity

137. Evaṃ [T 1.0150][V 1.0122][P 1.0103][M 1.0104] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “mutto vatamhi tāya dukkarakārikāya. Sādhu mutto vatamhi tāya anatthasaṃhitāya dukkarakārikāya. Sādhu vatamhi mutto bodhiṃ samajjhaga”nti sādhu ṭhito sato bodhiṃ samajjheganti (sī. pī.), sādhu vatamhi satto bodhisamajjhagūti (syā. kaṃ.).

137. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the Nerañjarā River, at the foot of the Goatherd's Banyan Tree, having just attained full awakening. Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind: “Indeed, I am freed from that arduous practice. It is good indeed that I am freed from that arduous practice which is not connected with benefit. It is good indeed that I am freed and have attained awakening!”

Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then Māra the Evil One, having known with his own mind the reflection in the Blessed One's mind, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Tapokammā apakkamma, yena na sujjhanti māṇavā;

Asuddho maññasi suddho, suddhimaggā aparaddho” suddhimaggamaparaddho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ti.

“Having turned away from the practice of austerity, by which youths are not purified, you, being impure, think yourself pure; you have strayed from the path of purity.”

Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, knowing, “This is Māra the Evil One,” addressed Māra the Evil One in verses:

“Anatthasaṃhitaṃ [T 1.0151] ñatvā, yaṃ kiñci amaraṃ tapaṃ aparaṃ tapaṃ (ka.);

Sabbaṃ natthāvahaṃ hoti, phiyārittaṃva dhammani vammani (sī.), dhammaniṃ (pī.), jammaniṃ (ka.) etthāyaṃ dhammasaddo sakkate dhanvanaṃ-saddena sadiso maruvācakoti veditabbo, yathā daḷhadhammātipadaṃ.

“Having realized that any ascetic practice for immortality is unconnected with benefit and entirely without advantage—like a useless oar on dry land—

“Sīlaṃ samādhi paññañca, maggaṃ bodhāya bhāvayaṃ;

Pattosmi paramaṃ suddhiṃ, nihato tvamasi antakā”ti.

“Developing virtue, concentration, and wisdom—the path to awakening—I have attained the supreme purity. You are defeated, O End-maker!”

Atha [V 1.0123] kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti, dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The Blessed One knows me, the Well-Gone One knows me,” grieved and dejected, vanished right there.

2. Hatthirājavaṇṇasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Appearance of an Elephant King

138. Evaṃ [M 1.0105] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho[P 1.0104]. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṃ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṃ phusāyati. Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo mahantaṃ hatthirājavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Seyyathāpi nāma mahāariṭṭhako maṇi, evamassa sīsaṃ hoti. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ rūpiyaṃ, evamassa dantā honti. Seyyathāpi nāma mahatī naṅgalīsā naṅgalasīsā (pī. ka.), evamassa soṇḍo hoti. Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

138. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the Nerañjarā River, at the foot of the Goatherd's Banyan Tree, having just attained full awakening. At that time, the Blessed One was sitting in the open air in the pitch-black darkness of night, and it was drizzling drop by drop. Then Māra the Evil One, wishing to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the Blessed One, created the appearance of a great elephant king and approached the Blessed One. Its head was like a great black gem; its tusks were like pure silver; and its trunk was like a great plow-pole. Then the Blessed One, knowing, “This is Māra the Evil One,” addressed Māra the Evil One in verse:

“Saṃsaraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ, vaṇṇaṃ katvā subhāsubhaṃ;

Alaṃ te tena pāpima, nihato tvamasi antakā”ti.

“Having wandered for a long time, creating appearances fair and foul, enough of that for you, O Evil One! You are defeated, O End-maker!”

Atha [T 1.0152] kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, "The Blessed One knows me, the Well-Gone One knows me," grieved and dejected, vanished right there.

3. Subhasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Beautiful

139. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṃ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṃ phusāyati. Atha kho māro pāpimā, bhagavato bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato avidūre uccāvacā vaṇṇanibhā upadaṃseti, subhā ceva asubhā ca. Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

139. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā, on the bank of the Nerañjarā River, at the foot of the Goatherd's Banyan Tree, having just attained supreme enlightenment. Now at that time the Blessed One was sitting in the open air in the pitch darkness of night, and it was drizzling drop by drop. Then Māra the Evil One, wishing to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the Blessed One, approached him. Having approached, not far from the Blessed One, he manifested various forms, both beautiful and ugly. Then the Blessed One, knowing, "This is Māra the Evil One," addressed Māra the Evil One in verses:

“Saṃsaraṃ [V 1.0124] dīghamaddhānaṃ, vaṇṇaṃ katvā subhāsubhaṃ;

Alaṃ te tena pāpima, nihato tvamasi antaka.

“Having wandered for a long time, fashioning forms both beautiful and ugly; enough of that for you, Evil One. You are defeated, End-maker.

“Ye [M 1.0106] ca kāyena vācāya, manasā ca susaṃvutā;

Na te māravasānugā, na te mārassa baddhagū” baddhabhū (ka.), paccagū (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ti.

“Those who are well-restrained in body, speech, and mind—they do not fall under Māra's sway, they are not Māra's followers.”

Atha kho māro…pe… tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra… and so on… vanished right there.

4. Paṭhamamārapāsasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse on Māra's Snare

140. Evaṃ [P 1.0105] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti [T 1.0153] te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

140. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks!” “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Mayhaṃ kho, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā yoniso sammappadhānā anuttarā vimutti anuppattā, anuttarā vimutti sacchikatā. Tumhepi, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā yoniso sammappadhānā anuttaraṃ vimuttiṃ anupāpuṇātha, anuttaraṃ vimuttiṃ sacchikarothā”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

“Monks, it is through my wise attention and wise right striving that unsurpassed liberation has been attained, that unsurpassed liberation has been realized. You too, monks, through wise attention and wise right striving, should attain unsurpassed liberation, should realize unsurpassed liberation.” Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Baddhosi mārapāsena, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā;

Mārabandhanabaddhosi, na me samaṇa mokkhasī”ti.

“You are bound by the snare of Māra, both the divine and the human. You are bound by Māra’s bond; you will not escape me, ascetic.”

“Muttāhaṃ muttohaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) mārapāsena, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā;

Mārabandhanamuttomhi, nihato tvamasi antakā”ti.

“I am freed from the snare of Māra, both the divine and the human; I am released from Māra’s bond. You are defeated, O End-maker!”

Atha kho māro pāpimā…pe… tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One… and so on… vanished right there.

5. Dutiyamārapāsasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on Māra's Snare

141. Ekaṃ [V 1.0125] samayaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

141. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: "Monks!" "Venerable sir," those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Muttāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbapāsehi ye dibbā ye ca mānusā. Tumhepi, bhikkhave, muttā sabbapāsehi ye dibbā ye ca mānusā. Caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya [T 1.0154] sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Mā ekena dve agamittha. Desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ [M 1.0107] kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa [P 1.0106] parihāyanti. Bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro. Ahampi, bhikkhave, yena uruvelā senānigamo tenupasaṅkamissāmi dhammadesanāyā”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

"I am freed, monks, from all snares, both those that are divine and those that are human. You too, monks, are freed from all snares, both those that are divine and those that are human. Go forth, monks, on tour for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. Let not two go by one path. Teach, monks, the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and its phrasing. Proclaim the holy life, which is utterly complete and pure. There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are declining through not hearing the Dhamma. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma. I too, monks, will go to Uruvelā, to the market town of Senā, to teach the Dhamma." Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Baddhosi sabbapāsehi, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā;

Mahābandhanabaddhosi, na me samaṇa mokkhasī”ti.

"You are bound by all snares, both those that are divine and those that are human. You are bound by the great bond; you will not escape me, ascetic!"

“Muttāhaṃ sabbapāsehi, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā;

Mahābandhanamuttomhi, nihato tvamasi antakā”ti.

"I am freed from all snares, both those that are divine and those that are human. I am freed from the great bond; you are defeated, O End-maker!"

Atha kho māro pāpimā…pe… tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One… and so on… vanished right there.

6. Sappasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Serpent

142. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṃ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṃ phusāyati.

142. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. Now at that time, the Blessed One was sitting in the open during a dark, gloomy night, and the sky was drizzling drop by drop.

Atha [T 1.0155][V 1.0126] kho māro pāpimā bhagavato bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo mahantaṃ sapparājavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Seyyathāpi nāma mahatī ekarukkhikā nāvā, evamassa kāyo hoti. Seyyathāpi nāma mahantaṃ soṇḍikākiḷañjaṃ, evamassa phaṇo hoti. Seyyathāpi nāma mahatī kosalikā kaṃsapāti, evamassa akkhīni bhavanti. Seyyathāpi nāma deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatā niccharanti, evamassa mukhato jivhā niccharati. Seyyathāpi nāma kammāragaggariyā dhamamānāya saddo hoti, evamassa assāsapassāsānaṃ saddo hoti.

Then Māra the Evil One, wishing to arouse fear, stiffness, and hair-raising terror in the Blessed One, created the form of a great serpent king and approached the Blessed One. His body was like a great boat hollowed from a single tree. His hood was like a large distiller's mat. His eyes were like great Kosalan bronze bowls. From his mouth, his tongue darted forth like flashes of lightning when the sky thunders. The sound of his in-breaths and out-breaths was like the sound of a smith's bellows being blown.

Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, having known, "This is Māra the Evil One," addressed Māra the Evil One with verses:

“Yo suññagehāni sevati,

Seyyo so muni attasaññato;

Vossajja careyya tattha so,

Patirūpañhi tathāvidhassa taṃ.

"The sage who resorts to empty dwellings, that sage is self-restrained. Having relinquished attachment, he should sojourn there. Indeed, that is fitting for one such as he.

“Carakā [M 1.0108] bahū bheravā bahū,

Atho ḍaṃsasarīsapā ḍaṃsa siriṃsapā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bahū;

Lomampi [P 1.0107] na tattha iñjaye,

Suññāgāragato mahāmuni.

"Many are the wandering creatures, many are the terrors; furthermore, many are the biting and crawling creatures. The great sage who has gone to an empty dwelling should not stir even a hair there.

“Nabhaṃ [T 1.0156] phaleyya pathavī caleyya,

Sabbepi pāṇā uda santaseyyuṃ;

Sallampi ce urasi pakappayeyyuṃ,

Upadhīsu tāṇaṃ na karonti buddhā”ti.

"Though the sky should split, the earth should quake, and all beings should be terrified; even if a spear were to be thrust into their chest, the Buddhas do not make a refuge in the substrates of existence."

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The Blessed One knows me, the Sugata knows me,” grieved and sad-minded, vanished right there.

7. Supatisuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Sleeping Well

143. Ekaṃ [V 1.0127] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho bhagavā bahudevarattiṃ abbhokāse caṅkamitvā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ pāde pakkhāletvā vihāraṃ pavisitvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

143. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground. Then the Blessed One, having spent much of the night walking back and forth in the open, at the break of dawn washed his feet and entered the dwelling. He lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, with one foot placed upon the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having established in his mind the perception of rising. Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kiṃ soppasi kiṃ nu soppasi,

Kimidaṃ soppasi dubbhago dubbhato (syā. kaṃ.), dubbhayo (pī.) viya;

Suññamagāranti soppasi,

Kimidaṃ soppasi sūriye uggate”ti.

“Why do you sleep? For what reason do you sleep? What is this, sleeping like an unfortunate one? Do you sleep thinking, ‘A secluded dwelling has been found’? What is this, sleeping when the sun has risen?”

“Yassa [T 1.0157] jālinī visattikā,

Taṇhā natthi kuhiñci netave;

Sabbūpadhiparikkhayā buddho,

Soppati kiṃ tavettha mārā”ti.

“For whom the ensnaring, clinging craving exists not to lead to any state of being; that Buddha, through the complete destruction of all substrates of existence, sleeps. Māra, what concern is that of yours?”

Atha kho māro pāpimā…pe… tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One… and so on… vanished right there.

8. Nandatisuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Delight

144. Evaṃ [M 1.0109] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

144. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Nandati puttehi puttimā, gomā gobhi tatheva nandati;

Upadhīhi [P 1.0108] narassa nandanā, na hi so nandati yo nirūpadhī”ti.

“One who has sons delights in his sons; one who has cattle likewise delights in his cattle. A person’s delight is in the substrates of existence; but he who is without substrates does not delight.”

“Socati [V 1.0128] puttehi puttimā, gomā gobhi tatheva socati;

Upadhīhi narassa socanā, na hi so socati yo nirūpadhī”ti.

“One who has sons grieves on account of his sons; one who has cattle likewise grieves on account of his cattle. A person’s sorrow is on account of the substrates of existence; but he who is without substrates does not grieve.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The Blessed One knows me, the Well-Farer knows me,” distressed and dejected, vanished right there.

9. Paṭhamaāyusuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on the Lifespan

145. Evaṃ [T 1.0158] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

145. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks!” “Venerable sir,” those monks responded to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Appamidaṃ, bhikkhave, manussānaṃ āyu. Gamanīyo samparāyo, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ. Natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yo, bhikkhave, ciraṃ jīvati, so vassasataṃ appaṃ vā bhiyyo”ti.

“Monks, this lifespan of humans is short. The future life must be journeyed to; the wholesome should be done; the holy life should be lived. For one who is born, there is no immortality. Monks, whoever lives long lives for a hundred years, or a little more or less.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Dīghamāyu manussānaṃ, na naṃ hīḷe suporiso;

Careyya khīramattova, natthi maccussa āgamo”ti.

“Long is the lifespan of humans; a good person should not disdain it. One should live like a milk-fed infant; there is no coming of death.”

“Appamāyu manussānaṃ, hīḷeyya naṃ suporiso;

Careyyādittasīsova, natthi maccussa nāgamo”ti.

“Short is the lifespan of humans; a good person should disdain it. One should live as if one’s head were on fire; there is no non-coming of death.”

Atha kho māro…pe… tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra… and so on… vanished right there.

10. Dutiyaāyusuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on the Lifespan

146. Evaṃ [V 1.0129][M 1.0110] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tatra kho bhagavā…pe… etadavoca –

146. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground. There the Blessed One… and so on… said this:

“Appamidaṃ, bhikkhave, manussānaṃ āyu. Gamanīyo samparāyo, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ. Natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yo, bhikkhave, ciraṃ jīvati, so vassasataṃ appaṃ vā bhiyyo”ti.

“Monks, this lifespan of humans is short. The future life must be journeyed to; the wholesome should be done; the holy life should be lived. For one who is born, there is no immortality. Monks, whoever lives long lives for a hundred years, or a little more or less.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [T 1.0159] bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Nāccayanti [P 1.0109] ahorattā, jīvitaṃ nūparujjhati;

Āyu anupariyāyati, maccānaṃ nemīva rathakubbara”nti.

“Days and nights do not pass by, life does not cease; the life of mortals follows along, like the rim of a chariot wheel follows the chariot-pole.”

“Accayanti ahorattā, jīvitaṃ uparujjhati;

Āyu khīyati maccānaṃ, kunnadīnaṃva odaka”nti.

“Days and nights pass by, life ceases; the life of mortals is exhausted, like the water of small rivers.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, ‘The Blessed One knows me, the Well-Farer knows me,’ afflicted and displeased, vanished right there.

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this chapter:

Tapokammañca nāgo ca, subhaṃ pāsena te duve;

Sappo supati nandanaṃ, āyunā apare duveti.

Austerity and the Elephant, Subha and Pāsa; the Snake, Supati, and Nandana, and two others on the Lifespan.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Pāsāṇasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Boulder

147. Ekaṃ [T 1.0160][V 1.0130] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṃ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṃ phusāyati. Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo yena bhagavā [M 1.0111] tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato avidūre mahante pāsāṇe padālesi.

147. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on Vulture Peak Mountain. Now at that time the Blessed One was sitting in the open air in the pitch darkness of night, and it was drizzling drop by drop. Then Māra the Evil One, wishing to arouse fear, terror, and hair-raising horror in the Blessed One, approached the Blessed One; having approached, not far from the Blessed One, he shattered huge boulders.

Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, knowing, “This is Māra the Evil One,” addressed Māra the Evil One with a verse:

“Sacepi kevalaṃ sabbaṃ, gijjhakūṭaṃ calessasi gaḷeyyasi (syā. kaṃ.), caleyyāsi (ka.);

Neva sammāvimuttānaṃ, buddhānaṃ atthi iñjita”nti.

“Even if you were to shake this entire Vulture Peak, for the Buddhas who are rightly liberated, there is no trembling.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, ‘The Blessed One knows me, the Well-Farer knows me,’ afflicted and displeased, vanished right there.

2. Kinnusīhasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on ‘Why Like a Lion?’

148. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa [T 1.0161] ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṃ deseti.

148. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time the Blessed One was teaching the Dhamma, surrounded by a great assembly.

Atha [P 1.0110] kho mārassa pāpimato etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṃ deseti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṃ vicakkhukammāyā”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then this thought occurred to Māra the Evil One: ‘This recluse Gotama is teaching the Dhamma surrounded by a great assembly. Why don’t I approach the recluse Gotama to destroy their vision?’ Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kinnu [V 1.0131] sīhova nadasi, parisāyaṃ visārado;

Paṭimallo hi te atthi, vijitāvī nu maññasī”ti.

“Why do you roar like a lion, bold in the assembly? Is there any rival to you? Or do you consider yourself victorious?”

“Nadanti ve mahāvīrā, parisāsu visāradā;

Tathāgatā balappattā, tiṇṇā loke visattika”nti.

“Indeed, the great heroes roar, bold in the assemblies. The Tathāgatas have attained the powers; they have crossed beyond attachment in the world.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, ‘The Blessed One knows me, the Well-Farer knows me,’ afflicted and displeased, vanished right there.

3. Sakalikasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Stone Splinter

149. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati maddakucchismiṃ migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavato pādo sakalikāya [M 1.0112] khato hoti, bhusā sudaṃ bhagavato vedanā vattanti sārīrikā dukkhā tibbā kharā kaṭukā asātā amanāpā. Tā sudaṃ bhagavā sato sampajāno adhivāseti avihaññamāno. Atha kho bhagavā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi [T 1.0162] pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

149. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi Deer Park. At that time, the Blessed One's foot had been struck by a stone splinter. Indeed, severe feelings arose for the Blessed One—bodily feelings that were painful, intense, harsh, sharp, unpleasant, and disagreeable. Indeed, the Blessed One endured them, being mindful and clearly comprehending, without being afflicted. Then the Blessed One, having spread his four-layered outer robe, adopted the lion's posture on his right side, placing one foot over the other, mindful and clearly comprehending. Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Mandiyā nu kho sesi udāhu kāveyyamatto,

Atthā nu te sampacurā na santi;

Eko vivitte sayanāsanamhi,

Niddāmukho kimidaṃ soppase vā”ti.

“Do you sleep out of sluggishness, or are you intoxicated with composing poetry? Are there not many goals for you to attain? Alone in a secluded resting place, with a face inclined to sleep, why do you indulge in this sleep?”

“Na mandiyā sayāmi nāpi kāveyyamatto,

Atthaṃ sameccāhamapetasoko;

Eko vivitte sayanāsanamhi,

Sayāmahaṃ sabbabhūtānukampī.

“I do not sleep out of sluggishness, nor am I intoxicated with composing poetry; having attained the goal, I am without sorrow. Alone in a secluded resting place, I sleep, having compassion for all beings.

“Yesampi sallaṃ urasi paviṭṭhaṃ,

Muhuṃ muhuṃ hadayaṃ vedhamānaṃ;

Tepīdha [V 1.0132] soppaṃ labhare sasallā,

Tasmā [P 1.0111] ahaṃ na supe vītasallo.

“Even those in whose breast a spear is embedded, causing the heart to tremble again and again, even they, with the spear, can find sleep. Why then should I, who am without a spear, not sleep?

“Jaggaṃ na saṅke napi bhemi sottuṃ,

Rattindivā nānutapanti māmaṃ;

Hāniṃ na passāmi kuhiñci loke,

Tasmā supe sabbabhūtānukampī”ti.

“I am not apprehensive when vigilant, nor am I afraid to sleep; days and nights do not cause me to grieve. I see no loss anywhere in the world; therefore, having compassion for all beings, I sleep.”

Atha [T 1.0163] kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The Blessed One knows me, the Sugata knows me,” afflicted and disappointed, vanished right there.

4. Patirūpasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on What is Fitting

150. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu viharati ekasālāyaṃ brāhmaṇagāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā mahatiyā gihiparisāya parivuto dhammaṃ deseti.

150. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans in the brahmin village of Ekasālā. At that time the Blessed One was teaching the Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly of householders.

Atha [M 1.0113] kho mārassa pāpimato etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo mahatiyā gihiparisāya parivuto dhammaṃ deseti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṃ vicakkhukammāyā”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then this thought occurred to Māra the Evil One: “This ascetic Gotama is teaching the Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly of householders. What if I were to approach the ascetic Gotama in order to blind the assembly?” Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Netaṃ tava patirūpaṃ, yadaññamanusāsasi;

Anurodhavirodhesu, mā sajjittho tadācara”nti.

“It is not fitting for you that you instruct others. While doing so, do not get caught in attachment and aversion.”

“Hitānukampī sambuddho, yadaññamanusāsati;

Anurodhavirodhehi, vippamutto tathāgato”ti.

“The Fully Enlightened One, compassionate for their welfare, instructs others. The Tathāgata is liberated from attachment and aversion.”

Atha [V 1.0133] kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, “The Blessed One knows me, the Sugata knows me,” afflicted and disappointed, vanished right there.

5. Mānasasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Mental

151. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha [T 1.0164] kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

151. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Antalikkhacaro pāso, yvāyaṃ carati mānaso;

Tena taṃ bādhayissāmi, na me samaṇa mokkhasī”ti.

“The snare that travels in the sky is a mental one; with it I will bind you. Ascetic, you shall not escape me.”

“Rūpā saddā rasā gandhā, phoṭṭhabbā ca manoramā;

Ettha me vigato chando, nihato tvamasi antakā”ti.

“Forms, sounds, scents, tastes, and tangible objects that are mind-delighting; for these, my desire is gone. You are struck down, O Ender!”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The Blessed One knows me, the Well-Farer knows me,” afflicted and dejected, vanished right there.

6. Pattasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Bowl

152. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 1.0112]. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ upādāya bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samādāpeti (?) samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā aṭṭhikatvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) manasi [M 1.0114] katvā sabbacetasā sabbacetaso (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sabbaṃ cetasā (ka.) samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṃ suṇanti.

152. At Sāvatthī. At that time, the Blessed One was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk concerning the five aggregates of clinging. And those bhikkhus, paying proper attention, applying their minds, concentrating with their whole mind, listened to the Dhamma with attentive ears.

Atha kho mārassa pāpimato etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ upādāya bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā [V 1.0134] dhammaṃ suṇanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṃ vicakkhukammāyā”ti.

Then this thought occurred to Māra the Evil One: 'This ascetic Gotama is instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk concerning the five aggregates of clinging. And those bhikkhus, paying proper attention, applying their minds, concentrating with their whole mind, are listening to the Dhamma with attentive ears. What if I were to approach the ascetic Gotama in order to destroy their vision?'

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā pattā abbhokāse nikkhittā honti. Atha [T 1.0165] kho māro pāpimā balībaddavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā yena te pattā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “bhikkhu, bhikkhu, eso balībaddo patte bhindeyyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “na so, bhikkhu, balībaddo. Māro eso pāpimā tumhākaṃ vicakkhukammāya āgato”ti. Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Now at that time, many bowls had been placed in the open. Then Māra the Evil One, having conjured up the form of a bull, approached those bowls. Then a certain bhikkhu said to another bhikkhu: 'Bhikkhu, bhikkhu, that bull might break the bowls!' When this was said, the Blessed One said to that bhikkhu: 'That is not a bull, bhikkhu. That is Māra the Evil One, who has come to destroy your vision.' Then the Blessed One, having understood, 'This is Māra the Evil One,' addressed Māra the Evil One with a verse:

“Rūpaṃ vedayitaṃ saññā, viññāṇaṃ yañca saṅkhataṃ;

Nesohamasmi netaṃ me, evaṃ tattha virajjati.

“Form, feeling, perception, consciousness, and whatever is conditioned—‘This I am not; this is not mine’; thus one becomes dispassionate towards it.

“Evaṃ virattaṃ khemattaṃ, sabbasaṃyojanātigaṃ;

Anvesaṃ sabbaṭṭhānesu, mārasenāpi nājjhagā”ti.

“Thus dispassionate, having reached security, having overcome all fetters—even Māra’s army, searching in all places, does not find one.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā…pe… tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One… afflicted and dejected, vanished right there.

7. Chaphassāyatanasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Six Bases for Contact

153. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena [P 1.0113] kho pana samayena bhagavā channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ upādāya bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṃ suṇanti.

153. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood at the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Now at that time, the Blessed One was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk based on the six bases for contact. And those bhikkhus, considering it beneficial, taking it to mind, applying their whole mind, listened to the Dhamma with attentive ears.

Atha [M 1.0115] kho mārassa pāpimato etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo channaṃ phassāyatanānaṃ upādāya bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sappahaṃseti[T 1.0166]. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā [V 1.0135] dhammaṃ suṇanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṃ vicakkhukammāyā”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato avidūre mahantaṃ bhayabheravaṃ saddamakāsi, apissudaṃ pathavī maññe undrīyati udrīyati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī) u + dara + ya + ti = udrīyati. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “bhikkhu, bhikkhu, esā pathavī maññe undrīyatī”ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “nesā bhikkhu pathavī undrīyati. Māro eso pāpimā tumhākaṃ vicakkhukammāya āgato”ti. Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then this thought occurred to Māra the Evil One: 'This ascetic Gotama is instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk based on the six bases for contact. And those bhikkhus, considering it beneficial, taking it to mind, applying their whole mind, are listening to the Dhamma with attentive ears. What if I were to approach the ascetic Gotama for the purpose of destroying their wisdom-eye?' Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One. Having approached, not far from the Blessed One, he made a great, terrifying sound, as if the earth were about to collapse. Then a certain bhikkhu said to another bhikkhu: 'Bhikkhu, bhikkhu, it seems this earth is about to collapse!' When this was said, the Blessed One said to that bhikkhu: 'Bhikkhu, that is not the earth collapsing. That is Māra the Evil One, who has come for the purpose of destroying your wisdom-eye.' Then the Blessed One, having known, 'This is Māra the Evil One,' addressed Māra the Evil One with a verse:

“Rūpā saddā rasā gandhā, phassā dhammā ca kevalā;

Etaṃ lokāmisaṃ ghoraṃ, ettha loko vimucchito.

“Forms, sounds, tastes, smells, touches, and mental objects—all of them; this is the world’s dreadful bait, wherein the world is engrossed.

“Etañca samatikkamma, sato buddhassa sāvako;

Māradheyyaṃ atikkamma, ādiccova virocatī”ti.

“Having overcome this, the mindful disciple of the Buddha, having surpassed the realm of Māra, shines like the sun.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā…pe… tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One… vanished right there.

8. Piṇḍasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Almsfood

154. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā magadhesu viharati pañcasālāyaṃ brāhmaṇagāme. Tena [P 1.0114] kho pana samayena pañcasālāyaṃ brāhmaṇagāme kumārikānaṃ [T 1.0167] pāhunakāni bhavanti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya pañcasālaṃ brāhmaṇagāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Tena kho pana samayena pañcasāleyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā mārena pāpimatā anvāviṭṭhā bhavanti – mā samaṇo gotamo piṇḍamalatthāti.

154. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans at the brahmin village of Pañcasālā. Now at that time, in the brahmin village of Pañcasālā, there were guest-gifts for the young maidens. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered the brahmin village of Pañcasālā for almsfood. Now at that time, the brahmin householders of Pañcasālā were possessed by Māra the Evil One, thinking: 'May the ascetic Gotama not obtain almsfood!'

Atha kho bhagavā yathādhotena pattena pañcasālaṃ brāhmaṇagāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi tathādhotena yathādhotena (?) pattena paṭikkami. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “api [M 1.0116] tvaṃ, samaṇa, piṇḍamalatthā”ti? “Tathā nu tvaṃ, pāpima, akāsi yathāhaṃ piṇḍaṃ [V 1.0136] na labheyya”nti. “Tena hi, bhante, bhagavā dutiyampi pañcasālaṃ brāhmaṇagāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisatu. Tathāhaṃ karissāmi yathā bhagavā piṇḍaṃ lacchatī”ti.

Then the Blessed One, just as he had entered the brahmin village of Pañcasālā for almsfood with a washed bowl, so he departed with a washed bowl. Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One and said to him: 'Ascetic, did you obtain any almsfood?' 'Evil One, was it not you who acted in such a way that I would not obtain almsfood?' 'In that case, venerable sir, let the Blessed One enter the brahmin village of Pañcasālā for almsfood a second time. I will act in such a way that the Blessed One will obtain almsfood.'

“Apuññaṃ pasavi māro, āsajja naṃ tathāgataṃ;

Kiṃ nu maññasi pāpima, na me pāpaṃ vipaccati.

“By assailing the Tathāgata, Māra has generated demerit. What do you think, Evil One? That your evil deed will not ripen?

“Susukhaṃ vata jīvāma, yesaṃ no natthi kiñcanaṃ;

Pītibhakkhā bhavissāma, devā ābhassarā yathā”ti.

“Oh, how happily we live, we who have nothing! We shall be feeders on joy, like the Ābhassara gods.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, 'The Blessed One knows me, the Sugata knows me,' grieved and despondent, vanished right there.

9. Kassakasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Farmer

155. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ nibbānapaṭisaṃyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti[T 1.0168]. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṃ suṇanti.

155. At Sāvatthī. On that occasion, the Blessed One was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk connected with Nibbāna. And those bhikkhus, considering it beneficial, taking it to mind, applying their whole mind, listened to the Dhamma with attentive ears.

Atha [P 1.0115] kho mārassa pāpimato etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo bhikkhūnaṃ nibbānapaṭisaṃyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya…pe… yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṃ vicakkhukammāyā”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā kassakavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā mahantaṃ naṅgalaṃ khandhe karitvā dīghapācanayaṭṭhiṃ gahetvā haṭahaṭakeso sāṇasāṭinivattho kaddamamakkhitehi pādehi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “api, samaṇa, balībadde addasā”ti? “Kiṃ pana, pāpima, te balībaddehī”ti? “Mameva, samaṇa, cakkhu, mama rūpā, mama cakkhusamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ. Kuhiṃ me, samaṇa, gantvā mokkhasi? Mameva, samaṇa, sotaṃ, mama saddā…pe… mameva, samaṇa, ghānaṃ, mama gandhā; mameva, samaṇa, jivhā, mama rasā; mameva, samaṇa, kāyo, mama phoṭṭhabbā; mameva, samaṇa, mano, mama dhammā, mama manosamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ. Kuhiṃ me, samaṇa, gantvā mokkhasī”ti?

Then this thought occurred to Māra the Evil One: “This ascetic Gotama is instructing the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk connected with Nibbāna… What if I were to approach the ascetic Gotama for the purpose of destroying their wisdom-eye?” Then Māra the Evil One, having created the appearance of a farmer, carrying a large plow on his shoulder, holding a long goad, with disheveled hair, wearing a hempen garment, and with feet smeared with mud, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: “Ascetic, have you seen the oxen?” “Evil One, what have you to do with oxen?” “Ascetic, the eye is mine, forms are mine, the sphere of consciousness based on eye-contact is mine. Where, ascetic, will you go to escape me? Ascetic, the ear is mine, sounds are mine… Ascetic, the nose is mine, odors are mine… Ascetic, the tongue is mine, tastes are mine… Ascetic, the body is mine, tangibles are mine… Ascetic, the mind is mine, mental objects are mine, the sphere of consciousness based on mind-contact is mine. Where, ascetic, will you go to escape me?”

“Taveva[V 1.0137][M 1.0117], pāpima, cakkhu, tava rūpā, tava cakkhusamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ. Yattha ca kho, pāpima, natthi cakkhu, natthi rūpā, natthi cakkhusamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ, agati tava tattha, pāpima. Taveva, pāpima[T 1.0169], sotaṃ, tava saddā, tava sotasamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ. Yattha ca kho, pāpima, natthi sotaṃ, natthi saddā, natthi sotasamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ, agati tava tattha, pāpima. Taveva[P 1.0116], pāpima, ghānaṃ, tava gandhā, tava ghānasamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ. Yattha ca kho, pāpima, natthi ghānaṃ, natthi gandhā, natthi ghānasamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ, agati tava tattha, pāpima. Taveva, pāpima, jivhā, tava rasā, tava jivhāsamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ…pe… taveva, pāpima, kāyo, tava phoṭṭhabbā, tava kāyasamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ…pe… taveva, pāpima, mano, tava dhammā, tava manosamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ. Yattha ca kho, pāpima, natthi mano, natthi dhammā, natthi manosamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ, agati tava tattha, pāpimā”ti.

“Yours indeed, Evil One, is the eye, yours are the forms, yours is the sphere of consciousness based on eye-contact. But where, Evil One, there is no eye, no forms, and no sphere of consciousness based on eye-contact—you have no access there, Evil One. Yours indeed, Evil One, is the ear, yours are the sounds, yours is the sphere of consciousness based on ear-contact. But where, Evil One, there is no ear, no sounds, and no sphere of consciousness based on ear-contact—you have no access there, Evil One. Yours indeed, Evil One, is the nose, yours are the odors, yours is the sphere of consciousness based on nose-contact. But where, Evil One, there is no nose, no odors, and no sphere of consciousness based on nose-contact—you have no access there, Evil One. Yours indeed, Evil One, is the tongue, yours are the tastes, yours is the sphere of consciousness based on tongue-contact… Yours indeed, Evil One, is the body, yours are the tangibles, yours is the sphere of consciousness based on body-contact… Yours indeed, Evil One, is the mind, yours are the mental objects, yours is the sphere of consciousness based on mind-contact. But where, Evil One, there is no mind, no mental objects, and no sphere of consciousness based on mind-contact—you have no access there, Evil One.”

“Yaṃ vadanti mama yidanti, ye vadanti mamanti ca;

Ettha ce te mano atthi, na me samaṇa mokkhasī”ti.

“Regarding that which they call ‘this is mine,’ and those who say ‘it is mine’—if your mind is attached to this, ascetic, you will not be freed from me.”

“Yaṃ vadanti na taṃ mayhaṃ, ye vadanti na te ahaṃ;

Evaṃ pāpima jānāhi, na me maggampi dakkhasī”ti.

“What they speak of is not mine; those who speak thus are not I. Thus, Evil One, know this: you will not even see my path.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā…pe… tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One… vanished right there.

10. Rajjasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Kingship

156. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu viharati himavantapadese himavantapasse (sī.) araññakuṭikāyaṃ. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso [T 1.0170] parivitakko udapādi – “sakkā nu kho rajjaṃ kāretuṃ ahanaṃ aghātayaṃ ajinaṃ ajāpayaṃ asocaṃ asocāpayaṃ dhammenā”ti?

156. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans in the Himalayan region, in a forest hut. Then, while the Blessed One was in solitude and seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind: “Is it possible to exercise kingship righteously, without killing or causing to kill, without conquering or causing to conquer, without grieving or causing to grieve?”

Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kāretu, bhante, bhagavā rajjaṃ, kāretu, sugato, rajjaṃ ahanaṃ aghātayaṃ ajinaṃ ajāpayaṃ asocaṃ asocāpayaṃ dhammenā”ti. “Kiṃ pana me tvaṃ, pāpima, passasi yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ evaṃ vadesi – ‘kāretu, bhante, bhagavā rajjaṃ, kāretu sugato[V 1.0138], rajjaṃ ahanaṃ aghātayaṃ ajinaṃ ajāpayaṃ asocaṃ asocāpayaṃ [M 1.0118] dhammenā’”ti? “Bhagavatā kho, bhante, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā. Ākaṅkhamāno ca, bhante, bhagavā himavantaṃ pabbatarājaṃ suvaṇṇaṃ tveva adhimucceyya suvaṇṇañca panassā”ti suvaṇṇapabbatassāti (sī. syā. kaṃ.), suvaṇṇañca pabbatassāti (pī.).

Then Māra the Evil One, having known with his own mind the reflection in the Blessed One’s mind, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, let the Blessed One exercise kingship! Sugata, exercise kingship without killing or causing to kill, without conquering or causing to conquer, without grieving or causing to grieve, righteously!” “What do you see in me, Evil One, that you speak to me thus: ‘Venerable sir, let the Blessed One exercise kingship! Sugata, exercise kingship without killing or causing to kill, without conquering or causing to conquer, without grieving or causing to grieve, righteously!’?” “Venerable sir, the four bases of psychic power have been developed by the Blessed One, made much of, made a vehicle, made a foundation, steadily pursued, practiced, and well undertaken. If he so wished, venerable sir, the Blessed One could resolve that the Himālaya, the king of mountains, be gold, and it would become gold.”

“Pabbatassa [P 1.0117] suvaṇṇassa, jātarūpassa kevalo;

Dvittāva nālamekassa, iti vidvā samañcare.

“A mountain entirely of gold, of pure gold—even two such would not be enough for one person. Knowing this, one should live rightly.

“Yo dukkhamaddakkhi yatonidānaṃ,

Kāmesu so jantu kathaṃ nameyya;

Upadhiṃ viditvā saṅgoti loke,

Tasseva jantu vinayāya sikkhe”ti.

“One who has seen suffering and from where it originates—how could such a being incline towards sensual pleasures? Having known the substrate as a bond in the world, that being should train for its very removal.”

Atha kho [T 1.0171] māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugato”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The Blessed One knows me, the Sugata knows me,” afflicted and dejected, vanished right there.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Pāsāṇo sīho sakalikaṃ sakkhalikaṃ (ka.), patirūpañca mānasaṃ;

Pattaṃ āyatanaṃ piṇḍaṃ, kassakaṃ rajjena te dasāti.

Stone, Lion, Splinter, Suitable, and Mind; Bowl, Sense Base, Alms-food, Farmer, and with Kingship—these are the ten.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

1. Sambahulasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse concerning Many

157. Evaṃ [T 1.0172][V 1.0139] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati silāvatiyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavato avidūre appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharanti. Atha kho māro pāpimā brāhmaṇavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā mahantena jaṭaṇḍuvena ajinakkhipanivattho jiṇṇo gopānasivaṅko ghurughurupassāsī udumbaradaṇḍaṃ gahetvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “daharā bhavanto [M 1.0119] pabbajitā susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikkīḷitāvino kāmesu. Bhuñjantu bhavanto mānusake kāme. Mā sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvitthā”ti. “Na kho mayaṃ, brāhmaṇa, sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvāma. Kālikañca kho mayaṃ, brāhmaṇa, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṃ anudhāvāma. Kālikā hi, brāhmaṇa, kāmā vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṃ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī”ti. Evaṃ [P 1.0118] vutte, māro pāpimā sīsaṃ okampetvā jivhaṃ nillāletvā tivisākhaṃ nalāṭe nalāṭikaṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā daṇḍamolubbha pakkāmi.

157. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Silāvatī. Now at that time, a number of monks were dwelling not far from the Blessed One—heedful, ardent, and resolute. Then Māra the Evil One created the form of a brahmin with a large topknot, wearing a black antelope hide, old, bent like a roof rafter, breathing heavily, and carrying a staff of udumbara wood. He approached those monks and, having approached, said this to them: “You venerables have gone forth while young, very young, with black hair, endowed with fine youth, in the first stage of life, not having had your fill of play with sensual pleasures. Enjoy human sensual pleasures, venerable sirs. Do not abandon what is present to pursue what is of the future.” “Brahmin, we do not abandon what is present to pursue what is of the future. Rather, Brahmin, we abandon what is of the future to pursue what is present. For, Brahmin, sensual pleasures that are of the future have been described by the Blessed One as being of much suffering and much distress, wherein the danger is greater. This Dhamma is present, not subject to time, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be realized for oneself by the wise.” When this was said, Māra the Evil One shook his head, lolled his tongue, made a three-pronged wrinkle appear on his forehead, and departed, leaning on his staff.

Atha [T 1.0173] kho te bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato avidūre appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāma. Atha kho, bhante, aññataro brāhmaṇo mahantena jaṭaṇḍuvena ajinakkhipanivattho jiṇṇo gopānasivaṅko ghurughurupassāsī udumbaradaṇḍaṃ gahetvā yena mayaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā amhe etadavoca – ‘daharā bhavanto pabbajitā susū kāḷakesā bhadrena yobbanena samannāgatā paṭhamena vayasā anikkīḷitāvino kāmesu. Bhuñjantu bhavanto mānusake kāme. Mā sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvitthā’ti. Evaṃ vutte, mayaṃ, bhante, taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavocumha – ‘na kho mayaṃ, brāhmaṇa, sandiṭṭhikaṃ hitvā kālikaṃ anudhāvāma. Kālikañca kho mayaṃ, brāhmaṇa, hitvā sandiṭṭhikaṃ anudhāvāma. Kālikā hi, brāhmaṇa, kāmā [V 1.0140] vuttā bhagavatā bahudukkhā bahupāyāsā, ādīnavo ettha bhiyyo. Sandiṭṭhiko ayaṃ dhammo akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, so brāhmaṇo sīsaṃ okampetvā jivhaṃ nillāletvā tivisākhaṃ nalāṭe nalāṭikaṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā daṇḍamolubbha pakkanto”ti.

Then those monks approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, we were dwelling here not far from the Blessed One—heedful, ardent, and resolute. Then, venerable sir, a certain brahmin with a large topknot, wearing a black antelope hide, old, bent like a roof rafter, breathing heavily, and carrying a staff of udumbara wood, approached us. Having approached, he said this to us: ‘You venerables have gone forth while young, very young, with black hair, endowed with fine youth, in the first stage of life, not having had your fill of play with sensual pleasures. Enjoy human sensual pleasures, venerable sirs. Do not abandon what is present to pursue what is of the future.’ When this was said, venerable sir, we said this to that brahmin: ‘Brahmin, we do not abandon what is present to pursue what is of the future. Rather, Brahmin, we abandon what is of the future to pursue what is present. For, Brahmin, sensual pleasures that are of the future have been described by the Blessed One as being of much suffering and much distress, wherein the danger is greater. This Dhamma is directly visible, not subject to time, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be realized for oneself by the wise.’ When this was said, venerable sir, that brahmin shook his head, lolled his tongue, made a three-pronged wrinkle appear on his forehead, and departed, leaning on his staff.”

“Neso, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇo. Māro eso pāpimā tumhākaṃ vicakkhukammāya āgato”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā [T 1.0174] tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

“Monks, that was not a brahmin. That was Māra the Evil One, who came to destroy your eye of wisdom.” Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, at that time uttered this verse:

“Yo [M 1.0120] dukkhamaddakkhi yatonidānaṃ,

Kāmesu so jantu kathaṃ nameyya;

Upadhiṃ viditvā saṅgoti loke,

Tasseva jantu vinayāya sikkhe”ti.

“One who has seen suffering and from where it originates—how could such a being incline towards sensual pleasures? Having known the substrate as a bond in the world, that being should train for its very removal.”

2. Samiddhisuttaṃ

2. Samiddhi Sutta

158. Ekaṃ [P 1.0119] samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati silāvatiyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā samiddhi bhagavato avidūre appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharati. Atha kho āyasmato samiddhissa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me satthā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho. Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yvāhaṃ evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajito. Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me sabrahmacārino sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā āyasmato samiddhissa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yenāyasmā samiddhi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmato samiddhissa avidūre mahantaṃ bhayabheravaṃ saddamakāsi, apissudaṃ pathavī maññe undrīyati.

158. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Silāvatī. Now at that time, Venerable Samiddhi was dwelling not far from the Blessed One—heedful, ardent, and resolute. Then, while Venerable Samiddhi was in seclusion, withdrawn, the following reflection arose in his mind: “It is truly a gain for me, it is well gained by me, that my teacher is the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. It is truly a gain for me, it is well gained by me, that I have gone forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline. It is truly a gain for me, it is well gained by me, that my companions in the holy life are virtuous and of good character.” Then Māra the Evil One, knowing with his mind the reflection in Venerable Samiddhi's mind, approached him. Having approached, not far from Venerable Samiddhi, he made a great, terrifying sound, as if the earth were collapsing.

Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno [T 1.0175] āyasmā samiddhi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idhāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato avidūre appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa [V 1.0141] paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me satthā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho. Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yvāhaṃ evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajito. Lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yassa me sabrahmacārino sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, avidūre mahābhayabheravasaddo ahosi, apissudaṃ pathavī maññe undrīyatī”ti.

Then Venerable Samiddhi approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Venerable Samiddhi said to the Blessed One: 'Here, venerable sir, I am dwelling not far from the Blessed One, heedful, ardent, and resolute. To me, venerable sir, while in seclusion, withdrawn, this reflection arose in my mind: “It is truly a gain for me, it is well gained by me, that my Teacher is the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. It is truly a gain for me, it is well gained by me, that I have gone forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline. It is truly a gain for me, it is well gained by me, that my companions in the holy life are virtuous and of good character.” Then, venerable sir, not far from me, there arose a great and terrifying sound, and it was as if the earth were collapsing.'

“Nesā, samiddhi, pathavī undrīyati. Māro eso pāpimā tuyhaṃ vicakkhukammāya āgato. Gaccha tvaṃ, samiddhi, tattheva appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharāhī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā samiddhi bhagavato paṭissutvā [M 1.0121][P 1.0120] uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā samiddhi tattheva appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihāsi. Dutiyampi kho āyasmato samiddhissa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa…pe… dutiyampi kho māro pāpimā āyasmato samiddhissa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya…pe… apissudaṃ pathavī maññe undrīyati. Atha kho āyasmā samiddhi māraṃ [T 1.0176] pāpimantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

'This earth is not collapsing, Samiddhi. This is Māra the Evil One, who has come to destroy your eye of wisdom. Go, Samiddhi, and dwell right there, heedful, ardent, and resolute.' 'Yes, venerable sir,' replied Venerable Samiddhi. He assented to the Blessed One, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed. For a second time, Venerable Samiddhi dwelled right there, heedful, ardent, and resolute. For a second time, while Venerable Samiddhi was in seclusion, withdrawn... For a second time, Māra the Evil One, knowing with his mind the reflection in Venerable Samiddhi’s mind... and again it was as if the earth were collapsing. Then Venerable Samiddhi addressed Māra the Evil One in verse:

“Saddhāyāhaṃ pabbajito, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ;

Sati paññā ca me buddhā, cittañca susamāhitaṃ;

Kāmaṃ karassu rūpāni, neva maṃ byādhayissasī”ti.

'Out of faith I went forth, from the household to homelessness; my mindfulness and wisdom are awakened, and my mind is well concentrated. Create fearsome forms as you wish; you will never make me tremble.'

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ samiddhi bhikkhū”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, realizing, "The monk Samiddhi knows me," grieved and displeased, vanished right there.

3. Godhikasuttaṃ

3. The Godhika Sutta

159. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā godhiko isigilipasse viharati kāḷasilāyaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṃ cetovimuttiṃ phusi. Atha kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā sāmayikāya cetovimuttiyā parihāyi[V 1.0142]. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṃ cetovimuttiṃ phusi. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā sāmayikāya cetovimuttiyā parihāyi. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṃ cetovimuttiṃ phusi. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā…pe… parihāyi. Catutthampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto…pe… vimuttiṃ phusi[T 1.0177]. Catutthampi kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā…pe… parihāyi. Pañcamampi [P 1.0121] kho āyasmā godhiko…pe… cetovimuttiṃ phusi. Pañcamampi kho āyasmā…pe… vimuttiyā parihāyi. Chaṭṭhampi kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṃ cetovimuttiṃ phusi. Chaṭṭhampi kho āyasmā godhiko tamhā sāmayikāya cetovimuttiyā parihāyi. Sattamampi [M 1.0122] kho āyasmā godhiko appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto sāmayikaṃ cetovimuttiṃ phusi.

159. Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary. At that time the Venerable Godhika was staying on the slope of Isigili, at the Black Rock. Then the Venerable Godhika, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, attained a temporary liberation of mind. But then the Venerable Godhika fell away from that temporary liberation of mind. For a second time, the Venerable Godhika, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, attained a temporary liberation of mind. For a second time, the Venerable Godhika fell away from that temporary liberation of mind. For a third time, the Venerable Godhika, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, attained a temporary liberation of mind. For a third time, the Venerable Godhika fell away from that temporary liberation of mind. For a fourth time, the Venerable Godhika, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, attained a temporary liberation of mind. For a fourth time, the Venerable Godhika fell away from that temporary liberation of mind. For a fifth time, the Venerable Godhika, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, attained a temporary liberation of mind. For a fifth time, the Venerable Godhika fell away from that temporary liberation of mind. For a sixth time, the Venerable Godhika, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, attained a temporary liberation of mind. For a sixth time, the Venerable Godhika fell away from that temporary liberation of mind. For a seventh time, the Venerable Godhika, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute, attained a temporary liberation of mind.

Atha kho āyasmato godhikassa etadahosi – “yāva chaṭṭhaṃ khvāhaṃ sāmayikāya cetovimuttiyā parihīno. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ satthaṃ āhareyya”nti. Atha kho māro pāpimā āyasmato godhikassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Godhika: “For the sixth time I have fallen away from temporary liberation of mind. What if I were to use the knife?” Then Māra the Evil One, knowing with his own mind the thought in the Venerable Godhika’s mind, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with verses:

“Mahāvīra mahāpañña, iddhiyā yasasā jala;

Sabbaverabhayātīta, pāde vandāmi cakkhuma.

“O Great Hero, great in wisdom, blazing with power and glory, passed beyond all enmity and fear; I bow to your feet, O One with Vision.”

“Sāvako te mahāvīra, maraṇaṃ maraṇābhibhū;

Ākaṅkhati cetayati, taṃ nisedha jutindhara.

“Your disciple, O Great Hero, is overcome by death; he longs for death and is intent upon it. Restrain him, O Bearer of Splendor.”

“Kathañhi bhagavā tuyhaṃ, sāvako sāsane rato;

Appattamānaso sekkho, kālaṃ kayirā janesutā”ti.

“How indeed, O Blessed One, could your disciple—who delights in the teaching, a learner whose goal is not yet reached, and is renowned among the people—pass away?”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato godhikena satthaṃ āharitaṃ hoti. Atha kho bhagavā “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ [T 1.0178] pāpimantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

At that time, the Venerable Godhika had taken up the knife. Then the Blessed One, knowing, “This is Māra the Evil One,” addressed Māra the Evil One in verse:

“Evañhi [V 1.0143] dhīrā kubbanti, nāvakaṅkhanti jīvitaṃ;

Samūlaṃ taṇhamabbuyha, godhiko parinibbuto”ti.

“Thus indeed do the wise act; they do not long for life. Having uprooted craving with its root, Godhika has attained final Nibbāna.”

Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “āyāma, bhikkhave, yena isigilipassaṃ kāḷasilā tenupasaṅkamissāma yattha godhikena kulaputtena satthaṃ āharita”nti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ.

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Come, monks, let us go to the Black Rock on the slope of Isigili, where the clansman Godhika has taken up the knife.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ yena isigilipassaṃ kāḷasilā tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ godhikaṃ dūratova mañcake vivattakkhandhaṃ semānaṃ seyyamānaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), soppamānaṃ (ka.). Tena [P 1.0122] kho pana samayena dhūmāyitattaṃ timirāyitattaṃ gacchateva purimaṃ disaṃ, gacchati pacchimaṃ disaṃ, gacchati uttaraṃ disaṃ, gacchati dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ, gacchati uddhaṃ, gacchati adho, gacchati anudisaṃ.

Then the Blessed One, together with a number of monks, approached the Black Rock on the slope of Isigili. The Blessed One saw from afar the Venerable Godhika lying on a bed with his shoulder turned. At that time, a smoky haze and a deep darkness was moving to the east, moving to the west, moving to the north, moving to the south, moving upwards, moving downwards, and moving to the intermediate directions.

Atha [M 1.0123] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “passatha no tumhe, bhikkhave, etaṃ dhūmāyitattaṃ timirāyitattaṃ gacchateva purimaṃ disaṃ, gacchati pacchimaṃ disaṃ, gacchati uttaraṃ disaṃ, gacchati dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ, gacchati uddhaṃ, gacchati adho, gacchati anudisa”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Eso kho, bhikkhave, māro pāpimā godhikassa kulaputtassa viññāṇaṃ samanvesati – ‘kattha godhikassa kulaputtassa viññāṇaṃ patiṭṭhita’nti? Appatiṭṭhitena ca, bhikkhave, viññāṇena godhiko kulaputto parinibbuto”ti. Atha [T 1.0179] kho māro pāpimā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Do you see, monks, that smoky haze and deep darkness moving to the east, moving to the west, moving to the north, moving to the south, moving upwards, moving downwards, and moving to the intermediate directions?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “That, monks, is Māra the Evil One searching for the consciousness of the clansman Godhika, thinking: ‘Where has the consciousness of the clansman Godhika been established?’ But, monks, with consciousness unestablished, the clansman Godhika has attained final Nibbāna.” Then Māra the Evil One, taking up a lute the color of a ripe beluva fruit, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Uddhaṃ adho ca tiriyaṃ, disā anudisā svahaṃ;

Anvesaṃ nādhigacchāmi, godhiko so kuhiṃ gato”ti.

“Upwards, downwards, and across, to the cardinal and intermediate directions, I have searched but do not find him. Where has that Godhika gone?”

“Yo so (sī. pī.) dhīro dhitisampanno, jhāyī jhānarato sadā;

Ahorattaṃ anuyuñjaṃ, jīvitaṃ anikāmayaṃ.

“The one who is wise, endowed with steadfastness, a meditator, ever delighting in meditation, striving day and night, unconcerned with life,

“Jetvāna [V 1.0144] maccuno bhetvā namucino (sī.) senaṃ, anāgantvā punabbhavaṃ;

Samūlaṃ taṇhamabbuyha, godhiko parinibbuto”ti.

“having conquered the army of Death, not returning to renewed existence, having uprooted craving with its root—Godhika has attained final Nibbāna.”

“Tassa sokaparetassa, vīṇā kacchā abhassatha;

Tato so dummano yakkho, tatthevantaradhāyathā”ti tatthevantaradhāyithāti (syā. kaṃ.), tattheva antaradhāyīti (ka.).

For him, overcome with sorrow, the lute slipped from his arm. Then that dejected yakkha vanished right there.

4. Sattavassānubandhasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Seven-Year Pursuit

160. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe. Tena kho pana samayena māro pāpimā sattavassāni bhagavantaṃ anubandho hoti otārāpekkho otāraṃ alabhamāno. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

160. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā, on the bank of the Nerañjarā River, at the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree. At that time, Māra the Evil One had been following the Blessed One for seven years, seeking an opportunity but not finding one. Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One and addressed him with a verse:

“Sokāvatiṇṇo [P 1.0123] nu vanamhi jhāyasi,

Vittaṃ nu jīno uda patthayāno;

Āguṃ nu gāmasmimakāsi kiñci,

Kasmā [T 1.0180] janena na karosi sakkhiṃ;

Sakkhī na sampajjati kenaci te”ti.

“Are you brooding in the forest, overcome by sorrow? Have you lost wealth, or are you longing for it? Have you committed some offense in a village? Why do you not make friends with people? Is it that you have no friend at all?”

“Sokassa [M 1.0124] mūlaṃ palikhāya sabbaṃ,

Anāgu jhāyāmi asocamāno;

Chetvāna sabbaṃ bhavalobhajappaṃ,

Anāsavo jhāyāmi pamattabandhū”ti.

“Having dug up the entire root of sorrow, free from offense and not sorrowing, I meditate. Having conquered all craving and greed for existence, free from taints, I meditate, O kinsman of the heedless.”

“Yaṃ vadanti mama yidanti, ye vadanti mamanti ca;

Ettha ce te mano atthi, na me samaṇa mokkhasī”ti.

“Regarding that of which they say, ‘This is mine,’ and those who say, ‘Mine’—if your mind is in this, O ascetic, you will not be freed from me.”

“Yaṃ [V 1.0145] vadanti na taṃ mayhaṃ, ye vadanti na te ahaṃ;

Evaṃ pāpima jānāhi, na me maggampi dakkhasī”ti.

“That of which they speak is not mine; those who speak thus are not me. Know this, O Evil One: you will not even see my path.”

“Sace maggaṃ anubuddhaṃ, khemaṃ amatagāminaṃ;

Apehi gaccha tvameveko, kimaññamanusāsasī”ti.

“If you have awakened to the path, secure and leading to the deathless, then go away by yourself alone. Why do you instruct another?”

“Amaccudheyyaṃ pucchanti, ye janā pāragāmino;

Tesāhaṃ puṭṭho akkhāmi, yaṃ saccaṃ taṃ nirūpadhi”nti.

“Those people who are journeying to the far shore ask about the deathless realm. Being asked, I declare to them that which is true, that which is without substrate.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhante, gāmassa vā nigamassa vā avidūre pokkharaṇī. Tatrassa kakkaṭako. Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā kumārakā vā kumārikāyo vā tamhā gāmā vā nigamā vā nikkhamitvā yena sā pokkharaṇī tenupasaṅkameyyuṃ; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ kakkaṭakaṃ udakā uddharitvā thale patiṭṭhapeyyuṃ. Yaṃ yadeva hi so, bhante, kakkaṭako aḷaṃ abhininnāmeyya taṃ tadeva te kumārakā vā [T 1.0181] kumārikāyo vā kaṭṭhena vā kathalāya vā sañchindeyyuṃ sambhañjeyyuṃ sampalibhañjeyyuṃ. Evañhi so, bhante, kakkaṭako sabbehi aḷehi sañchinnehi sambhaggehi sampalibhaggehi abhabbo taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ otarituṃ. Evameva kho, bhante, yāni kānici visūkāyikāni yāni visukāyikāni (sī. pī. ka.) visevitāni vipphanditāni, sabbāni tāni kānici kānici sabbāni (sī. pī. ka.) bhagavatā sañchinnāni sambhaggāni [P 1.0124] sampalibhaggāni. Abhabbo dānāhaṃ, bhante, puna bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamituṃ yadidaṃ otārāpekkho”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā bhagavato santike imā nibbejanīyā gāthāyo abhāsi –

“Venerable sir, it is as if there were a pond not far from a village or a town, and in it there was a crab. Then, venerable sir, many boys or girls, leaving that village or town, would approach that pond. Having approached, they would lift that crab out of the water and place it on dry land. Whatever claw that crab would extend, venerable sir, those boys or girls would cut, break, and shatter it with a stick or a potsherd. In this way, venerable sir, with all its claws cut, broken, and shattered, that crab would be unable to re-enter that pond. In the very same way, venerable sir, all Māra’s stakes, contortions, and agitations have been cut, broken, and shattered by the Blessed One. I am now unable to approach the Blessed One again for the purpose of seeking an opportunity.” Then Māra the Evil One, in the presence of the Blessed One, recited these verses of disenchantment:

“Medavaṇṇañca pāsāṇaṃ, vāyaso anupariyagā;

Apettha muduṃ vindema, api assādanā siyā.

“A crow circled a stone that had the color of fat, thinking: ‘Perhaps we might find something soft here, perhaps there might be some taste.’”

“Aladdhā [M 1.0125] tattha assādaṃ, vāyasetto apakkame;

Kākova selamāsajja, nibbijjāpema gotamā”ti.

“Finding no taste there, the crow departs from that place. Just like the crow with the rock, having approached Gotama and become disenchanted, we now depart.”

5. Māradhītusuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on the Daughters of Māra

161. Atha [V 1.0146] kho māro pāpimā bhagavato santike imā nibbejanīyā gāthāyo abhāsitvā tamhā ṭhānā apakkamma bhagavato avidūre pathaviyaṃ pallaṅkena nisīdi tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno kaṭṭhena bhūmiṃ vilikhanto. Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro yena māro pāpimā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāya [T 1.0182] ajjhabhāsiṃsu –

161. Then Māra the Evil One, having recited these disheartening verses in the presence of the Blessed One, departed from that place and sat down cross-legged on the ground not far from the Blessed One—silent, dismayed, with drooping shoulders, downcast, brooding, at a loss for words, scratching the ground with a stick. Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Rāga, the daughters of Māra, approached Māra the Evil One. Having approached, they addressed Māra the Evil One with a verse:

“Kenāsi dummano tāta, purisaṃ kaṃ nu socasi;

Mayaṃ taṃ rāgapāsena, āraññamiva kuñjaraṃ;

Bandhitvā ānayissāma, vasago te bhavissatī”ti.

“Father, why are you disheartened? For which man do you grieve? We shall bind him with the snare of passion, like a forest elephant, and bring him to you. He will be under your control.”

“Arahaṃ sugato loke, na rāgena suvānayo;

Māradheyyaṃ atikkanto, tasmā socāmahaṃ bhusa”nti.
