“He is an Arahant in the world, a Sugata, not easily led by passion. He has overcome Māra’s domain; therefore, I grieve intensely.”

Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “pāde te, samaṇa, paricāremā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā na manasākāsi, yathā taṃ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.

Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Rāga, the daughters of Māra, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they said this to the Blessed One: “Ascetic, we shall serve at your feet.” But the Blessed One paid no attention, as he was liberated in the unsurpassed exhaustion of substrates.

Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekamantaṃ apakkamma evaṃ samacintesuṃ – “uccāvacā kho purisānaṃ adhippāyā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ ekasataṃ ekasataṃ kumārivaṇṇasataṃ abhinimmineyyāmā”ti. Atha [P 1.0125] kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekasataṃ ekasataṃ kumārivaṇṇasataṃ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “pāde te, samaṇa, paricāremā”ti. Tampi bhagavā na manasākāsi, yathā taṃ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.

Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Rāga, the daughters of Māra, withdrawing to one side, considered thus in unison: “Indeed, the inclinations of men are varied. What if each of us were to create one hundred forms of young maidens?” Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Rāga, the daughters of Māra, each having created one hundred forms of young maidens, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they said this to the Blessed One: “Ascetic, we shall serve at your feet.” But the Blessed One paid no attention to that either, as he was liberated in the unsurpassed exhaustion of substrates.

Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekamantaṃ apakkamma evaṃ samacintesuṃ – “uccāvacā kho purisānaṃ adhippāyā[T 1.0183]. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ ekasataṃ ekasataṃ avijātavaṇṇasataṃ abhinimmineyyāmā”ti. Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekasataṃ ekasataṃ [M 1.0126] avijātavaṇṇasataṃ [V 1.0147] abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “pāde te, samaṇa, paricāremā”ti. Tampi bhagavā na manasākāsi, yathā taṃ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.

Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Rāga, the daughters of Māra, withdrawing to one side, considered thus in unison: “Indeed, the inclinations of men are varied. What if each of us were to create one hundred forms of women who have not yet given birth?” Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Rāga, the daughters of Māra, each having created one hundred forms of women who have not yet given birth, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they said this to the Blessed One: “Ascetic, we shall serve at your feet.” But the Blessed One paid no attention to that either, as he was liberated in the unsurpassed exhaustion of substrates.

Atha kho taṇhā ca…pe… yaṃnūna mayaṃ ekasataṃ ekasataṃ sakiṃ vijātavaṇṇasataṃ abhinimmineyyāmāti. Atha kho taṇhā ca…pe… sakiṃ vijātavaṇṇasataṃ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “pāde te, samaṇa, paricāremā”ti. Tampi bhagavā na manasākāsi, yathā taṃ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.

Then Taṇhā and the others... and so on... “What if each of us were to create one hundred forms of women who have given birth once?” Then Taṇhā and the others... and so on... each having created one hundred forms of women who have given birth once, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they said to the Blessed One: “Ascetic, we shall serve at your feet.” But the Blessed One paid no attention to that either, as he was liberated in the unsurpassed exhaustion of substrates.

Atha kho taṇhā ca…pe… yaṃnūna mayaṃ ekasataṃ ekasataṃ duvijātavaṇṇasataṃ abhinimmineyyāmāti. Atha kho taṇhā ca…pe… duvijātavaṇṇasataṃ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā…pe… yathā taṃ anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto. Atha kho taṇhā ca…pe… majjhimitthivaṇṇasataṃ abhinimmineyyāmāti. Atha kho taṇhā ca…pe… majjhimitthivaṇṇasataṃ abhinimminitvā…pe… anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto.

Then Taṇhā and the others... and so on... thought, “What if each of us were to create one hundred forms of women who have given birth twice?” Then Taṇhā and the others... and so on... having each created one hundred forms of women who have given birth twice... approached the Blessed One... and so on... but because he was liberated in the unsurpassed exhaustion of substrates, he paid them no mind. Then Taṇhā and the others... and so on... thought, “What if we were to create one hundred forms of middle-aged women?” Then Taṇhā and the others... and so on... having each created one hundred forms of middle-aged women... and so on... but because he was liberated in the unsurpassed exhaustion of substrates, he paid them no mind.

Atha kho taṇhā ca…pe… mahitthivaṇṇasataṃ abhinimmineyyāmāti[T 1.0184]. Atha kho taṇhā ca…pe… mahitthivaṇṇasataṃ abhinimminitvā yena bhagavā…pe… anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye vimutto. Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro ekamantaṃ apakkamma etadavocuṃ – saccaṃ kira no pitā avoca –

Then Taṇhā and the others... and so on... thought, “What if we were to create one hundred forms of elderly women?” Then Taṇhā and the others... and so on... having each created one hundred forms of elderly women... approached the Blessed One... and so on... but because he was liberated in the unsurpassed exhaustion of substrates, he paid them no mind. Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Ragā, the daughters of Māra, withdrew to one side and said this: “Indeed, our father spoke the truth:”

“Arahaṃ sugato loke, na rāgena suvānayo;

Māradheyyaṃ atikkanto, tasmā socāmahaṃ bhusa”nti.

“He is an Arahant, a Sugata in the world, not easily led by passion. He has overcome Māra’s domain; therefore, I grieve intensely.”

“Yañhi mayaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā avītarāgaṃ iminā upakkamena upakkameyyāma hadayaṃ vāssa phaleyya, uṇhaṃ lohitaṃ vā mukhato uggaccheyya, ummādaṃ [P 1.0126] vā pāpuṇeyya cittakkhepaṃ [V 1.0148] vā. Seyyathā vā pana naḷo harito luto ussussati visussati milāyati; evameva ussusseyya visusseyya milāyeyyā”ti.

“Indeed, if we were to assail any ascetic or brahmin who is not free from passion with this approach, his heart would burst, or hot blood would gush from his mouth, or he would go mad or become distracted. Just as a green reed that has been cut withers, dries up, and fades, so too would he wither, dry up, and fade.”

Atha [M 1.0127] kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho taṇhā māradhītā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Ragā, the daughters of Māra, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they stood to one side. Standing to one side, Taṇhā, the daughter of Māra, addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Sokāvatiṇṇo nu vanamhi jhāyasi,

Vittaṃ nu jīno uda patthayāno;

Āguṃ nu gāmasmimakāsi kiñci,

Kasmā janena na karosi sakkhiṃ;

Sakkhī na sampajjati kenaci te”ti.

“Are you overcome with sorrow, brooding in the forest? Have you lost wealth, or are you longing for it? Have you committed some offense in a village? Why do you not form friendships with people? Is there no one who can be your friend?”

“Atthassa [T 1.0185] pattiṃ hadayassa santiṃ,

Jetvāna senaṃ piyasātarūpaṃ;

Ekohaṃ ekāhaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) jhāyaṃ sukhamanubodhiṃ,

Tasmā janena na karomi sakkhiṃ;

Sakkhī na sampajjati kenaci me”ti.

“Having attained the goal, the peace of heart, and having conquered the army of what is dear and pleasing in form, I, alone, meditating, have realized bliss. Therefore, I do not form friendships with people; no one can be a friend to me.”

Atha kho arati arati ca (ka.) māradhītā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then Arati, the daughter of Māra, addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kathaṃ vihārībahulodha bhikkhu,

Pañcoghatiṇṇo atarīdha chaṭṭhaṃ;

Kathaṃ jhāyiṃ kathaṃ jhāyaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.), kathajjhāyaṃ (ka.) bahulaṃ kāmasaññā,

Paribāhirā honti aladdha yo ta”nti.

“How does a monk here, dwelling frequently, cross the five floods and traverse the sixth? By what kind of frequent meditation do perceptions of sensual pleasure remain external to him, finding no opportunity?”

“Passaddhakāyo suvimuttacitto,

Asaṅkharāno satimā anoko;

Aññāya [V 1.0149] dhammaṃ avitakkajhāyī,

Na kuppati na sarati na thino na kuppatī nassaratī na thīno (sī.).

“With body tranquil, with mind well-liberated, not fabricating, mindful, and homeless, having understood the Dhamma, one meditates without thought-conception. One is not agitated, does not yearn, and is not sluggish.”

“Evaṃvihārībahulodha bhikkhu,

Pañcoghatiṇṇo atarīdha chaṭṭhaṃ;

Evaṃ jhāyiṃ bahulaṃ kāmasaññā,

Paribāhirā honti aladdha yo ta”nti.

“A monk here, dwelling frequently in this way, has crossed the five floods and has traversed the sixth. For one meditating frequently in this way, perceptions of sensual pleasure remain external, finding no opportunity.”

Atha [M 1.0128][P 1.0127] kho ragā ragāca (ka.) māradhītā bhagavato santike gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then Ragā, the daughter of Māra, addressed the Blessed One in his presence with a verse:

“Acchejja [T 1.0186] taṇhaṃ gaṇasaṅghacārī,

Addhā carissanti tarissanti (sī.) bahū ca saddhā;

Bahuṃ vatāyaṃ janataṃ anoko,

Acchejja nessati maccurājassa pāra”nti.

“Having cut off craving, he frequents groups and assemblies. Surely many faithful ones will also practice accordingly. This homeless one will snatch away the great multitude of people from the King of Death and lead them to the far shore.”

“Nayanti ve mahāvīrā, saddhammena tathāgatā;

Dhammena nayamānānaṃ, kā usūyā vijānata”nti.

“Indeed, the Great Heroes, the Tathāgatas, lead by the True Dhamma. For one who understands, what envy can there be toward those being led by the Dhamma?”

Atha kho taṇhā ca arati ca ragā ca māradhītaro yena māro pāpimā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Addasā kho māro pāpimā taṇhañca aratiñca ragañca māradhītaro dūratova āgacchantiyo. Disvāna gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then Taṇhā, Arati, and Ragā, the daughters of Māra, approached Māra the Evil One. Māra the Evil One saw the daughters of Māra—Taṇhā, Arati, and Ragā—coming from afar. Having seen them, he addressed them in verses:

“Bālā kumudanāḷehi, pabbataṃ abhimatthatha abhimanthatha (sī.);

Giriṃ nakhena khanatha, ayo dantehi khādatha.

“Fools, you try to crush a mountain with lotus stalks; you dig at a mountain with your fingernails; you chew iron with your teeth.

“Selaṃva sirasūhacca sirasi ūhacca (sī.), sirasi ohacca (syā. kaṃ.), pātāle gādhamesatha;

Khāṇuṃva urasāsajja, nibbijjāpetha gotamā”ti.

“Like carrying a rock on your head, you seek a foothold in the abyss; like striking a tree stump with your chest, you should, being disgusted with Gotama, depart.”

“Daddallamānā [V 1.0150] āgañchuṃ, taṇhā ca aratī ragā;

Tā tattha panudī satthā, tūlaṃ bhaṭṭhaṃva māluto”ti.

Taṇhā, Arati, and Ragā came, shining brightly. But the Teacher drove them away from there, just as the wind scatters a tuft of cotton.

Tatiyo vaggo.

The Third Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Sambahulā [T 1.0187] samiddhi ca, godhikaṃ sattavassāni;

Dhītaraṃ desitaṃ buddha, seṭṭhena imaṃ mārapañcakanti.

Sambahulā, Samiddhi, Godhika, Sattavassāni, and Dhītara—this pentad on Māra was taught by the most excellent Buddha.

Mārasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Māra Saṃyutta is concluded.

5. Bhikkhunīsaṃyuttaṃ

5. 5. The Bhikkhunī Saṃyutta

1. Āḷavikāsuttaṃ

1. 1. The Āḷavikā Sutta

162. Evaṃ [T 1.0188][V 1.0151][P 1.0128][M 1.0129] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āḷavikā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena andhavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami vivekatthinī. Atha kho māro pāpimā āḷavikāya bhikkhuniyā bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo vivekamhā cāvetukāmo yena āḷavikā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āḷavikaṃ bhikkhuniṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

162. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā dressed, took her bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms. After wandering for alms in Sāvatthī and returning from her alms round after the meal, she approached Andhavana, desiring seclusion. Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā, and wishing to dislodge her from seclusion, approached her. Having approached, he addressed the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā in verse:

“Natthi nissaraṇaṃ loke, kiṃ vivekena kāhasi;

Bhuñjassu kāmaratiyo, māhu pacchānutāpinī”ti.

“There is no escape in the world; what will you do with seclusion? Enjoy the delights of sensual pleasures; may you not be one who repents later.”

Atha kho āḷavikāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “ko nu khvāyaṃ manusso vā amanusso vā gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti? Atha kho āḷavikāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “māro kho ayaṃ pāpimā mama bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo vivekamhā cāvetukāmo gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti. Atha kho āḷavikā bhikkhunī “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ [T 1.0189] gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā: “Who now is this, a human or a non-human, who speaks this verse?” Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā: “This is Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in me, wishing to dislodge me from seclusion, who speaks this verse.” Then the bhikkhunī Āḷavikā, having known, “This is Māra the Evil One,” replied to Māra the Evil One in verses:

“Atthi nissaraṇaṃ loke, paññāya me suphussitaṃ suphassitaṃ (sī. pī.);

Pamattabandhu pāpima, na tvaṃ jānāsi taṃ padaṃ.

“There is an escape in the world; it has been well attained by me with wisdom. O Evil One, friend of the heedless, you do not know that state.

“Sattisūlūpamā [V 1.0152] kāmā, khandhāsaṃ adhikuṭṭanā;

Yaṃ tvaṃ kāmaratiṃ brūsi, arati mayha sā ahū”ti.

“Sensual pleasures are like spears and stakes; they are a chopping block for the aggregates. That which you call delight in sensual pleasure has become non-delight for me.”

Atha [P 1.0129] kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ āḷavikā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, knowing, “The bhikkhunī Āḷavikā knows me,” afflicted and dejected, vanished right there.

2. Somāsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse with Somā

163. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 1.0130]. Atha kho somā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena andhavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Andhavanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māro pāpimā somāya bhikkhuniyā bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo yena somā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā somaṃ bhikkhuniṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

163. At Sāvatthī. Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Somā dressed, took her bowl and outer robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms. Having gone for alms in Sāvatthī, after her meal, on returning from her alms-round, she went to the Andhavana for the day’s abiding. Having entered the Andhavana, she sat down at the foot of a certain tree for the day’s abiding. Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the bhikkhunī Somā, and desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached the bhikkhunī Somā; having approached, he addressed the bhikkhunī Somā with a verse:

“Yaṃ taṃ isīhi pattabbaṃ, ṭhānaṃ durabhisambhavaṃ;

Na taṃ dvaṅgulapaññāya, sakkā pappotumitthiyā”ti.

“That state, difficult to reach, which is to be attained by seers—it cannot be attained by a woman with her two-finger wisdom.”

Atha kho somāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “ko nu khvāyaṃ manusso vā amanusso vā gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti? Atha kho somāya bhikkhuniyā [T 1.0190] etadahosi – “māro kho ayaṃ pāpimā mama bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti. Atha kho somā bhikkhunī “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

Then this thought arose in the bhikkhunī Somā: ‘Who now is this, a human or a non-human, who recites this verse?’ Then this thought arose in the bhikkhunī Somā: ‘Indeed, this is Māra the Evil One. Desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in me, and desiring to make me fall away from concentration, he recites this verse.’ Then the bhikkhunī Somā, knowing, ‘This is Māra the Evil One,’ replied to Māra the Evil One with verses:

“Itthibhāvo kiṃ kayirā, cittamhi susamāhite;

Ñāṇamhi vattamānamhi, sammā dhammaṃ vipassato.

“When the mind is well-concentrated, and knowledge is present, for one who rightly sees the Dhamma, what can womanhood do?

“Yassa [V 1.0153] nūna siyā evaṃ, itthāhaṃ purisoti vā;

Kiñci vā pana aññasmi asmīti (syā. kaṃ. pī.), taṃ māro vattumarahatī”ti.

“To one for whom it might occur, ‘I am a woman,’ or ‘I am a man,’ or ‘I am something else,’ to that one Māra is fit to speak.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ somā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, ‘The bhikkhunī Somā knows me,’ afflicted and dejected, vanished right there.

3. Kisāgotamīsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse with Kisāgotamī

164. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho kisāgotamī bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā [P 1.0130] yena andhavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami[M 1.0131], divāvihārāya. Andhavanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māro pāpimā kisāgotamiyā bhikkhuniyā bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo yena kisāgotamī bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kisāgotamiṃ bhikkhuniṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

164. At Sāvatthī. Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī dressed, took her bowl and outer robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms. Having gone for alms in Sāvatthī, after her meal, on returning from her alms-round, she went to the Andhavana for the day’s abiding. Having entered the Andhavana, she sat down at the foot of a certain tree for the day’s abiding. Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī, and desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī; having approached, he addressed the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī with a verse:

“Kiṃ [T 1.0191] nu tvaṃ mataputtāva, ekamāsi rudammukhī;

Vanamajjhagatā ekā, purisaṃ nu gavesasī”ti.

“Why now do you sit alone like one whose son is dead, with a weeping face? Having entered the middle of the forest alone, are you searching for a man?”

Atha kho kisāgotamiyā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “ko nu khvāyaṃ manusso vā amanusso vā gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti? Atha kho kisāgotamiyā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “māro kho ayaṃ pāpimā mama bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti.

Then this thought arose in the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī: ‘Who now is this, a human or a non-human, who recites this verse?’ Then this thought arose in the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī: ‘Indeed, this is Māra the Evil One. Desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in me, and desiring to make me fall away from concentration, he recites this verse.’

Atha kho kisāgotamī bhikkhunī “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

Then the bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī, knowing, ‘This is Māra the Evil One,’ replied to Māra the Evil One with verses:

“Accantaṃ [V 1.0154] mataputtāmhi, purisā etadantikā;

Na socāmi na rodāmi, na taṃ bhāyāmi āvuso.

“Friend, I am completely past having a son who has died; the matter of men is at an end. I do not grieve, nor do I weep. I do not fear you.

“Sabbattha vihatā nandī, tamokkhandho padālito;

Jetvāna maccuno jetvā namucino (sī.) senaṃ, viharāmi anāsavā”ti.

“Everywhere delight is destroyed, the mass of darkness is shattered. Having conquered the army of Death, I dwell free from the taints.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ kisāgotamī bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, ‘The bhikkhunī Kisāgotamī knows me,’ afflicted and dejected, vanished right there.

4. Vijayāsuttaṃ

4. The Discourse with Vijayā

165. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho vijayā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māro pāpimā vijayāya bhikkhuniyā bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo yena vijayā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vijayaṃ bhikkhuniṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

165. At Sāvatthī. Then the bhikkhunī Vijayā, in the morning, having dressed… and sat down at the foot of a certain tree for the day’s abiding. Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the bhikkhunī Vijayā, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:

“Daharā [T 1.0192][M 1.0132][P 1.0131] tvaṃ rūpavatī, ahañca daharo susu;

Pañcaṅgikena turiyena, ehayyebhiramāmase”ti ehi ayye ramāmaseti (sī.).

“You are young and beautiful, and I too am a dark-haired youth; come, venerable lady, let us enjoy ourselves with five-part music.”

Atha kho vijayāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “ko nu khvāyaṃ manusso vā amanusso vā gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti? Atha kho vijayāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “māro kho ayaṃ pāpimā mama bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti. Atha kho vijayā bhikkhunī “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunī Vijayā: “Who now is this, a human or a non-human, who speaks this verse?” Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunī Vijayā: “This is Māra the Evil One, who speaks this verse desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in me, desiring to make me fall away from concentration.” Then the bhikkhunī Vijayā, knowing, “This is Māra the Evil One,” replied to Māra the Evil One with verses:

“Rūpā saddā rasā gandhā, phoṭṭhabbā ca manoramā;

Niyyātayāmi tuyheva, māra nāhaṃ tenatthikā.

“Delightful forms, sounds, scents, tastes, and tactile objects—I hand them over to you, Māra. I have no need of them.

“Iminā [V 1.0155] pūtikāyena, bhindanena pabhaṅgunā;

Aṭṭīyāmi harāyāmi, kāmataṇhā samūhatā.

“With this foul body, which is of a breaking and crumbling nature, I am vexed and ashamed. Craving for sensual pleasures has been uprooted.

“Ye ca rūpūpagā sattā, ye ca arūpaṭṭhāyino āruppaṭṭhāyino (sī. pī.);

Yā ca santā samāpatti, sabbattha vihato tamo”ti.

“Whatever beings have gone to the form realm, and those who are established in the formless, and whatever peaceful attainments there are—in all these, the darkness has been dispelled.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ vijayā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Vijayā knows me,” miserable and dejected, vanished right there.

5. Uppalavaṇṇāsuttaṃ

5. The Discourse with Uppalavaṇṇā

166. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho uppalavaṇṇā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… aññatarasmiṃ supupphitasālarukkhamūle aṭṭhāsi. Atha [T 1.0193] kho māro pāpimā uppalavaṇṇāya bhikkhuniyā bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo yena uppalavaṇṇā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā uppalavaṇṇaṃ bhikkhuniṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

166. At Sāvatthī. Then the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā, having dressed in the morning… stood at the foot of a certain sāla tree in full bloom. Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā, desiring to make her fall away from concentration, approached her and addressed her in verse:

“Supupphitaggaṃ upagamma bhikkhuni,

Ekā tuvaṃ tiṭṭhasi sālamūle;

Na catthi te dutiyā vaṇṇadhātu,

Bāle na tvaṃ bhāyasi dhuttakāna”nti.

“Having approached a sāla tree with a beautifully flowered crest, O bhikkhunī, you stand alone at its root. There is no second like you in beauty. O foolish one, do you not fear the rogues?”

Atha [M 1.0133] kho uppalavaṇṇāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “ko [P 1.0132] nu khvāyaṃ manusso vā amanusso vā gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti? Atha kho uppalavaṇṇāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “māro kho ayaṃ pāpimā mama bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti. Atha kho uppalavaṇṇā bhikkhunī “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā: “Who now is this, a human or a non-human, who speaks this verse?” Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā: “This is Māra the Evil One, who speaks this verse desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in me, and desiring to make me fall away from concentration.” Then the bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā, knowing, “This is Māra the Evil One,” replied to Māra the Evil One with verses:

“Sataṃ [V 1.0156] sahassānipi dhuttakānaṃ,

Idhāgatā tādisakā bhaveyyuṃ;

Lomaṃ na iñjāmi na santasāmi,

Na māra bhāyāmi tamekikāpi.

“Even if a hundred thousand rogues just like you were to come here, I would not stir a single hair, nor would I be terrified. Māra, I do not fear you, even though I am alone.

“Esā antaradhāyāmi, kucchiṃ vā pavisāmi te;

Pakhumantarikāyampi, tiṭṭhantiṃ maṃ na dakkhasi.

“Here I shall disappear, or I shall enter your belly. Even standing between your eyelashes, you will not see me.

“Cittasmiṃ [T 1.0194] vasībhūtāmhi, iddhipādā subhāvitā;

Sabbabandhanamuttāmhi, na taṃ bhāyāmi āvuso”ti.

“I have mastery over my mind, the bases of psychic power are well-developed; I am freed from all bonds. I do not fear you, friend.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ uppalavaṇṇā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā knows me,” miserable and dejected, vanished right there.

6. Cālāsuttaṃ

6. The Discourse with Cālā

167. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho cālā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena cālā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā cālaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu tvaṃ, bhikkhuni, na rocesī”ti? “Jātiṃ khvāhaṃ, āvuso, na rocemī”ti.

167. At Sāvatthī. Then the bhikkhunī Cālā, having dressed in the morning… sat down at the foot of a certain tree for the day's abiding. Then Māra the Evil One approached the bhikkhunī Cālā and said to her: “What is it, bhikkhunī, that you do not approve of?” “Friend, I do not approve of birth.”

“Kiṃ nu jātiṃ na rocesi, jāto kāmāni bhuñjati;

Ko nu taṃ idamādapayi, jātiṃ mā roca mā rocesi (sī. pī.) bhikkhunī”ti.

“Why do you not approve of birth? One who is born enjoys sensual pleasures. Who has persuaded you to this: ‘Bhikkhunī, do not approve of birth’?”

“Jātassa maraṇaṃ hoti, jāto dukkhāni phussati passati (sī. pī.);

Bandhaṃ vadhaṃ pariklesaṃ, tasmā jātiṃ na rocaye.

“For one who is born, there is death; one who is born experiences sufferings: bondage, killing, and affliction. Therefore, I do not approve of birth.

“Buddho [M 1.0134] dhammamadesesi, jātiyā samatikkamaṃ;

Sabbadukkhappahānāya, so maṃ sacce nivesayi.

“The Buddha taught the Dhamma for the overcoming of birth, for the abandoning of all suffering. He has established me in the Truth.

“Ye [V 1.0157][P 1.0133] ca rūpūpagā sattā, ye ca arūpaṭṭhāyino;

Nirodhaṃ appajānantā, āgantāro punabbhava”nti.

“Those beings who have gone to the form realm, and those who are established in the formless—not knowing cessation, they are comers to renewed existence.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ cālā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Cālā knows me,” miserable and dejected, vanished right there.

7. Upacālāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse with Upacālā

168. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 1.0195]. Atha kho upacālā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena upacālā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā upacālaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kattha nu tvaṃ, bhikkhuni, uppajjitukāmā”ti? “Na khvāhaṃ, āvuso, katthaci uppajjitukāmā”ti.

168. At Sāvatthī. Then the bhikkhunī Upacālā, having dressed in the morning… sat down at the foot of a certain tree for the day's abiding. Then Māra the Evil One approached the bhikkhunī Upacālā and said to her: “Where, bhikkhunī, do you wish to be reborn?” “Friend, I do not wish to be reborn anywhere.”

“Tāvatiṃsā ca yāmā ca, tusitā cāpi devatā;

Nimmānaratino devā, ye devā vasavattino;

Tattha cittaṃ paṇidhehi, ratiṃ paccanubhossasī”ti.

“The Tāvatiṃsa and the Yāma gods, the devas in Tusita, the Nimmānaratī gods, and those gods who are Vasavattī—direct your mind there, and you will experience delight.”

“Tāvatiṃsā ca yāmā ca, tusitā cāpi devatā;

Nimmānaratino devā, ye devā vasavattino;

Kāmabandhanabaddhā te, enti māravasaṃ puna.

“The Tāvatiṃsa and the Yāma gods, the devas in Tusita, the Nimmānaratī gods, and those gods who are Vasavattī—they are bound by the bonds of sensual pleasure; they come again under Māra’s sway.

“Sabbo ādīpito sabbova āditto (syā. kaṃ.) loko, sabbo loko padhūpito;

Sabbo pajjalito pajjalito (sabbattha) loko, sabbo loko pakampito.

“The whole world is ablaze, the whole world is filled with smoke; the whole world is aflame, the whole world is trembling.

“Akampitaṃ apajjalitaṃ acalitaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), aputhujjanasevitaṃ;

Agati yattha mārassa, tattha me nirato mano”ti.

“That which is unshaken, not aflame, not frequented by worldlings, where there is no resort for Māra—there my mind delights.”

Atha [V 1.0158] kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ upacālā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Upacālā knows me,” miserable and dejected, vanished right there.

8. Sīsupacālāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse with Sīsupacālā

169. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 1.0135]. Atha kho sīsupacālā sīsūpacālā (sī.) bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā [T 1.0196] …pe… aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena sīsupacālā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā sīsupacālaṃ bhikkhuniṃ etadavoca – “kassa nu tvaṃ, bhikkhuni, pāsaṇḍaṃ rocesī”ti? “Na khvāhaṃ, āvuso, kassaci pāsaṇḍaṃ rocemī”ti.

169. At Sāvatthī. Then the bhikkhunī Sīsupacālā, having dressed in the morning... sat down for the day's abiding at the foot of a certain tree. Then Māra the Evil One approached the bhikkhunī Sīsupacālā and said to her: “Whose sectarian teaching, bhikkhunī, do you approve of?” “Friend, I do not approve of anyone’s sectarian teaching.”

“Kaṃ nu uddissa muṇḍāsi, samaṇī viya dissasi;

Na ca rocesi pāsaṇḍaṃ, kimiva carasi momūhā”ti.

“For whose sake are you shaven-headed? You appear like a female ascetic. Yet you do not approve of any sectarian teaching, so why do you wander about as if utterly deluded?”

“Ito bahiddhā pāsaṇḍā, diṭṭhīsu pasīdanti te;

Na tesaṃ dhammaṃ rocemi, te dhammassa akovidā.

“The sectarians outside this Dispensation are attached to their views. I do not approve of their doctrine; they are not skilled in the Dhamma.

“Atthi [P 1.0134] sakyakule jāto, buddho appaṭipuggalo;

Sabbābhibhū māranudo, sabbatthamaparājito.

“There is one born in the Sakyan clan, a Buddha, an unequalled person, all-surpassing, the dispeller of Māra, unvanquished everywhere.

“Sabbattha mutto asito, sabbaṃ passati cakkhumā;

Sabbakammakkhayaṃ patto, vimutto upadhisaṅkhaye;

So mayhaṃ bhagavā satthā, tassa rocemi sāsana”nti.

“Freed everywhere, unattached, the one with vision who sees all; he has attained the exhaustion of all kamma, and is liberated in the exhaustion of the substrates of existence. That Blessed One is my Teacher; I approve of his instruction.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ sīsupacālā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Sīsupacālā knows me,” miserable and dejected, vanished right there.

9. Selāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse with Selā

170. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0159]. Atha kho selā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māro pāpimā selāya bhikkhuniyā bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo…pe… selaṃ [T 1.0197] bhikkhuniṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

170. At Sāvatthī. Then the bhikkhunī Selā, having dressed in the morning... sat down for the day's abiding at the foot of a certain tree. Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the bhikkhunī Selā... addressed the bhikkhunī Selā in verse:

“Kenidaṃ pakataṃ bimbaṃ, kvanu kvannu (sī. pī.), kvaci (syā. kaṃ. ka.) bimbassa kārako;

Kvanu bimbaṃ samuppannaṃ, kvanu bimbaṃ nirujjhatī”ti.

“By whom was this form made? Who is the maker of the form? Why has this form arisen? Why does this form cease?”

Atha kho selāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “ko nu khvāyaṃ manusso vā amanusso vā gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti? Atha kho selāya bhikkhuniyā [M 1.0136] etadahosi – “māro kho ayaṃ pāpimā mama bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti. Atha kho selā bhikkhunī “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunī Selā: “Who now is this, a human or a non-human, who speaks this verse?” Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhunī Selā: “This is Māra the Evil One, who speaks this verse desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in me, desiring to make me fall away from concentration.” Then the bhikkhunī Selā, knowing, “This is Māra the Evil One,” replied to Māra the Evil One with verses:

“Nayidaṃ attakataṃ nayidaṃ pakataṃ (syā. kaṃ.) bimbaṃ, nayidaṃ parakataṃ nayidaṃ pakataṃ (syā. kaṃ.) aghaṃ;

Hetuṃ paṭicca sambhūtaṃ, hetubhaṅgā nirujjhati.

“This form is not self-made, nor is this misery made by another. It has arisen in dependence on a cause; with the breaking of the cause, it ceases.

“Yathā aññataraṃ bījaṃ, khette vuttaṃ virūhati;

Pathavīrasañcāgamma, sinehañca tadūbhayaṃ.

“Just as a certain seed, sown in a field, sprouts, relying on the earth’s essence and on moisture, relying on both of these.

“Evaṃ khandhā ca dhātuyo, cha ca āyatanā ime;

Hetuṃ paṭicca sambhūtā, hetubhaṅgā nirujjhare”ti.

“Even so, these aggregates, elements, and six sense bases have arisen in dependence on a cause; with the breaking of the cause, they cease.”

Atha kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ selā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Selā knows me,” afflicted and dejected, vanished right there.

10. Vajirāsuttaṃ

10. The Vajirā Sutta

171. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0160]. Atha kho vajirā bhikkhunī pubbaṇhasamayaṃ [T 1.0198] nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā [P 1.0135] yena andhavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Andhavanaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho māro pāpimā vajirāya bhikkhuniyā bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo yena vajirā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vajiraṃ bhikkhuniṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

171. At Sāvatthī. Then, in the morning, the bhikkhunī Vajirā dressed, took her bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms. After wandering for alms in Sāvatthī and returning from her almsround after her meal, she approached the Andhavana for her day's abiding. Having entered the Andhavana, she sat down at the foot of a certain tree for her day's abiding. Then Māra the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in the bhikkhunī Vajirā, and wishing to dislodge her from concentration, approached her. Having approached, he addressed the bhikkhunī Vajirā with a verse:

“Kenāyaṃ pakato satto, kuvaṃ sattassa kārako;

Kuvaṃ satto samuppanno, kuvaṃ satto nirujjhatī”ti.

“By whom is this being made? Who is the maker of the being? Why has the being arisen? Why does the being cease?”

Atha kho vajirāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “ko nu khvāyaṃ manusso vā amanusso vā gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti? Atha kho vajirāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi – “māro kho ayaṃ pāpimā mama bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃsaṃ uppādetukāmo samādhimhā cāvetukāmo gāthaṃ bhāsatī”ti. Atha kho [M 1.0137] vajirā bhikkhunī “māro ayaṃ pāpimā” iti viditvā, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi –

Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Vajirā: “Now who is this that recites the verse? Is it a human or a non-human being?” Then it occurred to the bhikkhunī Vajirā: “This is surely Māra the Evil One, who recites the verse desiring to arouse fear, terror, and horripilation in me, and wishing to dislodge me from concentration.” Then the bhikkhunī Vajirā, having understood, “This is Māra the Evil One,” replied to Māra the Evil One in verses:

“Kiṃ nu sattoti paccesi, māra diṭṭhigataṃ nu te;

Suddhasaṅkhārapuñjoyaṃ, nayidha sattupalabbhati.

“Why, Māra, do you resort to ‘a being’? Is that a speculative view of yours? This is a heap of sheer formations; here no being is found.

“Yathā hi aṅgasambhārā, hoti saddo ratho iti;

Evaṃ khandhesu santesu, hoti sattoti sammuti sammati (syā. kaṃ.).

“Just as from a collection of parts, the term ‘chariot’ comes to be; so too, when the aggregates are present, the convention ‘a being’ occurs.

“Dukkhameva [T 1.0199] hi sambhoti, dukkhaṃ tiṭṭhati veti ca;

Nāññatra dukkhā sambhoti, nāññaṃ dukkhā nirujjhatī”ti.

“For only suffering comes into being; suffering persists and passes away. Nothing other than suffering arises; nothing other than suffering ceases.”

Atha [V 1.0161] kho māro pāpimā “jānāti maṃ vajirā bhikkhunī”ti dukkhī dummano tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, “The bhikkhunī Vajirā knows me,” distressed and dejected, vanished right there.

Bhikkhunīsaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Bhikkhunī Saṃyutta is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Āḷavikā ca somā ca, gotamī vijayā saha;

Uppalavaṇṇā ca cālā, upacālā sīsupacālā ca;

Selā vajirāya te dasāti.

Āḷavikā and Somā, Gotamī along with Vijayā; Uppalavaṇṇā and Cālā, Upacālā and Sīsupacālā; Selā and Vajirā—these are the ten.

6. Brahmasaṃyuttaṃ

6. The Brahma Saṃyutta

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Brahmāyācanasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Request of Brahmā

172. Evaṃ [T 1.0200][V 1.0162][P 1.0136][M 1.0138] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo gambhīro duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo. Ālayarāmā kho panāyaṃ pajā ālayaratā ālayasammuditā. Ālayarāmāya kho pana pajāya ālayaratāya ālayasammuditāya duddasaṃ idaṃ ṭhānaṃ yadidaṃ idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppādo. Idampi kho ṭhānaṃ duddasaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ; pare ca me na ājāneyyuṃ; so mamassa kilamatho, sā mamassa vihesā”ti. Apissu bhagavantaṃ imā anacchariyā gāthāyo paṭibhaṃsu pubbe assutapubbā –

172. Thus have I heard: At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā, on the bank of the Nerañjarā River, at the foot of the Ajapāla banyan tree, right after his full awakening. Then, while the Blessed One was in solitude and seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind: 'This Dhamma that I have attained is profound, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the sphere of reasoning, subtle, to be experienced by the wise. But this generation delights in attachments, takes pleasure in attachments, rejoices in attachments. For a generation delighting in, taking pleasure in, and rejoicing in attachments, this state is hard to see, namely, specific conditionality, dependent origination. And this state is also hard to see: the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all substrates of existence, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna. If I were to teach the Dhamma, and others were not to understand me, that would be wearisome for me, that would be an affliction for me.' Then these amazing verses, unheard before, occurred to the Blessed One:

“Kicchena me adhigataṃ, halaṃ dāni pakāsituṃ;

Rāgadosaparetehi, nāyaṃ dhammo susambudho.

“What I have attained with difficulty, it is not suitable to proclaim it now. This Dhamma is not easily understood by those overcome with lust and hate.

“Paṭisotagāmiṃ [T 1.0201] nipuṇaṃ, gambhīraṃ duddasaṃ aṇuṃ;

Rāgarattā na dakkhanti, tamokhandhena āvuṭā”ti tamokkhandhena āvutāti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

“Going against the stream, subtle, profound, hard to see, and minute; those impassioned with lust, shrouded by the mass of darkness, will not see it.”

Itiha [P 1.0137] bhagavato paṭisañcikkhato appossukkatāya cittaṃ namati, no dhammadesanāya.

Thus, as the Blessed One reflected, his mind inclined toward inaction, not toward teaching the Dhamma.

Atha [V 1.0163] kho brahmuno sahampatissa bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya etadahosi – “nassati vata bho loko, vinassati vata bho loko, yatra hi nāma tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa appossukkatāya cittaṃ namati namissati (?), no dhammadesanāyā”ti. Atha [M 1.0139] kho brahmā sahampati – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ sammiñjitaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi. Atha kho brahmā sahampati ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dakkhiṇajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ pathaviyaṃ nihantvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “desetu, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ, desetu sugato dhammaṃ. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti. Bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro”ti. Idamavoca brahmā sahampati, idaṃ vatvā athāparaṃ etadavoca –

Then Brahmā Sahampati, having known with his own mind the reflection in the Blessed One's mind, thought: 'Alas, the world is perishing! Alas, the world is being destroyed! For the mind of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, inclines toward inaction, not toward teaching the Dhamma.' Then, just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm or bend his outstretched arm, so too did Brahmā Sahampati vanish from the Brahmā world and appear before the Blessed One. Then Brahmā Sahampati arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and inclining his joined palms toward the Blessed One, said this: 'Venerable sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma! Let the Well-Farer teach the Dhamma! There are beings with little dust in their eyes; from not hearing the Dhamma, they are declining. There will be those who understand the Dhamma.' This is what Brahmā Sahampati said. Having said this, he then said further:

“Pāturahosi magadhesu pubbe,

Dhammo asuddho samalehi cintito;

Apāpuretaṃ avāpuretaṃ (sī.) amatassa dvāraṃ,

Suṇantu [T 1.0202] dhammaṃ vimalenānubuddhaṃ.

“Formerly in Magadha there appeared an impure Dhamma, devised by those with defilements. Open this door to the Deathless! Let them hear the Dhamma thoroughly understood by the Stainless One.

“Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito,

Yathāpi passe janataṃ samantato;

Tathūpamaṃ dhammamayaṃ sumedha,

Pāsādamāruyha samantacakkhu;

Sokāvatiṇṇaṃ sokāvakiṇṇaṃ (sī.) janatamapetasoko,

Avekkhassu jātijarābhibhūtaṃ.

“Just as one standing on a mountain peak of solid rock might see the people all around, so too, O one of good wisdom, O all-seeing one, having ascended the palace made of Dhamma, being free from sorrow yourself, look upon the people sunk in sorrow, afflicted by birth and old age.

“Uṭṭhehi vīra vijitasaṅgāma,

Satthavāha anaṇa aṇaṇa (rūpasiddhiṭīkā) vicara loke;

Desassu desetu (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) bhagavā dhammaṃ,

Aññātāro bhavissantī”ti.

“Arise, O hero, victor in battle! O caravan leader, free from debt, wander in the world. O Blessed One, teach the Dhamma! There will be those who understand.”

Atha [P 1.0138] kho bhagavā brahmuno ca ajjhesanaṃ viditvā sattesu ca kāruññataṃ paṭicca buddhacakkhunā [V 1.0164] lokaṃ volokesi. Addasā kho bhagavā buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokento satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye, appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante, appekacce na paralokavajjabhayadassāvine [M 1.0140] dassāvino (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) viharante. Seyyathāpi nāma uppaliniyaṃ vā paduminiyaṃ vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṃ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni anto nimuggaposīni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā [T 1.0203] padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni samodakaṃ ṭhitāni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakā accuggamma ṭhitāni tiṭṭhanti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) anupalittāni udakena; evameva bhagavā buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokento addasa satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye, appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante, appekacce na paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante. Disvāna brahmānaṃ sahampatiṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, having understood Brahmā's request and on account of his compassion for beings, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. As the Blessed One surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, he saw beings with little dust and with much dust; with keen faculties and with dull faculties; with good qualities and with bad qualities; easy to instruct and hard to instruct; and some dwelling who see danger in the faults of the next world. Just as in a pond of blue, red, or white lotuses, some lotuses are born in the water, grow up in the water, and do not rise above the water but thrive while submerged; some lotuses are born in the water, grow up in the water, and stand at the water's surface; and some lotuses are born in the water, grow up in the water, and stand risen above the water, unstained by it; so too, as the Blessed One surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, he saw beings with little dust and with much dust; with keen faculties and with dull faculties; with good qualities and with bad qualities; easy to instruct and hard to instruct; and some dwelling who see danger in the faults of the next world. Having seen this, he replied to Brahmā Sahampati in verse:

“Apārutā tesaṃ amatassa dvārā,

Ye sotavanto pamuñcantu saddhaṃ;

Vihiṃsasaññī paguṇaṃ na bhāsiṃ,

Dhammaṃ paṇītaṃ manujesu brahme”ti.

“Opened for them are the doors to the Deathless; let those with ears release their faith. O Brahmā, perceiving it as a vexation, I did not speak this excellent and sublime Dhamma among humans.”

Atha kho brahmā sahampati “katāvakāso khomhi bhagavatā dhammadesanāyā”ti bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then Brahmā Sahampati, thinking, 'I have been granted the opportunity by the Blessed One for the teaching of the Dhamma,' paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and vanished right there.

2. Gāravasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Reverence

173. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha [P 1.0139] kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “dukkhaṃ kho agāravo viharati appatisso, kaṃ nu khvāhaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā garukatvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) upanissāya vihareyya”nti?

173. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā, on the bank of the river Nerañjarā, at the foot of the Goatherd's Banyan Tree, newly fully enlightened. Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in his mind: 'It is painful to live without reverence and deference. What ascetic or brahmin could I honor, respect, and live in dependence upon?'

Atha [M 1.0141] kho bhagavato etadahosi – “aparipuṇṇassa kho sīlakkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ[T 1.0204][V 1.0165]. Na kho panāhaṃ passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya attanā sīlasampannataraṃ aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā, yamahaṃ sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ.

Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: 'For the fulfillment of an unfulfilled aggregate of virtue, I would live in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin, honoring and respecting him. But I do not see in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, devas and humans, any other ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in virtue than myself, whom I could honor, respect, and live in dependence upon.'

“Aparipuṇṇassa kho samādhikkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ. Na kho panāhaṃ passāmi sadevake loke…pe… attanā samādhisampannataraṃ aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā, yamahaṃ sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ.

'For the fulfillment of an unfulfilled aggregate of concentration, I would live in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin, honoring and respecting him. But I do not see in this world with its devas… and so on… any other ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in concentration than myself, whom I could honor, respect, and live in dependence upon.'

“Aparipuṇṇassa paññākkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ. Na kho panāhaṃ passāmi sadevake…pe… attanā paññāsampannataraṃ aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā, yamahaṃ sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ.

'For the fulfillment of an unfulfilled aggregate of wisdom, I would live in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin, honoring and respecting him. But I do not see in this world with its devas… and so on… any other ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in wisdom than myself, whom I could honor, respect, and live in dependence upon.'

“Aparipuṇṇassa kho vimuttikkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ. Na kho panāhaṃ passāmi sadevake…pe… attanā vimuttisampannataraṃ aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā, yamahaṃ sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ.

“It would be well if, for the fulfillment of the as-yet-unfulfilled aggregate of liberation, I were to dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin, honoring and respecting him. But in this world with its devas... and so on... I do not see any other ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in liberation than myself, whom I could honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on.”

“Aparipuṇṇassa kho vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā [T 1.0205] sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ. Na kho panāhaṃ passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya attanā vimuttiñāṇadassanasampannataraṃ aññaṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā, yamahaṃ sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yvāyaṃ dhammo mayā abhisambuddho tameva dhammaṃ sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihareyya”nti.

“It would be well if, for the fulfillment of the as-yet-unfulfilled aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, I were to dwell in dependence on another ascetic or brahmin, honoring and respecting him. But in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, I do not see any other ascetic or brahmin more accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation than myself, whom I could honor, respect, and dwell in dependence on. What if I were to dwell in dependence on this very Dhamma to which I have fully awakened, honoring and respecting it?”

Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – brahmaloke [V 1.0166] antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi. Atha kho brahmā sahampati ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “evametaṃ[P 1.0140], bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata! Yepi te, bhante, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tepi [M 1.0142] bhagavanto dhammaññeva sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya vihariṃsu; yepi te, bhante, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā tepi bhagavanto dhammaññeva sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharissanti. Bhagavāpi, bhante, etarahi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dhammaññeva sakkatvā garuṃ katvā upanissāya viharatū”ti. Idamavoca brahmā sahampati, idaṃ vatvā athāparaṃ etadavoca –

Then Brahmā Sahampati, having known with his mind the thought in the Blessed One’s mind—just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm or bend his stretched-out arm—vanished from the Brahmā world and appeared before the Blessed One. Then Brahmā Sahampati arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined hands in reverential salutation toward the Blessed One, and said to him: “So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Sugata! Venerable Sir, those who were Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the past—those Blessed Ones also dwelt in dependence on the Dhamma itself, honoring and respecting it. Venerable Sir, those who will be Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the future—those Blessed Ones also will dwell in dependence on the Dhamma itself, honoring and respecting it. And may the Blessed One also, Venerable Sir, who is now the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwell in dependence on the Dhamma itself, honoring and respecting it.” This is what Brahmā Sahampati said. Having said this, he then said further:

“Ye [T 1.0206] ca atītā sambuddhā, ye ca buddhā anāgatā;

Yo cetarahi sambuddho, bahūnaṃ bahunnaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) sokanāsano.

“Those Perfectly Enlightened Ones who were in the past, and those Buddhas who will be in the future, and the Perfectly Enlightened One who is now, the dispeller of sorrow for many.”

“Sabbe saddhammagaruno, vihaṃsu vihariṃsu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) viharanti ca;

Tathāpi viharissanti, esā buddhāna dhammatā.

“All, revering the good Dhamma, have dwelt, are dwelling, and so too will they dwell. This is the nature of the Buddhas.”

“Tasmā hi attakāmena atthakāmena (sī. pī. ka.), mahattamabhikaṅkhatā;

Saddhammo garukātabbo, saraṃ buddhāna sāsana”nti.

“Therefore, one who desires their own welfare, aspiring to greatness, should revere the good Dhamma, remembering the teaching of the Buddhas.”

3. Brahmadevasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse to Brahmadeva

174. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarissā brāhmaṇiyā brahmadevo nāma putto bhagavato santike agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti.

174. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, a certain brahmin woman’s son, named Brahmadeva, had gone forth from the household life into homelessness under the Blessed One.

Atha kho āyasmā brahmadevo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti[V 1.0167], vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā brahmadevo arahataṃ ahosi.

Then the Venerable Brahmadeva, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, before long attained that supreme consummation of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life, and he dwelt therein. He understood: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.” And the Venerable Brahmadeva became one of the arahants.

Atha kho āyasmā brahmadevo pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāno yena sakamātu nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Tena [P 1.0141] kho pana [T 1.0207] samayena āyasmato brahmadevassa mātā brāhmaṇī brahmuno āhutiṃ niccaṃ paggaṇhāti[M 1.0143]. Atha kho brahmuno sahampatissa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmato brahmadevassa mātā brāhmaṇī brahmuno āhutiṃ niccaṃ paggaṇhāti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ taṃ upasaṅkamitvā saṃvejeyya”nti. Atha kho brahmā sahampati – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – brahmaloke antarahito āyasmato brahmadevassa mātu nivesane pāturahosi. Atha kho brahmā sahampati vehāsaṃ ṭhito āyasmato brahmadevassa mātaraṃ brāhmaṇiṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then, in the morning, the Venerable Brahmadeva dressed, and taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms. Wandering for alms from house to house in Sāvatthī, he approached his own mother’s residence. Now at that time, the Venerable Brahmadeva’s mother, a brahmin woman, was regularly making an offering to Brahmā. Then it occurred to Brahmā Sahampati: “This brahmin woman, the mother of the Venerable Brahmadeva, is regularly making an offering to Brahmā. What if I were to approach her and inspire a sense of spiritual urgency in her?” Then Brahmā Sahampati—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm—disappeared from the Brahmā world and appeared in the residence of the Venerable Brahmadeva’s mother. Standing in the air, Brahmā Sahampati addressed the brahmin woman, the mother of the Venerable Brahmadeva, in verse:

“Dūre ito brāhmaṇi brahmaloko,

Yassāhutiṃ paggaṇhāsi niccaṃ;

Netādiso brāhmaṇi brahmabhakkho,

Kiṃ jappasi brahmapathaṃ ajānaṃ ajānantī (sī. pī. ka.).

“Far from here, O brahmin woman, is the Brahmā world, to which you regularly make an offering. Such is not the food of Brahmā, O brahmin woman. Not knowing the path to Brahmā, why do you murmur prayers?”

“Eso hi te brāhmaṇi brahmadevo,

Nirūpadhiko atidevapatto;

Akiñcano bhikkhu anaññaposī,

Yo te so te so (sī. pī.), yo te sa (?) piṇḍāya gharaṃ paviṭṭho.

“This Brahmadeva of yours, O brahmin woman, is without attachments, having surpassed the devas. A bhikkhu with nothing, supporting no other, he has entered your house for alms.”

“Āhuneyyo vedagu bhāvitatto,

Narānaṃ devānañca dakkhiṇeyyo;

Bāhitvā pāpāni anūpalitto,

Ghāsesanaṃ [T 1.0208] iriyati sītibhūto.

“Worthy of offerings, a master of knowledge, with a developed self, worthy of the oblations of humans and devas; having cast off all evils, he is unsullied. He fares in search of sustenance, having become cool.”

“Na [V 1.0168] tassa pacchā na puratthamatthi,

Santo vidhūmo anigho nirāso;

Nikkhittadaṇḍo tasathāvaresu,

So tyāhutiṃ bhuñjatu aggapiṇḍaṃ.

“For him there is no after, no before; peaceful, smokeless, untroubled, without longing. Having laid down the rod toward beings frail and firm, let him partake of your offering, the choicest alms.”

“Visenibhūto upasantacitto,

Nāgova danto carati anejo;

Bhikkhu susīlo suvimuttacitto,

So tyāhutiṃ bhuñjatu aggapiṇḍaṃ.

“With his army dispersed, with a pacified mind, like a tamed great elephant he fares, free from craving. A bhikkhu of good virtue, with a well-liberated mind, let him partake of your offering, the choicest alms.”

“Tasmiṃ [M 1.0144] pasannā avikampamānā,

Patiṭṭhapehi [P 1.0142] dakkhiṇaṃ dakkhiṇeyye;

Karohi puññaṃ sukhamāyatikaṃ,

Disvā muniṃ brāhmaṇi oghatiṇṇa”nti.

“With unwavering confidence in him, establish your offering in one worthy of offerings. O brahmin woman, having seen the sage who has crossed the flood, make merit that will result in future happiness.”

“Tasmiṃ pasannā avikampamānā,

Patiṭṭhapesi dakkhiṇaṃ dakkhiṇeyye;

Akāsi puññaṃ sukhamāyatikaṃ,

Disvā muniṃ brāhmaṇī oghatiṇṇa”nti.

In him, one worthy of offerings, the brahmin woman, confident and unwavering, established her offering. Having seen the sage who had crossed over the flood, she made merit that would result in future happiness.

4. Bakabrahmasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Baka the Brahmā

175. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bakassa brahmuno evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ [T 1.0209] diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – “idaṃ niccaṃ, idaṃ dhuvaṃ, idaṃ sassataṃ, idaṃ kevalaṃ, idaṃ acavanadhammaṃ, idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, ito ca panaññaṃ uttariṃ uttariṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) nissaraṇaṃ natthī”ti.

175. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, to Baka the Brahmā such a pernicious wrong view had arisen: 'This is permanent, this is stable, this is eternal, this is complete, this is not subject to passing away. For indeed, herein one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn. And there is no other escape beyond this.'

Atha [V 1.0169] kho bhagavā bakassa brahmuno cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – jetavane antarahito tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahosi. Addasā kho bako brahmā bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ehi kho mārisa, svāgataṃ te, mārisa! Cirassaṃ kho mārisa! Imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Idañhi, mārisa, niccaṃ, idaṃ dhuvaṃ, idaṃ sassataṃ, idaṃ kevalaṃ, idaṃ acavanadhammaṃ, idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati. Ito ca panaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ natthī”ti.

Then the Blessed One, having known with his mind the thought in Baka the Brahmā’s mind—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm—vanished from Jeta’s Grove and appeared in that brahmā world. Baka the Brahmā saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he said this to the Blessed One: 'Come, good sir! Welcome to you, good sir! It has been a long time, good sir, since you have made this occasion, that is, for coming here. For this, good sir, is permanent, this is stable, this is eternal, this is complete, this is not subject to passing away. For indeed, herein one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn. And there is no other escape beyond this.'

Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā bakaṃ brahmānaṃ etadavoca – “avijjāgato vata, bho, bako brahmā; avijjāgato vata, bho, bako brahmā. Yatra [M 1.0145] hi nāma aniccaṃyeva samānaṃ niccanti vakkhati, adhuvaṃyeva samānaṃ dhuvanti vakkhati, asassataṃyeva samānaṃ sassatanti vakkhati, akevalaṃyeva [P 1.0143] samānaṃ kevalanti vakkhati, cavanadhammaṃyeva samānaṃ acavanadhammanti vakkhati. Yattha ca pana jāyati ca jīyati ca mīyati ca cavati ca upapajjati ca, tañca tathā vakkhati – ‘idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na [T 1.0210] upapajjati’. Santañca panaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇaṃ, ‘natthaññaṃ uttari nissaraṇa’nti vakkhatī”ti.

When this was said, the Blessed One said this to Baka the Brahmā: 'Indeed, Baka the Brahmā is overcome by ignorance! Indeed, Baka the Brahmā is overcome by ignorance! In that, being impermanent, he says "it is permanent"; being unstable, he says "it is stable"; being non-eternal, he says "it is eternal"; being incomplete, he says "it is complete"; being subject to passing away, he says "it is not subject to passing away." And where one is born, ages, dies, passes away, and is reborn, of that he speaks thus: "For indeed, herein one is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and is not reborn." And there being another, higher escape, he says: "There is no other, higher escape."

“Dvāsattati gotama puññakammā,

Vasavattino jātijaraṃ atītā;

Ayamantimā vedagū brahmupapatti,

Asmābhijappanti janā anekā”ti.

“Seventy-two, O Gotama, are we of meritorious deeds, wielding power, having transcended birth and aging. This is the final brahma-birth for one who has reached the end of knowledge; many people aspire to us.”

“Appañhi etaṃ na hi dīghamāyu,

Yaṃ tvaṃ baka maññasi dīghamāyuṃ;

Sataṃ sahassānaṃ sahassāna (syā. kaṃ.) nirabbudānaṃ,

Āyuṃ pajānāmi tavāhaṃ brahme”ti.

“Brief indeed is that life, not long, which you, Baka, consider to be a long life. I know your lifespan, O Brahmā, to be a hundred thousand nirabbudas.”

“Anantadassī bhagavāhamasmi,

Jātijaraṃ sokamupātivatto;

Kiṃ [V 1.0170] me purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ,

Ācikkha me taṃ yamahaṃ vijaññā”ti.

“You claim, ‘I am the Blessed One, the one of infinite vision, who has passed beyond birth, aging, and sorrow.’ What, then, was my ancient practice of vows and virtue? Declare it to me, so that I may know.”

“Yaṃ tvaṃ apāyesi bahū manusse,

Pipāsite ghammani samparete;

Taṃ te purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ,

Suttappabuddhova anussarāmi.

“That you gave drink to many people, thirsty and afflicted by the summer heat—that was your ancient practice of vows and virtue, which I recollect as one awakened from sleep.

“Yaṃ eṇikūlasmiṃ janaṃ gahītaṃ,

Amocayī gayhakaṃ nīyamānaṃ;

Taṃ [T 1.0211] te purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ,

Suttappabuddhova anussarāmi.

“That you freed the people seized on the bank of the Eṇī, captives who were being led away—that was your ancient practice of vows and virtue, which I recollect as one awakened from sleep.

“Gaṅgāya [M 1.0146] sotasmiṃ gahītanāvaṃ,

Luddena nāgena manussakamyā;

Pamocayittha balasā pasayha,

Taṃ te purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ,

Suttappabuddhova anussarāmi.

“That in the Ganges’ current, a boat seized by a fierce nāga with a desire for humans, you released with strength, having overpowered it by force—that was your ancient practice of vows and virtue, which I recollect as one awakened from sleep.

“Kappo [P 1.0144] ca te baddhacaro ahosiṃ,

Sambuddhimantaṃ sambuddhivantaṃ (bahūsu) vatinaṃ amaññi;

Taṃ te purāṇaṃ vatasīlavattaṃ,

Suttappabuddhova anussarāmī”ti.

“And I was your attendant, Kappa, and I considered you one of good wisdom, endowed with vows. That was your ancient practice of vows and virtue, which I recollect as one awakened from sleep.”

“Addhā pajānāsi mametamāyuṃ,

Aññepi aññampi (sī. pī.) jānāsi tathā hi buddho;

Tathā hi tyāyaṃ jalitānubhāvo,

Obhāsayaṃ tiṭṭhati brahmaloka”nti.

“Surely you know this lifespan of mine, and you know other things as well, for you are the Buddha. And so this blazing power of yours stands illuminating the brahma-world.”

5. Aññatarabrahmasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse with a Certain Brahmā

176. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0171]. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa brahmuno evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti – “natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo idha āgaccheyyā”ti. Atha [T 1.0212] kho bhagavā tassa brahmuno cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso…pe… tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahosi. Atha kho bhagavā tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṃ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā.

176. At Sāvatthī. At that time, to a certain Brahmā such a pernicious view had arisen: “There is no ascetic or brahmin who can come here.” Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thought-process in that Brahmā’s mind—just as a strong man might… and so on…—appeared in that Brahmā-world. The Blessed One then sat cross-legged in the air above that Brahmā, having entered the attainment of the fire element.

Atha kho āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa etadahosi – “kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharatī”ti? Addasā kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno mahāmoggalāno (ka.) bhagavantaṃ dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṃ pallaṅkena nisinnaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpannaṃ. Disvāna – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – jetavane antarahito tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahosi. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno [M 1.0147] puratthimaṃ disaṃ nissāya upanissāya (sī.) tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṃ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā nīcataraṃ bhagavato.

Then it occurred to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: “Where is the Blessed One dwelling now?” With his divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna saw the Blessed One seated cross-legged in the air above that Brahmā, having entered the attainment of the fire element. Having seen him—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, so too—he vanished from Jeta’s Grove and appeared in that Brahmā-world. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, taking up a position in the eastern direction, sat cross-legged in the air above that Brahmā, having entered the attainment of the fire element, lower than the Blessed One.

Atha kho āyasmato mahākassapassa etadahosi – “kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharatī”ti? Addasā kho āyasmā mahākassapo bhagavantaṃ dibbena cakkhunā…pe… disvāna – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso…pe… evameva – jetavane [P 1.0145] antarahito tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahosi. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ nissāya tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṃ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā nīcataraṃ bhagavato.

Then it occurred to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “Where is the Blessed One dwelling now?” With his divine eye, the Venerable Mahākassapa saw the Blessed One… and so on… Having seen him—just as a strong man might… and so on… so too—he vanished from Jeta’s Grove and appeared in that Brahmā-world. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa, relying on the southern direction, sat cross-legged in the air above that Brahmā, having entered the attainment of the fire element, lower than the Blessed One.

Atha [T 1.0213] kho āyasmato mahākappinassa etadahosi – “kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharatī”ti? Addasā kho āyasmā mahākappino bhagavantaṃ dibbena cakkhunā…pe… tejodhātuṃ samāpannaṃ. Disvāna – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso…pe… evameva – jetavane antarahito tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahosi. Atha kho āyasmā mahākappino pacchimaṃ disaṃ nissāya tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṃ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā nīcataraṃ bhagavato.

Then it occurred to the Venerable Mahākappina: “Where is the Blessed One dwelling now?” With his divine eye, the Venerable Mahākappina saw the Blessed One… and so on… having entered the attainment of the fire element. Having seen him—just as a strong man might… and so on… so too—he vanished from Jeta’s Grove and appeared in that Brahmā-world. Then the Venerable Mahākappina, relying on the western direction, sat cross-legged in the air above that Brahmā, having entered the attainment of the fire element, lower than the Blessed One.

Atha [V 1.0172] kho āyasmato anuruddhassa etadahosi – “kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharatī”ti? Addasā kho āyasmā anuruddho…pe… tejodhātuṃ samāpannaṃ. Disvāna – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso…pe… tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahosi. Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho uttaraṃ disaṃ nissāya tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṃ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā nīcataraṃ bhagavato.

Then it occurred to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Where is the Blessed One dwelling now?” The Venerable Anuruddha saw… and so on… the Blessed One seated, having entered the attainment of the fire element. Having seen him—just as a strong man might… and so on…—he appeared in that Brahmā-world. Then the Venerable Anuruddha, relying on the northern direction, sat cross-legged in the air above that Brahmā, having entered the attainment of the fire element, lower than the Blessed One.

Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṃ brahmānaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed that Brahmā with a verse:

“Ajjāpi te āvuso sā diṭṭhi, yā te diṭṭhi pure ahu;

Passasi vītivattantaṃ, brahmaloke pabhassara”nti.

“Friend, do you still today hold that view, the same view you held before? Do you see the one who has surpassed, radiant in the Brahmā-world?”

“Na me mārisa sā diṭṭhi, yā me diṭṭhi pure ahu;

Passāmi vītivattantaṃ, brahmaloke pabhassaraṃ;

Svāhaṃ ajja kathaṃ vajjaṃ, ahaṃ niccomhi sassato”ti.

“Good sir, I do not hold that view, the view I held before. I see the one who has surpassed, radiant in the Brahmā-world. How could I say today, ‘I am permanent, I am everlasting’?”

Atha [T 1.0214][M 1.0148] kho bhagavā taṃ brahmānaṃ saṃvejetvā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – tasmiṃ brahmaloke antarahito jetavane pāturahosi. Atha kho so brahmā aññataraṃ brahmapārisajjaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, mārisa, yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘atthi nu kho, mārisa moggallāna, aññepi tassa bhagavato sāvakā evaṃmahiddhikā evaṃmahānubhāvā[P 1.0146]; seyyathāpi bhavaṃ moggallāno kassapo kappino anuruddho’”ti? “Evaṃ, mārisā”ti kho so brahmapārisajjo tassa brahmuno paṭissutvā yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – “atthi nu kho, mārisa moggallāna, aññepi tassa bhagavato sāvakā evaṃmahiddhikā evaṃmahānubhāvā; seyyathāpi bhavaṃ moggallāno kassapo kappino anuruddho”ti? Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṃ brahmapārisajjaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, having inspired a sense of urgency in that Brahmā—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm, so too—vanished from that Brahmā-world and reappeared in Jeta’s Grove. Then that Brahmā addressed a certain Brahmā from his retinue: “Come, good sir, go to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and, having approached him, say this to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: ‘Good Moggallāna, are there other disciples of that Blessed One who are as powerful and mighty as the venerable Moggallāna, Kassapa, Kappina, and Anuruddha?’” “Yes, good sir,” that Brahmā from the retinue replied in assent to that Brahmā and approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna: “Good Moggallāna, are there other disciples of that Blessed One who are as powerful and mighty as the venerable Moggallāna, Kassapa, Kappina, and Anuruddha?” Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed that Brahmā from the retinue with a verse:

“Tevijjā [V 1.0173] iddhipattā ca, cetopariyāyakovidā;

Khīṇāsavā arahanto, bahū buddhassa sāvakā”ti.

“Endowed with the threefold knowledge, attained to psychic power, skilled in comprehending the minds of others, with taints destroyed, arahants—many are the disciples of the Buddha.”

Atha [T 1.0215] kho so brahmapārisajjo āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā yena so brahmā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ brahmānaṃ etadavoca – “āyasmā mārisa, mahāmoggallāno evamāha –

Then that Brahmā from the retinue, having delighted in and rejoiced at the words of the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, approached that Brahmā. Having approached, he said this to that Brahmā: “Revered sir, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna says this:

“Tevijjā iddhipattā ca, cetopariyāyakovidā;

Khīṇāsavā arahanto, bahū buddhassa sāvakā”ti.

“Endowed with the threefold knowledge, attained to psychic power, skilled in comprehending the minds of others, with taints destroyed, arahants—many are the disciples of the Buddha.”

Idamavoca so brahmapārisajjo. Attamano ca so brahmā tassa brahmapārisajjassa bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

This is what that Brahmā from the retinue said. And that Brahmā, being pleased, delighted in the words of that Brahmā from the retinue.

6. Brahmalokasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Brahmā World

177. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno. Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso [M 1.0149] ca paccekabrahmā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṃ dvārabāhaṃ paccekadvārabāhaṃ (pī. ka.) upanissāya aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā suddhāvāsaṃ paccekabrahmānaṃ etadavoca – “akālo kho tāva, mārisa, bhagavantaṃ payirupāsituṃ; divāvihāragato bhagavā paṭisallīno ca. Asuko ca brahmaloko iddho ceva phīto ca, brahmā ca tatra pamādavihāraṃ viharati. Āyāma, mārisa, yena so brahmaloko tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ brahmānaṃ saṃvejeyyāmā”ti. “Evaṃ[P 1.0147], mārisā”ti kho suddhāvāso paccekabrahmā subrahmuno paccekabrahmuno paccassosi.

177. At Sāvatthī. At that time, the Blessed One was dwelling for the day in seclusion. Then the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā and the Paccekabrahmā Suddhāvāsa approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they stood, each leaning against a doorpost. Then the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā said this to the Paccekabrahmā Suddhāvāsa: 'Friend, it is not yet the right time to attend upon the Blessed One; the Blessed One is dwelling for the day and is in seclusion. And there is a certain Brahmā world, prosperous and flourishing, and the Brahmā there dwells in heedlessness. Come, friend, let us approach that Brahmā world. Having approached, let us stir that Brahmā to a sense of urgency.' 'So be it, friend,' the Paccekabrahmā Suddhāvāsa assented to the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā.

Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā [T 1.0216] suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso…pe… evameva – bhagavato purato antarahitā tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahesuṃ. Addasā kho so brahmā te brahmāno dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna te brahmāno etadavoca – “handa kuto nu tumhe, mārisā, āgacchathā”ti? “Āgatā kho mayaṃ, mārisa, amha tassa bhagavato [V 1.0174] santikā arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Gaccheyyāsi pana tvaṃ, mārisa, tassa bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti?

Then the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā and the Paccekabrahmā Suddhāvāsa—just as a strong man might… and so on… in the same way—vanished from before the Blessed One and reappeared in that Brahma world. That Brahmā saw those Brahmās coming from afar. Having seen them, he said this to those Brahmās: 'Well now, friends, from where have you come?' 'We have come, friend, from the presence of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Would you, friend, go to attend upon that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One?'

Evaṃ vutto evaṃ vutte (sī. syā. kaṃ.) kho so brahmā taṃ vacanaṃ anadhivāsento sahassakkhattuṃ attānaṃ abhinimminitvā subrahmānaṃ paccekabrahmānaṃ etadavoca – “passasi me no tvaṃ, mārisa, evarūpaṃ iddhānubhāva”nti? “Passāmi kho tyāhaṃ, mārisa, evarūpaṃ iddhānubhāva”nti. “So khvāhaṃ, mārisa, evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo kassa aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā upaṭṭhānaṃ gamissāmī”ti?

When this was said, that Brahmā, not enduring that statement, created a thousand forms of himself and said this to the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā: 'Do you not see, friend, such psychic power and might of mine?' 'I do see, friend, such psychic power and might of yours.' 'I, friend, being so powerful and so mighty, to what other ascetic or brahmin should I go to attend upon?'

Atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā dvisahassakkhattuṃ attānaṃ abhinimminitvā taṃ brahmānaṃ etadavoca – “passasi me no tvaṃ, mārisa, evarūpaṃ iddhānubhāva”nti? “Passāmi kho tyāhaṃ, mārisa, evarūpaṃ iddhānubhāva”nti. “Tayā ca kho, mārisa, mayā ca sveva bhagavā mahiddhikataro ceva mahānubhāvataro ca. Gaccheyyāsi tvaṃ, mārisa, tassa bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti? Atha [T 1.0217] kho so brahmā subrahmānaṃ paccekabrahmānaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā, having created two thousand forms of himself, said this to that Brahmā: 'Do you not see, friend, such psychic power and might of mine?' 'I do see, friend, such psychic power and might of yours.' 'But, friend, that Blessed One is more powerful and more mighty than you and I. You should go, friend, to attend upon that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.' Then that Brahmā addressed the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā with a verse:

“Tayo [M 1.0150][P 1.0148] supaṇṇā caturo ca haṃsā,

Byagghīnisā pañcasatā ca jhāyino;

Tayidaṃ vimānaṃ jalate ca jalateva (pī. ka.) brahme,

Obhāsayaṃ uttarassaṃ disāya”nti.

“Three hundred Garuḍas and four hundred haṃsas, and five hundred tiger-like forms of me, the meditator; this mansion of mine blazes, O Brahmā, illuminating the northern direction.”

“Kiñcāpi te taṃ jalate vimānaṃ,

Obhāsayaṃ uttarassaṃ disāyaṃ;

Rūpe raṇaṃ disvā sadā pavedhitaṃ,

Tasmā na rūpe ramatī sumedho”ti.

“Though that mansion of yours blazes, illuminating the northern direction, having seen the conflict in form, ever agitated, the wise one therefore does not delight in form.”

Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā taṃ brahmānaṃ saṃvejetvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu[V 1.0175]. Agamāsi ca kho so brahmā aparena samayena bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassāti.
