Then the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā and the Paccekabrahmā Suddhāvāsa, having stirred that Brahmā to a sense of urgency, vanished right there. And that Brahmā, at a later time, did indeed go to attend upon the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

7. Kokālikasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Kokālika

178. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno. Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṃ dvārabāhaṃ nissāya aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā kokālikaṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha [T 1.0218] bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

178. At Sāvatthī. At that time the Blessed One was dwelling in seclusion for the day. Then the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā and the Paccekabrahmā Suddhāvāsa approached the Blessed One; having approached, they each stood leaning against a doorpost. Then the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā, concerning the bhikkhu Kokālika, recited this verse in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Appameyyaṃ paminanto, kodha vidvā vikappaye;

Appameyyaṃ pamāyinaṃ, nivutaṃ taṃ maññe puthujjana”nti.

“Measuring the immeasurable, what wise person here would make a judgment? I consider that common person who measures the immeasurable to be shrouded.”

8. Katamodakatissasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Katamodakatissa

179. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno. Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṃ dvārabāhaṃ nissāya aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha kho suddhāvāso paccekabrahmā katamodakatissakaṃ katamorakatissakaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.) bhikkhuṃ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

179. At Sāvatthī. At that time the Blessed One was dwelling in seclusion for the day. Then the Paccekabrahmā Subrahmā and the Paccekabrahmā Suddhāvāsa approached the Blessed One; having approached, they each stood leaning against a doorpost. Then the Paccekabrahmā Suddhāvāsa, concerning the bhikkhu Katamodakatissaka, recited this verse in the Blessed One’s presence:

“Appameyyaṃ [M 1.0151][P 1.0149] paminanto, kodha vidvā vikappaye;

Appameyyaṃ pamāyinaṃ, nivutaṃ taṃ maññe akissava”nti.

“Measuring the immeasurable, what wise person here would make a judgment? I consider one who measures the immeasurable to be shrouded and unwise.”

9. Turūbrahmasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Turū Brahmā

180. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena kokāliko bhikkhu ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho turū tudu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) paccekabrahmā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena kokāliko bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vehāsaṃ [V 1.0176] ṭhito kokālikaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “pasādehi, kokālika, sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti. “Kosi tvaṃ, āvuso”ti? “Ahaṃ turū paccekabrahmā”ti. “Nanu tvaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā [T 1.0219] anāgāmī byākato, atha kiñcarahi idhāgato? Passa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha”nti.

180. At Sāvatthī. At that time the bhikkhu Kokālika was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. Then, when the night was far advanced, the Paccekabrahmā Turū, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta Grove, approached the bhikkhu Kokālika. Standing in the air, he said to the bhikkhu Kokālika: “Kokālika, generate confidence in your mind towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are amiable.” “Who are you, friend?” “I am the Paccekabrahmā Turū.” “Friend, were you not declared a non-returner by the Blessed One? Then why have you come here? See how great this offense of yours is!”

“Purisassa hi jātassa, kuṭhārī dudhārī (syā. kaṃ. ka.) jāyate mukhe;

Yāya chindati attānaṃ, bālo dubbhāsitaṃ bhaṇaṃ.

“For a person, at birth, an axe is born in his mouth, with which the fool cuts himself by speaking ill-spoken words.

“Yo nindiyaṃ pasaṃsati,

Taṃ vā nindati yo pasaṃsiyo;

Vicināti mukhena so kaliṃ,

Kalinā tena sukhaṃ na vindati.

“He who praises the blameworthy, or blames the praiseworthy, gathers demerit with his mouth; through that demerit he finds no happiness.

“Appamattako ayaṃ kali,

Yo akkhesu dhanaparājayo;

Sabbassāpi sahāpi attanā,

Ayameva mahantataro kali;

Yo sugatesu manaṃ padosaye.

“Small is this demerit—the loss of wealth at dice, along with all one’s possessions and oneself. But this is a far greater demerit: to corrupt the mind towards the Well-Gone Ones.

“Sataṃ sahassānaṃ nirabbudānaṃ,

Chattiṃsati pañca ca abbudāni;

Yamariyagarahī yamariye garahī (syā. kaṃ.), yamariyaṃ garahaṃ (ka.) nirayaṃ upeti,

Vācaṃ manañca paṇidhāya pāpaka”nti.

“For one hundred thousand nirabbudas, and for thirty-six and five abbudas, the reviler of noble ones goes to hell, having directed evil speech and mind.”

10. Kokālikasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Kokālika

181. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 1.0152]. Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[P 1.0150]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho kokāliko bhikkhu [V 1.0177] bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “pāpicchā, bhante, sāriputtamoggallānā pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā”ti. Evaṃ [T 1.0220] vutte, bhagavā kokālikaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “mā hevaṃ, kokālika, avaca; mā hevaṃ, kokālika, avaca. Pasādehi, kokālika, sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti. Dutiyampi kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiñcāpi me, bhante, bhagavā saddhāyiko paccayiko; atha kho pāpicchāva bhante, sāriputtamoggallānā pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā”ti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā kokālikaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “mā hevaṃ, kokālika, avaca; mā hevaṃ, kokālika, avaca. Pasādehi, kokālika, sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti. Tatiyampi kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiñcāpi…pe… icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā”ti. Tatiyampi kho bhagavā kokālikaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “mā hevaṃ…pe… pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti.

181. At Sāvatthī. Then the bhikkhu Kokālika approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the bhikkhu Kokālika said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have evil wishes; they have fallen under the sway of evil wishes.” When this was said, the Blessed One said to the bhikkhu Kokālika: “Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Clarify your mind, Kokālika, towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are virtuous.” For a second time, the bhikkhu Kokālika said to the Blessed One: “Although, venerable sir, the Blessed One is trustworthy and reliable to me, still Sāriputta and Moggallāna have evil wishes; they have fallen under the sway of evil wishes.” For a second time, the Blessed One said to the bhikkhu Kokālika: “Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Clarify your mind, Kokālika, towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are virtuous.” For a third time, the bhikkhu Kokālika said to the Blessed One: “Although… they have fallen under the sway of evil wishes.” For a third time, the Blessed One said to the bhikkhu Kokālika: “Do not speak thus… Sāriputta and Moggallāna are virtuous.”

Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Acirapakkantassa ca kokālikassa bhikkhuno sāsapamattīhi pīḷakāhi piḷakāhi (sī. pī.) sabbo kāyo phuṭo ahosi. Sāsapamattiyo hutvā muggamattiyo ahesuṃ, muggamattiyo hutvā kalāyamattiyo ahesuṃ, kalāyamattiyo hutvā kolaṭṭhimattiyo ahesuṃ, kolaṭṭhimattiyo hutvā kolamattiyo ahesuṃ, kolamattiyo hutvā āmalakamattiyo ahesuṃ, āmalakamattiyo hutvā beluvasalāṭukamattiyo ahesuṃ, beluvasalāṭukamattiyo hutvā billamattiyo ahesuṃ, billamattiyo [T 1.0221] hutvā pabhijjiṃsu. Pubbañca lohitañca pagghariṃsu. Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu teneva ābādhena kālamakāsi[P 1.0151]. Kālaṅkato ca kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṃ nirayaṃ upapajji sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ āghātetvā.

Then the bhikkhu Kokālika rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him clockwise, and departed. Not long after the bhikkhu Kokālika had departed, his entire body became covered with boils the size of mustard seeds. Having been the size of mustard seeds, they became the size of mung beans; having been the size of mung beans, they became the size of chickpeas; having been the size of chickpeas, they became the size of jujube stones; having been the size of jujube stones, they became the size of jujube fruits; having been the size of jujube fruits, they became the size of myrobalan fruits; having been the size of myrobalan fruits, they became the size of young bael fruits; having been the size of young bael fruits, they became the size of mature bael fruits. Having become the size of mature bael fruits, they burst open, and pus and blood oozed out. Then the bhikkhu Kokālika died from that very affliction. Having died, the bhikkhu Kokālika was reborn in the Paduma hell, having established enmity in his mind towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

Atha [M 1.0153] kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho brahmā sahampati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kokāliko, bhante, bhikkhu kālaṅkato. Kālaṅkato ca, bhante, kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṃ nirayaṃ upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ āghātetvā”ti. Idamavoca brahmā sahampati, idaṃ vatvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

Then, when the night was far advanced, Brahmā Sahampati, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta Grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Brahmā Sahampati said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Kokālika has died. And, venerable sir, the bhikkhu Kokālika, having died, has been reborn in the Paduma hell, having established enmity in his mind towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna.” This is what Brahmā Sahampati said. Having said this, he paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him clockwise, and vanished right there.

Atha [V 1.0178] kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi – “imaṃ, bhikkhave, rattiṃ brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, brahmā sahampati maṃ etadavoca – ‘kokāliko, bhante, bhikkhu kālaṅkato. Kālaṅkato ca, bhante, kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṃ nirayaṃ upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ āghātetvā’ti. Idamavoca, bhikkhave[T 1.0222], brahmā sahampati, idaṃ vatvā maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.

Then the Blessed One, when that night had passed, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, last night, when the night was far advanced, Brahmā Sahampati, with his surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta Grove, approached me. Having approached, he paid homage to me and stood to one side. Standing to one side, bhikkhus, Brahmā Sahampati said this to me: ‘Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Kokālika has died. And, venerable sir, the bhikkhu Kokālika, having died, has been reborn in the Paduma hell, having established enmity in his mind towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna.’ This, bhikkhus, is what Brahmā Sahampati said. Having said this, he paid homage to me, circumambulated me clockwise, and vanished right there.”

Evaṃ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kīvadīghaṃ nu kho, bhante, padume niraye āyuppamāṇa”nti? “Dīghaṃ kho, bhikkhu, padume niraye āyuppamāṇaṃ. Taṃ na sukaraṃ saṅkhātuṃ – ettakāni vassāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasatāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasatasahassāni iti vā”ti. “Sakkā pana, bhante, upamaṃ kātu”nti? “Sakkā[P 1.0152], bhikkhū”ti bhagavā avoca –

When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “How long, venerable sir, is the lifespan in the Paduma hell?” “Long, bhikkhu, is the lifespan in the Paduma hell. It is not easy to calculate it as so many years, or so many hundreds of years, or so many thousands of years, or so many hundreds of thousands of years.” “But is it possible, venerable sir, to make a simile?” “It is possible, bhikkhus,” the Blessed One said.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu vīsatikhāriko kosalako tilavāho. Tato puriso vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena ekamekaṃ tilaṃ uddhareyya; khippataraṃ kho so, bhikkhu, vīsatikhāriko kosalako tilavāho iminā upakkamena parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya, na tveva eko abbudo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati abbudā nirayā, evameko nirabbudanirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati nirabbudā nirayā, evameko ababo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati ababā nirayā, evameko [M 1.0154] aṭaṭo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati aṭaṭā nirayā, evameko ahaho nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati ahahā nirayā, evameko kumudo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati kumudā nirayā, evameko sogandhiko nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati sogandhikā nirayā, evameko uppalanirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati uppalā nirayā, evameko puṇḍariko nirayo. Seyyathāpi[T 1.0223], bhikkhu, vīsati puṇḍarikā nirayā, evameko padumo nirayo. Padume pana, bhikkhu, niraye kokāliko bhikkhu upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ āghātetvā”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

“Suppose, monk, there was a Kosalan cartload of twenty khārīs of sesame seeds. From it, a man would remove one sesame seed at the end of every hundred years. By this method, monk, that Kosalan cartload of twenty khārīs of sesame seeds would more quickly be depleted and exhausted, but not so a single Abbuda hell. Just as twenty Abbuda hells, monk, so is one Nirabbuda hell. Just as twenty Nirabbuda hells, monk, so is one Ababa hell. Just as twenty Ababa hells, monk, so is one Aṭaṭa hell. Just as twenty Aṭaṭa hells, monk, so is one Ahaha hell. Just as twenty Ahaha hells, monk, so is one Kumuda hell. Just as twenty Kumuda hells, monk, so is one Sogandhika hell. Just as twenty Sogandhika hells, monk, so is one Uppala hell. Just as twenty Uppala hells, monk, so is one Puṇḍarīka hell. Just as twenty Puṇḍarīka hells, monk, so is one Paduma hell. It is in the Paduma hell, monk, that the monk Kokālika has been reborn, having harbored malice in his mind toward Sāriputta and Moggallāna.” The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further spoke these words:

“Purisassa [V 1.0179] hi jātassa,

Kuṭhārī jāyate mukhe;

Yāya chindati attānaṃ,

Bālo dubbhāsitaṃ bhaṇaṃ.

“For a person who is born, an axe is born in his mouth, with which the fool cuts himself when speaking ill-spoken words.”

“Yo nindiyaṃ pasaṃsati,

Taṃ vā nindati yo pasaṃsiyo;

Vicināti mukhena so kaliṃ,

Kalinā tena sukhaṃ na vindati.

“He who praises one who is blameworthy, or blames one who is praiseworthy, gathers demerit with his mouth. Because of that demerit, he finds no happiness.”

“Appamattako ayaṃ kali,

Yo akkhesu dhanaparājayo;

Sabbassāpi sahāpi attanā,

Ayameva mahantaro kali;

Yo sugatesu manaṃ padosaye.

“Insignificant is this demerit—the loss of wealth at dice, even along with oneself and all one’s possessions. This indeed is the far greater demerit: to harbor a corrupt thought toward the Sugatas.”

“Sataṃ sahassānaṃ nirabbudānaṃ,

Chattiṃsati pañca ca abbudāni;

Yamariyagarahī [P 1.0153] nirayaṃ upeti,

Vācaṃ manañca paṇidhāya pāpaka”nti.

“The reviler of noble ones, having directed his evil speech and mind, goes to hell for one hundred thousand and thirty-six Nirabbudas and five Abbudas.”

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Āyācanaṃ [T 1.0224][M 1.0155] gāravo brahmadevo,

Bako ca brahmā aparā ca diṭṭhi;

Pamādakokālikatissako ca,

Turū ca brahmā aparo ca kokālikoti.

The Request, Reverence, Brahmadeva, and Baka the Brahmā, and another on the View; Pamāda, Kokālika, and Tissaka; and Turū the Brahmā, and another Kokālika.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Sanaṅkumārasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse with Sanaṅkumāra

182. Evaṃ [T 1.0225][V 1.0180] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati sappinītīre. Atha kho brahmā sanaṅkumāro abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ sappinītīraṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

182. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagaha on the bank of the Sappinī River. Then, when the night was far advanced, the Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, of most pleasing appearance, having illuminated the entire bank of the Sappinī River with his radiance, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Khattiyo seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, ye gottapaṭisārino;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, so seṭṭho devamānuse”ti.

“Among people who trace their lineage, the Khattiya is best; but he who is endowed with knowledge and conduct is best among gods and humans.”

Idamavoca brahmā sanaṅkumāro. Samanuñño satthā ahosi. Atha kho brahmā sanaṅkumāro “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

The Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke this. The Teacher approved. Then the Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, thinking, 'The Teacher approves of me,' having paid homage to the Blessed One and circumambulated him to the right, vanished right there.

2. Devadattasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Devadatta

183. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate acirapakkante devadatte. Atha kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ gijjhakūṭaṃ [T 1.0226] pabbataṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0154] ṭhito kho brahmā sahampati devadattaṃ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

183. Thus have I heard. At one time, not long after Devadatta had departed, the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagaha on the Gijjhakūṭa mountain. Then, when the night was far advanced, the Brahmā Sahampati, of most pleasing appearance, having illuminated the entire Gijjhakūṭa mountain with his radiance, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Brahmā Sahampati, concerning Devadatta, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Phalaṃ [M 1.0156] ve kadaliṃ hanti, phalaṃ veḷuṃ phalaṃ naḷaṃ;

Sakkāro kāpurisaṃ hanti, gabbho assatariṃ yathā”ti.

“Indeed, its fruit destroys the banana tree, its fruit destroys the bamboo, and its fruit destroys the reed; honor destroys a wicked man, just as a fetus destroys the she-mule.”

3. Andhakavindasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse at Andhakavinda

184. Ekaṃ [V 1.0181] samayaṃ bhagavā māgadhesu viharati andhakavinde. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṃ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṃ phusāyati. Atha kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ andhakavindaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

184. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans in Andhakavinda. Now at that time, the Blessed One was sitting in the open air in the pitch-dark of night, and the rain was drizzling. Then, when the night was far advanced, the Brahmā Sahampati, of most pleasing appearance, having illuminated the entire Andhakavinda with his radiance, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Brahmā Sahampati recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Sevetha pantāni senāsanāni,

Careyya saṃyojanavippamokkhā;

Sace ratiṃ nādhigaccheyya tattha,

Saṅghe vase rakkhitatto satīmā.

“One should resort to secluded lodgings; one should practice for the sake of freedom from the fetters. If one does not find delight therein, one should dwell in the Saṅgha, self-guarded and mindful.

“Kulākulaṃ piṇḍikāya caranto,

Indriyagutto [T 1.0227] nipako satīmā;

Sevetha pantāni senāsanāni,

Bhayā pamutto abhaye vimutto.

“Going from family to family for alms-food, guarded in senses, prudent, and mindful; one should resort to secluded lodgings, freed from fear, liberated in the fearless.

“Yattha bheravā sarīsapā siriṃ sapā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.),

Vijju sañcarati thanayati devo;

Andhakāratimisāya rattiyā,

Nisīdi tattha bhikkhu vigatalomahaṃso.

“Where there are fearsome things and crawling creatures, where lightning flashes and the sky thunders; in the pitch-dark of the night, there a monk sat, with hair-raising fear gone.

“Idañhi jātu me diṭṭhaṃ, nayidaṃ itihītihaṃ;

Ekasmiṃ brahmacariyasmiṃ, sahassaṃ maccuhāyinaṃ.

“Indeed, this has been seen by me; this is not mere hearsay. In this one holy life, there are a thousand who have overcome death.

“Bhiyyo bhīyo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pañcasatā sekkhā, dasā ca dasadhā dasa;

Sabbe sotasamāpannā, atiracchānagāmino.

“Furthermore, there are five hundred trainees, and ten, and ten times ten more; all have attained the stream, not destined for the lower realms.

“Athāyaṃ [V 1.0182][M 1.0157] atthāyaṃ-itipi dī. ni. 2.290 itarā pajā, puññabhāgāti me mano;

Saṅkhātuṃ nopi sakkomi, musāvādassa ottapa”nti ottapeti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), ottappeti (ka.).

“As for this other populace, my mind thinks, 'They have a share in merit.' I am not able to count them, out of fear of falsehood.”

4. Aruṇavatīsuttaṃ

4. The Aruṇavatī Sutta

185. Evaṃ [P 1.0155] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati…pe… tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

185. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī... There the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: 'Monks!' 'Venerable sir,' those monks responded to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā ahosi aruṇavā nāma. Rañño kho pana, bhikkhave, aruṇavato aruṇavatī nāma rājadhānī ahosi. Aruṇavatiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, rājadhāniṃ aruṇavatiyaṃ kho pana bhikkhave rājadhāniyaṃ (pī. ka.) sikhī bhagavā [T 1.0228] arahaṃ sammāsambuddho upanissāya vihāsi. Sikhissa kho pana, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa abhibhūsambhavaṃ nāma sāvakayugaṃ ahosi aggaṃ bhaddayugaṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho abhibhuṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘āyāma, brāhmaṇa, yena aññataro brahmaloko tenupasaṅkamissāma, yāva bhattassa kālo bhavissatī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante’ti kho bhikkhave, abhibhū bhikkhu sikhissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paccassosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho abhibhū ca bhikkhu – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – aruṇavatiyā rājadhāniyā antarahitā tasmiṃ brahmaloke pāturahesuṃ.

“Monks, in a time long past, there was a king named Aruṇavā. And, monks, the royal capital of King Aruṇavā was named Aruṇavatī. Monks, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, dwelt in dependence on the royal capital Aruṇavatī. And, monks, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, had a pair of disciples named Abhibhū and Sambhava, a chief and excellent pair. Then, monks, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, addressed the monk Abhibhū: ‘Come, brāhmaṇa, let us approach a certain Brahma-world until it is time for the meal.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ responded the monk Abhibhū to the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. Then, monks, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and the monk Abhibhū—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—vanished from the royal capital Aruṇavatī and appeared in that Brahma-world.”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho abhibhuṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘paṭibhātu, brāhmaṇa, taṃ brahmuno ca brahmaparisāya ca brahmapārisajjānañca dhammī kathā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante’ti kho, bhikkhave, abhibhū bhikkhu sikhissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭissutvā, brahmānañca brahmaparisañca brahmapārisajje ca dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, brahmā ca brahmaparisā ca brahmapārisajjā [P 1.0156] ca ujjhāyanti khiyyanti khīyanti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vipācenti – ‘acchariyaṃ vata[M 1.0158], bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, kathañhi nāma satthari sammukhībhūte sāvako dhammaṃ desessatī’”ti[T 1.0229]!

“Then, monks, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, addressed the monk Abhibhū: ‘Brāhmaṇa, may a Dhamma talk for Brahmā, for the assembly of Brahmā, and for the attendants of Brahmā occur to you.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the monk Abhibhū responded to the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and having hearkened, he instructed, roused, inspired, and delighted Brahmā, the assembly of Brahmā, and the attendants of Brahmā with a Dhamma talk. At that time, monks, Brahmā, the assembly of Brahmā, and the attendants of Brahmā criticized, disparaged, and found fault, saying: ‘It is astonishing, sirs, it is amazing, sirs! How indeed can a disciple teach the Dhamma in the presence of the Teacher!’”

“Atha [V 1.0183] kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho abhibhuṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – ‘ujjhāyanti kho te, brāhmaṇa, brahmā ca brahmaparisā ca brahmapārisajjā ca – acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho, kathañhi nāma satthari sammukhībhūte sāvako dhammaṃ desessatīti! Tena hi tvaṃ brāhmaṇa, bhiyyosomattāya brahmānañca brahmaparisañca brahmapārisajje ca saṃvejehī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante’ti kho, bhikkhave, abhibhū bhikkhu sikhissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭissutvā dissamānenapi kāyena dhammaṃ desesi, adissamānenapi kāyena dhammaṃ desesi, dissamānenapi heṭṭhimena upaḍḍhakāyena adissamānena uparimena upaḍḍhakāyena dhammaṃ desesi, dissamānenapi uparimena upaḍḍhakāyena adissamānena heṭṭhimena upaḍḍhakāyena dhammaṃ desesi. Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, brahmā ca brahmaparisā ca brahmapārisajjā ca acchariyabbhutacittajātā ahesuṃ – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho, samaṇassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā’”ti!

“Then, monks, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, addressed the monk Abhibhū: ‘Brāhmaṇa, Brahmā, the assembly of Brahmā, and the attendants of Brahmā are criticizing you, saying: “It is astonishing, sirs, it is amazing, sirs! How indeed can a disciple teach the Dhamma in the presence of the Teacher?” Therefore, brāhmaṇa, you should startle Brahmā, the assembly of Brahmā, and the attendants of Brahmā even more.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the monk Abhibhū responded to the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and having hearkened, he taught the Dhamma with a visible body and taught the Dhamma with an invisible body; he taught the Dhamma with the lower half of his body visible and the upper half invisible, and he taught the Dhamma with the upper half of his body visible and the lower half invisible. At that time, monks, Brahmā, the assembly of Brahmā, and the attendants of Brahmā were struck with wonder and amazement, thinking: ‘It is astonishing, sirs, it is amazing, sirs, the great psychic power and might of the ascetic!’”

“Atha kho abhibhū bhikkhu sikhiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘abhijānāmi khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhikkhusaṅghassa majjhe evarūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā – pahomi khvāhaṃ āvuso, brahmaloke ṭhito sahassilokadhātuṃ [T 1.0230] sahassīlokadhātuṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) sarena viññāpetu’nti. ‘Etassa, brāhmaṇa, kālo, etassa, brāhmaṇa, kālo; yaṃ tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, brahmaloke ṭhito sahassilokadhātuṃ sarena viññāpeyyāsī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante’ti kho, bhikkhave, abhibhū bhikkhu sikhissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭissutvā brahmaloke ṭhito imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

“Then the monk Abhibhū said this to the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One: ‘Venerable sir, I recall having spoken words of this kind in the midst of the Saṅgha of monks: “Friends, while standing in the Brahma-world, I am able to make a thousandfold world-system know by my voice.”’ ‘This is the time for that, brāhmaṇa, this is the time for that; that you, standing in the Brahma-world, should make the thousandfold world-system know by your voice.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the monk Abhibhū responded to the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and having hearkened, standing in the Brahma-world, he recited these verses:”

“Ārambhatha ārabbhatha (sabbattha) nikkamatha nikkhamatha (sī. pī.), yuñjatha buddhasāsane;

Dhunātha maccuno senaṃ, naḷāgāraṃva kuñjaro.

“Strive, go forth, apply yourselves to the Buddha’s Dispensation. Shatter the army of Death, as an elephant a house of reeds.

“Yo [P 1.0157] imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, appamatto vihassati;

Pahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ, dukkhassantaṃ karissatī”ti.

“Whoever in this Dhamma-Vinaya lives heedfully, having abandoned the round of rebirth, will make an end to suffering.”

“Atha [M 1.0159] kho, bhikkhave, sikhī ca bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho abhibhū ca bhikkhu brahmānañca brahmaparisañca brahmapārisajje ca saṃvejetvā – seyyathāpi nāma…pe… tasmiṃ brahmaloke antarahitā aruṇavatiyā rājadhāniyā pāturahesuṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā [V 1.0184] arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘assuttha no, tumhe, bhikkhave, abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’ti? ‘Assumha kho mayaṃ, bhante, abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’ti. ‘Yathā kathaṃ pana tumhe, bhikkhave, assuttha abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’”ti? Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, assumha abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassa –

“Then, monks, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and the monk Abhibhū, having startled Brahmā, his assembly, and his retinue—just as a strong man might… and so on…—vanished from that Brahma-world and reappeared in the royal capital of Aruṇavatī. Then, monks, the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, addressed the monks: 'Did you hear, monks, the verses spoken by the monk Abhibhū while standing in the Brahma-world?' 'We did hear, Venerable Sir, the verses spoken by the monk Abhibhū while standing in the Brahma-world.' 'But how, monks, did you hear the verses spoken by the monk Abhibhū while standing in the Brahma-world?' 'Thus, Venerable Sir, we heard the monk Abhibhū speaking these verses while standing in the Brahma-world—'”

“Ārambhatha nikkamatha, yuñjatha buddhasāsane;

Dhunātha maccuno senaṃ, naḷāgāraṃva kuñjaro.

Strive, go forth, apply yourselves to the Buddha's Dispensation! Destroy the army of Death, as an elephant destroys a reed hut.

“Yo [T 1.0231] imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, appamatto vihassati;

Pahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ, dukkhassantaṃ karissatī”ti.

Whoever in this Dhamma and Discipline dwells heedfully, having abandoned the cycle of birth, will make an end of suffering.

“‘Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, assumha abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’ti. ‘Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhave; sādhu kho tumhe, bhikkhave! Assuttha abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’”ti.

‘Thus, Venerable Sir, we heard the verses spoken by the monk Abhibhū while he was in the Brahma-world.’ ‘Good, good, monks; it is good, monks, that you heard the verses spoken by the monk Abhibhū while he was in the Brahma-world!’

Idamavoca bhagavā, attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

The Blessed One said this. Those monks, glad at heart, rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

5. Parinibbānasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Final Nibbāna

186. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kusinārāyaṃ viharati upavattane mallānaṃ sālavane antarena yamakasālānaṃ parinibbānasamaye. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “handa dāni, bhikkhave[P 1.0158], āmantayāmi vo – ‘vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādethā’ti. Ayaṃ tathāgatassa pacchimā vācā”.

186. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kusinārā, in the Upavattana, the sāla grove of the Mallas, between the twin sāla trees, at the time of his final Nibbāna. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: ‘Come now, monks, I declare this to you: “Conditioned things are subject to decay. Strive on with heedfulness!”’ This was the Tathāgata's last word.

Atha [M 1.0160] kho bhagavā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ paṭhamajjhānaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) evaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ iccādīsupi samāpajji. Paṭhamā jhānā paṭhamajjhānā (syā. kaṃ.) evaṃ dutiyā jhānā iccādīsupi vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Dutiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Tatiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ [V 1.0185] jhānaṃ samāpajji. Catutthā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji. Ākāsānañcāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji. Viññāṇañcāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji. Ākiñcaññāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanā [T 1.0232] vuṭṭhahitvā saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajji.

Then the Blessed One entered the first jhāna. Emerging from the first jhāna, he entered the second jhāna. Emerging from the second jhāna, he entered the third jhāna. Emerging from the third jhāna, he entered the fourth jhāna. Emerging from the fourth jhāna, he entered the sphere of infinite space. Emerging from the sphere of infinite space, he entered the sphere of infinite consciousness. Emerging from the sphere of infinite consciousness, he entered the sphere of nothingness. Emerging from the sphere of nothingness, he entered the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception. Emerging from the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception, he entered the cessation of perception and feeling.

Saññāvedayitanirodhā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji. Ākiñcaññāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji. Viññāṇañcāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji. Ākāsānañcāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Catutthā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Tatiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Dutiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Paṭhamā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Dutiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Tatiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Catutthā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantaraṃ bhagavā parinibbāyi. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā brahmā sahampati imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Emerging from the cessation of perception and feeling, he entered the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception. Emerging from the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception, he entered the sphere of nothingness. Emerging from the sphere of nothingness, he entered the sphere of infinite consciousness. Emerging from the sphere of infinite consciousness, he entered the sphere of infinite space. Emerging from the sphere of infinite space, he entered the fourth jhāna. Emerging from the fourth jhāna, he entered the third jhāna. Emerging from the third jhāna, he entered the second jhāna. Emerging from the second jhāna, he entered the first jhāna. Emerging from the first jhāna, he entered the second jhāna. Emerging from the second jhāna, he entered the third jhāna. Emerging from the third jhāna, he entered the fourth jhāna. Immediately upon emerging from the fourth jhāna, the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna. When the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna, at the moment of his final passing, Brahmā Sahampati uttered this verse:

“Sabbeva nikkhipissanti, bhūtā loke samussayaṃ;

Yattha etādiso satthā, loke appaṭipuggalo;

Tathāgato balappatto, sambuddho parinibbuto”ti.

All beings in the world will lay down their composite body; for even such a Teacher, unequalled in the world, the Tathāgata who has attained the powers, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has attained final Nibbāna.

Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā sakko devānamindo imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

When the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna, at the moment of his final passing, Sakka, ruler of the gods, uttered this verse:

“Aniccā vata saṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho”ti.

Impermanent, alas, are conditioned things, whose nature is to arise and pass away. Having arisen, they cease; their stilling is bliss.

Parinibbute [T 1.0233][M 1.0161] bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā ānando imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

When the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna, at the moment of his final passing, the Venerable Ānanda uttered this verse:

“Tadāsi yaṃ bhiṃsanakaṃ, tadāsi lomahaṃsanaṃ;

Sabbākāravarūpete, sambuddhe parinibbute”ti.

Then there was terror, then there was hair-raising, when the Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with all excellent qualities, attained final Nibbāna.

Parinibbute [V 1.0186][P 1.0159] bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā anuruddho imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

When the Blessed One attained final Nibbāna, at the moment of his final passing, the Venerable Anuruddha uttered these verses:

“Nāhu assāsapassāso, ṭhitacittassa tādino;

Anejo santimārabbha, cakkhumā parinibbuto yaṃ kālamakarī muni (mahāparinibbānasutte).

There was no in-breath or out-breath for the steadfast one with a firm mind. Unshaken, intent on peace, the One with Vision attained final Nibbāna.

“Asallīnena cittena, vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayi;

Pajjotasseva nibbānaṃ, vimokkho cetaso ahū”ti.

With an unshrinking mind, he endured the feeling. Like the extinguishing of a lamp was the liberation of his mind.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Brahmāsanaṃ devadatto, andhakavindo aruṇavatī;

Parinibbānena ca desitaṃ, idaṃ brahmapañcakanti.

Brahmā's Request, Disrespect, Brahmadeva, Baka Brahmā, Another Brahmā, Kokālika, Tissaka, Turū Brahmā, the monk Kokālika, Sanaṅkumāra, Devadatta, Andhakavinda, Aruṇavatī, and with the Final Nibbāna, there are fifteen.

Brahmasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ. ito paraṃ marammapotthakesu evampi dissati –§brahmāyācanaṃ agāravañca, brahmadevo bako ca brahmā.§aññataro ca brahmākokālikañca, tissakañca turū ca.§brahmā kokālikabhikkhu, sanaṅkumārena devadattaṃ.§andhakavindaṃ aruṇavati, parinibbānena pannarasāti.

The Connected Discourses with Brahmās is complete.

7. Brāhmaṇasaṃyuttaṃ

7. The Connected Discourses with Brahmins

1. Arahantavaggo

1. The Chapter on Arahants

1. Dhanañjānīsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse concerning Dhanañjānī

187. Evaṃ [T 1.0235][V 1.0187][P 1.0160][M 1.0162] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa dhanañjānī dhānañjānī (pī. sī. aṭṭha.) nāma brāhmaṇī abhippasannā hoti buddhe ca dhamme ca saṅghe ca. Atha kho dhanañjānī brāhmaṇī bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa bhattaṃ upasaṃharantī upakkhalitvā tikkhattuṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

187. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. Now at that time, the brahmin lady named Dhanañjānī, wife of a certain brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, was exceedingly devout toward the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha. Then, while bringing food to the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, the brahmin lady Dhanañjānī stumbled and uttered an inspired utterance three times:

“Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa;

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa;

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti.

“Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One; Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One; Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.”

Evaṃ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo dhanañjāniṃ brāhmaṇiṃ etadavoca – “evamevaṃ panāyaṃ vasalī yasmiṃ vā tasmiṃ vā tassa muṇḍakassa samaṇassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Idāni tyāhaṃ, vasali, tassa satthuno vādaṃ āropessāmī”ti. “Na khvāhaṃ taṃ, brāhmaṇa, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo tassa bhagavato vādaṃ āropeyya arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Api ca tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, gaccha, gantvā vijānissasī”ti gantvāpi jānissasīti (syā. kaṃ.).

When this was said, the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan said to the brahmin lady Dhanañjānī: “This outcaste woman is always speaking in praise of that shaven-headed ascetic, whether it is appropriate or not. Now, outcaste, I will challenge the doctrine of that teacher of yours.” “Brahmin, I do not see anyone in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, devas and humans, who could challenge the doctrine of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Nevertheless, brahmin, go. Having gone, you will know.”

Atha [T 1.0236] kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo kupito anattamano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0161] nisinno kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the brāhmaṇa of the Bhāradvāja clan, angry and displeased, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One. After concluding a conversation that was courteous and memorable, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brāhmaṇa of the Bhāradvāja clan addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kiṃsu [V 1.0188] chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kiṃsu chetvā na socati;

Kissassu ekadhammassa, vadhaṃ rocesi gotamā”ti.

“Having cut off what does one sleep in ease? Having cut off what does one not grieve? The destruction of what single thing, Gotama, do you approve?”

“Kodhaṃ [M 1.0163] chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kodhaṃ chetvā na socati;

Kodhassa visamūlassa, madhuraggassa brāhmaṇa;

Vadhaṃ ariyā pasaṃsanti, tañhi chetvā na socatī”ti.

“Having cut off anger, one sleeps in ease; having cut off anger, one does not grieve. O brāhmaṇa, the noble ones praise the destruction of anger, which has a poisonous root and a sweet tip. For having destroyed that, one does not grieve.”

Evaṃ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti.

When this was said, the brāhmaṇa of the Bhāradvāja clan said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama, excellent, Master Gotama! It is as if, Master Gotama, one were to set upright what was overturned, to reveal what was hidden, to show the way to one who was lost, or to hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms. In the same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama. Venerable Sir, I go for refuge to the Blessed One, Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May I receive the going forth in the presence of Master Gotama, may I receive the higher ordination.”

Alattha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā bhāradvājo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto [T 1.0237] ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosīti.

The brāhmaṇa of the Bhāradvāja clan received the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, and he received the higher ordination. Not long after his higher ordination, while dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Bhāradvāja, in this very life, realized for himself with direct knowledge the unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having entered upon it, he dwelled therein. He understood: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.” And the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the Arahants.

2. Akkosasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Abuse

188. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Assosi kho akkosakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo – “bhāradvājagotto kira brāhmaṇo samaṇassa gotamassa santike agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito”ti kupito anattamano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [P 1.0162] bhagavantaṃ asabbhāhi pharusāhi vācāhi akkosati paribhāsati.

188. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary. The brahmin Akkosaka Bhāradvāja heard: “It is said that a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the presence of the ascetic Gotama.” Angry and displeased, he approached the Blessed One and, having approached, he abused and reviled the Blessed One with unsuitable and harsh words.

Evaṃ [V 1.0189] vutte, bhagavā akkosakabhāradvājaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, api nu kho te āgacchanti mittāmaccā ñātisālohitā atithiyo atithayo (?)”ti? “Appekadā me, bho gotama, āgacchanti mittāmaccā [M 1.0164] ñātisālohitā atithiyo”ti. “‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, api nu tesaṃ anuppadesi khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sāyanīyaṃ vā’”ti? “‘Appekadā nesāhaṃ, bho gotama, anuppademi khādanīyaṃ vā bhojanīyaṃ vā sāyanīyaṃ vā’”ti. “‘Sace kho pana te, brāhmaṇa, nappaṭiggaṇhanti[T 1.0238], kassa taṃ hotī’”ti? “‘Sace te, bho gotama, nappaṭiggaṇhanti, amhākameva taṃ hotī’”ti. “Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yaṃ tvaṃ amhe anakkosante akkosasi, arosente rosesi, abhaṇḍante bhaṇḍasi, taṃ te mayaṃ nappaṭiggaṇhāma. Tavevetaṃ, brāhmaṇa, hoti; tavevetaṃ, brāhmaṇa, hoti”.

When this was said, the Blessed One said to the brahmin Akkosaka Bhāradvāja: "What do you think, brahmin? Do friends and colleagues, relatives and kinsmen, and guests come to you?" "Sometimes, Master Gotama, friends and colleagues, relatives and kinsmen, and guests come to me." "What do you think, brahmin? Do you offer them hard food, soft food, or savories?" "Sometimes, Master Gotama, I offer them hard food, soft food, or savories." "But if they do not accept it, brahmin, to whom does it belong?" "If they do not accept it, Master Gotama, it belongs to us alone." "Just so, brahmin, since you abuse us who do not abuse, provoke us who are not angry, and revile us who do not revile—we do not accept that from you. It is all yours, brahmin; it is all yours."

“Yo kho, brāhmaṇa, akkosantaṃ paccakkosati, rosentaṃ paṭiroseti, bhaṇḍantaṃ paṭibhaṇḍati, ayaṃ vuccati, brāhmaṇa, sambhuñjati vītiharatīti. Te mayaṃ tayā neva sambhuñjāma na vītiharāma. Tavevetaṃ, brāhmaṇa, hoti; tavevetaṃ, brāhmaṇa, hotī”ti. “Bhavantaṃ kho gotamaṃ sarājikā parisā evaṃ jānāti – ‘arahaṃ samaṇo gotamo’ti. Atha ca pana bhavaṃ gotamo kujjhatī”ti.

"Brahmin, one who abuses in return when abused, gets angry in return when angered, and quarrels in return when quarreled with—this, brahmin, is called one who partakes and reciprocates. But we neither partake with you nor reciprocate. It is all yours, brahmin; it is all yours." "The assembly, along with the king, knows the venerable Gotama thus: 'The ascetic Gotama is an Arahant.' And yet the venerable Gotama gets angry!"

“Akkodhassa kuto kodho, dantassa samajīvino;

Sammadaññā vimuttassa, upasantassa tādino.

"For one without anger, whence is there anger? For the tamed one who lives righteously, for one liberated through perfect knowledge, for the peaceful, steadfast one?

“Tasseva tena pāpiyo, yo kuddhaṃ paṭikujjhati;

Kuddhaṃ appaṭikujjhanto, saṅgāmaṃ jeti dujjayaṃ.

"He who gets angry in return at one who is angry is, on that account, the more evil of the two. By not getting angry in return at one who is angry, one wins a battle hard to win.

“Ubhinnamatthaṃ carati, attano ca parassa ca;

Paraṃ saṅkupitaṃ ñatvā, yo sato upasammati.

"He practices for the welfare of both, his own and the other's, who, knowing the other is provoked, mindfully becomes calm.

“Ubhinnaṃ tikicchantānaṃ, attano ca parassa ca;

Janā maññanti bāloti, ye dhammassa akovidā”ti.

"When he is healing both himself and the other, people who are unskilled in the Dhamma consider him a fool."

Evaṃ [V 1.0190][P 1.0163] vutte, akkosakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… esāhaṃ [T 1.0239] bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Akkosaka Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One: "Excellent, Master Gotama! ... I go for refuge to the venerable Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. Venerable Sir, may I receive the going forth in the presence of Master Gotama, may I receive the higher ordination."

Alattha kho akkosakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā akkosakabhāradvājo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto [M 1.0165] nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosīti.

The brahmin Akkosaka Bhāradvāja received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, and he received the higher ordination. Not long after his higher ordination, the venerable Akkosakabhāradvāja, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, in no long time realized for himself with direct knowledge that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, he dwelled therein. He understood: "Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being." And the venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

3. Asurindakasuttaṃ

3. The Asurindaka Sutta

189. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Assosi kho asurindakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo – “bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo kira samaṇassa gotamassa santike agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito”ti kupito anattamano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ asabbhāhi pharusāhi vācāhi akkosati paribhāsati. Evaṃ vutte, bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi. Atha kho asurindakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “jitosi, samaṇa, jitosi, samaṇā”ti.

189. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. The brahmin Asurindakabhāradvāja heard: “It is said that a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the presence of the ascetic Gotama.” Angry and displeased, he approached the Blessed One and, having approached, he abused and reviled the Blessed One with unsuitable, harsh words. When this was said, the Blessed One remained silent. Then the brahmin Asurindakabhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: “You are defeated, ascetic! You are defeated, ascetic!”

“Jayaṃ [T 1.0240] ve maññati bālo, vācāya pharusaṃ bhaṇaṃ;

Jayañcevassa taṃ hoti, yā titikkhā vijānato.

“A fool, speaking harsh words, thinks it a victory. For one who understands, the victory is indeed forbearance.”

“Tasseva tena pāpiyo, yo kuddhaṃ paṭikujjhati;

Kuddhaṃ appaṭikujjhanto, saṅgāmaṃ jeti dujjayaṃ.

“He who gets angry in return at one who is angry is, on that account, the more evil of the two. By not getting angry in return at one who is angry, one wins a battle difficult to win.”

“Ubhinnamatthaṃ carati, attano ca parassa ca;

Paraṃ saṅkupitaṃ ñatvā, yo sato upasammati.

“He who, knowing the other is angry, mindfully becomes calm, practices for the welfare of both—for his own and for the other's.”

“Ubhinnaṃ [V 1.0191] tikicchantānaṃ, attano ca parassa ca;

Janā maññanti bāloti, ye dhammassa akovidā”ti.

“While he is healing both, himself and the other, people who are unskilled in the Dhamma consider him a fool.”

Evaṃ [P 1.0164] vutte, asurindakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosī”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin Asurindakabhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! ...pe... And the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

4. Bilaṅgikasuttaṃ

4. The Bilaṅgika Sutta

190. Ekaṃ [M 1.0166] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Assosi kho bilaṅgikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo – “bhāradvājagotto kira brāhmaṇo samaṇassa gotamassa santike agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito”ti kupito anattamano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tuṇhībhūto ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho bhagavā bilaṅgikassa bhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya bilaṅgikaṃ bhāradvājaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi [T 1.0241] –

190. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. The brahmin Bilaṅgikabhāradvāja heard: “It is said that a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan has gone forth from the household life into homelessness in the presence of the ascetic Gotama.” Angry and displeased, he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he stood silently to one side. Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the thought in the mind of the brahmin Bilaṅgikabhāradvāja, addressed the brahmin Bilaṅgikabhāradvāja with a verse:

“Yo appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati,

Suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa;

Tameva bālaṃ pacceti pāpaṃ,

Sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṃva khitto”ti.

“Whoever offends a man who is not corrupt, a person who is pure and without defilements, that evil returns to that very fool, like fine dust thrown against the wind.”

Evaṃ vutte, vilaṅgikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosī”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin Bilaṅgikabhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! ...pe... And the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

5. Ahiṃsakasuttaṃ

5. The Ahiṃsaka Sutta

191. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho ahiṃsakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0165] nisinno kho ahiṃsakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahiṃsakāhaṃ, bho gotama, ahiṃsakāhaṃ, bho gotamā”ti.

191. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then the brahmin Ahiṃsakabhāradvāja approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged pleasantries with the Blessed One. After concluding a pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Ahiṃsakabhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: 'Master Gotama, I am Ahiṃsaka. Master Gotama, I am Ahiṃsaka.'

“Yathā [T 1.0242][V 1.0192] nāmaṃ tathā cassa, siyā kho tvaṃ ahiṃsako;

Yo ca kāyena vācāya, manasā ca na hiṃsati;

Sa ve ahiṃsako hoti, yo paraṃ na vihiṃsatī”ti.

“If you were in accordance with your name, you would indeed be Ahiṃsaka (one who is non-harming). He who does not harm another by body, speech, or mind—he is truly an Ahiṃsaka, one who does not harm others.”

Evaṃ vutte, ahiṃsakabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā ahiṃsakabhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosī”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin Ahiṃsakabhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! ...pe... And the venerable Ahiṃsakabhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

6. Jaṭāsuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Tangle

192. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 1.0167]. Atha kho jaṭābhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jaṭābhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

192. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then the brahmin Jaṭābhāradvāja approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged pleasantries with the Blessed One. After concluding a pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Jaṭābhāradvāja addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Antojaṭā bahijaṭā, jaṭāya jaṭitā pajā;

Taṃ taṃ gotama pucchāmi, ko imaṃ vijaṭaye jaṭa”nti.

“An inner tangle and an outer tangle—this generation is entangled by a tangle. Therefore, I ask you this, Gotama: who can disentangle this tangle?”

“Sīle patiṭṭhāya naro sapañño, cittaṃ paññañca bhāvayaṃ;

Ātāpī nipako bhikkhu, so imaṃ vijaṭaye jaṭaṃ.

“A wise person, established in virtue, developing concentration and wisdom—an ardent and discerning bhikkhu, he can disentangle this tangle.”

“Yesaṃ rāgo ca doso ca, avijjā ca virājitā;

Khīṇāsavā arahanto, tesaṃ vijaṭitā jaṭā.

“For those in whom lust, hatred, and ignorance have faded away—the arahants, whose taints are destroyed—for them, the tangle is disentangled.”

“Yattha nāmañca rūpañca, asesaṃ uparujjhati;

Paṭighaṃ rūpasaññā ca, etthesā chijjate jaṭā”ti.

“Where name-and-form, together with perception of resistance and perception of form, cease without remainder—it is there that this tangle is cut.”

Evaṃ [T 1.0243] vutte, jaṭābhāradvājo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosī”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin Jaṭābhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! ...pe... And the venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the arahants.

7. Suddhikasuttaṃ

7. The Suddhika Sutta

193. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 1.0193]. Atha kho suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0166] nisinno kho suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ ajjhabhāsi –

193. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then the brahmin Suddhikabhāradvāja approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged pleasantries with the Blessed One. After concluding a pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Suddhikabhāradvāja recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Na brāhmaṇo nābrāhmaṇo (?) sujjhati koci, loke sīlavāpi tapokaraṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, so sujjhati na aññā itarā pajā”ti.

“In this world, no brahmin is purified merely by being virtuous or by practicing austerities. Only one who is accomplished in knowledge and conduct is purified; other people are not.”

“Bahumpi palapaṃ jappaṃ, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo;

Antokasambu saṅkiliṭṭho, kuhanaṃ upanissito.

“Though one may mutter much prattle, one does not become a brahmin by birth if one is inwardly rotten, defiled, and given to deceit.”

“Khattiyo [M 1.0168] brāhmaṇo vesso, suddo caṇḍālapukkuso;

Āraddhavīriyo pahitatto, niccaṃ daḷhaparakkamo;

Pappoti paramaṃ suddhiṃ, evaṃ jānāhi brāhmaṇā”ti.

“Be it a noble, a brahmin, a merchant, a worker, an outcaste, or a scavenger—anyone who is energetic, resolute, and always firmly striving attains supreme purity. Know this, O brahmin.”

Evaṃ vutte, suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosī”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin Suddhika Bhāradvāja said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable Gotama! …” … And the venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the Arahants.

8. Aggikasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse concerning Aggika

194. Ekaṃ [T 1.0244] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena aggikabhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa sappinā pāyaso sannihito hoti – “aggiṃ juhissāmi, aggihuttaṃ paricarissāmī”ti.

194. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary. At that time the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja had prepared milk-rice with ghee, thinking: “I will make an offering to the fire, I will attend to the fire sacrifice.”

Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Rājagahe sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāno yena aggikabhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami[V 1.0194]; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Addasā kho aggikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ piṇḍāya ṭhitaṃ. Disvāna bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms. While wandering for alms in Rājagaha from house to house, he approached the dwelling of the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja; having approached, he stood to one side. The brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja saw the Blessed One standing for alms. Having seen him, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Tīhi vijjāhi sampanno, jātimā sutavā bahū;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, somaṃ bhuñjeyya pāyasa”nti.

“Endowed with the three Vedas, of noble birth, and widely learned; endowed with knowledge and conduct, such a one is worthy to eat this milk-rice.”

“Bahumpi palapaṃ jappaṃ, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo;

Antokasambu saṃkiliṭṭho, kuhanāparivārito.

“Though one may chant much empty talk, one does not become a brahmin by birth if one is inwardly rotten, defiled, and surrounded by deceit.”

“Pubbenivāsaṃ [P 1.0167] yo vedī, saggāpāyañca passati;

Atho jātikkhayaṃ patto, abhiññāvosito muni.

“He who knows his past lives, and sees heaven and the planes of misery, and has attained the destruction of birth—that sage, perfected in higher knowledge,

“Etāhi tīhi vijjāhi, tevijjo hoti brāhmaṇo;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, somaṃ bhuñjeyya pāyasa”nti.

“by these three knowledges, a brahmin is one of threefold knowledge; endowed with knowledge and conduct, such a one is worthy to eat this milk-rice.”

“Bhuñjatu bhavaṃ gotamo. Brāhmaṇo bhava”nti.

“Let Master Gotama eat. You are a brahmin.”

“Gāthābhigītaṃ [T 1.0245][M 1.0169] me abhojaneyyaṃ,

Sampassataṃ brāhmaṇa nesa dhammo;

Gāthābhigītaṃ panudanti buddhā,

Dhamme sati brāhmaṇa vuttiresā.

“Food obtained by reciting verses is not to be eaten by me. Brahmin, this is not the principle for those who see rightly. The Buddhas reject food obtained by reciting verses. Brahmin, when the Dhamma exists, this is the proper way of life.

“Aññena ca kevalinaṃ mahesiṃ,

Khīṇāsavaṃ kukkuccavūpasantaṃ;

Annena pānena upaṭṭhahassu,

Khettañhi taṃ puññapekkhassa hotī”ti.

“With other food and drink should you attend to a great sage who is consummate, whose taints are destroyed, and whose remorse is stilled. For he is the field for one who seeks merit.”

Evaṃ [V 1.0195] vutte, aggikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… aññataro ca panāyasmā aggikabhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosī”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin Aggikabhāradvāja said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! … and the venerable Aggikabhāradvāja became one of the arahants.”

9. Sundarikasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse concerning Sundarika

195. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu viharati sundarikāya nadiyā tīre. Tena kho pana samayena sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo sundarikāya nadiyā tīre aggiṃ juhati, aggihuttaṃ paricarati. Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo aggiṃ juhitvā aggihuttaṃ paricaritvā uṭṭhāyāsanā samantā catuddisā anuvilokesi – “ko nu kho imaṃ habyasesaṃ bhuñjeyyā”ti? Addasā kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle sasīsaṃ pārutaṃ nisinnaṃ. Disvāna vāmena hatthena [T 1.0246] habyasesaṃ gahetvā dakkhiṇena hatthena kamaṇḍaluṃ gahetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho bhagavā sundarikabhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa padasaddena sīsaṃ vivari. Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo ‘muṇḍo ayaṃ [P 1.0168] bhavaṃ, muṇḍako ayaṃ bhava’nti tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi. Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘muṇḍāpi hi idhekacce brāhmaṇā bhavanti; yaṃnūnāhaṃ taṃ upasaṅkamitvā jātiṃ puccheyya’nti.

195. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans on the bank of the Sundarikā River. Now at that time the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja was offering to the fire and attending to the fire sacrifice on the bank of the Sundarikā River. Then, having offered to the fire and attended to the fire sacrifice, the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja rose from his seat and looked around in all four directions, thinking: “Who might eat this remainder of the offering?” He saw the Blessed One sitting at the foot of a certain tree with his head covered. Seeing him, he took the remainder of the offering in his left hand and a water pot in his right hand and approached the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One uncovered his head at the sound of the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja’s footsteps. Then the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja thought: “This venerable one is shaven-headed, this venerable one is a shaveling,” and he wanted to turn back from there. Then it occurred to the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja: “Some brahmins here are also shaven-headed; what if I were to approach him and ask about his birth?”

Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘kiṃjacco bhava’nti?

Then the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja approached the Blessed One, and on approaching, said to him: “Of what birth are you, venerable sir?”

“Mā [M 1.0170] jātiṃ puccha caraṇañca puccha,

Kaṭṭhā have jāyati jātavedo;

Nīcākulīnopi muni dhitimā,

Ājānīyo hoti hirīnisedho.

“Do not ask about birth, but ask about conduct. From wood, indeed, fire is born. A sage, though from a lowly family, is resolute, a thoroughbred, restrained by shame.

“Saccena danto damasā upeto,

Vedantagū vusitabrahmacariyo;

Yaññopanīto [V 1.0196] tamupavhayetha,

Kālena so juhati dakkhiṇeyye”ti.

“Tamed by truth, endowed with self-restraint, one who has reached the end of knowledge, who has lived the holy life; one for whom a sacrifice is prepared should invite such a person. At the proper time, one offers to those worthy of offerings.”

“Addhā suyiṭṭhaṃ suhutaṃ mama yidaṃ,

Yaṃ tādisaṃ vedagumaddasāmi;

Tumhādisānañhi [T 1.0247] adassanena,

Añño jano bhuñjati habyasesa”nti.

“Surely, this sacrifice of mine is well-offered, well-sacrificed, since I have seen such a one who has gone to the end of knowledge; for in not seeing one such as you, another person would eat the remains of the offering.”

“Bhuñjatu bhavaṃ gotamo. Brāhmaṇo bhava”nti.

“Let Master Gotama eat. You are a brahmin.”

“Gāthābhigītaṃ me abhojaneyyaṃ,

Sampassataṃ brāhmaṇa nesa dhammo;

Gāthābhigītaṃ panudanti buddhā,

Dhamme sati brāhmaṇa vuttiresā.

“Food obtained by reciting verses is not to be eaten by me. Brahmin, this is not the principle for those who see rightly. The Buddhas reject food obtained by reciting verses. Brahmin, when the Dhamma exists, this is the proper way of life.

“Aññena ca kevalinaṃ mahesiṃ,

Khīṇāsavaṃ kukkuccavūpasantaṃ;

Annena pānena upaṭṭhahassu,

Khettañhi taṃ puññapekkhassa hotī”ti.

“With other food and drink should you attend to a great sage who is consummate, whose taints are destroyed, and whose remorse is stilled. For he is the field for one who seeks merit.”

“Atha kassa cāhaṃ, bho gotama, imaṃ habyasesaṃ dammī”ti? “Na khvāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya yasseso habyaseso bhutto sammā pariṇāmaṃ gaccheyya [P 1.0169] aññatra, brāhmaṇa, tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā. Tena hi tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, taṃ habyasesaṃ appaharite vā chaḍḍehi appāṇake vā udake opilāpehī”ti.

“Then, Master Gotama, to whom should I give this remainder of the offering?” “Brahmin, I do not see anyone in this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, who could properly digest this remainder of the offering after eating it, except for the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata. Therefore, brahmin, either discard that remainder of the offering in a place without green vegetation or submerge it in water where there are no living beings.”

Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo taṃ habyasesaṃ appāṇake udake opilāpesi. Atha kho so habyaseso udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati [M 1.0171] ciṭiciṭāyati sandhūpāyati sampadhūpāyati[V 1.0197]. Seyyathāpi nāma [T 1.0248] phālo loho (ka.) divasaṃsantatto divasasantatto (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati ciṭiciṭāyati sandhūpāyati sampadhūpāyati; evameva so habyaseso udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati ciṭiciṭāyati sandhūpāyati sampadhūpāyati.

Then the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja submerged that remainder of the offering in water where there were no living beings. And when that remainder of the offering was placed in the water, it sizzled and sputtered, fumed and smoked. Just as a ploughshare, heated all day, when placed in water sizzles and sputters, fumes and smokes—so too did that remainder of the offering, when placed in the water, sizzle and sputter, fume and smoke.

Atha kho sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sundarikabhāradvājaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhagavā gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja, alarmed and with his hair standing on end, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he stood to one side. The Blessed One addressed the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja, who was standing to one side, with verses:

“Mā brāhmaṇa dāru samādahāno,

Suddhiṃ amaññi bahiddhā hi etaṃ;

Na hi tena suddhiṃ kusalā vadanti,

Yo bāhirena parisuddhimicche.

“O brahmin, do not think that by producing a wood-fire there is purity, for this is indeed external. The wise do not declare purity through that for one who desires purification by external means.”

“Hitvā ahaṃ brāhmaṇa dārudāhaṃ

Ajjhattamevujjalayāmi ajjhattameva jalayāmi (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) jotiṃ;

Niccagginī niccasamāhitatto,

Arahaṃ ahaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carāmi.

“Having abandoned, O brahmin, the producing of a wood-fire, I cause the flame to blaze only within. Constantly afire, with self ever-composed, I, an Arahant, practice the holy life.”

“Māno hi te brāhmaṇa khāribhāro,

Kodho dhumo bhasmani mosavajjaṃ;

Jivhā sujā hadayaṃ jotiṭhānaṃ,

Attā sudanto purisassa joti.

“Conceit, O brahmin, is your yoke-burden; anger is the smoke, falsehood the ashes. The tongue is the sacrificial ladle, the heart is the place of the flame; a person's well-tamed self is the flame.”

“Dhammo [T 1.0249] rahado brāhmaṇa sīlatittho,

Anāvilo sabbhi sataṃ pasattho;

Yattha have vedaguno sinātā,

Anallagattāva anallīnagattāva (sī. pī. ka.) taranti pāraṃ.

“The Dhamma, O brahmin, is a lake with virtue as its ford, clear and praised by the good. Therein, indeed, those who have attained the final knowledge bathe, and with bodies unmoistened, they cross to the further shore.”

“Saccaṃ dhammo saṃyamo brahmacariyaṃ,

Majjhe sitā brāhmaṇa brahmapatti;

Sa [V 1.0198][P 1.0170] tujjubhūtesu namo karohi,

Tamahaṃ naraṃ dhammasārīti brūmī”ti.

“Truth, Dhamma, restraint, and the holy life: based on the middle, O brahmin, is the attainment of the sublime. Pay homage to those who are upright. Such a person I call one who has the Dhamma as their essence.”

Evaṃ [M 1.0172] vutte, sundarikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosī”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin Sundarikabhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama!...” and the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the Arahants.

10. Bahudhītarasuttaṃ

10. The Sutta about Many Daughters

196. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa catuddasa balībaddā naṭṭhā honti. Atha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo te balībadde gavesanto yena so vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā addasa bhagavantaṃ tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe nisinnaṃ pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

196. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time, fourteen oxen belonging to a certain brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan were lost. Then that brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, searching for those oxen, approached that forest grove. Having approached, he saw the Blessed One sitting in that forest grove, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him. Having seen him, he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Na [T 1.0250] hi nūnimassa nahanūnimassa (sī. syā. kaṃ.) samaṇassa, balībaddā catuddasa;

Ajjasaṭṭhiṃ na dissanti, tenāyaṃ samaṇo sukhī.

“Surely, for this ascetic, there are no fourteen oxen that have been missing for six days now; therefore, this ascetic is happy.”

“Na hi nūnimassa samaṇassa, tilākhettasmi pāpakā;

Ekapaṇṇā dupaṇṇā dvipaṇṇā (sī. pī.) ca, tenāyaṃ samaṇo sukhī.

“Surely, for this ascetic, there are no wretched sesame stumps in his field with only one or two leaves remaining; therefore, this ascetic is happy.”

“Na hi nūnimassa samaṇassa, tucchakoṭṭhasmi mūsikā;

Ussoḷhikāya naccanti, tenāyaṃ samaṇo sukhī.

“Surely, for this ascetic, there are no mice dancing boisterously in his empty granary; therefore, this ascetic is happy.”

“Na hi nūnimassa samaṇassa, santhāro sattamāsiko;

Uppāṭakehi sañchanno, tenāyaṃ samaṇo sukhī.

“Surely, for this ascetic, there is no seven-month-old grass mat covered with bugs; therefore, this ascetic is happy.”

“Na [V 1.0199] hi nūnimassa samaṇassa, vidhavā satta dhītaro;

Ekaputtā duputtā dviputtā (sī. pī.) ca, tenāyaṃ samaṇo sukhī.

“Surely, for this ascetic, there are no seven widowed daughters, some with one son, some with two; therefore, this ascetic is happy.”

“Na hi nūnimassa samaṇassa, piṅgalā tilakāhatā;

Sottaṃ pādena bodheti, tenāyaṃ samaṇo sukhī.

“Surely, for this ascetic, there is no tawny, spotted wife who wakes him from sleep by kicking him with her foot; therefore, this ascetic is happy.”

“Na hi nūnimassa samaṇassa, paccūsamhi iṇāyikā;

Detha dethāti codenti, tenāyaṃ samaṇo sukhī”ti.

“Surely, for this ascetic, there are no creditors at dawn urging him, saying, ‘Pay up! Pay up!’; therefore, this ascetic is happy.”

“Na [M 1.0173] hi mayhaṃ brāhmaṇa, balībaddā catuddasa;

Ajjasaṭṭhiṃ na dissanti, tenāhaṃ brāhmaṇā sukhī.

“Truly, O brahmin, for me there are no fourteen oxen that have been missing for six days now; therefore I, O brahmin, am happy.”

“Na [P 1.0171] hi mayhaṃ brāhmaṇa, tilākhettasmi pāpakā;

Ekapaṇṇā dupaṇṇā ca, tenāhaṃ brāhmaṇā sukhī.

“Truly, O brahmin, for me there are no wretched sesame stumps in a field with only one or two leaves remaining; therefore I, O brahmin, am happy.”

“Na hi mayhaṃ brāhmaṇa, tucchakoṭṭhasmi mūsikā;

Ussoḷhikāya naccanti, tenāhaṃ brāhmaṇā sukhī.

“Truly, O brahmin, for me there are no mice dancing boisterously in an empty granary; therefore I, O brahmin, am happy.”

“Na [T 1.0251] hi mayhaṃ brāhmaṇa, santhāro sattamāsiko;

Uppāṭakehi sañchanno, tenāhaṃ brāhmaṇā sukhī.

“Truly, O brahmin, for me there is no seven-month-old grass mat covered with bugs; therefore I, O brahmin, am happy.”

“Na hi mayhaṃ brāhmaṇa, vidhavā satta dhītaro;

Ekaputtā duputtā ca, tenāhaṃ brāhmaṇā sukhī.

“Truly, O brahmin, for me there are no seven widowed daughters, some with one son, some with two; therefore I, O brahmin, am happy.”

“Na hi mayhaṃ brāhmaṇa, piṅgalā tilakāhatā;

Sottaṃ pādena bodheti, tenāhaṃ brāhmaṇā sukhī.

“Truly, O brahmin, for me there is no tawny, spotted wife who wakes me from sleep by kicking me with her foot; therefore I, O brahmin, am happy.”

“Na [V 1.0200] hi mayhaṃ brāhmaṇa, paccūsamhi iṇāyikā;

Detha dethāti codenti, tenāhaṃ brāhmaṇā sukhī”ti.

“Truly, O brahmin, for me there are no creditors at dawn urging me, saying, ‘Pay up! Pay up!’; therefore I, O brahmin, am happy.”

Evaṃ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evameva bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ bhoto gotamassa santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan said this to the Blessed One: ‘Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! Just as one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the path to one who is lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—in the same way has the Dhamma been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama. I go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May I receive the going forth in Master Gotama's presence, may I receive the higher ordination.’”

Alattha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno panāyasmā bhāradvājo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ [T 1.0252] diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ [M 1.0174] itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṃ ahosīti.

The brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, and he received the higher ordination. And not long after his higher ordination, the Venerable Bhāradvāja, dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute, before long realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. Having actualized it, he entered upon and dwelled in it. He understood: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’ And the Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the Arahants.

Arahantavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Arahants.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Dhanañjānī ca akkosaṃ, asurindaṃ bilaṅgikaṃ;

Ahiṃsakaṃ jaṭā ceva, suddhikañceva aggikā;

Sundarikaṃ bahudhītarena ca te dasāti.

Dhanañjānī, Akkosa, Asundarī, Biliṅgika; Ahiṃsaka and Jaṭā, as well as Suddhika and Aggika; Sundarika, and with Bahudhītu—these are the ten.

2. Upāsakavaggo

2. The Chapter on Lay Followers

1. Kasibhāradvājasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse to Kasibhāradvāja

197. Evaṃ [T 1.0253][V 1.0201][P 1.0172] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā magadhesu viharati dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ ekanāḷāyaṃ brāhmaṇagāme. Tena kho pana samayena kasibhāradvājassa kasikabhāradvājassa (ka.) brāhmaṇassa pañcamattāni naṅgalasatāni payuttāni honti vappakāle. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kasibhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa kammanto tenupasaṅkami.

197. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans in the Southern Hills, in the brahmin village of Ekanāḷā. At that time, five hundred of the brahmin Kasibhāradvāja's plows were yoked for the time of sowing. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having adjusted his lower robe and taking his bowl and outer robe, approached the place where the brahmin Kasibhāradvāja was working.
