Tena kho pana samayena kasibhāradvājassa brāhmaṇassa parivesanā vattati. Atha kho bhagavā yena parivesanā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Addasā kho kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ piṇḍāya ṭhitaṃ. Disvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahaṃ kho, samaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmi. Tvampi, samaṇa, kasassu ca vapassu ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjassū”ti. “Ahampi kho, brāhmaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmī”ti. Na kho mayaṃ passāma bhoto gotamassa yugaṃ vā naṅgalaṃ vā phālaṃ vā pācanaṃ vā balībadde vā, atha ca pana [T 1.0254] bhavaṃ gotamo evamāha – “ahampi kho, brāhmaṇa, kasāmi ca vapāmi ca, kasitvā ca vapitvā ca bhuñjāmī”ti[M 1.0175]. Atha kho kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

At that time, the brahmin Kasibhāradvāja's distribution of food was taking place. Then the Blessed One approached where the distribution was and, having approached, stood to one side. The brahmin Kasibhāradvāja saw the Blessed One standing for alms. Having seen him, he said this to the Blessed One: “I, ascetic, plow and sow, and having plowed and sown, I eat. You too, ascetic, should plow and sow; having plowed and sown, you should eat.” “I too, brahmin, plow and sow, and having plowed and sown, I eat.” “We do not see the Venerable Gotama’s yoke, or plow, or plowshare, or goad, or oxen. And yet the Venerable Gotama says this: ‘I too, brahmin, plow and sow, and having plowed and sown, I eat.’” Then the brahmin Kasibhāradvāja addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kassako paṭijānāsi, na ca passāmi te kasiṃ;

Kassako pucchito brūhi, kathaṃ jānemu taṃ kasi”nti.

“You claim to be a farmer, yet I do not see your farming. Being asked, O farmer, tell me, how may we know of that farming of yours?”

“Saddhā bījaṃ tapo vuṭṭhi, paññā me yuganaṅgalaṃ;

Hirī īsā mano yottaṃ, sati me phālapācanaṃ.

“Faith is the seed, restraint the rain; wisdom is my yoke and plow. Moral shame is the pole, mind the yoke-tie; mindfulness is my plowshare and goad.

“Kāyagutto [V 1.0202] vacīgutto, āhāre udare yato;

Saccaṃ karomi niddānaṃ, soraccaṃ me pamocanaṃ.

Guarded in body, guarded in speech, restrained in food in the belly; I make truth my weeding, gentleness my unharnessing.

“Vīriyaṃ [P 1.0173] me dhuradhorayhaṃ, yogakkhemādhivāhanaṃ;

Gacchati anivattantaṃ, yattha gantvā na socati.

Energy is my beast of burden, bearing me to security from bondage. It goes on without turning back, to where, having gone, one does not grieve.

“Evamesā kasī kaṭṭhā, sā hoti amatapphalā;

Etaṃ kasiṃ kasitvāna, sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti.

In this way is this farming tilled; it has the Deathless as its fruit. Having tilled this farming, one is freed from all suffering.”

“Bhuñjatu bhavaṃ gotamo. Kassako bhavaṃ. Yañhi bhavaṃ gotamo amatapphalampi kasiṃ kasatī”ti bhāsatīti (ka.).

“Let the Venerable Gotama eat. The Venerable One is a farmer, for the Venerable Gotama tills a farming that has the Deathless as its fruit.”

“Gāthābhigītaṃ me abhojaneyyaṃ,

Sampassataṃ brāhmaṇa nesa dhammo;

Gāthābhigītaṃ panudanti buddhā,

Dhamme sati brāhmaṇa vuttiresā.

“What is gained by the reciting of verses is not to be eaten by me. Brahmin, this is not the principle for those who see. The Buddhas reject what is gained by reciting verses; Brahmin, while this principle exists, this is their way of life.

“Aññena [T 1.0255] ca kevalinaṃ mahesiṃ,

Khīṇāsavaṃ kukkuccavūpasantaṃ;

Annena pānena upaṭṭhahassu,

Khettañhi taṃ puññapekkhassa hotī”ti.

But with other food and drink you should serve the one who is whole, the great sage, the one whose taints are destroyed and whose remorse is stilled. For that is the field for one who looks for merit.”

Evaṃ vutte, kasibhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Kasibhāradvāja said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Venerable Gotama! … From this day forward, may the Venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for as long as life lasts.”

2. Udayasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse to Udaya

198. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena [V 1.0203] udayassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Atha [M 1.0176] kho udayo brāhmaṇo bhagavato pattaṃ odanena pūresi. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena udayassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami…pe… tatiyampi kho udayo brāhmaṇo bhagavato pattaṃ odanena [P 1.0174] pūretvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “pakaṭṭhakoyaṃ samaṇo gotamo punappunaṃ āgacchatī”ti.

198. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having adjusted his lower robe and taking his bowl and outer robe, approached the residence of the brahmin Udaya. Then the brahmin Udaya filled the Blessed One's bowl with rice. For a second time... for a third time, the brahmin Udaya, having filled the Blessed One's bowl with rice, said this to the Blessed One: 'This ascetic Gotama is addicted to taste; he comes again and again.'

“Punappunañceva [T 1.0256] vapanti bījaṃ, punappunaṃ vassati devarājā;

Punappunaṃ khettaṃ kasanti kassakā, punappunaṃ dhaññamupeti raṭṭhaṃ.

“Again and again they sow the seed; again and again the cloud-god king sends rain. Again and again the farmers plow the field; again and again grain comes to the country.

“Punappunaṃ yācakā yācayanti, punappunaṃ dānapatī dadanti;

Punappunaṃ dānapatī daditvā, punappunaṃ saggamupenti ṭhānaṃ.

“Again and again beggars beg; again and again donors give. Again and again, having given, donors approach a heavenly place.

“Punappunaṃ khīranikā duhanti, punappunaṃ vaccho upeti mātaraṃ;

Punappunaṃ kilamati phandati ca, punappunaṃ gabbhamupeti mando.

“Again and again those who want milk do the milking; again and again the calf approaches its mother. Again and again one becomes weary and trembles; again and again the fool enters a womb.

“Punappunaṃ jāyati mīyati ca, punappunaṃ sivathikaṃ sīvathikaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) haranti;

Maggañca laddhā apunabbhavāya, na punappunaṃ jāyati bhūripañño”ti punappunaṃ jāyati bhūripaññoti (syā. kaṃ. ka.).

“Again and again one is born and dies; again and again they carry one to the charnel ground. But having found the path to no further becoming, the one of vast wisdom is not born again and again.”

Evaṃ vutte, udayo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Udaya said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, Master Gotama! ... From this day forward, may Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for as long as life lasts.'

3. Devahitasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse concerning Devahita

199. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 1.0257]. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā vātehābādhiko hoti; āyasmā ca upavāṇo bhagavato upaṭṭhāko hoti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ āmantesi – “iṅgha me tvaṃ, upavāṇa, uṇhodakaṃ jānāhī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavato paṭissutvā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena devahitassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tuṇhībhūto ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Addasā kho devahito brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṃ [V 1.0204] upavāṇaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ. Disvāna āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

199. At Sāvatthī. Now at that time, the Blessed One was afflicted with a wind-ailment, and the Venerable Upavāṇa was the Blessed One's attendant. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Upavāṇa: 'Come now, Upavāṇa, please find some hot water for me.' 'Yes, venerable sir,' the Venerable Upavāṇa replied to the Blessed One. Having assented, he adjusted his lower robe, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he approached the residence of the brahmin Devahita. Having approached, he stood to one side in silence. The brahmin Devahita saw the Venerable Upavāṇa standing to one side in silence. Seeing him, he addressed the Venerable Upavāṇa in verse:

“Tuṇhībhūto [M 1.0177][P 1.0175] bhavaṃ tiṭṭhaṃ, muṇḍo saṅghāṭipāruto;

Kiṃ patthayāno kiṃ esaṃ, kiṃ nu yācitumāgato”ti.

“Standing there in silence, venerable sir, shaven-headed, draped in the patchwork robe; what are you hoping for, what are you seeking, what have you come to ask for?”

“Arahaṃ sugato loke, vātehābādhiko muni;

Sace uṇhodakaṃ atthi, munino dehi brāhmaṇa.

“The Arahant, the Well-Farer in the world, the Sage, is afflicted by a wind-ailment. Brahmin, if there is hot water, please give it for the Sage.

“Pūjito pūjaneyyānaṃ, sakkareyyāna sakkato;

Apacito apaceyyānaṃ apacineyyānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.) ṭīkā oloketabbā, tassa icchāmi hātave”ti.

“He is honored by the honorable, respected by the respectable, venerated by the venerable. It is for him that I wish to fetch it.”

Atha kho devahito brāhmaṇo uṇhodakassa kājaṃ purisena gāhāpetvā phāṇitassa ca puṭaṃ āyasmato upavāṇassa pādāsi. Atha kho āyasmā upavāṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ [T 1.0258] uṇhodakena nhāpetvā nahāpetvā (sī. pī.) uṇhodakena phāṇitaṃ āloletvā bhagavato pādāsi. Atha kho bhagavato ābādho paṭippassambhi.

Then the brahmin Devahita had a man take up a carrying-pole load of hot water and a packet of molasses, and gave it to the Venerable Upavāṇa. Then the Venerable Upavāṇa approached the Blessed One and, having bathed the Blessed One with the hot water, he dissolved the molasses in hot water and offered it to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One's ailment subsided.

Atha kho devahito brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho devahito brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the brahmin Devahita approached the Blessed One and exchanged courteous and memorable greetings with him. Having concluded this exchange, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Devahita addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Kattha dajjā deyyadhammaṃ, kattha dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ;

Kathañhi yajamānassa, kathaṃ ijjhati dakkhiṇā”ti.

“To whom should a gift be given? A gift to whom has great fruit? How for the one who sacrifices, how is the offering successful?”

“Pubbenivāsaṃ yo vedī, saggāpāyañca passati;

Atho jātikkhayaṃ patto, abhiññāvosito muni.

“The sage who knows former lives, who sees the heavens and the planes of deprivation, and who has reached the destruction of birth, one who has reached perfection through direct knowledge—

“Ettha [V 1.0205] dajjā deyyadhammaṃ, ettha dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ;

Evañhi yajamānassa, evaṃ ijjhati dakkhiṇā”ti.

“To such a one a gift should be given; a gift to such a one has great fruit. Thus for the one who sacrifices, thus is the offering successful.”

Evaṃ vutte, devahito brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Devahita said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, venerable Gotama! ... From this day forward, may venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for as long as life lasts.'

4. Mahāsālasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Wealthy Brahmin

200. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 1.0178]. Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇamahāsālo lūkho lūkhapāvuraṇo [P 1.0176] lūkhapāpuraṇo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho taṃ brāhmaṇamahāsālaṃ bhagavā [T 1.0259] etadavoca – “kinnu tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, lūkho lūkhapāvuraṇo”ti? “Idha me, bho gotama, cattāro puttā. Te maṃ dārehi saṃpuccha gharā nikkhāmentī”ti. “Tena hi tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, imā gāthāyo pariyāpuṇitvā sabhāyaṃ mahājanakāye sannipatite puttesu ca sannisinnesu bhāsassu –

200. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain wealthy brahmin, shabby and wearing shabby clothes, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One. After exchanging courteous and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. To that wealthy brahmin seated to one side, the Blessed One said this: “Why, brahmin, are you shabby and wearing shabby clothes?” “Here, venerable Gotama, I have four sons. They, having consulted with their wives, drive me out of the house.” “Well then, brahmin, having learned these verses, you should recite them in the assembly when the great crowd has gathered and your sons are seated there:

“Yehi jātehi nandissaṃ, yesañca bhavamicchisaṃ;

Te maṃ dārehi saṃpuccha, sāva vārenti sūkaraṃ.

“Those at whose birth I rejoiced, and for whom I desired prosperity; they, having consulted with their wives, now drive me away, as dogs would a pig.

“Asantā kira maṃ jammā, tāta tātāti bhāsare;

Rakkhasā puttarūpena, te jahanti vayogataṃ.

“Indeed, those ignoble, base ones call me ‘father, father’; they are demons in the form of sons who abandon me now that I am old.

“Assova jiṇṇo nibbhogo, khādanā apanīyati;

Bālakānaṃ pitā thero, parāgāresu bhikkhati.

“Just as an old horse, no longer of use, is removed from its fodder; so the father of fools, an elder, begs in others’ houses.

“Daṇḍova kira me seyyo, yañce puttā anassavā;

Caṇḍampi goṇaṃ vāreti, atho caṇḍampi kukkuraṃ.

“Indeed, a staff is better for me than disobedient sons; for it restrains even a fierce ox, and also a fierce dog.

“Andhakāre [V 1.0206] pure hoti, gambhīre gādhamedhati;

Daṇḍassa ānubhāvena, khalitvā patitiṭṭhatī”ti.

“In darkness it goes before, in deep places it finds a foothold; by the power of the staff, having stumbled, one stands firm again.”

Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo pariyāpuṇitvā sabhāyaṃ mahājanakāye sannipatite puttesu ca sannisinnesu abhāsi –

Then that wealthy brahmin, having learned these verses in the presence of the Blessed One, recited them in the assembly when the great crowd had gathered and his sons were seated:

“Yehi jātehi nandissaṃ, yesañca bhavamicchisaṃ;

Te [T 1.0260] maṃ dārehi saṃpuccha, sāva vārenti sūkaraṃ.

“Those at whose birth I rejoiced, and for whom I desired prosperity; they, having consulted with their wives, now drive me away, as dogs would a pig.

“Asantā kira maṃ jammā, tāta tātāti bhāsare;

Rakkhasā puttarūpena, te jahanti vayogataṃ.

“Indeed, those ignoble, base ones call me ‘father, father’; they are demons in the form of sons who abandon me now that I am old.

“Assova [M 1.0179] jiṇṇo nibbhogo, khādanā apanīyati;

Bālakānaṃ pitā thero, parāgāresu bhikkhati.

“Just as an old horse, no longer of use, is removed from its fodder; so the father of fools, an elder, begs in others’ houses.

“Daṇḍova kira me seyyo, yañce puttā anassavā;

Caṇḍampi goṇaṃ vāreti, atho caṇḍampi kukkuraṃ.

“Indeed, a staff is better for me than disobedient sons; for it restrains even a fierce ox, and also a fierce dog.

“Andhakāre pure hoti, gambhīre gādhamedhati;

Daṇḍassa ānubhāvena, khalitvā patitiṭṭhatī”ti.

“In darkness it goes before, in deep places it finds a foothold; by the power of the staff, having stumbled, one stands firm again.”

Atha [P 1.0177] kho naṃ brāhmaṇamahāsālaṃ puttā gharaṃ netvā nhāpetvā paccekaṃ dussayugena acchādesuṃ. Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo ekaṃ dussayugaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “mayaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā nāma ācariyassa ācariyadhanaṃ pariyesāma. Paṭiggaṇhatu me bhavaṃ gotamo ācariyadhana”nti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā anukampaṃ upādāya. Atha kho so brāhmaṇamahāsālo bhagavantaṃ [V 1.0207] etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

Then the sons took that wealthy brahmin home, bathed him, and each dressed him in a pair of cloths. Then that wealthy brahmin, taking one pair of cloths, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One. After exchanging courteous and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that wealthy brahmin said to the Blessed One: “We who are called brahmins, venerable Gotama, seek a teacher’s fee for the teacher. May venerable Gotama accept this teacher’s fee from me.” The Blessed One accepted it out of compassion. Then that wealthy brahmin said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable Gotama! ... From this day forward, may venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for as long as life lasts.”

5. Mānatthaddhasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the One Stiff with Conceit

201. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 1.0261]. Tena kho pana samayena mānatthaddho nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati. So neva mātaraṃ abhivādeti, na pitaraṃ abhivādeti, na ācariyaṃ abhivādeti, na jeṭṭhabhātaraṃ abhivādeti. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṃ deseti. Atha kho mānatthaddhassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho samaṇo gotamo mahatiyā parisāya parivuto dhammaṃ deseti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṃ. Sace maṃ samaṇo gotamo ālapissati, ahampi taṃ ālapissāmi. No ce maṃ samaṇo gotamo ālapissati, ahampi nālapissāmī”ti. Atha kho mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tuṇhībhūto ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ nālapi. Atha kho mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo – ‘nāyaṃ samaṇo [M 1.0180] gotamo kiñci jānātī’ti tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi. Atha [P 1.0178] kho bhagavā mānatthaddhassa brāhmaṇassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mānatthaddhaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

201. At Sāvatthī. At that time, a brahmin named Mānatthaddha was dwelling in Sāvatthī. He did not pay homage to his mother, nor to his father, nor to his teacher, nor to his elder brother. Now at that time, the Blessed One was teaching the Dhamma surrounded by a large assembly. Then this thought occurred to the brahmin Mānatthaddha: “This recluse Gotama is teaching the Dhamma surrounded by a large assembly. It would be good if I were to approach the recluse Gotama. If the recluse Gotama speaks to me, I too will speak to him. But if the recluse Gotama does not speak to me, I too will not speak to him.” Then the brahmin Mānatthaddha approached the Blessed One; having approached, he stood silently to one side. Then the Blessed One did not speak to him. Then the brahmin Mānatthaddha, thinking, “This recluse Gotama knows nothing,” desired to turn back from that very place. Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the thought in the mind of the brahmin Mānatthaddha, addressed the brahmin Mānatthaddha with a verse:

“Na mānaṃ brāhmaṇa sādhu, atthikassīdha brāhmaṇa;

Yena atthena āgacchi, tamevamanubrūhaye”ti.

“Conceit is not good, O brahmin, for one who has a purpose here. That very purpose for which you have come, that you should cultivate.”

Atha kho mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo – “cittaṃ me samaṇo gotamo jānātī”ti tattheva bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavato pādāni [T 1.0262] mukhena ca paricumbati pāṇīhi ca parisambāhati, nāmañca sāveti – “mānatthaddhāhaṃ, bho gotama, mānatthaddhāhaṃ, bho gotamā”ti. Atha kho sā parisā abbhutacittajātā abbhutacittajātā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), acchariyabbhutacittajātā (ka.) ahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho! Ayañhi mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo neva mātaraṃ abhivādeti, na pitaraṃ abhivādeti, na ācariyaṃ abhivādeti, na jeṭṭhabhātaraṃ abhivādeti; atha ca pana samaṇe gotame evarūpaṃ paramanipaccakāraṃ karotī’ti. Atha kho bhagavā mānatthaddhaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “alaṃ, brāhmaṇa[V 1.0208], uṭṭhehi, sake āsane nisīda. Yato te mayi cittaṃ pasanna”nti. Atha kho mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo sake āsane nisīditvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the brahmin Mānatthaddha, thinking, “The recluse Gotama knows my mind,” right there fell at the Blessed One's feet with his head, kissed the Blessed One's feet with his mouth and massaged them with his hands, and announced his name: “I am Mānatthaddha, venerable Gotama, I am Mānatthaddha, venerable Gotama!” Then that assembly was filled with wonder and amazement, thinking: “It is wonderful, sirs, it is astonishing! For this brahmin Mānatthaddha does not pay homage to his mother, nor to his father, nor to his teacher, nor to his elder brother; and yet towards the recluse Gotama he performs such supreme reverence!” Then the Blessed One said this to the brahmin Mānatthaddha: “Enough, brahmin. Arise and sit in your own seat, since your mind has become serene towards me.” Then the brahmin Mānatthaddha, having sat down in his own seat, addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Kesu na mānaṃ kayirātha, kesu cassa sagāravo;

Kyassa apacitā assu, kyassu sādhu supūjitā”ti.

“Towards whom should one not be conceited? Towards whom should one be respectful? Who should be revered by one? And who should be well and truly honored by one?”

“Mātari pitari cāpi, atho jeṭṭhamhi bhātari;

Ācariye catutthamhi,

Tesu na mānaṃ kayirātha;

Tesu assa sagāravo,

Tyassa apacitā assu;

Tyassu sādhu supūjitā.

“Towards one's mother and one's father, and also towards one's elder brother, and the teacher as the fourth—towards them one should not be conceited, towards them one should be respectful. They should be revered by one; they should be well and truly honored by one.

“Arahante sītībhūte, katakicce anāsave;

Nihacca mānaṃ athaddho, te namasse anuttare”ti.

“Towards the Arahants—who have become tranquil, have done what was to be done, are free from taints—having subdued conceit and being no longer stiff, you should pay homage to them, the unsurpassed.”

Evaṃ [M 1.0181] vutte, mānatthaddho brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Mānatthaddha said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable Gotama! … From this day forward, may the venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

6. Paccanīkasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Antagonist

202. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 1.0263][P 1.0179]. Tena kho pana samayena paccanīkasāto nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati. Atha kho paccanīkasātassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena samaṇo gotamo tenupasaṅkameyyaṃ. Yaṃ yadeva samaṇo gotamo bhāsissati taṃ tadevassāhaṃ tadeva sāhaṃ (ka.) paccanīkāssa”nti paccanīkassanti (pī.), paccanīkasātanti (ka.). Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā abbhokāse caṅkamati. Atha kho paccanīkasāto brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ caṅkamantaṃ etadavoca – ‘bhaṇa samaṇadhamma’nti.

202. At Sāvatthī. At that time, a brahmin named Paccanīkasāta was residing in Sāvatthī. Then this thought occurred to the brahmin Paccanīkasāta: “It would be good if I were to approach the recluse Gotama. Whatever the recluse Gotama says, I will oppose that very thing.” At that time, the Blessed One was walking in an open space. Then the brahmin Paccanīkasāta approached the Blessed One; having approached, while the Blessed One was walking, he said to him: “Recluse, declare the Dhamma.”

“Na [V 1.0209] paccanīkasātena, suvijānaṃ subhāsitaṃ;

Upakkiliṭṭhacittena, sārambhabahulena ca.

“A well-spoken teaching is not easily understood by one who delights in opposition, by one with a defiled mind, and by one who is full of animosity.

“Yo ca vineyya sārambhaṃ, appasādañca cetaso;

Āghātaṃ paṭinissajja, sa ve sace (syā. kaṃ. ka.) jaññā subhāsita”nti.

“But whoever, having dispelled animosity and displeasure of mind, and having relinquished ill will, would indeed understand the well-spoken teaching.”

Evaṃ vutte, paccanīkasāto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Paccanīkasāta said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable Gotama, excellent, venerable Gotama! … May the venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.”

7. Navakammikasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Overseer of Works

203. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe[T 1.0264]. Tena kho pana samayena navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe kammantaṃ kārāpeti. Addasā kho navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ aññatarasmiṃ sālarukkhamūle nisinnaṃ pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. Disvānassa etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho imasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe kammantaṃ kārāpento ramāmi. Ayaṃ samaṇo gotamo kiṃ kārāpento ramatī”ti? Atha [M 1.0182] kho navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā [P 1.0180] tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

203. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time the brahmin Navakammika Bhāradvāja was having work done in that forest grove. The brahmin Navakammika Bhāradvāja saw the Blessed One sitting at the foot of a certain sāl tree, having folded his legs crosswise, held his body erect, and established mindfulness before him. Having seen him, this thought occurred to him: “I delight in having work done in this forest grove. In having what work done does this recluse Gotama delight?” Then the brahmin Navakammika Bhāradvāja approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Ke nu kammantā karīyanti, bhikkhu sālavane tava;

Yadekako araññasmiṃ, ratiṃ vindati gotamo”ti.

“What works indeed are being done, monk, in your sāl forest, that you, Gotama, find delight alone in the wilderness?”

“Na me vanasmiṃ karaṇīyamatthi,

Ucchinnamūlaṃ me vanaṃ visūkaṃ;

Svāhaṃ vane nibbanatho visallo,

Eko rame aratiṃ vippahāyā”ti.

“For me, there is no work to be done in the forest; my forest has been uprooted, its thorns cleared away. Therefore I, being without the forest of craving and free from the dart of passion, delight alone, having abandoned discontent.”

Evaṃ [V 1.0210] vutte, navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Navakammikabhāradvāja said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! … May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.”

8. Kaṭṭhahārasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Firewood Gatherers

204. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhāradvājagottassa brāhmaṇassa [T 1.0265] sambahulā antevāsikā kaṭṭhahārakā māṇavakā yena vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā addasaṃsu bhagavantaṃ tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe nisinnaṃ pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. Disvāna yena bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhāradvājagottaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavocuṃ – “yagghe, bhavaṃ jāneyyāsi! Asukasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe samaṇo nisinno pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā”. Atha kho bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo tehi māṇavakehi saddhiṃ yena so vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho bhagavantaṃ tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe nisinnaṃ pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

204. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time, several young brahmin students, who were firewood gatherers and pupils of a certain brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, approached that forest grove. Having approached, they saw the Blessed One sitting in that forest grove, having folded his legs crosswise, with his body held erect, and having established mindfulness before him. Seeing him, they approached the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan and said to him: 'Sir, you should know! In such-and-such a forest grove, an ascetic is sitting, having folded his legs crosswise, with his body held erect, and having established mindfulness before him.' Then the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, together with those young students, approached that forest grove. He saw the Blessed One sitting there, having folded his legs crosswise, with his body held erect, and having established mindfulness before him. Seeing him, he approached the Blessed One and addressed him with a verse:

“Gambhīrarūpe bahubherave vane,

Suññaṃ araññaṃ vijanaṃ vigāhiya;

Aniñjamānena [P 1.0181] ṭhitena vaggunā,

Sucārurūpaṃ vata bhikkhu jhāyasi.

“In the forest, deep and fearsome, having entered this empty, desolate, and secluded wilderness; with a posture unmoving, steadfast, and graceful, how beautifully, O monk, you meditate!”

“Na [M 1.0183] yattha gītaṃ napi yattha vāditaṃ,

Eko araññe vanavassito muni;

Accherarūpaṃ paṭibhāti maṃ idaṃ,

Yadekako pītimano vane vase.

“Where there is no song, nor any music, the sage dwells alone, resorting to the forest. This appears wondrous to me: that you dwell alone in the forest with a joyful mind.”

“Maññāmahaṃ [T 1.0266] lokādhipatisahabyataṃ,

Ākaṅkhamāno tidivaṃ anuttaraṃ;

Kasmā [V 1.0211] bhavaṃ vijanamaraññamassito,

Tapo idha kubbasi brahmapattiyā”ti.

“I suppose that, longing for the unsurpassed celestial realm, you desire companionship with the lord of the world. Why, sir, do you resort to this desolate wilderness? Do you practice austerity here for the attainment of Brahma?”

“Yā kāci kaṅkhā abhinandanā vā,

Anekadhātūsu puthū sadāsitā;

Aññāṇamūlappabhavā pajappitā,

Sabbā mayā byantikatā samūlikā.

“Whatever longings and delights, manifold, always dependent on diverse elements, those cravings arisen from the root of ignorance—all have been eliminated by me, together with their root.”

“Svāhaṃ akaṅkho asito anūpayo,

Sabbesu dhammesu visuddhadassano;

Pappuyya sambodhimanuttaraṃ sivaṃ,

Jhāyāmahaṃ brahma raho visārado”ti.

“So I, without longing, unattached, and without clinging, with pure vision regarding all dhammas, having attained the unsurpassed, sublime enlightenment, meditate fearlessly in seclusion in the great forest.”

Evaṃ vutte, bhāradvājagotto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! … From this day forth, may Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for as long as life lasts.”

9. Mātuposakasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Supporting Parents

205. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho mātuposako brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mātuposako brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahañhi, bho [T 1.0267] gotama, dhammena bhikkhaṃ pariyesāmi, dhammena bhikkhaṃ pariyesitvā mātāpitaro posemi. Kaccāhaṃ, bho gotama, evaṃkārī kiccakārī homī”ti? “Taggha tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, evaṃkārī kiccakārī hosi. Yo kho, brāhmaṇa, dhammena bhikkhaṃ pariyesati, dhammena bhikkhaṃ [P 1.0182] pariyesitvā mātāpitaro poseti, bahuṃ so puññaṃ pasavatī”ti.

205. At Sāvatthī. Then the brahmin Mātuposaka approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged courteous and memorable greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded this talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the brahmin Mātuposaka said to the Blessed One: 'I, Master Gotama, seek alms righteously; having sought alms righteously, I support my mother and father. Master Gotama, in acting thus, am I doing what should be done?' 'Indeed, brahmin, in acting thus, you are doing what should be done. Whoever, brahmin, seeks alms righteously, and having sought alms righteously, supports his mother and father, generates much merit.'

“Yo [V 1.0212][M 1.0184] mātaraṃ pitaraṃ vā, macco dhammena posati;

Tāya naṃ pāricariyāya, mātāpitūsu paṇḍitā;

Idheva naṃ pasaṃsanti, pecca sagge pamodatī”ti.

That mortal who righteously supports his mother or father—for that service to his parents the wise praise him here in this very life, and after passing away, he rejoices in heaven.

Evaṃ vutte, mātuposako brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Mātuposaka said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, Master Gotama, excellent, Master Gotama! … From this day forth, may Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for as long as life lasts.'

10. Bhikkhakasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse with the Beggar

206. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho bhikkhako brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho bhikkhako brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahampi kho, bho gotama, bhikkhako, bhavampi bhikkhako, idha no kiṃ nānākaraṇa”nti?

206. At Sāvatthī. Then the begging brahmin approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged courteous and memorable greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded this talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the begging brahmin said to the Blessed One: 'I too, Master Gotama, am a mendicant, and you too are a mendicant. Herein, what is the difference between us?'

“Na tena bhikkhako hoti, yāvatā bhikkhate pare;

Vissaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya, bhikkhu hoti na tāvatā.

One is not a mendicant merely because one begs from others. By undertaking a foul practice, one is not a monk on that account.

“Yodha [T 1.0268] puññañca pāpañca, bāhitvā brahmacariyaṃ;

Saṅkhāya loke carati, sa ve bhikkhūti vuccatī”ti.

Whoever here, having dispelled both merit and evil, lives the holy life, conducting himself in the world with understanding—he, indeed, is called a monk.

Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhako brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the begging brahmin said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, Master Gotama, excellent, Master Gotama! … From this day forth, may Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for as long as life lasts.'

11. Saṅgāravasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse with Saṅgārava

207. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena saṅgāravo nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati udakasuddhiko, udakena parisuddhiṃ pacceti, sāyaṃ pātaṃ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya [V 1.0213] pāvisi. Sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [P 1.0183] nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante, saṅgāravo nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasati udakasuddhiko[M 1.0185], udakena suddhiṃ pacceti, sāyaṃ pātaṃ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena saṅgāravassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.

207. At Sāvatthī. At that time, a brahmin named Saṅgārava resided in Sāvatthī. He believed in purification by water and trusted in it, living devoted to the practice of descending into water in the evening and the morning. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms. Having walked for alms in Sāvatthī and returned from his alms round after the meal, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, here in Sāvatthī there is a brahmin named Saṅgārava who believes in purification by water and trusts in it, living devoted to the practice of descending into water in the evening and the morning. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would visit the residence of the brahmin Saṅgārava, out of compassion.' The Blessed One consented through silence.

Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena saṅgāravassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami[T 1.0269]; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho saṅgāravaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, udakasuddhiko, udakena suddhiṃ paccesi, sāyaṃ pātaṃ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharasī”ti? “Evaṃ, bho gotama”. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, atthavasaṃ sampassamāno udakasuddhiko, udakasuddhiṃ paccesi, sāyaṃ pātaṃ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharasī”ti? “Idha me, bho gotama idha me bho gotama ahaṃ (pī. ka.), yaṃ divā pāpakammaṃ kataṃ hoti, taṃ sāyaṃ nhānena nahānena (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pavāhemi, yaṃ rattiṃ pāpakammaṃ kataṃ hoti taṃ pātaṃ nhānena pavāhemi. Imaṃ khvāhaṃ, bho gotama, atthavasaṃ sampassamāno udakasuddhiko, udakena suddhiṃ paccemi, sāyaṃ pātaṃ udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharāmī”ti.

Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and went to the residence of the brahmin Saṅgārava. Having gone there, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the brahmin Saṅgārava approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. When their courteous and memorable conversation was concluded, he sat down to one side. To the brahmin Saṅgārava seated to one side, the Blessed One said this: 'Is it true, Brahmin, as it is said, that you believe in purification by water, trust in it, and live devoted to the practice of descending into water in the evening and the morning?' 'Yes, Master Gotama.' 'But, Brahmin, seeing what benefit do you believe in purification by water, trust in it, and live devoted to the practice of descending into water in the evening and the morning?' 'Here, Master Gotama, whatever evil deed I have done during the day, I wash it away by bathing in the evening. Whatever evil deed I have done during the night, I wash it away by bathing in the morning. Seeing this benefit, Master Gotama, I believe in purification by water, trust in it, and live devoted to the practice of descending into water in the evening and the morning.'

“Dhammo rahado brāhmaṇa sīlatittho,

Anāvilo sabbhi sataṃ pasattho;

Yattha have vedaguno sinātā,

Anallagattāva anallīnagattāva (ka.) taranti pāra”nti.

The Dhamma is a lake, Brahmin, with virtue as its bathing-place, clear and unclouded, praised by the good for the good. Therein, indeed, those perfected in knowledge bathe; and with bodies unwet, they cross to the far shore.

Evaṃ vutte, saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, the brahmin Saṅgārava said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! ... May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life, from this day forward.'

12. Khomadussasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse at Khomadussa

208. Evaṃ [T 1.0270][V 1.0214][P 1.0184] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati khomadussaṃ nāmaṃ sakyānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā [M 1.0186] pattacīvaramādāya khomadussaṃ nigamaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Tena kho pana samayena khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā sabhāyaṃ sannipatitā honti kenacideva karaṇīyena, devo ca ekamekaṃ phusāyati. Atha kho bhagavā yena sā sabhā tenupasaṅkami. Addasaṃsu khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna etadavocuṃ – “ke ca muṇḍakā samaṇakā, ke ca sabhādhammaṃ jānissantī”ti? Atha kho bhagavā khomadussake brāhmaṇagahapatike gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

208. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans in a market town of the Sakyans named Khomadussa. Then, the Blessed One dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe, and entered the market town of Khomadussa for alms-food. At that time, the brahmin householders of Khomadussa were gathered in the assembly hall for some business, and it was drizzling drop by drop. Then the Blessed One approached that assembly hall. The brahmin householders of Khomadussa saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, they said this: 'Who are these shavelings, these wretched ascetics? What could they know of the law of the assembly?' Then the Blessed One addressed the brahmin householders of Khomadussa with a verse:

“Nesā sabhā yattha na santi santo,

Santo na te ye na vadanti dhammaṃ;

Rāgañca dosañca pahāya mohaṃ,

Dhammaṃ vadantā ca bhavanti santo”ti.

That is not an assembly where the good are not present; they are not the good who do not speak the Dhamma. Having abandoned lust, hatred, and delusion, those who speak the Dhamma are indeed the good.

Evaṃ vutte, khomadussakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama; seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti, evamevaṃ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena [T 1.0271] dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṃ gate”ti.

When this was said, the brahmin householders of Khomadussa said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, venerable Gotama! Excellent, venerable Gotama! It is as if one were to set upright what was overturned, or to reveal what was hidden, or to point out the way to one who was lost, or to hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms. In the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by the venerable Gotama in numerous ways. We go for refuge to the venerable Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the venerable Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.'

Upāsakavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Lay Followers.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Kasi udayo devahito, aññataramahāsālaṃ;

Mānathaddhaṃ paccanīkaṃ, navakammikakaṭṭhahāraṃ;

Mātuposakaṃ bhikkhako, saṅgāravo ca khomadussena dvādasāti.

Kasi, Udaya, Devahita, and A Certain Great Sāla; Mānatthaddha, Paccanīka, Navakammika, and Kaṭṭhahāra; Mātuposaka, Bhikkhaka, Saṅgārava, and with Khomadussa make twelve.

Brāhmaṇasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses with Brahmins is concluded.

8. Vaṅgīsasaṃyuttaṃ

8. The Connected Discourses with Vaṅgīsa

1. Nikkhantasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Going Forth

209. Evaṃ [T 1.0272][V 1.0215][M 1.0187][P 1.0185] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā vaṅgīso āḷaviyaṃ viharati aggāḷave cetiye āyasmatā nigrodhakappena upajjhāyena saddhiṃ. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā vaṅgīso navako hoti acirapabbajito ohiyyako vihārapālo. Atha kho sambahulā itthiyo samalaṅkaritvā yena aggāḷavako ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu vihārapekkhikāyo. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa tā itthiyo disvā anabhirati uppajjati, rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseti. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa etadahosi – “alābhā vata me, na vata me lābhā; dulladdhaṃ vata me, na vata me suladdhaṃ; yassa me anabhirati uppannā, rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseti, taṃ kutettha labbhā, yaṃ me paro anabhiratiṃ vinodetvā abhiratiṃ uppādeyya. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ attanāva attano anabhiratiṃ vinodetvā abhiratiṃ uppādeyya”nti. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso attanāva attano anabhiratiṃ vinodetvā abhiratiṃ uppādetvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

209. Thus have I heard. At one time the Venerable Vaṅgīsa was dwelling in Āḷavī at the Aggāḷava shrine, together with his preceptor, the Venerable Nigrodhakappa. At that time, the Venerable Vaṅgīsa was a junior, having not long gone forth, and was the monastery guardian who had been left behind. Then many women, having adorned themselves, approached the Aggāḷava monastery, wishing to see it. Upon seeing those women, discontent arose in the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, and lust assailed his mind. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Vaṅgīsa: “It is a loss for me, indeed, not a gain for me! It is ill-gotten for me, indeed, not well-gotten for me, that discontent has arisen in me and lust assails my mind. Where could it be found that another could dispel my discontent and arouse delight in me? What if I myself were to dispel my own discontent and arouse delight in myself?” Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, having by himself dispelled his own discontent and aroused delight, on that occasion recited these verses:

“Nikkhantaṃ vata maṃ santaṃ, agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

Vitakkā upadhāvanti, pagabbhā kaṇhato ime.

“Though I have gone forth from the home life into homelessness and am at peace, these bold thoughts, arising from the Dark One, rush upon me.”

“Uggaputtā [T 1.0273] mahissāsā, sikkhitā daḷhadhammino;

Samantā parikireyyuṃ, sahassaṃ apalāyinaṃ.

“Even if a thousand noble sons—great archers, well-trained, with strong bows, who would not flee—were to surround me on all sides,”

“Sacepi etato ettato (sī. pī. ka.), ettakā (syā. kaṃ.) bhiyyo, āgamissanti itthiyo;

Neva maṃ byādhayissanti byāthayissanti (?), dhamme samhi patiṭṭhitaṃ.

“And if even more women than that were to come, they could not make me tremble, for I am firmly established in the Dhamma.”

“Sakkhī [V 1.0216][P 1.0186] hi me sutaṃ etaṃ, buddhassādiccabandhuno;

Nibbānagamanaṃ maggaṃ, tattha me nirato mano.

“For I have heard this directly from the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun—the path that leads to Nibbāna. In that my mind delights.”

“Evañce maṃ viharantaṃ, pāpima upagacchasi;

Tathā maccu karissāmi, na me maggampi dakkhasī”ti.

“If you should approach me while I am dwelling thus, O Evil One, I will act in such a way, O Death, that you will not even see my path.”

2. Aratisuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Discontent

210. Ekaṃ [M 1.0188] samayaṃ…pe… āyasmā vaṅgīso āḷaviyaṃ viharati aggāḷave cetiye āyasmatā nigrodhakappena upajjhāyena saddhiṃ. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā nigrodhakappo pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto vihāraṃ pavisati, sāyaṃ vā nikkhamati aparajju vā kāle. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato vaṅgīsassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseti. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa etadahosi – “alābhā vata me, na vata me lābhā; dulladdhaṃ vata me, na vata me suladdhaṃ; yassa me anabhirati uppannā, rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseti; taṃ kutettha labbhā, yaṃ me paro anabhiratiṃ vinodetvā abhiratiṃ uppādeyya. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ attanāva attano anabhiratiṃ vinodetvā abhiratiṃ uppādeyya”nti. Atha [T 1.0274] kho āyasmā vaṅgīso attanāva attano anabhiratiṃ vinodetvā abhiratiṃ uppādetvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

210. On one occasion… Venerable Vaṅgīsa was dwelling at Āḷavī, at the Aggāḷava Shrine, together with his preceptor, Venerable Nigrodhakappa. Now at that time, Venerable Nigrodhakappa would enter the monastery after the meal, having returned from his almsround, and would emerge either in the evening or on the following day at the proper time. Then, discontent arose in Venerable Vaṅgīsa, and lust assailed his mind. Then this thought occurred to him: ‘It is a loss for me, indeed, not a gain for me; it is ill-gotten for me, indeed, not well-gotten for me, that discontent has arisen in me, and lust assails my mind. From where could it be obtained that another could dispel my discontent and arouse delight in me? What if I myself were to dispel my own discontent and arouse delight in myself?’ Then, Venerable Vaṅgīsa, having himself dispelled his own discontent and aroused delight, on that occasion recited these verses:

“Aratiñca ratiñca pahāya, sabbaso gehasitañca vitakkaṃ;

Vanathaṃ na kareyya kuhiñci, nibbanatho arato sa hi bhikkhu sa bhikkhu (ka.).

“Having abandoned discontent and delight, and every household-based thought completely, one should not create a forest of defilements anywhere. Free from that forest, free from craving—he is indeed a bhikkhu.”

“Yamidha pathaviñca vehāsaṃ, rūpagatañca jagatogadhaṃ;

Kiñci parijīyati sabbamaniccaṃ, evaṃ samecca caranti mutattā.

“Whatever form exists here on earth and in the sky, and whatever has gone into the world—all of it decays; everything is impermanent. Having thus understood, the liberated fare on.”

“Upadhīsu janā gadhitāse gathitāse (sī.), diṭṭhasute paṭighe ca mute ca;

Ettha vinodaya chandamanejo, yo ettha na limpati taṃ munimāhu.

“People are attached to the substrates of existence—to the seen and heard, to sensory impacts and the cognized. Here, dispel desire and be unagitated. One who is not smeared by these, him they call a sage.”

“Atha [V 1.0217][P 1.0187] saṭṭhinissitā savitakkā, puthū janatāya adhammā niviṭṭhā;

Na ca vaggagatassa kuhiñci, no pana duṭṭhullabhāṇī sa bhikkhu.

“Furthermore, the many common people, with thoughts dependent on the six sense spheres, are established in what is not the Dhamma. But a bhikkhu is not one who has gone to any faction, nor is he a speaker of coarse speech.”

“Dabbo cirarattasamāhito, akuhako nipako apihālu;

Santaṃ [T 1.0275] padaṃ ajjhagamā muni paṭicca, parinibbuto kaṅkhati kāla”nti.

“Skilled, long composed, not deceitful, discerning, and free from craving, the sage has realized the peaceful state. Fully extinguished, he awaits the time.”

3. Pesalasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Virtuous

211. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā vaṅgīso āḷaviyaṃ viharati aggāḷave cetiye āyasmatā nigrodhakappena upajjhāyena saddhiṃ. Tena kho pana samayena [M 1.0189] āyasmā vaṅgīso attano paṭibhānena aññe pesale bhikkhū atimaññati. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa etadahosi – “alābhā vata me, na vata me lābhā; dulladdhaṃ vata me, na vata me suladdhaṃ; yvāhaṃ attano paṭibhānena aññe pesale bhikkhū atimaññāmī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso attanāva attano vippaṭisāraṃ uppādetvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

211. On one occasion, Venerable Vaṅgīsa was dwelling at Āḷavī, at the Aggāḷava Shrine, together with his preceptor, Venerable Nigrodhakappa. Now at that time, Venerable Vaṅgīsa looked down upon other virtuous monks on account of his own eloquence. Then this thought occurred to him: ‘It is a loss for me, indeed, not a gain for me; it is ill-gained for me, indeed, not well-gained for me, that I look down upon other virtuous monks on account of my own eloquence.’ Then, Venerable Vaṅgīsa, having himself generated remorse in himself, on that occasion spoke these verses:

“Mānaṃ pajahassu gotama, mānapathañca pajahassu;

Asesaṃ mānapathasmiṃ, samucchito vippaṭisārīhuvā cirarattaṃ.

“Abandon pride, O Gotama! Abandon the path of pride completely. Infatuated on the path of pride, you have been remorseful for a long, long time.”

“Makkhena makkhitā pajā, mānahatā nirayaṃ papatanti;

Socanti janā cirarattaṃ, mānahatā nirayaṃ upapannā.

“Beings smeared with contempt, struck down by pride, fall into hell. People grieve for a long, long time, having been reborn in hell, struck down by pride.”

“Na [T 1.0276] hi socati bhikkhu kadāci, maggajino sammāpaṭipanno;

Kittiñca sukhañca anubhoti, dhammadasoti tamāhu pahitattaṃ.

“A bhikkhu never grieves at all—one who has conquered by the path, who is rightly practicing. He experiences both fame and happiness. They call that resolute person ‘one who sees the Dhamma.’”

“Tasmā [P 1.0188] akhilodha padhānavā, nīvaraṇāni pahāya visuddho;

Mānañca pahāya asesaṃ, vijjāyantakaro samitāvī”ti.

“Therefore, here, be one free from resentment, diligent, and pure, having abandoned the hindrances. Having completely abandoned conceit, with defilements pacified, make an end with knowledge.”

4. Ānandasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse to Ānanda

212. Ekaṃ [V 1.0218] samayaṃ āyasmā ānando sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi āyasmatā vaṅgīsena pacchāsamaṇena. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato vaṅgīsassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, rāgo cittaṃ anuddhaṃseti. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

212. On one occasion, the Venerable Ānanda was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda, having dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms, together with the Venerable Vaṅgīsa as his attendant monk. At that time, discontent had arisen in the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, and lust was destroying his mind. Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa addressed the Venerable Ānanda with a verse:

“Kāmarāgena ḍayhāmi, cittaṃ me pariḍayhati;

Sādhu nibbāpanaṃ brūhi, anukampāya gotamā”ti.

“I am burned by the fire of sensual passion; my mind is consumed. Well, out of compassion, O Gotama, please teach the way to extinguish it.”

“Saññāya [T 1.0277] vipariyesā, cittaṃ te pariḍayhati;

Nimittaṃ parivajjehi, subhaṃ rāgūpasaṃhitaṃ.

“Because of the perversion of perception, your mind is consumed. Avoid the beautiful sign associated with lust.

“Saṅkhāre parato passa, dukkhato mā ca attato;

Nibbāpehi mahārāgaṃ, mā ḍayhittho punappunaṃ.

“See conditioned formations as impermanent, as suffering, and not as self. Extinguish the great lust; do not be burned again and again.

“Asubhāya [M 1.0190] cittaṃ bhāvehi, ekaggaṃ susamāhitaṃ;

Sati kāyagatā tyatthu, nibbidābahulo bhava.

“Develop the mind with the sign of the unattractive; develop it to be one-pointed and well-composed. Let mindfulness directed to the body be yours, and be one who is greatly disenchanted.

“Animittañca bhāvehi, mānānusayamujjaha;

Tato mānābhisamayā, upasanto carissasī”ti.

“And develop the signless; abandon the underlying tendency to conceit. Then, from the full understanding of conceit, you will fare on, at peace.”

5. Subhāsitasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Well-Spoken Speech

213. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

213. At Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Catūhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatā vācā subhāsitā hoti, no dubbhāsitā; anavajjā ca ananuvajjā ca viññūnaṃ. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu [V 1.0219] subhāsitaṃyeva bhāsati no dubbhāsitaṃ, dhammaṃyeva bhāsati no adhammaṃ, piyaṃyeva [P 1.0189] bhāsati no appiyaṃ, saccaṃyeva bhāsati no alikaṃ. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi aṅgehi samannāgatā vācā subhāsitā hoti, no dubbhāsitā, anavajjā ca ananuvajjā ca viññūna”nti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

“Bhikkhus, speech endowed with four factors is well-spoken, not ill-spoken; it is blameless and not censured by the wise. With which four? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu speaks only what is well-spoken, not what is ill-spoken; he speaks only Dhamma, not non-Dhamma; he speaks only what is pleasing, not what is unpleasing; he speaks only what is true, not what is false. Bhikkhus, speech endowed with these four factors is well-spoken, not ill-spoken; it is blameless and not censured by the wise.” This is what the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Subhāsitaṃ [T 1.0278] uttamamāhu santo,

Dhammaṃ bhaṇe nādhammaṃ taṃ dutiyaṃ;

Piyaṃ bhaṇe nāppiyaṃ taṃ tatiyaṃ,

Saccaṃ bhaṇe nālikaṃ taṃ catuttha”nti.

“The good say well-spoken speech is supreme; speak the Dhamma, not non-Dhamma—that is the second. Speak what is pleasing, not unpleasing—that is the third. Speak what is true, not what is false—that is the fourth.”

Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭibhāti maṃ bhagavā, paṭibhāti maṃ sugatā”ti. “Paṭibhātu taṃ vaṅgīsā”ti bhagavā avoca. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso bhagavantaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and, extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: “An inspiration has come to me, Blessed One; an inspiration has come to me, Well-farer!” “Let that inspiration come to you, Vaṅgīsa,” the Blessed One said. Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa extolled the Blessed One in his presence with suitable verses:

“Tameva vācaṃ bhāseyya, yāyattānaṃ na tāpaye;

Pare ca na vihiṃseyya, sā ve vācā subhāsitā.

“One should speak only that speech that does not torment oneself and does not harm others; that, indeed, is well-spoken speech.

“Piyavācaṃva bhāseyya, yā vācā paṭinanditā;

Yaṃ anādāya pāpāni, paresaṃ bhāsate piyaṃ.

“One should speak only pleasing speech, speech that is welcomed. Not taking up what is evil, one speaks what is pleasing to others.

“Saccaṃ [M 1.0191] ve amatā vācā, esa dhammo sanantano;

Sacce atthe ca dhamme ca, āhu santo patiṭṭhitā.

“Truth, indeed, is speech like ambrosia; this is an eternal principle. The good, they say, are established in truth, in benefit, and in the Dhamma.

“Yaṃ buddho bhāsate vācaṃ, khemaṃ nibbānapattiyā;

Dukkhassantakiriyāya, sā ve vācānamuttamā”ti.

“The speech the Buddha speaks, which is safe, for the attainment of Nibbāna, for making an end of suffering—that is indeed the supreme of all speech.”

6. Sāriputtasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Sāriputta

214. Ekaṃ [T 1.0279][V 1.0220] samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti poriyā vācāya vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya aneḷagalāya (sī. ka.), anelagaḷāya (syā. kaṃ. pī.) atthassa viññāpaniyā. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṃ suṇanti. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmā [P 1.0190] sāriputto bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti poriyā vācāya vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṃ suṇanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthaveyya”nti.

214. On one occasion, the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, the Venerable Sāriputta was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk—with speech that was urbane, clear, faultless, and capable of making the meaning known. And those bhikkhus were paying attention, applying their minds, directing their whole mind to it, and listening to the Dhamma with attentive ears. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Vaṅgīsa: "This Venerable Sāriputta is instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk—with speech that is urbane, clear, faultless, and capable of making the meaning known. And those bhikkhus are paying attention, applying their minds, directing their whole mind to it, and listening to the Dhamma with attentive ears. It would be good if I were to extol the Venerable Sāriputta in his presence with fitting verses."

Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “paṭibhāti maṃ, āvuso sāriputta, paṭibhāti maṃ, āvuso sāriputtā”ti. “Paṭibhātu taṃ, āvuso vaṅgīsā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and, extending his joined palms toward the Venerable Sāriputta, said to him: “An inspiration has come to me, friend Sāriputta, an inspiration has come to me.” “Let it come to you, friend Vaṅgīsa.” Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa extolled the Venerable Sāriputta in his presence with fitting verses:

“Gambhīrapañño medhāvī, maggāmaggassa kovido;

Sāriputto mahāpañño, dhammaṃ deseti bhikkhunaṃ.

“Sāriputta, of profound wisdom, intelligent, skilled in the path and the non-path, of great wisdom, teaches the Dhamma to the bhikkhus.

“Saṃkhittenapi deseti, vitthārenapi bhāsati;

Sāḷikāyiva nigghoso, paṭibhānaṃ udīrayi udīriyi (syā. kaṃ.) udīriyati (sāmaññaphalasuttaṭīkānurūpaṃ).

“He teaches concisely and speaks in detail; like the sound of a sāḷikā bird, he brings forth inspired eloquence.

“Tassa [M 1.0192] taṃ desayantassa, suṇanti madhuraṃ giraṃ;

Sarena [T 1.0280] rajanīyena, savanīyena vaggunā;

Udaggacittā muditā, sotaṃ odhenti bhikkhavo”ti.

“As he is teaching that Dhamma, the bhikkhus listen to his sweet speech, with a voice that is charming, pleasant to hear, and melodious; with uplifted and joyful minds, the bhikkhus lend an ear.”

7. Pavāraṇāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Invitation

215. Ekaṃ [V 1.0221] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe pannarase pavāraṇāya bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto abbhokāse nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anuviloketvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “handa dāni, bhikkhave, pavāremi vo. Na ca me kiñci garahatha kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā”ti.

215. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in the Eastern Park, in the palace of Migāra’s mother, together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants. Now on that occasion, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, for the Pavāraṇā, the Blessed One was seated in the open, surrounded by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then the Blessed One, having surveyed the silent Saṅgha of bhikkhus, addressed the bhikkhus: “Come now, bhikkhus, I invite you. Do you not censure me for anything, whether of body or of speech?”

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “na kho mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato kiñci garahāma kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā. Bhagavā hi[P 1.0191], bhante, anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā, asañjātassa maggassa sañjanetā, anakkhātassa maggassa akkhātā, maggaññū maggavidū maggakovido. Maggānugā ca, bhante, etarahi sāvakā viharanti pacchā samannāgatā; ahañca kho, bhante, bhagavantaṃ pavāremi. Na ca me bhagavā kiñci garahati kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā”ti.

When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and, extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, we do not censure the Blessed One for anything, whether of body or of speech. For, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One is the producer of the unarisen path, the generator of the ungenerated path, the declarer of the undeclared path. He is the knower of the path, one versed in the path, one skilled in the path. And now, Venerable Sir, the disciples dwell as followers of the path, having come after. I too, Venerable Sir, invite the Blessed One. Does the Blessed One censure me for anything, whether of body or of speech?”

“Na khvāhaṃ te, sāriputta, kiñci garahāmi kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā. Paṇḍito tvaṃ, sāriputta, mahāpañño tvaṃ, sāriputta[T 1.0281], puthupañño tvaṃ, sāriputta, hāsapañño tvaṃ, sāriputta, javanapañño tvaṃ, sāriputta, tikkhapañño tvaṃ, sāriputta, nibbedhikapañño tvaṃ, sāriputta. Seyyathāpi, sāriputta, rañño cakkavattissa jeṭṭhaputto pitarā pavattitaṃ cakkaṃ sammadeva anuppavatteti; evameva kho tvaṃ, sāriputta, mayā anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ sammadeva anuppavattesī”ti.

“Sāriputta, I do not censure you for anything, whether of body or of speech. You are wise, Sāriputta; you are of great wisdom, Sāriputta; you are of broad wisdom, Sāriputta; you are of joyful wisdom, Sāriputta; you are of swift wisdom, Sāriputta; you are of sharp wisdom, Sāriputta; you are of penetrating wisdom, Sāriputta. Just as, Sāriputta, the eldest son of a wheel-turning monarch rightly keeps rolling the wheel set in motion by his father, even so, Sāriputta, do you rightly keep rolling the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel that has been set in motion by me.”

“No ce kira me, bhante, bhagavā kiñci garahati kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā. Imesaṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ na kiñci garahati kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā”ti. “Imesampi khvāhaṃ, sāriputta, pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ na [M 1.0193] kiñci garahāmi kāyikaṃ vā vācasikaṃ vā. Imesañhi, sāriputta, pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ saṭṭhi bhikkhū tevijjā, saṭṭhi bhikkhū chaḷabhiññā, saṭṭhi bhikkhū ubhatobhāgavimuttā, atha itare paññāvimuttā”ti.

“Venerable Sir, if the Blessed One does not censure me for anything, whether of body or of speech, does the Blessed One then censure these five hundred bhikkhus for anything, whether of body or of speech?” “Sāriputta, I do not censure these five hundred bhikkhus either for anything, whether of body or of speech. For, Sāriputta, among these five hundred bhikkhus, sixty bhikkhus possess the three true knowledges, sixty bhikkhus possess the six supernormal powers, sixty bhikkhus are liberated in both ways, and the others are liberated by wisdom.”

Atha [V 1.0222] kho āyasmā vaṅgīso uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭibhāti maṃ bhagavā, paṭibhāti maṃ sugatā”ti. “Paṭibhātu taṃ, vaṅgīsā”ti bhagavā avoca. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso bhagavantaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and, extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: “An inspiration has come to me, Blessed One! An inspiration has come to me, Sugata!” “Let it come to you, Vaṅgīsa,” the Blessed One said. Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa extolled the Blessed One in his presence with fitting verses:

“Ajja pannarase visuddhiyā, bhikkhū pañcasatā samāgatā;

Saṃyojanabandhanacchidā[T 1.0282], anīghā khīṇapunabbhavā isī.

“Today on the fifteenth, for the sake of purity, five hundred bhikkhus have assembled—seers who have cut the bonds of fetters, who are without trouble, their renewed existence destroyed.

“Cakkavattī [P 1.0192] yathā rājā, amaccaparivārito;

Samantā anupariyeti, sāgarantaṃ mahiṃ imaṃ.

“Just as a wheel-turning king, surrounded by his ministers, travels all around this earth, up to the ocean’s edge,

“Evaṃ vijitasaṅgāmaṃ, satthavāhaṃ anuttaraṃ;

Sāvakā payirupāsanti, tevijjā maccuhāyino.

“Even so do the disciples, possessors of the three true knowledges and conquerors of death, attend upon the one victorious in battle, the unsurpassed caravan leader.

“Sabbe bhagavato puttā, palāpettha na vijjati;

Taṇhāsallassa hantāraṃ, vande ādiccabandhuna”nti.

“All are the Blessed One’s sons; no chaff is found here. I pay homage to the destroyer of the dart of craving, the Kinsman of the Sun.”

8. Parosahassasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on More Than a Thousand

216. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhū nibbānapaṭisaṃyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṃ suṇanti. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho bhagavā bhikkhū nibbānapaṭisaṃyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṃ suṇanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthaveyya”nti.

216. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park, with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, together with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus. At that time, the Blessed One was instructing, establishing, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk connected with Nibbāna. And those bhikkhus, paying attention, taking it to heart, comprehending it all with their minds, were listening to the Dhamma with attentive ears. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Vaṅgīsa: 'Indeed, the Blessed One is instructing, establishing, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk connected with Nibbāna. And those bhikkhus, paying attention, taking it to heart, comprehending it all with their minds, are listening to the Dhamma with attentive ears. What if I were to extol the Blessed One in his presence with fitting verses?'

Atha [T 1.0283][V 1.0223][M 1.0194] kho āyasmā vaṅgīso uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭibhāti maṃ bhagavā, paṭibhāti maṃ sugatā”ti. “Paṭibhātu taṃ, vaṅgīsā”ti bhagavā avoca. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso bhagavantaṃ sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms towards the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: 'An inspiration comes to me, Blessed One! An inspiration comes to me, Sugata!' The Blessed One said: 'Let the inspiration come to you, Vaṅgīsa.' Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa extolled the Blessed One in his presence with fitting verses:

“Parosahassaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, sugataṃ payirupāsati;

Desentaṃ virajaṃ dhammaṃ, nibbānaṃ akutobhayaṃ.

“More than a thousand bhikkhus attend upon the Sugata, as he teaches the dust-free Dhamma, Nibbāna, where there is no fear from any quarter.

“Suṇanti dhammaṃ vimalaṃ, sammāsambuddhadesitaṃ;

Sobhati vata sambuddho, bhikkhusaṅghapurakkhato.

“They listen to the stainless Dhamma, taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One. Indeed, the Perfectly Enlightened One shines, attended by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

“Nāganāmosi bhagavā, isīnaṃ isisattamo;

Mahāmeghova hutvāna, sāvake abhivassati.

“You are named Nāga, O Blessed One, the seventh and most excellent of seers. Having become like a great cloud, you rain upon your disciples.

“Divāvihārā [P 1.0193] nikkhamma, satthudassanakamyatā satthudassanakāmatā (sī. syā. kaṃ.);

Sāvako te mahāvīra, pāde vandati vaṅgīso”ti.

“Having emerged from the day-dwelling, desiring to see the Teacher, your disciple VaᅆgĦsa, O Great Hero, pays homage at your feet.”

“Kiṃ nu te, vaṅgīsa, imā gāthāyo pubbe parivitakkitā, udāhu ṭhānasova taṃ paṭibhantī”ti? ‘Na kho me, bhante, imā gāthāyo pubbe parivitakkitā, atha kho ṭhānasova maṃ paṭibhantī’ti. ‘Tena hi taṃ, vaṅgīsa, bhiyyosomattāya pubbe aparivitakkitā gāthāyo paṭibhantū’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante’ti kho āyasmā vaṅgīso bhagavato paṭissutvā bhiyyosomattāya [T 1.0284] bhagavantaṃ pubbe aparivitakkitāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

“Vaṅgīsa, were these verses previously thought out by you, or do they appear to you on the spot?” “Venerable Sir, these verses were not previously thought out by me; rather, they appear to me on the spot.” “In that case, Vaṅgīsa, may even more verses, not previously thought out, appear to you.” “So be it, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Vaṅgīsa replied to the Blessed One, and he extolled the Blessed One to an even greater extent with verses not previously thought out:

“Ummaggapathaṃ ummaggasataṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) mārassa abhibhuyya, carati pabhijja khilāni;

Taṃ passatha bandhapamuñcakaraṃ, asitaṃ bhāgaso pavibhajaṃ.

“Having overcome the wrong path of Māra, he wanders, having broken the spiritual barrennesses. See him, the maker of release from bonds, the unattached one, who analyzes the Dhamma portion by portion.”

“Oghassa nittharaṇatthaṃ, anekavihitaṃ maggaṃ akkhāsi;

Tasmiñce amate akkhāte, dhammaddasā ṭhitā asaṃhīrā.

For the purpose of crossing over the flood, He declared the path of many kinds; and when that deathless path was declared, the seers of the Dhamma stand firm, unshakeable.

“Pajjotakaro [V 1.0224] ativijjha ativijjha dhammaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.), sabbaṭṭhitīnaṃ atikkamamaddasa;

Ñatvā ca sacchikatvā ca, aggaṃ so desayi dasaddhānaṃ.

The Illuminator, having penetrated all standpoints, saw the transcending. Having known and realized it, He taught the supreme Dhamma to the five endowed with faith.

“Evaṃ [M 1.0195] sudesite dhamme,

Ko pamādo vijānataṃ dhammaṃ ko pamādo vijānataṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.);

Tasmā hi tassa bhagavato sāsane;

Appamatto sadā namassamanusikkhe”ti.

When the Dhamma is thus well-taught, for those who understand, what room is there for negligence? Therefore, in the dispensation of that Blessed One, ever heedful, I shall pay homage and continue to train.

9. Koṇḍaññasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Koṇḍañña

217. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Atha kho āyasmā aññāsikoṇḍañño aññākoṇḍañño (sī. syā. kaṃ.) sucirasseva yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā [T 1.0285] bhagavato pādāni mukhena ca paricumbati, pāṇīhi [P 1.0194] ca parisambāhati, nāmañca sāveti – “koṇḍaññohaṃ, bhagavā, koṇḍaññohaṃ, sugatā”ti. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmā aññāsikoṇḍañño sucirasseva yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavato pādāni mukhena ca paricumbati, pāṇīhi ca parisambāhati, nāmañca sāveti – ‘koṇḍaññohaṃ, bhagavā, koṇḍaññohaṃ, sugatā’ti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ āyasmantaṃ aññāsikoṇḍaññaṃ bhagavato sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthaveyya”nti.

217. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Then, after a very long time, the Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he fell with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, kissed the Blessed One’s feet with his mouth, massaged them with his hands, and announced his name: “I am Koṇḍañña, Blessed One! I am Koṇḍañña, Well-Gone One!” Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Vaṅgīsa: “This Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña, after a very long time, has approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he fell with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, kissed the Blessed One’s feet with his mouth, and massaged them with his hands, announcing his name: ‘I am Koṇḍañña, Blessed One! I am Koṇḍañña, Well-Gone One!’ What if I were to praise the Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña in the presence of the Blessed One with suitable verses?”

Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭibhāti maṃ, bhagavā, paṭibhāti maṃ, sugatā”ti. “Paṭibhātu taṃ, vaṅgīsā”ti bhagavā avoca. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso āyasmantaṃ aññāsikoṇḍaññaṃ bhagavato sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: “An inspiration comes to me, Blessed One! An inspiration comes to me, Well-Gone One!” The Blessed One said: “Let the inspiration come to you, Vaṅgīsa.” Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa extolled the Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña in the presence of the Blessed One with suitable verses:

“Buddhānubuddho so thero, koṇḍañño tibbanikkamo;

Lābhī sukhavihārānaṃ, vivekānaṃ abhiṇhaso.

That elder, Koṇḍañña, enlightened in sequence to the Buddha, is of keen persistence; he is a frequent obtainer of blissful abidings, of seclusions.

“Yaṃ [V 1.0225] sāvakena pattabbaṃ, satthusāsanakārinā;

Sabbassa taṃ anuppattaṃ, appamattassa sikkhato.

Whatever is to be attained by a disciple who carries out the Teacher’s instruction, all of that has been attained by him, training with diligence.

“Mahānubhāvo [T 1.0286] tevijjo, cetopariyāyakovido;

Koṇḍañño buddhadāyādo buddhasāvako (pī.), pāde vandati satthuno”ti.

Of great power, possessing the three knowledges, skilled in the penetration of minds, Koṇḍañña, an heir of the Buddha, venerates the Teacher’s feet.

10. Moggallānasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Moggallāna

218. Ekaṃ [M 1.0196] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati isigilipasse kāḷasilāyaṃ mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi. Tesaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno cetasā cittaṃ samannesati samanvesati (syā. aṭṭha.) vippamuttaṃ nirupadhiṃ. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho bhagavā rājagahe viharati isigilipasse kāḷasilāyaṃ mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi. Tesaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno cetasā cittaṃ samannesati vippamuttaṃ nirupadhiṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ bhagavato sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthaveyya”nti.

218. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha on the Black Rock at the slope of Mount Isigili, together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was investigating with his mind the minds of those who were liberated and without substrate. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Vaṅgīsa: “This Blessed One is dwelling at Rājagaha on the Black Rock at the slope of Mount Isigili, together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna is investigating with his mind the minds of those who were liberated and without substrate. What if I were to praise the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna in the presence of the Blessed One with suitable verses?”

Atha [P 1.0195] kho āyasmā vaṅgīso uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭibhāti maṃ, bhagavā, paṭibhāti maṃ, sugatā”ti. “Paṭibhātu taṃ, vaṅgīsā”ti bhagavā avoca. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ bhagavato sammukhā sāruppāhi gāthāhi abhitthavi –

Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: “An inspiration comes to me, Blessed One! An inspiration comes to me, Well-Gone One!” The Blessed One said: “Let the inspiration come to you, Vaṅgīsa.” Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa extolled the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna in the presence of the Blessed One with suitable verses:

“Nagassa passe āsīnaṃ, muniṃ dukkhassa pāraguṃ;

Sāvakā payirupāsanti, tevijjā maccuhāyino.

Disciples, possessors of the three knowledges who have abandoned Death, attend upon the Sage seated on the mountainside, who has gone to the far shore of suffering.

“Te [T 1.0287] cetasā anupariyeti anupariyesati (sī. syā. kaṃ.), moggallāno mahiddhiko;

Cittaṃ nesaṃ samannesaṃ samanvesaṃ (syā. aṭṭha.), vippamuttaṃ nirūpadhiṃ.

Moggallāna of great psychic power investigates them with his mind, discerning their minds to be liberated and without substrate.

“Evaṃ [V 1.0226] sabbaṅgasampannaṃ, muniṃ dukkhassa pāraguṃ;

Anekākārasampannaṃ, payirupāsanti gotama”nti.

Thus do the disciples attend upon Gotama, the Sage endowed with all noble characteristics, who has gone to the far shore of suffering, endowed with numerous qualities.

11. Gaggarāsuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on Gaggarā

219. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā campāyaṃ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sattahi ca upāsakasatehi sattahi ca upāsikāsatehi anekehi ca devatāsahassehi. Tyāssudaṃ bhagavā atirocati ativirocati (ka.) vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Atha kho āyasmato vaṅgīsassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho [M 1.0197] bhagavā campāyaṃ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sattahi ca upāsakasatehi sattahi ca upāsikāsatehi anekehi ca devatāsahassehi. Tyāssudaṃ bhagavā atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ sammukhā sāruppāya gāthāya abhitthaveyya”nti.

219. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Campā on the bank of the Gaggarā lotus pond, together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus, with seven hundred male lay followers, with seven hundred female lay followers, and with many thousands of deities. And there the Blessed One outshone them all in beauty and glory. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Vaṅgīsa: 'This Blessed One is dwelling at Campā on the bank of the Gaggarā lotus pond, together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus, with seven hundred male lay followers, with seven hundred female lay followers, and with many thousands of deities. And there the Blessed One outshones them all in beauty and glory. It would be good if I were to extol the Blessed One in his presence with a suitable verse!'
