Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭibhāti maṃ, bhagavā, paṭibhāti maṃ, sugatā”ti. “Paṭibhātu taṃ, vaṅgīsā”ti bhagavā avoca. Atha kho āyasmā vaṅgīso bhagavantaṃ sammukhā sāruppāya gāthāya abhitthavi –

Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and, extending his joined hands in reverence towards the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'An inspiration occurs to me, Blessed One; an inspiration occurs to me, Well-Gone One.' 'Let the inspiration occur to you, Vaṅgīsa,' the Blessed One said. Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa extolled the Blessed One in his presence with a suitable verse:

“Cando [T 1.0288][P 1.0196] yathā vigatavalāhake nabhe,

Virocati vigatamalova bhāṇumā;

Evampi aṅgīrasa tvaṃ mahāmuni,

Atirocasi yasasā sabbaloka”nti.

Just as the moon in a cloudless sky shines, and just as the sun, free from impurity, shines; so too, O Aṅgīrasa, Great Sage, you outshine the entire world with your glory.

12. Vaṅgīsasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on Vaṅgīsa

220. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā vaṅgīso sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme[V 1.0227]. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā vaṅgīso aciraarahattappatto hutvā hoti (sī. syā. kaṃ.) vimuttisukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedī vimuttisukhapaṭisaṃvedī (sī. pī.) tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

220. On one occasion, the Venerable Vaṅgīsa was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, having attained Arahantship not long before, was experiencing the bliss of liberation. On that occasion, he recited these verses:

“Kāveyyamattā vicarimha pubbe, gāmā gāmaṃ purā puraṃ;

Athaddasāma sambuddhaṃ, saddhā no upapajjatha.

“Formerly, intoxicated with poetry, we wandered from village to village, from town to town. Then we saw the Fully Enlightened One, and faith arose in us.

“So me dhammamadesesi, khandhāyatanadhātuyo khandhe āyatanāni dhātuyo (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.);

Tassāhaṃ dhammaṃ sutvāna, pabbajiṃ anagāriyaṃ.

“He taught me the Dhamma—the aggregates, the sense bases, and the elements. Having heard his Dhamma, I went forth into the homeless life.

“Bahunnaṃ vata atthāya, bodhiṃ ajjhagamā muni;

Bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnañca, ye niyāmagataddasā.

“Truly, for the benefit of many the Sage attained enlightenment—for those bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs who see the fixed course.

“Svāgataṃ [M 1.0198] vata me āsi, mama buddhassa santike;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, kataṃ buddhassa sāsanaṃ.

“Indeed, my coming to the presence of the Buddha was a welcome one! The three true knowledges have been attained; the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.

“Pubbenivāsaṃ jānāmi, dibbacakkhuṃ visodhitaṃ;

Tevijjo iddhipattomhi, cetopariyāyakovido”ti.

“I know my former abodes, the divine eye is purified; I am one with the three true knowledges, I have attained psychic power, I am skilled in the knowledge of penetrating the minds of others.”

Vaṅgīsasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses with Vaṅgīsa is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Nikkhantaṃ [T 1.0289] arati ceva, pesalā atimaññanā;

Ānandena subhāsitā, sāriputtapavāraṇā;

Parosahassaṃ koṇḍañño, moggallānena gaggarā;

Vaṅgīsena dvādasāti.

Nikkhanta, Arati, Pesalā, Atimaññanā, Ānanda, Subhāsita, Sāriputta, Pavāraṇā, Parosahassa, Koṇḍañña, Moggallāna, and Gaggarā; together with Vaṅgīsa, these are twelve.

9. Vanasaṃyuttaṃ

9. The Connected Discourses on the Forest

1. Vivekasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Seclusion

221. Evaṃ [T 1.0290][V 1.0228][P 1.0197][M 1.0199] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena so bhikkhu divāvihāragato pāpake akusale vitakke vitakketi gehanissite. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tassa bhikkhuno anukampikā atthakāmā taṃ bhikkhuṃ saṃvejetukāmā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

221. Thus have I heard. On one occasion, a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time, while in his day-dwelling, that bhikkhu was thinking evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with the household life. Then the deity who dwelt in that forest grove, being compassionate and wishing for his welfare, desiring to stir him, approached that bhikkhu and addressed him in verses:

“Vivekakāmosi vanaṃ paviṭṭho,

Atha te mano niccharatī bahiddhā;

Jano janasmiṃ vinayassu chandaṃ,

Tato sukhī hohisi vītarāgo.

“You entered the forest desiring seclusion, yet your mind wanders outside. O man, discipline your desire for other people; then you will be happy, free from passion.

“Aratiṃ pajahāsi sato, bhavāsi sataṃ taṃ sārayāmase;

Pātālarajo hi duttaro, mā taṃ kāmarajo avāhari.

“Abandon discontent and be mindful. We would remind you who are mindful. The dust of the abyss is indeed hard to cross over; may the dust of sensual pleasure not carry you away.

“Sakuṇo yathā paṃsukunthito paṃsukuṇṭhito (ka.), paṃsukuṇḍito (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), vidhunaṃ pātayati sitaṃ rajaṃ;

Evaṃ [T 1.0291] bhikkhu padhānavā satimā, vidhunaṃ pātayati sitaṃ raja”nti.

“Just as a bird covered with dust, by shaking, makes the clinging dust fall, so too, a bhikkhu who is diligent and mindful, by shaking, should make the clinging dust fall.”

Atha kho so bhikkhu tāya devatāya saṃvejito saṃvegamāpādīti.

Then that bhikkhu, having been stirred by that deity, attained a sense of spiritual urgency.

2. Upaṭṭhānasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Attendance

222. Ekaṃ [V 1.0229] samayaṃ aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena [P 1.0198] kho pana samayena so bhikkhu divāvihāragato supati. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tassa bhikkhuno anukampikā atthakāmā taṃ bhikkhuṃ saṃvejetukāmā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

222. On one occasion, a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time, while in his day-dwelling, that bhikkhu was sleeping. Then the deity who dwelt in that forest grove, being compassionate and wishing for his welfare, desiring to stir him, approached that bhikkhu and addressed him in verses:

“Uṭṭhehi bhikkhu kiṃ sesi, ko attho supitena supinena (sī.) te;

Āturassa hi kā niddā, sallaviddhassa ruppato.

“Arise, O bhikkhu! Why do you sleep? What benefit is there in sleep for you? For one who is sick, pierced by a dart, and afflicted, what sleep can there be?

“Yāya [M 1.0200] saddhāya pabbajito yāya saddhāpabbajito (sī. syā. kaṃ.), agārasmānagāriyaṃ;

Tameva saddhaṃ brūhehi, mā niddāya vasaṃ gamī”ti.

“With the faith by which you went forth from the household life into homelessness, you should develop that very faith. Do not come under the sway of sleep.”

“Aniccā addhuvā kāmā, yesu mandova mucchito;

Baddhesu khandhesu (sī.) muttaṃ asitaṃ, kasmā pabbajitaṃ tape.

“O deity, sensual pleasures are impermanent and unstable, in which the foolish person is infatuated. Why should sleeping in the day torment a renunciant who is freed from those bonds and unattached?

“Chandarāgassa vinayā, avijjāsamatikkamā;

Taṃ ñāṇaṃ paramodānaṃ pariyodātaṃ (sī. pī.), paramodātaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), paramavodānaṃ (sī. aṭṭha.), kasmā pabbajitaṃ tape.

“O deity, through the disciplining of desire and lust and the overcoming of ignorance, one possesses that supremely pure knowledge. Why should sleeping in the day torment a renunciant?

“Chetvā [T 1.0292] bhetvā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) avijjaṃ vijjāya, āsavānaṃ parikkhayā;

Asokaṃ anupāyāsaṃ, kasmā pabbajitaṃ tape.

“O deity, having destroyed ignorance with knowledge, through the destruction of the taints, why should sleeping in the day torment a renunciant who is sorrowless and free from distress?

“Āraddhavīriyaṃ pahitattaṃ, niccaṃ daḷhaparakkamaṃ;

Nibbānaṃ abhikaṅkhantaṃ, kasmā pabbajitaṃ tape”ti.

“O deity, why should sleeping in the day torment a renunciant with aroused energy, a resolute mind, constantly firm striving, who is longing for Nibbāna?”

3. Kassapagottasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Kassapagotta

223. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā kassapagotto kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena [V 1.0230] kho pana samayena āyasmā kassapagotto divāvihāragato aññataraṃ chetaṃ ovadati. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā āyasmantaṃ kassapagottaṃ saṃvejetukāmā yenāyasmā kassapagotto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ kassapagottaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

223. On one occasion, the Venerable Kassapagotta was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time, the Venerable Kassapagotta, while dwelling for the day, was instructing a certain hunter. Then the deity who dwelt in that forest grove, wishing to stir the Venerable Kassapagotta, approached him; having approached, he addressed the Venerable Kassapagotta in verses:

“Giriduggacaraṃ chetaṃ, appapaññaṃ acetasaṃ;

Akāle ovadaṃ bhikkhu, mandova paṭibhāti maṃ.

“O bhikkhu, advising at the wrong time a hunter who roams in mountain defiles, who is without wisdom and without sense, you appear to me as a fool.

“Suṇāti na vijānāti, āloketi na passati;

Dhammasmiṃ bhaññamānasmiṃ, atthaṃ bālo na bujjhati.

“He hears, but does not understand; he looks, but does not see. When the Dhamma is being spoken, the fool does not comprehend the meaning.

“Sacepi [P 1.0199] dasa pajjote, dhārayissasi kassapa;

Neva dakkhati rūpāni, cakkhu hissa na vijjatī”ti.

“Even if you were to hold up ten lamps, O Kassapa, he would not see forms, for he has no eye.”

Atha kho āyasmā kassapagotto tāya devatāya saṃvejito saṃvegamāpādīti.

Then the Venerable Kassapagotta, stirred by that deity, attained a sense of spiritual urgency.

4. Sambahulasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse concerning Many Bhikkhus

224. Ekaṃ [T 1.0293][M 1.0201] samayaṃ sambahulā bhikkhū kosalesu viharanti aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Atha kho te bhikkhū vassaṃvuṭṭhā vassaṃvutthā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) temāsaccayena cārikaṃ pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā te bhikkhū apassantī paridevamānā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

224. On one occasion, many bhikkhus were dwelling in a certain forest grove among the Kosalans. Then those bhikkhus, having completed the rains-residence, after the passing of three months, set out on a wandering tour. Then the deity who dwelt in that forest grove, not seeing those bhikkhus and lamenting, at that time spoke this verse:

“Arati viya mejja khāyati,

Bahuke disvāna vivitte āsane;

Te cittakathā bahussutā,

Kome gotamasāvakā gatā”ti.

“Today it seems to me there is discontent, having seen the many secluded seats. These disciples of Gotama, skilled in varied discourse and very learned—where have they gone?”

Evaṃ vutte, aññatarā devatā taṃ devataṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi –

When this was said, another deity replied to that deity in verse:

“Māgadhaṃ [V 1.0231] gatā kosalaṃ gatā, ekacciyā pana vajjibhūmiyā;

Magā viya asaṅgacārino, aniketā viharanti bhikkhavo”ti.

“Some have gone to Magadha, some to Kosala, and some to the land of the Vajjis. The bhikkhus dwell without a home, wandering unattached like deer.”

5. Ānandasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse concerning Ānanda

225. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ānando kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando ativelaṃ gihisaññattibahulo viharati. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā āyasmato ānandassa [T 1.0294] anukampikā atthakāmā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ saṃvejetukāmā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

225. At one time, the Venerable Ānanda was dwelling in a certain forest grove among the Kosalans. Now at that time, the Venerable Ānanda was dwelling much occupied with instructing householders for an excessive time. Then the deity who dwelt in that forest grove, being compassionate, desiring his welfare, and wishing to stir the Venerable Ānanda, approached him; having approached, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda with a verse:

“Rukkhamūlagahanaṃ pasakkiya, nibbānaṃ hadayasmiṃ opiya;

Jhā [P 1.0200] gotama mā pamādo mā ca pamādo (sī. pī.), kiṃ te biḷibiḷikā karissatī”ti.

“Having entered the dense grove at the foot of a tree, and placed Nibbāna in your heart, meditate, O Gotama! Do not be heedless. What will this chattering accomplish for you?”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando tāya devatāya saṃvejito saṃvegamāpādīti.

Then the Venerable Ānanda, stirred by that deity, attained a sense of spiritual urgency.

6. Anuruddhasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Anuruddha

226. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā anuruddho kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Atha kho aññatarā tāvatiṃsakāyikā devatā jālinī [M 1.0202] nāma āyasmato anuruddhassa purāṇadutiyikā yenāyasmā anuruddho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

226. On one occasion, the Venerable Anuruddha was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Then a certain deity of the Tāvatiṃsa realm named Jālinī, who had been a former consort of the Venerable Anuruddha, approached the Venerable Anuruddha. Having approached, she addressed the Venerable Anuruddha with a verse:

“Tattha cittaṃ paṇidhehi, yattha te vusitaṃ pure;

Tāvatiṃsesu devesu, sabbakāmasamiddhisu;

Purakkhato parivuto, devakaññāhi sobhasī”ti.

“Direct your mind there, where you dwelt before, among the Tāvatiṃsa devas, endowed with all sensual pleasures. Honored and surrounded by celestial maidens, you shone.”

“Duggatā [V 1.0232] devakaññāyo, sakkāyasmiṃ patiṭṭhitā;

Te cāpi duggatā sattā, devakaññāhi patthitā”ti.

“Woeful are the celestial maidens, established in identity-view. And those beings too are woeful, who are longed for by the celestial maidens.”

“Na [T 1.0295] te sukhaṃ pajānanti, ye na passanti nandanaṃ;

Āvāsaṃ naradevānaṃ, tidasānaṃ yasassina”nti.

“They do not know happiness, those who do not see Nandana, the abode of the human-devas, the glorious Thirty-three.”

“Na tvaṃ bāle vijānāsi, yathā arahataṃ vaco;

Aniccā sabbasaṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho.

“O foolish one, you do not know the word of the Arahants. All conditioned formations are impermanent, having the nature of arising and passing away. Having arisen, they cease. Their pacification is happiness.”

“Natthi dāni punāvāso, devakāyasmi jālini;

Vikkhīṇo jātisaṃsāro, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

“O Jālinī, there is now no further dwelling for me in the celestial realm. The round of births is destroyed; there is now no renewed existence.”

7. Nāgadattasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Nāgadatta

227. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā nāgadatto kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā nāgadatto atikālena gāmaṃ pavisati, atidivā paṭikkamati. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā āyasmato nāgadattassa anukampikā atthakāmā āyasmantaṃ nāgadattaṃ saṃvejetukāmā yenāyasmā nāgadatto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [P 1.0201] āyasmantaṃ nāgadattaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

227. On one occasion, the Venerable Nāgadatta was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. At that time, the Venerable Nāgadatta would enter the village too early and return too late in the day. Then the deity who inhabited that forest grove, being compassionate and desiring his welfare, wishing to stir the Venerable Nāgadatta, approached the Venerable Nāgadatta. Having approached, he addressed the Venerable Nāgadatta with verses:

“Kāle pavisa nāgadatta, divā ca āgantvā ativelacārī;

Saṃsaṭṭho gahaṭṭhehi, samānasukhadukkho.

“O Nāgadatta, you enter the village early in the morning and, returning late in the day, you are one who wanders at improper times. You are mingled with householders, sharing their happiness and suffering.”

“Bhāyāmi nāgadattaṃ suppagabbhaṃ, kulesu vinibaddhaṃ;

Mā heva maccurañño balavato, antakassa vasaṃ upesī”ti vasameyyāti (sī. pī.), vasamesīti (syā. kaṃ.).

“I fear for Nāgadatta, who is very bold and bound to families. May you not come under the sway of the powerful King of Death, the Ender.”

Atha [M 1.0203] kho āyasmā nāgadatto tāya devatāya saṃvejito saṃvegamāpādīti.

Then the Venerable Nāgadatta, having been stirred by that deity, attained a sense of spiritual urgency.

8. Kulagharaṇīsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Mistress of the House

228. Ekaṃ [T 1.0296][V 1.0233] samayaṃ aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena so bhikkhu aññatarasmiṃ kule ativelaṃ ajjhogāḷhappatto viharati. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tassa bhikkhuno anukampikā atthakāmā taṃ bhikkhuṃ saṃvejetukāmā yā tasmiṃ kule kulagharaṇī, tassā vaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

228. On one occasion, a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. At that time, that bhikkhu was dwelling having become excessively involved with a certain family. Then the deity who inhabited that forest grove, being compassionate and desiring his welfare, wishing to stir that bhikkhu, created the appearance of the mistress of that family and approached that bhikkhu. Having approached, he addressed the bhikkhu with a verse:

“Nadītīresu saṇṭhāne, sabhāsu rathiyāsu ca;

Janā saṅgamma mantenti, mañca tañca tvañca (ka.) kimantara”nti.

“On riverbanks and at resting places, in assembly halls and on the main roads, people gather and whisper about me and you. For what reason is this?”

“Bahūhi saddā paccūhā, khamitabbā tapassinā;

Na tena maṅku hotabbaṃ, na hi tena kilissati.

“O mistress of the house, obstructive sounds are many; they are to be endured by an ascetic. One should not be downcast because of that, for one is not defiled by it.”

“Yo ca saddaparittāsī, vane vātamigo yathā;

Lahucittoti taṃ āhu, nāssa sampajjate vata”nti.

“Whoever is startled by a sound, like a wind-deer in the forest, him the wise call ‘fickle-minded’; his practice does not succeed.”

9. Vajjiputtasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Vajjian's Son

229. Ekaṃ samayaṃ aññataro vajjiputtako bhikkhu vesāliyaṃ viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena vesāliyaṃ vajjiputtako sabbaratticāro hoti. Atha [P 1.0202] kho so bhikkhu vesāliyā tūriya-tāḷita-vādita-nigghosasaddaṃ [T 1.0297] sutvā paridevamāno tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

229. On one occasion, a certain bhikkhu who was a Vajjian's son was dwelling in a certain forest grove in Vesālī. Now at that time, there was an all-night festival in Vesālī. Then that bhikkhu, hearing from Vesālī the sound of musical instruments being struck and played and the sound of shouting, lamenting, on that occasion recited this verse:

“Ekakā mayaṃ araññe viharāma,

Apaviddhaṃva apaviṭṭhaṃva (syā. kaṃ.) vanasmiṃ dārukaṃ;

Etādisikāya rattiyā,

Ko su nāmamhehi nāma amhehi (sī. pī.) pāpiyo”ti.

“We dwell alone in the forest, like a discarded log in the woods. On a night such as this, who indeed could be more wretched than us?”

Atha [V 1.0234] kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tassa bhikkhuno anukampikā atthakāmā taṃ bhikkhuṃ saṃvejetukāmā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then the deity who dwelt in that forest grove, being compassionate and desiring his welfare, wishing to stir that bhikkhu, approached him. Having approached, he addressed that bhikkhu with a verse:

“Ekakova [M 1.0204] tvaṃ araññe viharasi, apaviddhaṃva vanasmiṃ dārukaṃ;

Tassa te bahukā pihayanti, nerayikā viya saggagāmina”nti.

“You dwell all alone in the forest, like a discarded log in the woods. Many long for you, like beings in hell long for those going to heaven.”

Atha kho so bhikkhu tāya devatāya saṃvejito saṃvegamāpādīti.

Then that bhikkhu, stirred by that deity, attained a sense of spiritual urgency.

10. Sajjhāyasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Recitation

230. Ekaṃ samayaṃ aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena so bhikkhu yaṃ sudaṃ pubbe ativelaṃ sajjhāyabahulo viharati so aparena samayena appossukko tuṇhībhūto saṅkasāyati. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tassa bhikkhuno dhammaṃ asuṇantī yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ [T 1.0298] bhikkhuṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

230. On one occasion, a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time, that bhikkhu, who formerly had spent much time in recitation, at a later time became unconcerned, silent, and passed his time in the bliss of the attainment of fruition. Then the deity who dwelt in that forest grove, not hearing the Dhamma from that bhikkhu, approached him. Having approached, she addressed that bhikkhu with a verse:

“Kasmā tuvaṃ dhammapadāni bhikkhu, nādhīyasi bhikkhūhi saṃvasanto;

Sutvāna dhammaṃ labhatippasādaṃ, diṭṭheva dhamme labhatippasaṃsa”nti.

“Why, bhikkhu, do you not recite the words of the Dhamma? One who associates with bhikkhus, having heard the Dhamma, gains confidence in the reciter. In this very life, one gains praise.”

“Ahu pure dhammapadesu chando, yāva virāgena samāgamimha;

Yato [P 1.0203] virāgena samāgamimha, yaṃ kiñci diṭṭhaṃva sutaṃ mutaṃ vā;

Aññāya nikkhepanamāhu santo”ti.

“Formerly, we had a desire for the teachings of the Dhamma, until we attained dispassion. Since we have attained dispassion, the virtuous praise the relinquishment of whatever is seen, heard, or cognized, after having understood it.”

11. Akusalavitakkasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on Unwholesome Thoughts

231. Ekaṃ samayaṃ aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena so bhikkhu divāvihāragato pāpake akusale vitakke vitakketi, seyyathidaṃ [V 1.0235] – kāmavitakkaṃ, byāpādavitakkaṃ, vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tassa bhikkhuno anukampikā atthakāmā taṃ bhikkhuṃ saṃvejetukāmā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

231. On one occasion, a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time, that bhikkhu, having gone to his day-abode, was thinking evil, unwholesome thoughts, namely: thoughts of sensuality, thoughts of ill will, and thoughts of harming. Then the devatā who dwelt in that forest grove, being compassionate and desiring his welfare, wishing to stir that bhikkhu, approached him. Having approached, she addressed that bhikkhu with these verses:

“Ayoniso [T 1.0299] manasikārā, so vitakkehi khajjasi;

Ayoniso ayoniṃ (pī. ka.) paṭinissajja, yoniso anucintaya.

“Through unwise attention, you are being consumed by thoughts. Having abandoned unwise attention, reflect wisely.

“Satthāraṃ [M 1.0205] dhammamārabbha, saṅghaṃ sīlāni attano;

Adhigacchasi pāmojjaṃ, pītisukhamasaṃsayaṃ;

Tato pāmojjabahulo, dukkhassantaṃ karissasī”ti.

“Reflecting on the Teacher, the Dhamma, the Sangha, and your own virtues, you will without doubt obtain joy, and rapture and happiness. Then, abounding in joy, you will make an end of suffering.”

Atha kho so bhikkhu tāya devatāya saṃvejito saṃvegamāpādīti.

Then that bhikkhu, stirred by that devatā, attained a sense of urgency.

12. Majjhanhikasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse at Midday

232. Ekaṃ samayaṃ aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Atha kho tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tassa bhikkhuno santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

232. At one time, a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Then, the deity inhabiting that forest grove approached that bhikkhu. Having approached, the deity recited this verse in the presence of that bhikkhu:

“Ṭhite majjhanhike kāle, sannisīvesu sannisinnesu (syā. kaṃ. pī.) pakkhisu;

Saṇateva brahāraññaṃ, taṃ bhayaṃ paṭibhāti maṃ.

“When it is high noon and the birds are settled, the great forest seems to resound; that fear appears to me.”

“Ṭhite majjhanhike kāle, sannisīvesu pakkhisu;

Saṇateva brahāraññaṃ, sā rati paṭibhāti ma”nti.

“When it is high noon and the birds are settled, the great forest seems to resound; that delight appears to me.”

13. Pākatindriyasuttaṃ

13. The Discourse on Unrestrained Faculties

233. Ekaṃ samayaṃ sambahulā bhikkhū kosalesu viharanti aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe uddhatā unnaḷā capalā mukharā vikiṇṇavācā [P 1.0204] muṭṭhassatino asampajānā asamāhitā vibbhantacittā [V 1.0236] pākatindriyā. Atha [T 1.0300] kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anukampikā atthakāmā te bhikkhū saṃvejetukāmā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

233. At one time, many bhikkhus were dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove—restless, arrogant, fickle, harsh-mouthed, of scattered speech, unmindful, not clearly comprehending, unconcentrated, with wandering minds, and with unrestrained faculties. Then, the devatā inhabiting that forest grove, being compassionate and wishing for their welfare, desiring to stir them, approached those bhikkhus. Having approached, she addressed them with verses:

“Sukhajīvino pure āsuṃ, bhikkhū gotamasāvakā;

Anicchā piṇḍamesanā, anicchā sayanāsanaṃ;

Loke aniccataṃ ñatvā, dukkhassantaṃ akaṃsu te.

“In the past, the bhikkhus, disciples of Gotama, lived in ease. Without desire they sought alms; without desire, a resting place. Having known impermanence in the world, they made an end of suffering.

“Dupposaṃ katvā attānaṃ, gāme gāmaṇikā viya;

Bhutvā bhutvā nipajjanti, parāgāresu mucchitā.

“Having made themselves difficult to support, like a village headman in a village, having eaten and eaten, they lie down, infatuated, in the houses of others.

“Saṅghassa [M 1.0206] añjaliṃ katvā, idhekacce vadāmahaṃ;

Apaviddhā apaviṭṭhā (syā. kaṃ.) anāthā te, yathā petā tatheva te.

“Having paid reverence to the Saṅgha, I speak of some here: they are cast off, without refuge; just as are the departed, so too are they.

“Ye kho pamattā viharanti, te me sandhāya bhāsitaṃ;

Ye appamattā viharanti, namo tesaṃ karomaha”nti.

“This was spoken by me with reference to those who dwell in heedlessness. To those who dwell in heedfulness, I pay homage.”

Atha kho te bhikkhū tāya devatāya saṃvejitā saṃvegamāpādunti.

Then those bhikkhus, stirred by that devatā, attained a sense of spiritual urgency.

14. Gandhatthenasuttaṃ

14. The Discourse on the Scent-Thief

234. Ekaṃ samayaṃ aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe. Tena kho pana samayena so bhikkhu pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto pokkharaṇiṃ ogāhetvā padumaṃ upasiṅghati. Atha kho yā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tassa bhikkhuno anukampikā atthakāmā taṃ bhikkhuṃ saṃvejetukāmā yena [T 1.0301] so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

234. At one time, a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain forest grove. Now at that time, that bhikkhu, after his meal, having returned from his alms-round, went down into a lotus pond and smelled a lotus flower. Then, the devatā inhabiting that forest grove, being compassionate and wishing for that bhikkhu's welfare, desiring to stir him, approached that bhikkhu. Having approached, she addressed that bhikkhu with a verse:

“Yametaṃ vārijaṃ pupphaṃ, adinnaṃ upasiṅghasi;

Ekaṅgametaṃ theyyānaṃ, gandhatthenosi mārisā”ti.

“This water-born flower which you smell, not having been given—this is one component of theft. You are a scent-thief, good sir!”

“Na [V 1.0237] harāmi na bhañjāmi, ārā siṅghāmi vārijaṃ;

Atha kena nu vaṇṇena, gandhatthenoti vuccati.

“I do not take it, nor do I break it; from afar I smell the water-born flower. For what reason, then, am I called a scent-thief?

“Yvāyaṃ bhisāni khanati, puṇḍarīkāni bhañjati;

Evaṃ ākiṇṇakammanto, kasmā eso na vuccatī”ti.

“That one who digs up lotus roots and breaks the white lotuses—one of such impure conduct, why is he not called a thief?”

“Ākiṇṇaluddo [P 1.0205] puriso, dhāticelaṃva makkhito;

Tasmiṃ me vacanaṃ natthi, tvañcārahāmi vattave.

“A man who is coarse and cruel, smeared like a soiled cloth—I have nothing to say to him, but it is you whom I am fit to address.

“Anaṅgaṇassa posassa, niccaṃ sucigavesino;

Vālaggamattaṃ pāpassa, abbhāmattaṃva khāyatī”ti.

“To a person who is stainless, ever seeking purity, even a hair-tip’s measure of evil appears as large as a cloud.”

“Addhā maṃ yakkha jānāsi, atho me anukampasi;

Punapi yakkha vajjāsi, yadā passasi edisa”nti.

“Surely, yakkha, you know me and have compassion for me. Speak again, yakkha, whenever you see such a thing.”

“Neva [M 1.0207] taṃ upajīvāma, napi te bhatakāmhase;

Tvameva bhikkhu jāneyya, yena gaccheyya suggati”nti.

“We do not live depending on you, nor are we your hired servants. You yourself, bhikkhu, should know the way by which you may go to a good destination.”

Atha kho so bhikkhu tāya devatāya saṃvejito saṃvegamāpādīti.

Then that bhikkhu, stirred by that devatā, attained a sense of spiritual urgency.

Vanasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Forest Saṃyutta is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Vivekaṃ [T 1.0302] upaṭṭhānañca, kassapagottena sambahulā;

Ānando anuruddho ca, nāgadattañca kulagharaṇī.

Seclusion and Attendance, Kassapagotta and Many Bhikkhus; Ānanda and Anuruddha, Nāgadatta and Kulagharaṇī.

Vajjiputto ca vesālī, sajjhāyena ayoniso;

Majjhanhikālamhi pākatindriya, padumapupphena cuddasa bhaveti.

The Vajjian Son, Vesālī, Recitation, Unwise Attention; Midday, Unrestrained Faculties, and with the Lotus Flower, there are fourteen.

10. Yakkhasaṃyuttaṃ

10. The Connected Discourses with Yakkhas

1. Indakasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse with Indaka

235. Evaṃ [T 1.0303][V 1.0238][M 1.0208] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ [P 1.0206] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati indakūṭe pabbate, indakassa yakkhassa bhavane. Atha kho indako yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

235. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on Mount Indakūṭa, in the dwelling of the yakkha Indaka. Then the yakkha Indaka approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Rūpaṃ na jīvanti vadanti buddhā, kathaṃ nvayaṃ vindatimaṃ sarīraṃ;

Kutassa aṭṭhīyakapiṇḍameti, kathaṃ nvayaṃ sajjati gabbharasmi”nti.

“The Buddhas say that form is not a living being; how then does this being obtain this body? From where does this lump of bones come to be, and how does it become attached in the womb?”

“Paṭhamaṃ kalalaṃ hoti, kalalā hoti abbudaṃ;

Abbudā jāyate pesi, pesi nibbattatī ghano;

Ghanā pasākhā jāyanti, kesā lomā nakhāpi ca.

“First, the kalala comes to be; from the kalala, the abbuda comes to be. From the abbuda, the pesi is born; from the pesi, the ghana is produced. From the ghana, the main limbs are born, and also hair of the head, hair of the body, and nails.”

“Yañcassa bhuñjatī mātā, annaṃ pānañca bhojanaṃ;

Tena so tattha yāpeti, mātukucchigato naro”ti.

Whatever food, drink, and nourishment his mother consumes, by that the person situated in the mother's womb is sustained there.

2. Sakkanāmasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse with Sakka

236. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Atha kho sakkanāmako yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [T 1.0304] bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

236. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on the Vulture Peak Mountain. Then the yakkha named Sakka approached the Blessed One; having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Sabbaganthappahīnassa[V 1.0239], vippamuttassa te sato;

Samaṇassa na taṃ sādhu, yadaññamanusāsasī”ti yadaññamanusāsatīti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.).

For you, a contemplative who has abandoned all ties, is released, and is mindful, it is not good that you instruct another.

“Yena kenaci vaṇṇena, saṃvāso sakka jāyati;

Na taṃ arahati sappañño, manasā anukampituṃ.

Sakka, by whatever reason association arises, a wise person is not fit to feel compassion for that one, even in mind.

“Manasā ce pasannena, yadaññamanusāsati;

Na tena hoti saṃyutto, yānukampā sānukampā (sī. pī.) anuddayā”ti.

If with a serene mind one instructs another, one is not bound by that. One is connected by means of whatever compassion and sympathy there is.

3. Sūcilomasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse with Sūciloma

237. Ekaṃ [P 1.0207] samayaṃ bhagavā gayāyaṃ viharati ṭaṅkitamañce sūcilomassa yakkhassa bhavane. Tena kho pana samayena kharo ca yakkho sūcilomo [M 1.0209] ca yakkho bhagavato avidūre atikkamanti. Atha kho kharo yakkho sūcilomaṃ yakkhaṃ etadavoca – “eso samaṇo”ti! “Neso samaṇo, samaṇako eso”. “Yāva jānāmi yadi vā so samaṇo yadi vā pana so samaṇako”ti.

237. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Gayā on the Ṭaṅkita stone-slab, in the abode of the yakkha Sūciloma. Now at that time, the yakkha Kharo and the yakkha Sūciloma were passing by not far from the Blessed One. Then the yakkha Kharo said to the yakkha Sūciloma, 'This is an ascetic!' 'This is no ascetic, this is a contemptible ascetic. I shall find out whether he is an ascetic or a contemptible ascetic.'

Atha kho sūcilomo yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato kāyaṃ upanāmesi. Atha kho bhagavā kāyaṃ apanāmesi. Atha kho sūcilomo yakkho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhāyasi maṃ samaṇā”ti? “Na khvāhaṃ taṃ, āvuso, bhāyāmi; api ca te samphasso pāpako”ti. “Pañhaṃ taṃ, samaṇa pucchissāmi. Sace me na byākarissasi, cittaṃ vā te khipissāmi, hadayaṃ vā te phālessāmi, pādesu [T 1.0305] vā gahetvā pāragaṅgāya pāraṃ gaṅgāya (ka.) khipissāmī”ti. “Na khvāhaṃ taṃ, āvuso, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo me cittaṃ vā khipeyya hadayaṃ vā phāleyya pādesu vā gahetvā pāragaṅgāya khipeyya; api ca tvaṃ, āvuso, puccha yadā kaṅkhasī”ti. Atha kho sūcilomo yakkho bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi – ( ) (atha kho sūcilomo yakkho bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi.) (sī.)

Then the yakkha Sūciloma approached the Blessed One; having approached, he pressed his body against the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One drew his body away. Then the yakkha Sūciloma said to the Blessed One: 'Are you afraid of me, ascetic?' 'I am not afraid of you, friend, but your touch is evil.' 'I will ask you a question, ascetic. If you do not answer me, I will either drive your mind to distraction, or I will split your heart, or I will seize you by the feet and throw you to the far shore of the Ganges.' 'Friend, I do not see anyone in the world with its devas, its Māra, and its Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, who could drive my mind to distraction, or split my heart, or seize me by the feet and throw me to the far shore of the Ganges. Nevertheless, friend, ask what you wish.'

“Rāgo [V 1.0240] ca doso ca kutonidānā,

Aratī ratī lomahaṃso kutojā;

Kuto samuṭṭhāya manovitakkā,

Kumārakā dhaṅkamivossajantī”ti.

From what source do lust and hatred have their origin? From what are discontent, delight, and horripilation born? Arising from what do thoughts of the mind spring forth, like boys letting loose a crow?

“Rāgo ca doso ca itonidānā,

Aratī ratī lomahaṃso itojā;

Ito samuṭṭhāya manovitakkā,

Kumārakā dhaṅkamivossajanti.

Lust and hatred have their origin from this; discontent, delight, and horripilation are born from this. Arising from this, thoughts of the mind spring forth, like boys letting loose a crow.

“Snehajā attasambhūtā, nigrodhasseva khandhajā;

Puthū visattā kāmesu, māluvāva vitatā vitthatā (syā. kaṃ.) vane.

Born of affection, arisen from the self, like offshoots from a banyan's trunk; they are widely attached to sensual pleasures, like a māluvā creeper spreading through a forest.

“Ye [M 1.0210][P 1.0208] naṃ pajānanti yatonidānaṃ,

Te naṃ vinodenti suṇohi yakkha;

Te duttaraṃ oghamimaṃ taranti,

Atiṇṇapubbaṃ apunabbhavāyā”ti.

Those who understand this and its source—listen, O yakkha—they dispel it. They cross over this flood, so difficult to cross, never crossed before, for the sake of no further becoming.

4. Maṇibhaddasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse with Maṇibhadda

238. Ekaṃ [T 1.0306] samayaṃ bhagavā magadhesu viharati maṇimālike cetiye maṇibhaddassa yakkhassa bhavane. Atha kho maṇibhaddo yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

238. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans at the Maṇimālaka Shrine, in the abode of the yakkha Maṇibhadda. Then the yakkha Maṇibhadda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Satīmato [V 1.0241] sadā bhaddaṃ, satimā sukhamedhati;

Satīmato suve seyyo, verā ca parimuccatī”ti.

For the mindful one, there is always good; the mindful one attains happiness. For the mindful one, it is ever better; and one is freed from enmity.

“Satīmato sadā bhaddaṃ, satimā sukhamedhati;

Satīmato suve seyyo, verā na parimuccati.

For the mindful one, there is always good; the mindful one attains happiness. For the mindful one, it is ever better; but one is not freed from enmity.

“Yassa sabbamahorattaṃ rattiṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.), ahiṃsāya rato mano;

Mettaṃ so sabbabhūtesu, veraṃ tassa na kenacī”ti.

Whose mind delights in harmlessness all day and night, who has loving-kindness towards all beings—for that person, there is enmity with none.

5. Sānusuttaṃ

5. The Discourse about Sānu

239. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarissā upāsikāya sānu nāma putto yakkhena gahito hoti. Atha kho sā upāsikā paridevamānā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

239. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, a certain female lay follower’s son named Sānu had been seized by a yakkha. Then that female lay follower, lamenting, on that occasion spoke these verses:

“Cātuddasiṃ [T 1.0307] pañcadasiṃ, yā ca pakkhassa aṭṭhamī;

Pāṭihāriyapakkhañca, aṭṭhaṅgasusamāgataṃ.

The fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the eighth day of the fortnight, and the special observance day, well-endowed with the eight factors,

“Uposathaṃ upavasanti, brahmacariyaṃ caranti ye;

Na tehi yakkhā kīḷanti, iti me arahataṃ sutaṃ;

Sā dāni ajja passāmi, yakkhā kīḷanti sānunā”ti.

Those who observe the Uposatha and practice the holy life—yakkhas do not harass them; thus have I heard from the Arahants. But now today I see yakkhas harassing Sānu.

“Cātuddasiṃ [M 1.0211] pañcadasiṃ, yā ca pakkhassa aṭṭhamī;

Pāṭihāriyapakkhañca, aṭṭhaṅgasusamāgataṃ;

Uposathaṃ [P 1.0209] upavasanti, brahmacariyaṃ caranti ye.

The fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the eighth day of the fortnight, and the special observance day, well-endowed with the eight factors; those who observe the Uposatha and practice the holy life—

“Na tehi yakkhā kīḷanti, sāhu te arahataṃ sutaṃ;

Sānuṃ pabuddhaṃ vajjāsi, yakkhānaṃ vacanaṃ idaṃ;

Mākāsi pāpakaṃ kammaṃ, āvi vā yadi vā raho.

‘Yakkhas do not harass them’—well have you heard this from the Arahants. Tell this word of the yakkhas to the awakened Sānu: ‘Do no evil deed, whether in the open or in secret.

“Sace [V 1.0242] ca saceva (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), yañceva (sī.) pāpakaṃ kammaṃ, karissasi karosi vā;

Na te dukkhā pamutyatthi, uppaccāpi palāyato”ti.

And if you will do an evil deed, or are doing one, there is no escape from suffering for you, even if you fly up and flee.’

“Mataṃ vā amma rodanti, yo vā jīvaṃ na dissati;

Jīvantaṃ amma passantī, kasmā maṃ amma rodasī”ti.

Mother, they weep for the dead, or for one who, though living, is not seen. Seeing me alive, mother, why do you weep for me?

“Mataṃ vā putta rodanti, yo vā jīvaṃ na dissati;

Yo ca kāme cajitvāna, punarāgacchate idha;

Taṃ vāpi putta rodanti, puna jīvaṃ mato hi so.

Son, they weep for the dead, or for one who, though living, is not seen; and for one who, having renounced sensual pleasures, returns here again—for him too, son, they weep, for though living, he is as one dead.

“Kukkuḷā ubbhato tāta, kukkuḷaṃ kukkuḷe (sī.) patitumicchasi;

Narakā ubbhato tāta, narakaṃ patitumicchasi.

My dear, having been lifted out from the hot embers, you wish to fall back into the hot embers. My dear, having been lifted out from the abyss, you wish to fall back into the abyss.

“Abhidhāvatha [T 1.0308] bhaddante, kassa ujjhāpayāmase;

Ādittā nīhataṃ nibbhataṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.), nibhataṃ (pī. ka.) bhaṇḍaṃ, puna ḍayhitumicchasī”ti.

Run for help, good sirs! To whom shall we complain? You wish to be burned again, like goods taken out from a fire!

6. Piyaṅkarasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse with Piyaṅkara

240. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā anuruddho sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā anuruddho rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya dhammapadāni bhāsati. Atha kho piyaṅkaramātā yakkhinī puttakaṃ evaṃ tosesi –

240. On one occasion the Venerable Anuruddha was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, the Venerable Anuruddha, having risen early, was reciting verses of the Dhamma. Then the yakkhiṇī, the mother of Piyaṅkara, soothed her young child thus:

“Mā saddaṃ kari piyaṅkara, bhikkhu dhammapadāni bhāsati;

Api api (sī.) ca dhammapadaṃ vijāniya, paṭipajjema hitāya no siyā.

“O Piyaṅkara, do not make a sound. The monk is reciting verses of the Dhamma. Having understood a verse of the Dhamma, let us practice it. It may be for our welfare.”

“Pāṇesu ca saṃyamāmase, sampajānamusā na bhaṇāmase;

Sikkhema susīlyamattano susīlamattano (sī. ka.), api muccema pisācayoniyā”ti.

“Let us restrain ourselves with regard to beings, and let us not speak a deliberate falsehood. Let us train ourselves in good virtue; we may then be freed from the pisāca birth.”

7. Punabbasusuttaṃ

7. The Punabbasu Sutta

241. Ekaṃ [V 1.0243][M 1.0212] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena [P 1.0210] kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhū nibbānapaṭisaṃyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṃseti. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā [T 1.0309] samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṃ suṇanti. Atha kho punabbasumātā yakkhinī puttake evaṃ tosesi –

241. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time, the Blessed One was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the monks with a Dhamma talk connected with Nibbāna. And those monks, treating it as essential, bringing it to mind, encompassing it with their whole mind, and with attentive ears, were listening to the Dhamma. Then the yakkhiṇī, the mother of Punabbasu, soothed her children thus:

“Tuṇhī uttarike hohi, tuṇhī hohi punabbasu;

Yāvāhaṃ buddhaseṭṭhassa, dhammaṃ sossāmi satthuno.

“Be silent, O Uttarika; be silent, O Punabbasu, so that I may listen to the Dhamma of the Teacher, the best of Buddhas.”

“Nibbānaṃ bhagavā āha, sabbaganthappamocanaṃ;

Ativelā ca me hoti, asmiṃ dhamme piyāyanā.

“The Blessed One speaks of Nibbāna, the release from all fetters. And my love for this Dhamma is exceedingly great.”

“Piyo loke sako putto, piyo loke sako pati;

Tato piyatarā mayhaṃ, assa dhammassa magganā.

“Dear in the world is one’s own child, dear in the world is one’s own husband; but to me, the seeking of this Dhamma is far dearer than that.”

“Na hi putto pati vāpi, piyo dukkhā pamocaye;

Yathā saddhammassavanaṃ, dukkhā moceti pāṇinaṃ.

“For a dear child or husband cannot release one from suffering in the way that hearing the good Dhamma releases beings from suffering.”

“Loke dukkhaparetasmiṃ, jarāmaraṇasaṃyute;

Jarāmaraṇamokkhāya, yaṃ dhammaṃ abhisambudhaṃ;

Taṃ dhammaṃ sotumicchāmi, tuṇhī hohi punabbasū”ti.

“In this world, afflicted by suffering and connected with aging and death, I wish to hear that Dhamma for release from aging and death, which the Fully Enlightened One has understood. Be silent, O Punabbasu!”

“Ammā na byāharissāmi, tuṇhībhūtāyamuttarā;

Dhammameva nisāmehi, saddhammassavanaṃ sukhaṃ;

Saddhammassa anaññāya, ammā dukkhaṃ carāmase.

“Mother, I will not speak; this Uttarā is silent. You should just listen to the Dhamma. Hearing the good Dhamma is happiness. Mother, from not knowing the good Dhamma, we wander in suffering.”

“Esa [V 1.0244] devamanussānaṃ, sammūḷhānaṃ pabhaṅkaro;

Buddho antimasārīro, dhammaṃ deseti cakkhumā”ti.

“This is the light-maker for the deluded devas and humans; the Buddha, bearing his final body, the one with vision, teaches the Dhamma.”

“Sādhu kho paṇḍito nāma, putto jāto uresayo;

Putto me buddhaseṭṭhassa, dhammaṃ suddhaṃ piyāyati.

“It is indeed good that a son, one who is wise, was born from my breast. My son delights in the pure Dhamma of the best of Buddhas.”

“Punabbasu [T 1.0310] sukhī hohi, ajjāhamhi samuggatā;

Diṭṭhāni ariyasaccāni, uttarāpi suṇātu me”ti.

“Punabbasu, be happy! Today I have emerged from the cycle. The Noble Truths have been seen. Let Uttarā also listen to my Dhamma.”

8. Sudattasuttaṃ

8. The Sudatta Sutta

242. Ekaṃ [M 1.0213] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati sītavane. Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati rājagahaṃ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Assosi kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati – “buddho kira loke uppanno”ti. Tāvadeva ca pana bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamitukāmo hoti. Athassa [P 1.0211] anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa etadahosi – “akālo kho ajja bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ. Sve dānāhaṃ kālena bhagavantaṃ dassanāya gamissāmī”ti buddhagatāya satiyā nipajji. Rattiyā sudaṃ tikkhattuṃ vuṭṭhāsi pabhātanti maññamāno. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena sivathikadvāraṃ sīvathikadvāraṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) tenupasaṅkami. Amanussā dvāraṃ vivariṃsu. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nagaramhā nikkhamantassa āloko antaradhāyi, andhakāro pāturahosi, bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso udapādi, tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi. Atha kho sivako sīvako (sī. pī.) yakkho antarahito saddamanussāvesi –

242. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Sītavana. Now at that time, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had arrived in Rājagaha on some business. The householder Anāthapiṇḍika heard: “A Buddha, it is said, has arisen in the world.” And just at that moment, he became desirous of approaching to see the Blessed One. Then this thought occurred to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “It is not the right time today to approach to see the Blessed One. Tomorrow, at the proper time, I will go to see the Blessed One.” With mindfulness directed toward the Buddha, he lay down. During the night, thinking it was dawn, he arose three times. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the charnel ground gate. Non-human beings opened the gate. Then, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, as he was leaving the city, the light disappeared, darkness appeared, and fear, stiffness, and horripilation arose, and from there he became desirous of turning back again. Then the yakkha Sīvaka, having made himself invisible, caused a sound to be heard:

“Sataṃ hatthī sataṃ assā, sataṃ assatarīrathā;

Sataṃ kaññāsahassāni, āmukkamaṇikuṇḍalā;

Ekassa padavītihārassa, kalaṃ nāgghanti soḷasiṃ.

“A hundred thousand elephants, a hundred thousand horses, a hundred thousand mule-drawn chariots, and a hundred thousand maidens adorned with jeweled earrings, are not worth the sixteenth part of a single footstep.”

“Abhikkama [T 1.0311] gahapati, abhikkama gahapati;

Abhikkamanaṃ te seyyo, no paṭikkamana”nti.

“Go forward, householder! Go forward, householder! Going forward is better for you, not retreating.”

Atha [V 1.0245] kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa andhakāro antaradhāyi, āloko pāturahosi, yaṃ ahosi bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso, so paṭippassambhi. Dutiyampi kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa āloko antaradhāyi, andhakāro pāturahosi, bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso udapādi, tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi. Dutiyampi kho sivako yakkho antarahito saddamanussāvesi –

Then, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, the darkness disappeared and light appeared. Whatever fear, stiffness, and horripilation there had been, that subsided. For a second time, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, the light disappeared and darkness appeared; fear, stiffness, and horripilation arose, and from there he again became desirous of turning back. For a second time, the yakkha Sīvaka, having made himself invisible, caused a sound to be heard:

“Sataṃ [M 1.0214] hatthī sataṃ assā…pe…

Kalaṃ nāgghanti soḷasiṃ.

“A hundred thousand elephants, a hundred thousand horses, a hundred thousand chariots drawn by thoroughbreds, a hundred thousand maidens adorned with jeweled earrings—these are not worth a sixteenth part of a single step taken towards the monastery.”

“Abhikkama gahapati, abhikkama gahapati;

Abhikkamanaṃ te seyyo, no paṭikkamana”nti.

“Go forward, householder! Go forward, householder! Going forward is better for you, not retreating.”

Atha [T 1.0312] kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa andhakāro antaradhāyi[P 1.0212], āloko pāturahosi, yaṃ ahosi bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso, so paṭippassambhi. Tatiyampi kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa āloko antaradhāyi, andhakāro pāturahosi, bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso udapādi, tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi. Tatiyampi kho sivako yakkho antarahito saddamanussāvesi –

Then, for the householder Anāthapiᅁᅁika, the darkness disappeared and light appeared. Whatever fear, stiffness, and horripilation there had been, that subsided. For a third time, the light disappeared for the householder Anāthapiᅁᅁika, and darkness appeared; fear, stiffness, and horripilation arose, and he then wished to turn back again. For a third time, the yakkha SĦvaka, remaining invisible, caused a sound to be heard:

“Sataṃ hatthī sataṃ assā…pe…

Kalaṃ nāgghanti soḷasiṃ.

“A hundred thousand elephants, a hundred thousand horses… and so on… are not worth the sixteenth part.”

“Abhikkama gahapati, abhikkama gahapati;

Abhikkamanaṃ te seyyo, no paṭikkamana”nti.

“Go forward, householder! Go forward, householder! Going forward is better for you, not retreating.”

Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa andhakāro antaradhāyi, āloko pāturahosi, yaṃ [V 1.0246] ahosi bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso, so paṭippassambhi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena sītavanaṃ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami.

Then, for the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, the darkness disappeared and light appeared. Whatever fear, stiffness, and horripilation there had been, that subsided. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the Sītavana where the Blessed One was.

Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya abbhokāse caṅkamati. Addasā kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna caṅkamā orohitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “ehi sudattā”ti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati, nāmena maṃ bhagavā ālapatīti, haṭṭho udaggo tattheva bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kacci, bhante, bhagavā sukhamasayitthā”ti?

Now at that time, the Blessed One, having arisen in the pre-dawn hours of the night, was walking back and forth in the open air. The Blessed One saw the householder Anāthapiṇḍika coming from afar. Having seen him, he descended from the walking path and sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “Come, Sudatta.” Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, thinking, “The Blessed One addresses me by my given name,” became joyful and elated, and right there, having fallen with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I trust the Blessed One has rested in comfort?”

“Sabbadā ve sukhaṃ seti, brāhmaṇo parinibbuto;

Yo na limpati kāmesu, sītibhūto nirūpadhi.

“Always, indeed, does the brahmin who is fully extinguished sleep in comfort; he who is not smeared by sensual pleasures, who has become cool, and is without substratum.

“Sabbā āsattiyo chetvā, vineyya hadaye daraṃ;

Upasanto sukhaṃ seti, santiṃ pappuyya cetasā”ti cetasoti (sī.).

“Having cut off all attachments, having dispelled distress in the heart, the calmed one sleeps in comfort, having attained peace with the mind.”

9. Paṭhamasukkāsuttaṃ

9. The First Sukkā Sutta

243. Ekaṃ [M 1.0215] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena sukkā bhikkhunī mahatiyā parisāya parivutā dhammaṃ deseti. Atha kho sukkāya bhikkhuniyā abhippasanno yakkho rājagahe rathikāya [T 1.0313] rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

243. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Now at that time the bhikkhunī Sukkā was teaching the Dhamma surrounded by a large assembly. Then a yakkha, devoted to the bhikkhunī Sukkā, approaching from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads in Rājagaha, at that time recited these verses:

“Kiṃ me katā rājagahe manussā, madhupītāva seyare;

Ye sukkaṃ na payirupāsanti, desentiṃ amataṃ padaṃ.

“What have these people in Rājagaha done? They lie as if drunk with honey; they do not attend upon Sukkā, who teaches the deathless state.

“Tañca pana appaṭivānīyaṃ, asecanakamojavaṃ;

Pivanti maññe sappaññā, valāhakamiva panthagū”ti valāhakamivaddhagūti (sī.).

“And that which is irresistible, with its inherently potent essence; the wise, I think, drink it, as travelers drink from a rain cloud.”

10. Dutiyasukkāsuttaṃ

10. The Second Sukkā Sutta

244. Ekaṃ [V 1.0247] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena [P 1.0213] kho pana samayena aññataro upāsako sukkāya bhikkhuniyā bhojanaṃ adāsi. Atha kho sukkāya bhikkhuniyā abhippasanno yakkho rājagahe rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

244. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now on that occasion a certain lay follower gave food to the bhikkhunī Sukkā. Then a yakkha who was deeply devoted to the bhikkhunī Sukkā, went from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads in Rājagaha, and at that time recited this verse:

“Puññaṃ vata pasavi bahuṃ, sappañño vatāyaṃ upāsako;

Yo sukkāya adāsi bhojanaṃ, sabbaganthehi vippamuttiyā”ti vippamuttāyāti (syā. kaṃ.).

“Indeed, this lay follower has generated much merit, and is truly wise; he who gave food to Sukkā, for liberation from all ties.”

11. Cīrāsuttaṃ

11. The Cīrā Sutta

245. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro upāsako cīrāya cirāya (ka.) bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṃ adāsi. Atha [T 1.0314] kho cīrāya bhikkhuniyā abhippasanno yakkho rājagahe rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

245. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. Now at that time a certain lay follower gave a robe to the bhikkhunī Cīrā. Then, a yakkha, deeply devoted to the bhikkhunī Cīrā, going from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads in Rājagaha, at that time spoke this verse:

“Puññaṃ [M 1.0216] vata pasavi bahuṃ, sappañño vatāyaṃ upāsako;

Yo cīrāya adāsi cīvaraṃ, sabbayogehi vippamuttiyā”ti vippamuttāyāti (syā. kaṃ.).

“Indeed, this lay follower has generated much merit, and is truly wise; he who gave a robe to Cīrā, for liberation from all yokes.”

12. Āḷavakasuttaṃ

12. The Āᄷavaka Sutta

246. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā āḷaviyaṃ viharati āḷavakassa yakkhassa bhavane. Atha kho āḷavako yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “nikkhama, samaṇā”ti. “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā nikkhami. “Pavisa, samaṇā”ti. “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā pāvisi. Dutiyampi kho āḷavako yakkho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “nikkhama, samaṇā”ti. “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā nikkhami. “Pavisa, samaṇā”ti. “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā pāvisi. Tatiyampi [P 1.0214] kho āḷavako yakkho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [V 1.0248] – “nikkhama, samaṇā”ti. “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā nikkhami. “Pavisa, samaṇā”ti. “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā pāvisi. Catutthampi kho āḷavako yakkho bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “nikkhama, samaṇā”ti. “Na khvāhaṃ taṃ, āvuso, nikkhamissāmi. Yaṃ te karaṇīyaṃ taṃ karohī”ti. “Pañhaṃ taṃ, samaṇa, pucchissāmi. Sace me na byākarissasi, cittaṃ vā te khipissāmi, hadayaṃ vā te phālessāmi, pādesu vā gahetvā pāragaṅgāya khipissāmī”ti. “Na khvāhaṃ taṃ, āvuso, passāmi sadevake loke samārake [T 1.0315] sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, ye me cittaṃ vā khipeyya hadayaṃ vā phāleyya, pādesu vā gahetvā pāragaṅgāya khipeyya. Api ca tvaṃ, āvuso, puccha yadā kaṅkhasī”ti (atha kho āḷavako yakkho bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi.) (sī.).

246. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Āḷavī, in the abode of the yakkha Āḷavaka. Then the yakkha Āḷavaka approached the Blessed One and said to him: “Get out, ascetic!” “Very well, friend,” said the Blessed One, and he went out. “Come in, ascetic!” “Very well, friend,” said the Blessed One, and he entered. A second time, the yakkha Āḷavaka said to the Blessed One: “Get out, ascetic!” “Very well, friend,” said the Blessed One, and he went out. “Come in, ascetic!” “Very well, friend,” said the Blessed One, and he entered. A third time, the yakkha Āḷavaka said to the Blessed One: “Get out, ascetic!” “Very well, friend,” said the Blessed One, and he went out. “Come in, ascetic!” “Very well, friend,” said the Blessed One, and he entered. A fourth time, the yakkha Āḷavaka said to the Blessed One: “Get out, ascetic!” “I will not get out, friend. Do what you must.” “I will ask you a question, ascetic. If you do not answer me, I will scatter your mind, or split your heart, or seize you by the feet and throw you across the Ganges!” “I do not see anyone in this world, friend, with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans, who could scatter my mind, split my heart, or seize me by the feet and throw me across the Ganges. But ask, friend, whatever you wish.”

“Kiṃsūdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ, kiṃsu suciṇṇaṃ sukhamāvahāti;

Kiṃsu have sādutaraṃ rasānaṃ, kathaṃjīviṃ jīvitamāhu seṭṭha”nti.

“What here is a person's best wealth? What, well-practiced, brings happiness? What, indeed, is the sweetest of flavors? Living in what way is called the best life?”

“Saddhīdha vittaṃ purissa seṭṭhaṃ, dhammo suciṇṇo sukhamāvahāti;

Saccaṃ have sādutaraṃ rasānaṃ, paññājīviṃ jīvitamāhu seṭṭha”nti.

“Here, faith is a person's best wealth; the well-practiced Dhamma brings happiness. Truth, indeed, is the sweetest of flavors; a life lived by wisdom, they say, is the best.”

“Kathaṃsu tarati oghaṃ, kathaṃsu tarati aṇṇavaṃ;

Kathaṃsu dukkhamacceti, kathaṃsu parisujjhatī”ti.

“How does one cross the flood? How does one cross the ocean? How does one overcome suffering? How does one become pure?”

“Saddhāya [M 1.0217] tarati oghaṃ, appamādena aṇṇavaṃ;

Vīriyena dukkhamacceti, paññāya parisujjhatī”ti.

“By faith one crosses the flood, by heedfulness the ocean; by energy one overcomes suffering, by wisdom one is purified.”

“Kathaṃsu labhate paññaṃ, kathaṃsu vindate dhanaṃ;

Kathaṃsu kittiṃ pappoti, kathaṃ mittāni ganthati;

Asmā lokā paraṃ lokaṃ, kathaṃ pecca na socatī”ti.

“How does one obtain wisdom? How does one find wealth? How does one attain renown? How does one win friends? Having passed from this world to the next, how does one not grieve?”

“Saddahāno arahataṃ, dhammaṃ nibbānapattiyā;

Sussūsaṃ [T 1.0316] sussūsā (sī. pī.) labhate paññaṃ, appamatto vicakkhaṇo.

“Having faith in the Dhamma of the Arahants for the attainment of Nibbāna, one who is eager to listen, heedful, and discerning, obtains wisdom.

“Patirūpakārī [V 1.0249] dhuravā, uṭṭhātā vindate dhanaṃ;

Saccena [P 1.0215] kittiṃ pappoti, dadaṃ mittāni ganthati;

Asmā lokā paraṃ lokaṃ, evaṃ pecca na socati.

“One who acts appropriately, is steadfast and energetic, finds wealth. By truth one attains renown; by giving one wins friends. Thus, having passed from this world to the next, one does not grieve.

“Yassete caturo dhammā, saddhassa gharamesino;

Saccaṃ dammo dhiti cāgo, sa ve pecca na socati.

“For the faithful householder who possesses these four qualities—truth, self-control, steadfastness, and generosity—he indeed does not grieve after passing away.

“Iṅgha aññepi pucchassu, puthū samaṇabrāhmaṇe;

Yadi saccā dammā cāgā, khantyā bhiyyodha vijjatī”ti.

“Go on, ask other various ascetics and brahmins, if anything superior to truth, self-control, generosity, and patience is found here.”

“Kathaṃ nu dāni puccheyyaṃ, puthū samaṇabrāhmaṇe;

Yohaṃ sohaṃ (sī.), svāhaṃ (ka.) ajja pajānāmi, yo attho samparāyiko.

“Why now should I ask the various ascetics and brahmins? For today I understand that which is for the welfare of the future life.

“Atthāya vata me buddho, vāsāyāḷavimāgamā māgato (pī. ka.);

Yohaṃ sohaṃ (sī.) ajja pajānāmi, yattha dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ.

“Indeed, for my benefit the Buddha came to Āḷavī to dwell; today I understand where a gift given bears great fruit.

“So ahaṃ vicarissāmi, gāmā gāmaṃ purā puraṃ;

Namassamāno sambuddhaṃ, dhammassa ca sudhammata”nti.

“So I shall wander from village to village, from town to town, paying homage to the Sambuddha and to the excellent nature of the Dhamma.”

Yakkhasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Yakkha Saṃyutta is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Indako sakka sūci ca, maṇibhaddo ca sānu ca;

Piyaṅkara punabbasu sudatto ca, dve sukkā cīraāḷavīti dvādasa.

Indaka, Sakka, Sūci, and Maṇibhadda, Sānu, Piyaṅkara, Punabbasu, and Sudatta, the two Sukkās, Cīra, and Āḷavī—thus there are twelve.

11. Sakkasaṃyuttaṃ

11. The Saᅃyutta on Sakka

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Suvīrasuttaṃ

1. The SuvĦra Sutta

247. Evaṃ [T 1.0317][V 1.0250][P 1.0216][M 1.0218] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

247. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, asurā deve abhiyaṃsu. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṃ devaputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘ete, tāta suvīra, asurā deve abhiyanti. Gaccha, tāta suvīra, asure paccuyyāhī’ti. ‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, suvīro devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā pamādaṃ āpādesi āharesi (katthaci) navaṅguttare sīhanādasuttepi. Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṃ devaputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘ete, tāta suvīra, asurā deve abhiyanti. Gaccha, tāta suvīra, asure paccuyyāhī’ti. ‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, suvīro devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā dutiyampi pamādaṃ āpādesi. Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṃ devaputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘ete, tāta suvīra, asurā deve abhiyanti. Gaccha, tāta suvīra, asure paccuyyāhī’ti[T 1.0318]. ‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, suvīro devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā tatiyampi pamādaṃ āpādesi. Atha [P 1.0217] kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṃ devaputtaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

“Formerly, bhikkhus, the asuras marched against the devas. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the devaputta Suvīra: ‘Dear Suvīra, these asuras are marching against the devas. Go, dear Suvīra, go forth to meet the asuras.’ ‘So be it, venerable sir,’ the devaputta Suvīra replied to Sakka, lord of the devas, and then became negligent. For a second time, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the devaputta Suvīra: ‘Dear Suvīra, these asuras are marching against the devas. Go, dear Suvīra, go forth to meet the asuras.’ ‘So be it, venerable sir,’ the devaputta Suvīra replied to Sakka, lord of the devas, and for a second time became negligent. For a third time, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the devaputta Suvīra: ‘Dear Suvīra, these asuras are marching against the devas. Go, dear Suvīra, go forth to meet the asuras.’ ‘So be it, venerable sir,’ the devaputta Suvīra replied to Sakka, lord of the devas, and for a third time became negligent. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, recited this verse to the devaputta Suvīra:

“Anuṭṭhahaṃ avāyāmaṃ, sukhaṃ yatrādhigacchati;

Suvīra tattha gacchāhi, mañca tattheva pāpayā”ti.

“‘Where one attains happiness without striving, without exerting oneself, go there, Suvīra, and make me arrive there as well.’”

“Alasvassa [V 1.0251] alasa’ssa (sī. pī.), alasvāyaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) anuṭṭhātā, na ca kiccāni kāraye;

Sabbakāmasamiddhassa, taṃ me sakka varaṃ disā”ti.

“‘For one who is lazy and inactive, who does not perform their duties, yet is fulfilled in all desires—Sakka, please point out that excellent place to me.’”

“Yatthālaso [M 1.0219] anuṭṭhātā, accantaṃ sukhamedhati;

Suvīra tattha gacchāhi, mañca tattheva pāpayā”ti.

“‘Where the lazy and inactive one certainly attains happiness, go there, Suvīra, and make me arrive there as well.’”

“Akammunā akammanā (sī. pī.) devaseṭṭha, sakka vindemu yaṃ sukhaṃ;

Asokaṃ anupāyāsaṃ, taṃ me sakka varaṃ disā”ti.

“‘O Sakka, chief of devas, that we might find happiness without action—a sorrowless, untroubled state—Sakka, please point out that excellent place to me.’”

“Sace atthi akammena, koci kvaci na jīvati;

Nibbānassa hi so maggo, suvīra tattha gacchāhi;

Mañca tattheva pāpayā”ti.

“‘If there is a state without action, no one anywhere lives. That indeed would be the path to Nibbāna. Go there, Suvīra, and make me arrive there as well.’”

“So hi nāma, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sakaṃ puññaphalaṃ upajīvamāno devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kārento uṭṭhānavīriyassa vaṇṇavādī bhavissati. Idha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, sobhetha, yaṃ tumhe evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā uṭṭhaheyyātha [T 1.0319] ghaṭeyyātha vāyameyyātha appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.

“Indeed, bhikkhus, that Sakka, lord of the devas, while living on the fruit of his own merit and exercising sovereignty and dominion over the Tāvatiṃsa devas, is one who speaks in praise of striving and energy. How much more fitting it is for you, bhikkhus, who have gone forth in such a well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline, that you should strive, endeavor, and exert yourselves for the attainment of the unattained, for the achievement of the unachieved, and for the realization of the unrealized.”

2. Susīmasuttaṃ

2. The Susīma Sutta

248. Sāvatthiyaṃ. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

248. At Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this:

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, asurā deve abhiyaṃsu. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṃ susimaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) devaputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘ete, tāta susīma, asurā deve abhiyanti. Gaccha, tāta susīma, asure paccuyyāhī’ti. ‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, susīmo devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā pamādaṃ āpādesi. Dutiyampi [P 1.0218] kho, bhikkhave, sakko [V 1.0252] devānamindo susīmaṃ devaputtaṃ āmantesi…pe… dutiyampi pamādaṃ āpādesi. Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṃ devaputtaṃ āmantesi…pe… tatiyampi pamādaṃ āpādesi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṃ devaputtaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

“Formerly, bhikkhus, the asuras marched against the devas. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the devaputta Susīma: ‘Dear Susīma, these asuras are marching against the devas. Go, dear Susīma, go forth to meet the asuras.’ ‘So be it, venerable sir,’ replied the devaputta Susīma to Sakka, lord of the devas, but he became negligent. A second time, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed him… and a second time he became negligent. A third time, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed him… and a third time he became negligent. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the devaputta Susīma with a verse:

“Anuṭṭhahaṃ [T 1.0320] avāyāmaṃ, sukhaṃ yatrādhigacchati;

Susīma tattha gacchāhi, mañca tattheva pāpayā”ti.

“‘Where one attains happiness without striving, without exerting oneself—go there, Susīma, and make me arrive there as well!’”

“Alasvassa [M 1.0220] anuṭṭhātā, na ca kiccāni kāraye;

Sabbakāmasamiddhassa, taṃ me sakka varaṃ disā”ti.

“‘For one who is lazy and inactive, who does not do what should be done, yet is fulfilled in all desires—Sakka, point out that excellent state to me!’”

“Yatthālaso anuṭṭhātā, accantaṃ sukhamedhati;

Susīma tattha gacchāhi, mañca tattheva pāpayā”ti.

“‘Where the lazy and inactive find utter happiness—go there, Susīma, and bring me there too!’”

“Akammunā devaseṭṭha, sakka vindemu yaṃ sukhaṃ;

Asokaṃ anupāyāsaṃ, taṃ me sakka varaṃ disā”ti.

“‘O Sakka, chief of devas, that we might find happiness without action, a sorrowless, untroubled state—Sakka, point out that excellent state to me!’”

“Sace atthi akammena, koci kvaci na jīvati;

Nibbānassa hi so maggo, susīma tattha gacchāhi;

Mañca tattheva pāpayā”ti.

“‘If there is, through inaction, anyone anywhere who lives—for that is the path to Nibbāna—Susīma, go there, and bring me there too!’”

“So hi nāma, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sakaṃ puññaphalaṃ upajīvamāno devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kārento uṭṭhānavīriyassa vaṇṇavādī bhavissati. Idha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, sobhetha, yaṃ tumhe evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā uṭṭhaheyyātha ghaṭeyyātha vāyameyyātha appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.

“Indeed, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, living by the fruit of his own merit while exercising sovereignty and dominion over the Tāvatiṃsa devas, is a speaker of praise for energy and exertion. How much more, then, bhikkhus, does it befit you, who have gone forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline, to rise up, strive, and exert yourselves for the attainment of the unattained, for the gaining of the ungained, for the realization of the unrealized.”

3. Dhajaggasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Crest of the Banner

249. Sāvatthiyaṃ[V 1.0253]. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti[T 1.0321]. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

249. At Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus.” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus responded to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

“Formerly, bhikkhus, a battle was arrayed between the devas and the asuras. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the Tāvatiṃsa devas:

‘Sace, mārisā, devānaṃ saṅgāmagatānaṃ uppajjeyya [P 1.0219] bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, mameva tasmiṃ samaye dhajaggaṃ ullokeyyātha. Mamañhi vo dhajaggaṃ ullokayataṃ yaṃ bhavissati bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, so pahīyissati’.

‘Sirs, if for you devas who have gone to the battlefield, fear or stupefaction or horripilation should arise, at that time you should look up at my banner crest. For when you look up at my banner crest, whatever fear, stupefaction, or horripilation there may be, it will be abandoned.’

‘No ce me dhajaggaṃ ullokeyyātha, atha pajāpatissa devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokeyyātha. Pajāpatissa hi vo devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokayataṃ yaṃ bhavissati bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, so pahīyissati’.

‘If you should not look up at my banner crest, then you should look up at the banner crest of Pajāpati, the deva-king. For when you look up at the banner crest of Pajāpati, the deva-king, whatever fear, stupefaction, or horripilation there may be, it will be abandoned.’

‘No [M 1.0221] ce pajāpatissa devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokeyyātha, atha varuṇassa devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokeyyātha. Varuṇassa hi vo devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokayataṃ yaṃ bhavissati bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, so pahīyissati’.

‘If you should not look up at the banner crest of Pajāpati, the deva-king, then you should look up at the banner crest of Varuṇa, the deva-king. For when you look up at the banner crest of Varuṇa, the deva-king, whatever fear, stupefaction, or horripilation there may be, it will be abandoned.’

‘No ce varuṇassa devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokeyyātha, atha īsānassa devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokeyyātha. Īsānassa hi vo devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokayataṃ yaṃ bhavissati bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, so pahīyissatī’”ti.

‘If you should not look up at the banner crest of Varuṇa, the deva-king, then you should look up at the banner crest of Īsāna, the deva-king. For when you look up at the banner crest of Īsāna, the deva-king, whatever fear, stupefaction, or horripilation there may be, it will be abandoned.’”

“Taṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkassa vā devānamindassa dhajaggaṃ ullokayataṃ, pajāpatissa vā devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokayataṃ, varuṇassa vā devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokayataṃ, īsānassa vā devarājassa dhajaggaṃ ullokayataṃ yaṃ [T 1.0322] bhavissati bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, so pahīyethāpi nopi pahīyetha no pahīyetha (ka.).

“However, bhikkhus, for those looking up at the banner crest of Sakka, lord of the devas, or of Pajāpati, the deva-king, or of Varuṇa, the deva-king, or of Īsāna, the deva-king—whatever fear, stupefaction, or horripilation they may have, it might be abandoned, or it might not be abandoned.”

“Taṃ [V 1.0254] kissa hetu? Sakko hi, bhikkhave, devānamindo avītarāgo avītadoso avītamoho bhīru chambhī utrāsī palāyīti.

“For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, is not free from lust, not free from hatred, and not free from delusion; he is fearful, prone to stupefaction, easily startled, and prone to flee.”

“Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, evaṃ vadāmi – ‘sace tumhākaṃ, bhikkhave, araññagatānaṃ vā rukkhamūlagatānaṃ vā suññāgāragatānaṃ vā uppajjeyya bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, mameva tasmiṃ samaye anussareyyātha – itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Mamañhi vo, bhikkhave, anussarataṃ yaṃ bhavissati bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, so pahīyissati.

“But I, bhikkhus, say this: ‘If for you, bhikkhus, having gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, fear or stupefaction or horripilation should arise, at that time you should recollect me alone: “Thus indeed is the Blessed One: an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, the Well-Farer, the Knower of the world, the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, the Teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.” For when you recollect me, bhikkhus, whatever fear, stupefaction, or horripilation you may have will be abandoned.’

“No [P 1.0220] ce maṃ anussareyyātha, atha dhammaṃ anussareyyātha – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Dhammañhi vo, bhikkhave, anussarataṃ yaṃ bhavissati bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, so pahīyissati.

‘If you should not recollect me, then you should recollect the Dhamma: “The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One, visible in this very life, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be experienced by the wise for themselves.” For when you recollect the Dhamma, bhikkhus, whatever fear, stupefaction, or horripilation you may have will be abandoned.’

“No ce dhammaṃ anussareyyātha, atha saṅghaṃ anussareyyātha – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho [M 1.0222] ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti. Saṅghañhi vo, bhikkhave, anussarataṃ [T 1.0323] yaṃ bhavissati bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā, so pahīyissati.

‘If you should not recollect the Dhamma, then you should recollect the Saṅgha: “The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the upright way; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the methodical way; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the proper way. That is, the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals—this Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.” For when you recollect the Saṅgha, bhikkhus, whatever fear, stupefaction, or horripilation you may have will be abandoned.’

“Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāgato hi, bhikkhave, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho abhīru acchambhī anutrāsī apalāyī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

“For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion; he is fearless, not prone to stupefaction, not easily startled, and does not flee.” This the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Well-Farer, the Teacher, said this further:

“Araññe rukkhamūle vā, suññāgāreva bhikkhavo;

Anussaretha anussareyyātha (ka.) padasiddhi pana cintetabbā sambuddhaṃ, bhayaṃ tumhāka no siyā.

“In the forest, or at the foot of a tree, or in an empty dwelling, bhikkhus, you should recollect the Perfectly Enlightened One; fear will not be yours.

“No [V 1.0255] ce buddhaṃ sareyyātha, lokajeṭṭhaṃ narāsabhaṃ;

Atha dhammaṃ sareyyātha, niyyānikaṃ sudesitaṃ.

“If you should not recollect the Buddha, chief of the world, bull among men, then you should recollect the Dhamma, leading out, well-taught.

“No ce dhammaṃ sareyyātha, niyyānikaṃ sudesitaṃ;

Atha saṅghaṃ sareyyātha, puññakkhettaṃ anuttaraṃ.

“If you should not recollect the Dhamma, leading out, well-taught, then you should recollect the Saṅgha, the unsurpassed field of merit.

“Evaṃ buddhaṃ sarantānaṃ, dhammaṃ saṅghañca bhikkhavo;

Bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā, lomahaṃso na hessatī”ti.

“Bhikkhus, for you who are recollecting the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha, fear or terror or horripilation will not arise.”

4. Vepacittisuttaṃ

4. The Vepacitti Sutta

250. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Bhūtapubbaṃ[P 1.0221], bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo asure āmantesi – ‘sace, mārisā, devānaṃ asurasaṅgāme samupabyūḷhe asurā [T 1.0324] jineyyuṃ devā parājineyyuṃ parājeyyuṃ (sī. pī.), yena naṃ sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi bandhitvā mama santike āneyyātha asurapura’nti. Sakkopi kho, bhikkhave, devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘sace, mārisā, devānaṃ asurasaṅgāme samupabyūḷhe devā jineyyuṃ asurā parājineyyuṃ, yena naṃ vepacittiṃ asurindaṃ kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi bandhitvā mama santike āneyyātha sudhammasabha’”nti. Tasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, saṅgāme devā jiniṃsu[M 1.0223], asurā parājiniṃsu parājiṃsu (sī. pī.). Atha kho, bhikkhave, devā tāvatiṃsā vepacittiṃ asurindaṃ kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi bandhitvā sakkassa devānamindassa santike ānesuṃ sudhammasabhaṃ. Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi baddho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ sudhammasabhaṃ pavisantañca nikkhamantañca asabbhāhi pharusāhi vācāhi akkosati paribhāsati. Atha kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

250. At Sāvatthī. “Once upon a time, monks, a battle was arrayed between the devas and the asuras.
