Then Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, addressed the asuras: ‘If, sirs, in the battle arrayed between the devas and the asuras, the asuras win and the devas are defeated, then bind Sakka, the lord of the devas, with bonds including the neck as the fifth, and bring him to my presence in the city of the asuras.’ And Sakka, the lord of the devas, also addressed the devas of Tāvatiṃsa: ‘If, sirs, in the battle arrayed between the devas and the asuras, the devas win and the asuras are defeated, then bind Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, with bonds including the neck as the fifth, and bring him to my presence in the Sudhammā assembly hall.’ In that battle, monks, the devas won and the asuras were defeated. Then the devas of Tāvatiṃsa bound Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, with bonds including the neck as the fifth, and brought him to the presence of Sakka, the lord of the devas, in the Sudhammā assembly hall. There, monks, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, bound with bonds including the neck as the fifth, reviled and abused Sakka, the lord of the devas, with rude and harsh words as he entered and left the Sudhammā assembly hall. Then, monks, Mātali the charioteer addressed Sakka, the lord of the devas, in verses:

“Bhayā nu maghavā sakka, dubbalyā no titikkhasi;

Suṇanto pharusaṃ vācaṃ, sammukhā vepacittino”ti.

‘Is it out of fear, Maghavā Sakka, or out of weakness that you forbear, when hearing the harsh speech of Vepacitti in your presence?’

“Nāhaṃ [V 1.0256] bhayā na dubbalyā, khamāmi vepacittino;

Kathañhi mādiso viññū, bālena paṭisaṃyuje”ti.

“Neither from fear nor from weakness do I forbear with Vepacitti. For how could a wise one such as I contend with a fool?”

“Bhiyyo bālā pabhijjeyyuṃ, no cassa paṭisedhako;

Tasmā bhusena daṇḍena, dhīro bālaṃ nisedhaye”ti.

“Fools would become even more quarrelsome if there were no one to restrain them. Therefore, the wise should restrain the fool with severe punishment.”

“Etadeva [T 1.0325] ahaṃ maññe, bālassa paṭisedhanaṃ;

Paraṃ saṅkupitaṃ ñatvā, yo sato upasammatī”ti.

“This I consider to be the fool's restraint: that one who, knowing the other is angered, mindfully becomes calm.”

“Etadeva titikkhāya, vajjaṃ passāmi vāsava;

Yadā naṃ maññati bālo, bhayā myāyaṃ titikkhati;

Ajjhāruhati dummedho, gova bhiyyo palāyina”nti.

“This very fault I see in forbearance, Vāsava: when a fool thinks, ‘It is from fear of me that this one forbears.’ The one of little wisdom then presses down on him all the more, like a herd of cattle on a fleeing cow.”

“Kāmaṃ [P 1.0222] maññatu vā mā vā, bhayā myāyaṃ titikkhati;

Sadatthaparamā atthā, khantyā bhiyyo na vijjati.

“Let him think as he wishes, or not, ‘It is from fear of me that this one forbears.’ One's own welfare is the highest good, and nothing is found to be better than patience.

“Yo have balavā santo, dubbalassa titikkhati;

Tamāhu paramaṃ khantiṃ, niccaṃ khamati dubbalo.

“Whoever, being strong, forbears with the weak—that they call the supreme patience. The weak, for their part, are always forbearing.

“Abalaṃ taṃ balaṃ āhu, yassa bālabalaṃ balaṃ;

Balassa dhammaguttassa, paṭivattā na vijjati.

“That strength which is the strength of a fool, they call no strength at all. For one who is strong and guarded by the Dhamma, no adversary is found.

“Tasseva tena pāpiyo, yo kuddhaṃ paṭikujjhati;

Kuddhaṃ appaṭikujjhanto, saṅgāmaṃ jeti dujjayaṃ.

“One who returns anger for anger is made the worse by that. By not returning anger for anger, one wins a battle hard to win.

“Ubhinnamatthaṃ [M 1.0224] carati, attano ca parassa ca;

Paraṃ saṅkupitaṃ ñatvā, yo sato upasammati.

“One works for the welfare of both—one's own and the other's—who, knowing the other is angered, mindfully becomes calm.

“Ubhinnaṃ [V 1.0257] tikicchantānaṃ, attano ca parassa ca;

Janā maññanti bāloti, ye dhammassa akovidā”ti.

“When one is healing both—oneself and the other—those who are unskilled in the Dhamma think one a fool.”

“So hi nāma, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sakaṃ puññaphalaṃ upajīvamāno devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kārento khantisoraccassa vaṇṇavādī bhavissati. Idha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, sobhetha yaṃ [T 1.0326] tumhe evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā khamā ca bhaveyyātha soratā cā”ti.

“Indeed, monks, Sakka, the lord of the devas—while living on the fruit of his own merit and exercising sovereignty and lordship over the devas of Tāvatiṃsa—is a speaker in praise of patience and gentleness. How much more fitting it is for you here, monks, who have gone forth in such a well-expounded Dhamma and Discipline, to be patient and gentle.”

5. Subhāsitajayasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Victory Through What Is Well-Spoken

251. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – ‘hotu, devānaminda, subhāsitena jayo’ti. ‘Hotu, vepacitti, subhāsitena jayo’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, devā ca asurā ca pārisajje ṭhapesuṃ – ‘ime no subhāsitadubbhāsitaṃ ājānissantī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacittiṃ asurindo sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – ‘bhaṇa, devānaminda, gātha’nti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacitti asurindaṃ etadavoca – ‘tumhe khvettha, vepacitti, pubbadevā. Bhaṇa, vepacitti, gātha’nti. Evaṃ [P 1.0223] vutte, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

251. At Sāvatthī. “Once upon a time, monks, a battle between the devas and the asuras was drawn up in array. Then, monks, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, said to Sakka, the lord of the devas: ‘Lord of the devas, let there be victory through what is well-spoken.’ ‘Vepacitti, let there be victory through what is well-spoken.’ Then, monks, the devas and the asuras appointed witnesses, thinking: ‘These will know for us what is well-spoken and ill-spoken.’ Then, monks, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, said to Sakka, the lord of the devas: ‘Recite a verse, lord of the devas.’ When this was said, monks, Sakka, the lord of the devas, said to Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras: ‘You, Vepacitti, are the elder devas here. You, Vepacitti, recite a verse first.’ When this was said, monks, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, recited this verse:

“Bhiyyo bālā pabhijjeyyuṃ, no cassa paṭisedhako;

Tasmā bhusena daṇḍena, dhīro bālaṃ nisedhaye”ti.

“Fools would become even more quarrelsome if there were no one to restrain them; therefore, the wise one should restrain the fool with a severe rod.”

“Bhāsitāya kho pana, bhikkhave, vepacittinā asurindena gāthāya asurā anumodiṃsu, devā tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – ‘bhaṇa, devānaminda, gātha’nti. Evaṃ [T 1.0327] vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

“When the verse was recited by Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, monks, the asuras rejoiced, but the devas became silent. Then, monks, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, said to Sakka, the lord of the devas: ‘Recite a verse, lord of the devas!’ When this was said, monks, Sakka, the lord of the devas, recited this verse:

“Etadeva [V 1.0258] ahaṃ maññe, bālassa paṭisedhanaṃ;

Paraṃ saṅkupitaṃ ñatvā, yo sato upasammatī”ti.

“This very thing I consider to be the restraint of the fool: knowing that another is angered, one who is mindful becomes calm.”

“Bhāsitāya [M 1.0225] kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkena devānamindena gāthāya, devā anumodiṃsu, asurā tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacittiṃ asurindaṃ etadavoca – ‘bhaṇa, vepacitti, gātha’nti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

“When the verse was recited by Sakka, the lord of the devas, monks, the devas rejoiced, but the asuras became silent. Then, monks, Sakka, the lord of the devas, said to Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras: ‘Recite a verse, Vepacitti.’ When this was said, monks, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, recited this verse:

“Etadeva titikkhāya, vajjaṃ passāmi vāsava;

Yadā naṃ maññati bālo, bhayā myāyaṃ titikkhati;

Ajjhāruhati dummedho, gova bhiyyo palāyina”nti.

“Vāsava, this is the very fault I see in forbearance: when a fool thinks, ‘This one forbears with me out of fear,’ the witless one overpowers him all the more, like a bull does one who flees.”

“Bhāsitāya kho pana, bhikkhave, vepacittinā asurindena gāthāya asurā anumodiṃsu, devā tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – ‘bhaṇa, devānaminda, gātha’nti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

“Indeed, monks, when the verse was recited by Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, the asuras rejoiced, but the devas became silent. Then, monks, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, said to Sakka, the lord of the devas: ‘Recite a verse, lord of the devas.’ When this was said, monks, Sakka, the lord of the devas, recited these verses:

“Kāmaṃ maññatu vā mā vā, bhayā myāyaṃ titikkhati;

Sadatthaparamā atthā, khantyā bhiyyo na vijjati.

“Let him think as he wishes or not, ‘This one forbears with me out of fear.’ One’s own welfare is the highest good; there is nothing greater than patience.

“Yo have balavā santo, dubbalassa titikkhati;

Tamāhu paramaṃ khantiṃ, niccaṃ khamati dubbalo.

“Indeed, one who, being strong, forbears with the weak—that the good call the highest patience. The weak one always forbears.

“Abalaṃ [T 1.0328] taṃ balaṃ āhu, yassa bālabalaṃ balaṃ;

Balassa dhammaguttassa, paṭivattā na vijjati.

“That strength they call weakness, the strength that is the fool's strength. For one with strength who is guarded by the Dhamma, no adversary is found.

“Tasseva tena pāpiyo, yo kuddhaṃ paṭikujjhati;

Kuddhaṃ appaṭikujjhanto, saṅgāmaṃ jeti dujjayaṃ.

“One who gets angry back at one who is angry is thereby the worse of the two. By not getting angry back at one who is angry, one wins a battle hard to win.

“Ubhinnamatthaṃ [V 1.0259] carati, attano ca parassa ca;

Paraṃ saṅkupitaṃ ñatvā, yo sato upasammati.

“He practices for the welfare of both, his own and another’s, who, knowing the other is angered, mindfully becomes calm.

“Ubhinnaṃ [P 1.0224] tikicchantānaṃ, attano ca parassa ca;

Janā maññanti bāloti, ye dhammassa akovidā”ti.

“When one is healing both oneself and the other, those who are unskilled in the Dhamma consider one a fool.”

“Bhāsitāsu kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkena devānamindena gāthāsu, devā anumodiṃsu, asurā tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, devānañca asurānañca pārisajjā etadavocuṃ – ‘bhāsitā kho vepacittinā asurindena gāthāyo. Tā ca kho sadaṇḍāvacarā sasatthāvacarā, iti bhaṇḍanaṃ iti [M 1.0226] viggaho iti kalaho. Bhāsitā kho bhāsitā kho pana (sī.) sakkena devānamindena gāthāyo. Tā ca kho adaṇḍāvacarā asatthāvacarā, iti abhaṇḍanaṃ iti aviggaho iti akalaho. Sakkassa devānamindassa subhāsitena jayo’ti. Iti kho, bhikkhave sakkassa devānamindassa subhāsitena jayo ahosī”ti.

“Indeed, monks, when these verses were recited by Sakka, the lord of the devas, the devas rejoiced, but the asuras became silent. Then, monks, the assembly members for both the devas and the asuras said this: ‘The verses recited by Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, involve the rod and involve the sword; thus there is contention, conflict, and quarrel. The verses recited by Sakka, the lord of the devas, do not involve the rod and do not involve the sword; thus there is no contention, no conflict, and no quarrel. Victory belongs to Sakka, the lord of the devas, through what is well-spoken.’ Thus, monks, the victory of Sakka, the lord of the devas, was through what is well-spoken.”

6. Kulāvakasuttaṃ

6. The Sutta on Nests

252. Sāvatthiyaṃ. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi. Tasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, saṅgāme asurā jiniṃsu[T 1.0329], devā parājiniṃsu. Parājitā ca kho, bhikkhave, devā apāyaṃsveva uttarenamukhā, abhiyaṃsveva ne asurā. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo mātali saṅgāhakaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

252. At Sāvatthī. “Formerly, monks, a battle was arrayed between the devas and the asuras. In that battle, monks, the asuras won and the devas were defeated. Defeated, monks, the devas fled northwards, and the asuras pursued them. Then, monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed Mātali the charioteer in verse:

“Kulāvakā mātali simbalismiṃ,

Īsāmukhena parivajjayassu;

Kāmaṃ cajāma asuresu pāṇaṃ,

Māyime dijā vikulāvakā vikulāvā (syā. kaṃ. ka.) ahesu”nti.

“‘O Mātali, there are nests in the silk-cotton tree; avoid it with the chariot-pole. We would rather give up our lives to the asuras; let not these birds be without their nests.’”

“‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā sahassayuttaṃ ājaññarathaṃ paccudāvattesi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, asurānaṃ etadahosi [V 1.0260] – ‘paccudāvatto kho dāni sakkassa devānamindassa sahassayutto ājaññaratho[P 1.0225]. Dutiyampi kho devā asurehi saṅgāmessantīti bhītā asurapurameva pāvisiṃsu. Iti kho, bhikkhave, sakkassa devānamindassa dhammena jayo ahosī’”ti.

“‘So be it, venerable sir.’ Thus, monks, Mātali the charioteer, having assented to Sakka, lord of the devas, turned back the thoroughbred chariot yoked with a thousand. Then, monks, this thought occurred to the asuras: ‘Now the thoroughbred chariot of Sakka, lord of the devas, yoked with a thousand, has turned back. For a second time, the devas will do battle with the asuras.’ Frightened, they entered the very city of the asuras. In this way, monks, the victory of Sakka, lord of the devas, was by righteousness.”

7. Nadubbhiyasuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on Not Harming

253. Sāvatthiyaṃ. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sakkassa devānamindassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘yopi me assa supaccatthiko tassapāhaṃ na dubbheyya’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkassa devānamindassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya [T 1.0330] yena sakko devānamindo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā [M 1.0227] kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacittiṃ asurindaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna vepacittiṃ asurindaṃ etadavoca – ‘tiṭṭha, vepacitti, gahitosī’”ti.

253. At Sāvatthī. “Formerly, monks, while Sakka, lord of the devas, was in a secluded place and dwelling in solitude, this reflection arose in his mind: ‘Even towards one who might be my greatest adversary, I should not harbor ill will.’ Then, monks, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, knowing with his mind that reflection in the mind of Sakka, lord of the devas, approached him. Monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, saw Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, coming from afar. Having seen him, he said this to Vepacitti, lord of the asuras: ‘Stop, Vepacitti! You are seized!’”

“Yadeva te, mārisa, pubbe cittaṃ, tadeva tvaṃ mā pajahāsī”ti tadeva tvaṃ mārisa pahāsīti (sī. syā. kaṃ.).

“Sir, that very thought you had just now—do not abandon it.”

“Sapassu ca me, vepacitti, adubbhāyā”ti adrubbhāya (ka.).

“Swear an oath to me, Vepacitti, that you will not harm me.”

“Yaṃ musā bhaṇato pāpaṃ, yaṃ pāpaṃ ariyūpavādino;

Mittadduno ca yaṃ pāpaṃ, yaṃ pāpaṃ akataññuno;

Tameva pāpaṃ phusatu phusati (sī. pī.), yo te dubbhe sujampatī”ti.

“Whatever evil befalls one who speaks falsely, whatever evil befalls a slanderer of noble ones, whatever evil befalls a betrayer of friends, and whatever evil befalls an ungrateful one—may that very same evil befall whoever would harm you, O husband of Sujā.”

8. Verocanaasurindasuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on Verocana, Lord of the Asuras

254. Sāvatthiyaṃ jetavane. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno. Atha kho sakko ca devānamindo verocano ca asurindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṃ dvārabāhaṃ nissāya aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha kho verocano asurindo bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

254. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove. At that time the Blessed One was abiding for the day in seclusion. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, and Verocana, lord of the asuras, approached the Blessed One; having approached, they stood each leaning against a doorpost. Then Verocana, lord of the asuras, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Vāyametheva [V 1.0261] puriso, yāva atthassa nipphadā;

Nipphannasobhano sobhino (sī.), sobhaṇo (pī. ka.) attho atthā (sī.), verocanavaco ida”nti.

“‘A person should indeed strive until the aim is accomplished. The accomplished aim is lovely; this is Verocana’s saying.’”

“Vāyametheva [P 1.0226] puriso, yāva atthassa nipphadā;

Nipphannasobhano attho nipphannasobhino atthā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), khantyā bhiyyo na vijjatī”ti.

“‘A person should indeed strive until the aim is accomplished. The accomplished aim is lovely, but there is nothing higher than patience. This is Sakka’s saying.’”

“Sabbe [T 1.0331] sattā atthajātā, tattha tattha yathārahaṃ;

Saṃyogaparamā tveva, sambhogā sabbapāṇinaṃ;

Nipphannasobhano attho, verocanavaco ida”nti.

“‘All beings are born for a purpose, each in their respective place according to what is fitting; yet indeed, for all living beings, enjoyments are supreme through association. The accomplished aim is lovely; this is Verocana’s saying.’”

“Sabbe sattā atthajātā, tattha tattha yathārahaṃ;

Saṃyogaparamā tveva, sambhogā sabbapāṇinaṃ;

Nipphannasobhano attho, khantyā bhiyyo na vijjatī”ti.

“‘All beings are born for a purpose, each in their respective place according to what is fitting; yet indeed, for all living beings, enjoyments are supreme through association. The accomplished aim is lovely, but there is nothing higher than patience. This is Sakka’s saying.’”

9. Araññāyatanaisisuttaṃ

9. The Sutta on the Seers of the Wilderness Abode

255. Sāvatthiyaṃ[M 1.0228]. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sambahulā isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu sammanti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko ca devānamindo vepacitti ca asurindo yena te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo paṭaliyo aṭaliyo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), āṭaliyo (ka.) ma. ni. 2.410 upāhanā ārohitvā khaggaṃ olaggetvā chattena dhāriyamānena aggadvārena assamaṃ pavisitvā te isayo sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme apabyāmato karitvā atikkami. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo paṭaliyo upāhanā orohitvā khaggaṃ aññesaṃ datvā chattaṃ apanāmetvā dvāreneva assamaṃ pavisitvā te isayo sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme anuvātaṃ pañjaliko namassamāno aṭṭhāsi”. Atha kho, bhikkhave, te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsiṃsu –

255. At Sāvatthī. “Formerly, bhikkhus, many seers—virtuous and of good character—were dwelling in leaf huts in a wilderness abode. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, and Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, approached those virtuous seers of good character. Then, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, lord of the asuras, putting on multi-layered sandals, slinging on his sword, and with a parasol being held over him, entered the hermitage through the main gate and passed by, treating those virtuous seers of good character disrespectfully. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, took off his multi-layered sandals, gave his sword to another, lowered his parasol, and entering the hermitage through the doorway, he stood downwind, paying homage with reverently joined hands to those virtuous seers of good character.” Then, bhikkhus, those virtuous seers of good character addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, with a verse:

“Gandho [T 1.0332] isīnaṃ ciradikkhitānaṃ,

Kāyā cuto gacchati mālutena;

Ito [V 1.0262] paṭikkamma sahassanetta,

Gandho isīnaṃ asuci devarājā”ti.

‘The scent of the seers who have long undertaken vows, departing from their bodies, is carried by the wind. Go away from here, O Thousand-eyed One; the scent of the seers is impure, O King of Devas.’

“Gandho isīnaṃ ciradikkhitānaṃ,

Kāyā cuto gacchatu gacchati (sī. syā. kaṃ.) mālutena,

Sucitrapupphaṃ sirasmiṃva mālaṃ;

Gandhaṃ [P 1.0227] etaṃ paṭikaṅkhāma bhante,

Na hettha devā paṭikūlasaññino”ti.

‘Let the scent of the seers who have long undertaken vows, departing from their bodies, be carried by the wind. We desire this scent, venerable sirs, as one desires a garland of exquisite flowers for the head. For the devas hold no aversion to it.’

10. Samuddakasuttaṃ

10. The Seashore Discourse

256. Sāvatthiyaṃ. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sambahulā isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā samuddatīre paṇṇakuṭīsu sammanti. Tena kho pana samayena devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, tesaṃ isīnaṃ sīlavantānaṃ kalyāṇadhammānaṃ etadahosi – ‘dhammikā kho devā, adhammikā asurā. Siyāpi no asurato bhayaṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sambaraṃ asurindaṃ upasaṅkamitvā [M 1.0229] abhayadakkhiṇaṃ yāceyyāmā’”ti. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā – seyyathāpi [T 1.0333] nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – samuddatīre paṇṇakuṭīsu antarahitā sambarassa asurindassa sammukhe pāturahesuṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā sambaraṃ asurindaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsiṃsu –

256. At Sāvatthī. “Formerly, bhikkhus, many seers—virtuous and of good character—were dwelling peacefully in leaf huts on the seashore. At that time, a battle between the devas and the asuras was fully arrayed. Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to those virtuous seers of good character: ‘Indeed, the devas are righteous, the asuras are unrighteous. There might be danger for us from the asuras. What if we were to approach Sambara, the lord of the asuras, and ask for the gift of safety?’ Then, bhikkhus, those virtuous seers of good character—just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm or bend his outstretched arm—vanished from their leaf huts on the seashore and appeared before Sambara, the lord of the asuras. Then, bhikkhus, those virtuous seers of good character addressed Sambara, the lord of the asuras, with a verse:”

“Isayo sambaraṃ pattā, yācanti abhayadakkhiṇaṃ;

Kāmaṃkaro hi te dātuṃ, bhayassa abhayassa vā”ti.

‘The seers, having reached Sambara, ask for the gift of safety; for you are able to give as you wish, either fear or safety.’

“Isīnaṃ abhayaṃ natthi, duṭṭhānaṃ sakkasevinaṃ;

Abhayaṃ yācamānānaṃ, bhayameva dadāmi vo”ti.

‘For hostile seers who serve Sakka, there is no safety. To you who ask for safety, I give only fear.’

“Abhayaṃ [V 1.0263] yācamānānaṃ, bhayameva dadāsi no;

Paṭiggaṇhāma te etaṃ, akkhayaṃ hotu te bhayaṃ.

‘To us who ask for safety, you give only fear. We accept this from you; may your fear be inexhaustible.

“Yādisaṃ vapate bījaṃ, tādisaṃ harate phalaṃ;

Kalyāṇakārī kalyāṇaṃ, pāpakārī ca pāpakaṃ;

Pavuttaṃ tāta te bījaṃ, phalaṃ paccanubhossasī”ti.

‘Whatever kind of seed is sown, that is the kind of fruit one reaps. A doer of good experiences good, and a doer of evil, evil. The seed has been sown by you, dear sir; you will experience the fruit.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā sambaraṃ asurindaṃ abhisapitvā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – sambarassa asurindassa sammukhe antarahitā samuddatīre paṇṇakuṭīsu pāturahesuṃ. Atha [T 1.0334][P 1.0228] kho, bhikkhave, sambaro asurindo tehi isīhi sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehi abhisapito rattiyā sudaṃ tikkhattuṃ ubbijjī”ti.

“Then, bhikkhus, those virtuous seers of good character, having cursed Sambara, the lord of the asuras—just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm or bend his outstretched arm—vanished from the presence of Sambara and reappeared in their leaf huts on the seashore. Then, bhikkhus, Sambara, the lord of the asuras, having been cursed by those virtuous seers of good character, was startled three times during the night.”

Paṭhamo vaggo.

The First Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

This is the summary:

Suvīraṃ susīmañceva, dhajaggaṃ vepacittino;

Subhāsitaṃ jayañceva, kulāvakaṃ nadubbhiyaṃ;

Verocana asurindo, isayo araññakañceva;

Isayo ca samuddakāti.

Suvīra and Susīma, Dhajagga, Vepacitti; Subhāsitajaya, Kulāvaka, Nadubbhiya; Verocana Asurinda, and the Forest Seers; and the Seashore Seers.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter.

1. Vatapadasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Items of Observance

257. Sāvatthiyaṃ[T 1.0335][M 1.0230]. “Sakkassa, bhikkhave, devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa satta vatapadāni [V 1.0264] vattapadāni (ka.) samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṃ, yesaṃ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṃ ajjhagā. Katamāni satta vatapadāni? Yāvajīvaṃ mātāpettibharo assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ kule jeṭṭhāpacāyī assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ saṇhavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ apisuṇavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṃ ajjhāvaseyyaṃ muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato, yāvajīvaṃ saccavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ akkodhano assaṃ – sacepi me kodho uppajjeyya, khippameva naṃ paṭivineyya”nti. “Sakkassa, bhikkhave, devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa imāni satta vatapadāni samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṃ, yesaṃ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṃ ajjhagā”ti.

257. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, for Sakka, lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, seven items of observance were completely undertaken. It was because of having undertaken these that Sakka attained the state of being Sakka. What were the seven items of observance? ‘For my whole life, may I support my parents. For my whole life, may I be respectful to the elders in my family. For my whole life, may I be gentle in speech. For my whole life, may I be without divisive speech. For my whole life, may I dwell at home with a mind free from the stain of stinginess, being open-handed in generosity, with hands ready to give, delighting in relinquishment, worthy of being asked, delighting in giving and sharing. For my whole life, may I be truthful in speech. For my whole life, may I be without anger—and if anger should arise in me, may I quickly dispel it.’ Bhikkhus, for Sakka, lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, these seven items of observance were completely undertaken. It was because of having undertaken these that Sakka attained the state of being Sakka.”

“Mātāpettibharaṃ [T 1.0336] jantuṃ, kule jeṭṭhāpacāyinaṃ;

Saṇhaṃ sakhilasambhāsaṃ, pesuṇeyyappahāyinaṃ.

“A person who supports his mother and father, who is respectful to the elders in the family, who is gentle and friendly in speech, and who has abandoned divisive speech.

“Maccheravinaye yuttaṃ, saccaṃ kodhābhibhuṃ naraṃ;

Taṃ ve devā tāvatiṃsā, āhu sappuriso itī”ti.

“That person who is engaged in subduing stinginess, is truthful, and overcomes anger—him, indeed, the Tāvatiṃsa devas call a good person.”

2. Sakkanāmasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Names of Sakka

258. Sāvatthiyaṃ [P 1.0229] jetavane. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū etadavoca – “sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno magho nāma māṇavo ahosi, tasmā maghavāti vuccati.

258. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, was a young man named Magha; therefore, he is called Maghavā.

“Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno pure pure pure (sī. pī.) dānaṃ adāsi, tasmā purindadoti vuccati.

“Bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, gave gifts first; therefore, he is called Purindada.”

“Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno sakkaccaṃ dānaṃ adāsi, tasmā sakkoti vuccati.

“Bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, gave gifts respectfully; therefore, he is called Sakka.

“Sakko[V 1.0265][M 1.0231], bhikkhave, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno āvasathaṃ adāsi, tasmā vāsavoti vuccati.

“Bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, gave lodging; therefore, he is called Vāsava.

“Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo sahassampi atthānaṃ muhuttena cinteti, tasmā sahassakkhoti vuccati.

“Bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, thinks of a thousand matters in a moment; therefore, he is called Sahassakkha.

“Sakkassa, bhikkhave, devānamindassa sujā nāma asurakaññā pajāpati, tasmā sujampatīti vuccati.

“Bhikkhus, the wife of Sakka, lord of the devas, is the asura-maiden named Sujā; therefore, he is called Sujampati.

“Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti, tasmā devānamindoti vuccati.

“Bhikkhus, Sakka, lord of the devas, exercises sovereignty and rulership as king over the Tāvatiṃsa devas; therefore, he is called Devānaminda (Lord of the Devas).

“Sakkassa[T 1.0337], bhikkhave devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa satta vatapadāni samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṃ, yesaṃ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṃ ajjhagā. Katamāni satta vatapadāni? Yāvajīvaṃ mātāpettibharo assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ kule jeṭṭhāpacāyī assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ saṇhavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ apisuṇavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṃ ajjhāvaseyyaṃ muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato, yāvajīvaṃ saccavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ akkodhano assaṃ – sacepi me kodho uppajjeyya, khippameva naṃ paṭivineyya”nti. “Sakkassa, bhikkhave, devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa imāni satta vatapadāni samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṃ, yesaṃ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṃ ajjhagā”ti.

“Bhikkhus, for Sakka, lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, seven items of observance were completely undertaken. It was because of having undertaken these that Sakka attained the state of being Sakka. What were the seven items of observance? ‘For my whole life, may I support my parents. For my whole life, may I be respectful to the elders in my family. For my whole life, may I be gentle in speech. For my whole life, may I be without slanderous speech. For my whole life, may I dwell at home with a mind free from the stain of stinginess, being open-handed in generosity, with hands ready to give, delighting in relinquishment, worthy of being asked, delighting in giving and sharing. For my whole life, may I be truthful in speech. For my whole life, may I be without anger—and if anger should arise in me, may I quickly dispel it.’ Bhikkhus, for Sakka, lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, these seven items of observance were completely undertaken. It was because of having undertaken these that Sakka attained the state of being Sakka.”

“Mātāpettibharaṃ [P 1.0230] jantuṃ, kule jeṭṭhāpacāyinaṃ;

Saṇhaṃ sakhilasambhāsaṃ, pesuṇeyyappahāyinaṃ.

“A being who supports his mother and father, who is respectful to the elders in the family, who is gentle and courteous in speech, and who has abandoned slanderous speech;

“Maccheravinaye yuttaṃ, saccaṃ kodhābhibhuṃ naraṃ;

Taṃ ve devā tāvatiṃsā, āhu sappuriso itī”ti.

one who is engaged in subduing stinginess, is truthful, and overcomes anger—that person, indeed, the Tāvatiṃsa devas call a good person.”

3. Mahālisuttaṃ

3. The Mahāli Sutta

259. Evaṃ [V 1.0266] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Atha kho mahāli licchavī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [T 1.0338] nisinno kho mahāli licchavī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

259. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof. Then Mahāli the Licchavi approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, Mahāli the Licchavi said this to the Blessed One:

“Diṭṭho kho[M 1.0232], bhante, bhagavatā sakko devānamindo”ti?

“Venerable sir, has the Blessed One seen Sakka, the lord of the devas?”

“Diṭṭho kho me, mahāli, sakko devānamindo”ti.

“I have indeed seen, Mahāli, Sakka, the lord of the devas.”

“So hi nūna, bhante, sakkapatirūpako bhavissati. Duddaso hi, bhante, sakko devānamindo”ti.

“Surely, venerable sir, that must have been a counterfeit of Sakka. For Sakka, the lord of the devas, is difficult to see, venerable sir.”

“Sakkañca khvāhaṃ, mahāli, pajānāmi sakkakaraṇe ca dhamme, yesaṃ dhammānaṃ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṃ ajjhagā, tañca pajānāmi.

“Mahāli, I know Sakka, and I know the qualities that make one a Sakka. And I know those qualities by the undertaking of which Sakka attained the state of being Sakka.

“Sakko, mahāli, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno magho nāma māṇavo ahosi, tasmā maghavāti vuccati.

“Mahāli, Sakka, the lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, was a young man named Magha; therefore he is called Maghavā.

“Sakko, mahāli, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno sakkaccaṃ dānaṃ adāsi, tasmā sakkoti vuccati.

“Mahāli, Sakka, the lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, gave gifts respectfully; therefore he is called Sakka.

“Sakko, mahāli, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno pure dānaṃ adāsi, tasmā purindadoti vuccati.

“Mahāli, Sakka, the lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, gave gifts first; therefore he is called Purindada.

“Sakko, mahāli, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno āvasathaṃ adāsi, tasmā vāsavoti vuccati.

“Mahāli, Sakka, the lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, gave lodging; therefore he is called Vāsava.

“Sakko, mahāli, devānamindo sahassampi atthānaṃ muhuttena cinteti, tasmā sahassakkhoti vuccati.

“Mahāli, Sakka, the lord of the devas, thinks of a thousand matters in a moment; therefore he is called Sahassakkha.

“Sakkassa[V 1.0267], mahāli, devānamindassa sujā nāma asurakaññā pajāpati, tasmā sujampatīti vuccati.

“Mahāli, the wife of Sakka, the lord of the devas, is the asura-maiden named Sujā; therefore he is called Sujampati.

“Sakko, mahāli, devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ issariyādhipaccaṃ [P 1.0231] rajjaṃ kāreti, tasmā devānamindoti vuccati.

“Mahāli, Sakka, the lord of the devas, exercises lordship, sovereignty, and kingship over the devas of Tāvatiṃsa; therefore he is called the lord of the devas.

“Sakkassa, mahāli, devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa satta [T 1.0339] vatapadāni samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṃ, yesaṃ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṃ ajjhagā. Katamāni satta vatapadāni? Yāvajīvaṃ mātāpettibharo assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ kule jeṭṭhāpacāyī assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ saṇhavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ apisuṇavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṃ ajjhāvaseyyaṃ muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato, yāvajīvaṃ saccavāco assaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ akkodhano assaṃ – sacepi me kodho uppajeyya, khippameva naṃ paṭivineyya”nti. “Sakkassa, mahāli, devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa imāni [M 1.0233] satta vatapadāni samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṃ, yesaṃ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṃ ajjhagā”ti.

“Mahāli, when Sakka, the lord of the devas, was formerly a human being, there were seven vow-practices undertaken and fulfilled by him, by the undertaking of which Sakka attained the state of being Sakka. What were the seven vow-practices? ‘For as long as I live, may I support my parents. For as long as I live, may I revere the elders in my family. For as long as I live, may I be of gentle speech. For as long as I live, may I be of non-slanderous speech. For as long as I live, may I dwell at home with a mind free from the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, delighting in relinquishment, amenable to requests, delighting in giving and sharing. For as long as I live, may I be of truthful speech. For as long as I live, may I be without anger—and if anger should arise in me, may I quickly dispel it.’ Mahāli, for Sakka, the lord of the devas, when he was formerly a human being, these seven vow-practices were undertaken and fulfilled, by the undertaking of which Sakka attained the state of being Sakka.”

“Mātāpettibharaṃ jantuṃ, kule jeṭṭhāpacāyinaṃ;

Saṇhaṃ sakhilasambhāsaṃ, pesuṇeyyappahāyinaṃ.

“A person who supports his mother and father, who reveres the elders in his family, who is gentle and courteous in speech, and who has abandoned slanderous talk;

“Maccheravinaye yuttaṃ, saccaṃ kodhābhibhuṃ naraṃ;

Taṃ ve devā tāvatiṃsā, āhu sappuriso itī”ti.

who is engaged in subduing stinginess, is truthful, and overcomes anger—that person, the devas of Tāvatiṃsa truly call a good person.”

4. Daliddasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Impoverished

260. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

260. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Place. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks!” “Venerable sir!” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, aññataro puriso imasmiṃyeva [T 1.0340] rājagahe manussadaliddo manussadaḷiddo (sī. syā. kaṃ.) ahosi manussakapaṇo [V 1.0268] manussavarāko. So tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye saddhaṃ samādiyi, sīlaṃ samādiyi, sutaṃ samādiyi, cāgaṃ samādiyi, paññaṃ samādiyi. So tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye saddhaṃ samādiyitvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā sutaṃ samādiyitvā cāgaṃ samādiyitvā paññaṃ samādiyitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ [P 1.0232] saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajji devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ. So aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, devā tāvatiṃsā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – ‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho! Ayañhi devaputto pubbe manussabhūto samāno manussadaliddo ahosi manussakapaṇo manussavarāko; so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapanno devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ. So aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā cā’”ti.

“Once upon a time, monks, a certain man in this very Rājagaha was a human pauper, a human wretch, a lowly human. He undertook faith in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, he undertook virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom. Having undertaken faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he was reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, in companionship with the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. There he outshone the other devas in beauty and glory. Then, monks, the devas of Tāvatiṃsa grumbled, complained, and disparaged: ‘It is astonishing, friends, it is amazing! This deva, formerly a human being, was a human pauper, a human wretch, a lowly human; yet on the dissolution of the body, after death, he has been reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, in companionship with the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. He outshines the other devas in beauty and glory!’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘mā kho tumhe, mārisā, etassa devaputtassa ujjhāyittha. Eso kho, mārisā, devaputto pubbe manussabhūto samāno tathāgatappavedite [M 1.0234] dhammavinaye saddhaṃ samādiyi, sīlaṃ samādiyi, sutaṃ samādiyi, cāgaṃ samādiyi, paññaṃ samādiyi. So tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye saddhaṃ samādiyitvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā sutaṃ samādiyitvā cāgaṃ samādiyitvā paññaṃ samādiyitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapanno devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ[T 1.0341]. So aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā cā’”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse anunayamāno tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

“Then, monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the devas of Tāvatiṃsa: ‘Do not, friends, criticize this deva. This deva, friends, formerly a human being, undertook faith in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata; he undertook virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom. Having undertaken faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he was reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, in companionship with the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. He outshines the other devas in beauty and glory.’ Then, monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, conciliating the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, on that occasion recited these verses:

“Yassa saddhā tathāgate, acalā suppatiṭṭhitā;

Sīlañca yassa kalyāṇaṃ, ariyakantaṃ pasaṃsitaṃ.

“One whose faith in the Tathāgata is unshakeable, well-established; and whose virtue is excellent, beloved of and praised by the noble ones;

“Saṅghe pasādo yassatthi, ujubhūtañca dassanaṃ;

Adaliddoti taṃ āhu, amoghaṃ tassa jīvitaṃ.

“And who has confidence in the Saṅgha, and whose view is upright— him they call not poor; his life is not in vain.”

“Tasmā saddhañca sīlañca, pasādaṃ dhammadassanaṃ;

Anuyuñjetha medhāvī, saraṃ buddhāna sāsana”nti.

“Therefore, the wise should apply themselves to faith, virtue, confidence, and vision of the Dhamma, remembering the teaching of the Buddhas.”

5. Rāmaṇeyyakasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Delightful Place

261. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0269] jetavane. Atha kho sakko devānamindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, bhante, bhūmirāmaṇeyyaka”nti?

261. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Sakka, lord of the devas, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what, indeed, is a delightful place?”

“Ārāmacetyā [P 1.0233] vanacetyā, pokkharañño sunimmitā;

Manussarāmaṇeyyassa, kalaṃ nāgghanti soḷasiṃ.

“Parks with their shrines, woods with their shrines, and well-constructed lotus ponds are not worth a sixteenth part of that which is delightful to humans.

“Gāme vā yadi vāraññe, ninne vā yadi vā thale;

Yattha arahanto viharanti, taṃ bhūmirāmaṇeyyaka”nti.

“Whether in a village or in the forest, in a low-lying place or on high ground—wherever Arahants dwell, that place is delightful.”

6. Yajamānasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Sacrificers

262. Ekaṃ [T 1.0342] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Atha kho sakko devānamindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ [M 1.0235] abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

262. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on the Vulture Peak mountain. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Yajamānānaṃ manussānaṃ, puññapekkhāna pāṇinaṃ;

Karotaṃ opadhikaṃ puññaṃ, kattha dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti.

“For sacrificing humans, for beings who desire merit, performing merit that has its basis in the aggregates, where is a gift of great fruit?”

“Cattāro ca paṭipannā, cattāro ca phale ṭhitā;

Esa saṅgho ujubhūto, paññāsīlasamāhito.

“Four are practicing the path, and four are established in the fruit; this is the Saṅgha, upright, endowed with wisdom, virtue, and concentration.

“Yajamānānaṃ manussānaṃ, puññapekkhāna pāṇinaṃ;

Karotaṃ opadhikaṃ puññaṃ, saṅghe dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti.

“For sacrificing humans, for beings who desire merit, performing merit that has its basis in the aggregates, a gift to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.”

7. Buddhavandanāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Veneration of the Buddha

263. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0270] jetavane. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno. Atha kho sakko ca devānamindo brahmā ca sahampati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṃ dvārabāhaṃ nissāya aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha kho sakko devānamindo bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

263. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove. Now at that time, the Blessed One had gone for his day's abiding and was in seclusion. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, and Brahmā Sahampati approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they stood, each leaning against a doorpost. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Uṭṭhehi [T 1.0343] vīra vijitasaṅgāma,

Pannabhāra anaṇa vicara loke;

Cittañca te suvimuttaṃ,

Cando yathā pannarasāya ratti”nti.

“Arise, O hero, victor in battle, who has laid down the burden, debtless one, wander in the world. Your mind is well-liberated, like the moon on the night of the fifteenth day.”

“Na [P 1.0234] kho, devānaminda, tathāgatā evaṃ vanditabbā. Evañca kho, devānaminda, tathāgatā vanditabbā –

“Indeed, Lord of Devas, Tathāgatas should not be venerated in this way. And indeed, Lord of Devas, Tathāgatas should be venerated in this way:

“Uṭṭhehi vīra vijitasaṅgāma,

Satthavāha anaṇa vicara loke;

Desassu bhagavā dhammaṃ,

Aññātāro bhavissantī”ti.

“Arise, O hero, victor in battle, caravan leader, debtless one, wander in the world. Let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma; there will be those who understand.”

8. Gahaṭṭhavandanāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Homage by a Householder

264. Sāvatthiyaṃ. Tatra…pe… etadavoca – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo mātaliṃ saṅgāhakaṃ āmantesi – ‘yojehi, samma mātali, sahassayuttaṃ [M 1.0236] ājaññarathaṃ. Uyyānabhūmiṃ gacchāma subhūmiṃ dassanāyā’ti. ‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā sahassayuttaṃ ājaññarathaṃ yojetvā sakkassa devānamindassa paṭivedesi – ‘yutto kho te, mārisa, sahassayutto ājaññaratho. Yassa dāni kālaṃ maññasī’”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vejayantapāsādā orohanto [V 1.0271] añjaliṃ katvā pañjaliko (pī.), pañjaliṃ katvā (ka.) sudaṃ puthuddisā namassati. Atha [T 1.0344] kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

264. At Sāvatthī. There… the Blessed One said this: “Once upon a time, monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed Mātali the charioteer: ‘Harness the thousand-yoked thoroughbred chariot, dear Mātali. Let us go to the pleasure garden to see the beautiful grounds.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ Mātali the charioteer replied to Sakka, lord of the devas. He harnessed the thousand-yoked thoroughbred chariot and informed Sakka, lord of the devas: ‘The thousand-yoked thoroughbred chariot is harnessed for you, sir. Now is the time for whatever you think fit.’ Then, monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, while descending from the Vejayanta Palace, with palms joined in reverence, paid homage to the various directions. Then, monks, Mātali the charioteer addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:

“Taṃ namassanti tevijjā, sabbe bhummā ca khattiyā;

Cattāro ca mahārājā, tidasā ca yasassino;

Atha ko nāma so yakkho, yaṃ tvaṃ sakka namassasī”ti.

“Those with the threefold knowledge pay homage to you, and all earthly beings and khattiyas; the Four Great Kings, and the glorious devas of the Thirty-Three. And yet, O Sakka, what is the name of that yakkha to whom you pay homage?”

“Maṃ namassanti tevijjā, sabbe bhummā ca khattiyā;

Cattāro ca mahārājā, tidasā ca yasassino.

“Those with the threefold knowledge pay homage to me, and all earthly beings and khattiyas; the Four Great Kings, and the glorious devas of the Thirty-Three.

“Ahañca sīlasampanne, cirarattasamāhite;

Sammāpabbajite vande, brahmacariyaparāyane.

“But I venerate those endowed with virtue, long-established in concentration, who have gone forth rightly, and are devoted to the holy life.

“Ye gahaṭṭhā puññakarā, sīlavanto upāsakā;

Dhammena dāraṃ posenti, te namassāmi mātalī”ti.

“Those householders who make merit, virtuous lay disciples who righteously support their wives—them I venerate, Mātali.”

“Seṭṭhā hi kira lokasmiṃ, ye tvaṃ sakka namassasi;

Ahampi te namassāmi, ye namassasi vāsavā”ti.

“Indeed, the best in the world are they whom you, O Sakka, venerate. I too, O Vāsava, venerate those whom you venerate.”

“Idaṃ vatvāna maghavā, devarājā sujampati;

Puthuddisā namassitvā, pamukho rathamāruhī”ti.

Having said this, Maghavā, Sujampati, the king of devas, after paying homage to the various directions, mounted the chariot as the foremost among them.

9. Satthāravandanāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Homage to the Teacher

265. Sāvatthiyaṃ [P 1.0235] jetavane. “Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo mātaliṃ saṅgāhakaṃ āmantesi – ‘yojehi, samma mātali, sahassayuttaṃ ājaññarathaṃ, uyyānabhūmiṃ gacchāma subhūmiṃ dassanāyā’ti. ‘Evaṃ bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā [M 1.0237] sahassayuttaṃ ājaññarathaṃ yojetvā sakkassa devānamindassa [T 1.0345] paṭivedesi [V 1.0272] – ‘yutto kho te, mārisa, sahassayutto ājaññaratho. Yassa dāni kālaṃ maññasī’”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vejayantapāsādā orohanto añjaliṃ katvā sudaṃ bhagavantaṃ namassati. Atha kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

265. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove. “Once upon a time, monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed Mātali the charioteer: ‘Harness the thousand-yoked thoroughbred chariot, dear Mātali. Let us go to the pleasure garden to see the beautiful grounds.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ Mātali the charioteer replied to Sakka, lord of the devas. He harnessed the thousand-yoked thoroughbred chariot and informed Sakka, lord of the devas: ‘The thousand-yoked thoroughbred chariot is harnessed for you, sir. Now is the time for whatever you think fit.’ Then, monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, while descending from the Vejayanta Palace, with palms joined in reverence, paid homage to the Blessed One. Then, monks, Mātali the charioteer addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:

“Yañhi devā manussā ca, taṃ namassanti vāsava;

Atha ko nāma so yakkho, yaṃ tvaṃ sakka namassasī”ti.

“Gods and humans pay homage to you, O Vāsava. And yet, O Sakka, what is the name of that yakkha to whom you pay homage?”

“Yo idha sammāsambuddho, asmiṃ loke sadevake;

Anomanāmaṃ satthāraṃ, taṃ namassāmi mātali.

“The one who is the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One here in this world with its devas, the Teacher with a peerless name—that Teacher, Mātali, I venerate.

“Yesaṃ rāgo ca doso ca, avijjā ca virājitā;

Khīṇāsavā arahanto, te namassāmi mātali.

“Those for whom lust, hatred, and ignorance have faded away, the Arahants whose taints are destroyed—them, Mātali, I venerate.

“Ye rāgadosavinayā, avijjāsamatikkamā;

Sekkhā apacayārāmā, appamattānusikkhare;

Te namassāmi mātalī”ti.

“Those trainees who, for the removal of lust and hatred and for the overcoming of ignorance, delight in non-accumulation and heedfully pursue the training—them, Mātali, I venerate.”

“Seṭṭhā hi kira lokasmiṃ, ye tvaṃ sakka namassasi;

Ahampi te namassāmi, ye namassasi vāsavā”ti.

“Indeed, the best in the world are they whom you, O Sakka, venerate. I too, O Vāsava, venerate those whom you venerate.”

“Idaṃ vatvāna maghavā, devarājā sujampati;

Bhagavantaṃ namassitvā, pamukho rathamāruhī”ti.

Having said this, Maghavā, Sujampati, the king of devas, after paying homage to the Blessed One, mounted the chariot as the foremost among them.

10. Saṅghavandanāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Veneration of the Saṅgha

266. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 1.0346] jetavane. Tatra kho…pe… etadavoca – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo mātaliṃ saṅgāhakaṃ āmantesi – ‘yojehi, samma mātali, sahassayuttaṃ ājaññarathaṃ[V 1.0273], uyyānabhūmiṃ gacchāma subhūmiṃ dassanāyā’ti. ‘Evaṃ [P 1.0236] bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā, sahassayuttaṃ ājaññarathaṃ yojetvā sakkassa devānamindassa paṭivedesi – ‘yutto kho te, mārisa, sahassayutto ājaññaratho, yassa dāni kālaṃ maññasī’”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave[M 1.0238], sakko devānamindo vejayantapāsādā orohanto añjaliṃ katvā sudaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ namassati. Atha kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

266. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove. There… the Blessed One said this: “Once upon a time, bhikkhus, Sakka, the lord of the devas, addressed his charioteer Mātali: ‘Harness the chariot of thoroughbreds yoked with a thousand, dear Mātali. Let us go to the pleasure garden to see the beautiful grounds.’ ‘So be it, venerable sir,’ replied Mātali, the charioteer, to Sakka, the lord of the devas. Having harnessed the chariot of thoroughbreds yoked with a thousand, he informed Sakka, the lord of the devas: ‘The chariot of thoroughbreds yoked with a thousand is harnessed for you, sir. Now is the time for whatever you think fit.’ Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, the lord of the devas, descending from the Vejayanta Palace, made the añjali gesture and venerated the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then, bhikkhus, the charioteer Mātali addressed Sakka, the lord of the devas, in verse:

“Tañhi ete namasseyyuṃ, pūtidehasayā narā;

Nimuggā kuṇapamhete, khuppipāsasamappitā.

“It is they who should worship you, these men who lie in a putrid body, are immersed in what is vile, and are afflicted with hunger and thirst.

“Kiṃ nu tesaṃ pihayasi, anāgārāna vāsava;

Ācāraṃ isinaṃ brūhi, taṃ suṇoma vaco tavā”ti.

“What is it that you admire in them, Vāsava, in these homeless ones? Speak of the conduct of the seers; we wish to hear that word of yours.”

“Etaṃ tesaṃ pihayāmi, anāgārāna mātali;

Yamhā gāmā pakkamanti, anapekkhā vajanti te.

“This is what I admire in them, Mātali, in the homeless ones: from whichever village they depart, they go without attachment.

“Na tesaṃ koṭṭhe openti, na kumbhi na kumbhā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) na kaḷopiyaṃ khaḷopiyaṃ (sī.);

Paraniṭṭhitamesānā paraniṭṭhitamesanā (syā. kaṃ. ka.), tena yāpenti subbatā.

“They do not store grains in a granary, nor in a pot, nor in a basket; they seek what has been prepared by others, and by that the virtuous subsist.

“Sumantamantino [T 1.0347] dhīrā, tuṇhībhūtā samañcarā;

Devā viruddhā asurehi, puthu maccā ca mātali.

“The wise, with well-considered counsel, become silent and live in concord. Devas are in conflict with asuras, Mātali, and many mortals with one another.

“Aviruddhā viruddhesu, attadaṇḍesu nibbutā;

Sādānesu anādānā, te namassāmi mātalī”ti.

“Those who are not in conflict among the conflicted, who have laid down the rod among those who have taken it up, who are without grasping among those who grasp—it is them I venerate, Mātali.”

“Seṭṭhā hi kira lokasmiṃ, ye tvaṃ sakka namassasi;

Ahampi te namassāmi, ye namassasi vāsavā”ti.

“Indeed, the best in the world are they whom you, O Sakka, venerate. I too, O Vāsava, venerate those whom you venerate.”

“Idaṃ [V 1.0274] vatvāna maghavā, devarājā sujampati;

Bhikkhusaṅghaṃ namassitvā, pamukho rathamāruhī”ti.

Having said this, Maghavā, the king of devas, husband of Sujā, after paying homage to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, mounted the chariot as the foremost among them.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary:

Devā pana va tapadena (sī. syā. kaṃ.) tayo vuttā, daliddañca rāmaṇeyyakaṃ;

Yajamānañca vandanā, tayo sakkanamassanāti.

Three suttas on devas, then on the poor, the charming, the sacrificer, and veneration; three are about Sakka’s homage.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

1. Chetvāsuttaṃ

1. The Chetvā Sutta

267. Sāvatthiyaṃ [T 1.0348][M 1.0239][P 1.0237] jetavane. Atha kho sakko devānamindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

267. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove. Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Sakka, the lord of the devas, addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Kiṃsu chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kiṃsu chetvā na socati;

Kissassu ekadhammassa, vadhaṃ rocesi gotamā”ti.

“Having cut off what, does one live happily? Having cut off what, does one not grieve? The destruction of which one thing, O Gotama, do you approve?”

“Kodhaṃ chetvā sukhaṃ seti, kodhaṃ chetvā na socati;

Kodhassa visamūlassa, madhuraggassa vāsava;

Vadhaṃ ariyā pasaṃsanti, tañhi chetvā na socatī”ti.

“Having cut off anger, one lives happily; having cut off anger, one does not grieve. O Vāsava, the noble ones praise the destruction of anger, which has a poisonous root and a sweet tip; for indeed, having cut it off, one does not grieve.”

2. Dubbaṇṇiyasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Ill-Favored One

268. Sāvatthiyaṃ [V 1.0275] jetavane. Tatra kho…pe… etadavoca – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, aññataro yakkho dubbaṇṇo okoṭimako sakkassa devānamindassa āsane nisinno ahosi. Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, devā tāvatiṃsā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – ‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ayaṃ yakkho dubbaṇṇo okoṭimako sakkassa devānamindassa āsane nisinno’”ti! Yathā [T 1.0349] yathā kho, bhikkhave, devā tāvatiṃsā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti, tathā tathā so yakkho abhirūpataro ceva hoti dassanīyataro ca pāsādikataro ca.

268. At Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove. There… the Blessed One said this: “Once upon a time, bhikkhus, a certain yakkha—ill-favored, with a hunched and protruding belly—was seated on the throne of Sakka, the lord of the devas. Then, bhikkhus, the Tāvatiṃsa devas disparaged, condemned, and criticized him, saying: ‘How astonishing, sirs, how marvelous, sirs! This yakkha—ill-favored, with a hunched and protruding belly—is seated on the throne of Sakka, the lord of the devas!’ But the more, bhikkhus, the Tāvatiṃsa devas disparaged, condemned, and criticized him, the more that yakkha became exceedingly handsome, exceedingly attractive, and exceedingly inspiring.”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, devā tāvatiṃsā yena sakko devānamindo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘idha te, mārisa, aññataro yakkho dubbaṇṇo okoṭimako sakkassa devānamindassa āsane nisinno. Tatra sudaṃ, mārisa, devā tāvatiṃsā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ayaṃ yakkho dubbaṇṇo okoṭimako [P 1.0238] sakkassa devānamindassa āsane nisinnoti. Yathā yathā kho, mārisa, devā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti, tathā tathā so yakkho abhirūpataro ceva hoti dassanīyataro [M 1.0240] ca pāsādikataro cāti. So hi nūna, mārisa, kodhabhakkho yakkho bhavissatī’”ti.

“Then, bhikkhus, the Tāvatiṃsa devas approached Sakka, the lord of the devas. Having approached, they said this to Sakka, the lord of the devas: ‘Sir, here a certain yakkha—ill-favored, with a hunched and protruding belly—is seated on your throne. Then, sir, the Tāvatiṃsa devas disparage, condemn, and criticize him, saying: “How astonishing, sirs, how marvelous, sirs! This yakkha—ill-favored, with a hunched and protruding belly—is seated on the throne of Sakka, the lord of the devas!” But the more, sir, the devas disparage, condemn, and criticize him, the more that yakkha becomes exceedingly handsome, exceedingly attractive, and exceedingly inspiring.’ Sakka then said: ‘Surely, friends, that must be the Kodhabhakkha yakkha.’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo yena so kodhabhakkho yakkho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dakkhiṇajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ pathaviyaṃ nihantvā yena so kodhabhakkho yakkho tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ nāmaṃ sāveti – ‘sakkohaṃ mārisa, devānamindo, sakkohaṃ, mārisa, devānamindo’ti. Yathā yathā kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo nāmaṃ sāvesi, tathā tathā so yakkho dubbaṇṇataro ceva ahosi okoṭimakataro ca. Dubbaṇṇataro ceva [T 1.0350] hutvā okoṭimakataro ca tatthevantaradhāyī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sake āsane nisīditvā deve tāvatiṃse anunayamāno tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

“Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, the lord of the devas, approached that Kodhabhakkha yakkha. Having approached, he arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, extended his joined hands in reverence towards that Kodhabhakkha yakkha, and three times announced his name: ‘I am Sakka, sir, the lord of the devas; I am Sakka, sir, the lord of the devas.’ The more, bhikkhus, Sakka, the lord of the devas, announced his name, the more that yakkha became exceedingly ill-favored and exceedingly hunched with a protruding belly. Having become exceedingly ill-favored and exceedingly hunched with a protruding belly, he disappeared right there. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, the lord of the devas, having seated himself on his own throne, while instructing the Tāvatiṃsa devas, recited these verses on that occasion:”

“Na [V 1.0276] sūpahatacittomhi, nāvattena suvānayo;

Na vo cirāhaṃ kujjhāmi, kodho mayi nāvatiṭṭhati.

“My mind is not afflicted; I am not easily led by the power of anger. I am not angry for long; anger does not remain in me.”

“Kuddhāhaṃ na pharusaṃ brūmi, na ca dhammāni kittaye;

Sanniggaṇhāmi attānaṃ, sampassaṃ atthamattano”ti.

“When angry, I do not speak harshly, nor do I proclaim unwholesome things. Seeing my own benefit, I restrain myself.”

3. Sambarimāyāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Sambari's Illusion

269. Sāvatthiyaṃ…pe… bhagavā etadavoca – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo ābādhiko ahosi dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami gilānapucchako. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – ‘tikiccha maṃ devānamindā’ti. ‘Vācehi [P 1.0239] maṃ, vepacitti, sambarimāya’nti. ‘Na tāvāhaṃ vācemi, yāvāhaṃ, mārisa, asure paṭipucchāmī’”ti. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo asure paṭipucchi – ‘vācemahaṃ, mārisā, sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ sambarimāya’nti? ‘Mā kho tvaṃ, mārisa, vācesi sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ sambarimāya’”nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ gāthāya [T 1.0351] ajjhabhāsi –

269. At Sāvatthī… the Blessed One said this: “Once in the past, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. Then, bhikkhus, Sakka, the lord of the devas, approached Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, to inquire about his illness. Vepacitti, bhikkhus, saw Sakka, the lord of the devas, coming from afar. Having seen him, he said to Sakka, the lord of the devas: ‘Heal me, lord of the devas.’ ‘Teach me, Vepacitti, the Sambari illusion.’ ‘I will not teach it, good sir, until I have consulted the asuras.’ Then, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, consulted the asuras: ‘Should I teach the Sambari illusion to Sakka, the lord of the devas, good sirs?’ ‘Do not teach the Sambari illusion to Sakka, the lord of the devas, good sir.’ Then, bhikkhus, Vepacitti, the lord of the asuras, addressed Sakka, the lord of the devas, with a verse:

“Māyāvī [M 1.0241] maghavā sakka, devarāja sujampati;

Upeti nirayaṃ ghoraṃ, sambarova sataṃ sama”nti.

“One who possesses illusion, O Maghavā, Sakka, king of devas, husband of Sujā, goes to a terrible hell, just as Sambara did for a hundred years.”

4. Accayasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Transgression

270. Sāvatthiyaṃ…pe… ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena dve bhikkhū sampayojesuṃ. Tatreko bhikkhu accasarā. Atha kho so bhikkhu tassa bhikkhuno santike accayaṃ accayato deseti; so bhikkhu nappaṭiggaṇhāti. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha, bhante, dve bhikkhū sampayojesuṃ, tatreko bhikkhu accasarā[V 1.0277]. Atha kho so, bhante, bhikkhu tassa bhikkhuno santike accayaṃ accayato deseti, so bhikkhu nappaṭiggaṇhātī”ti.

270. At Sāvatthī… in the monastery. Now at that time two bhikkhus were quarreling. One bhikkhu transgressed. Then that bhikkhu declared his transgression as such to the other bhikkhu; but that bhikkhu did not accept it. Then several bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One: “Here, Venerable Sir, two bhikkhus were quarreling. One bhikkhu transgressed. Then, Venerable Sir, that bhikkhu declared his transgression as such to the other bhikkhu, but that bhikkhu does not accept it.”

“Dveme, bhikkhave, bālā. Yo ca accayaṃ accayato na passati, yo ca accayaṃ desentassa yathādhammaṃ nappaṭiggaṇhā”ti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dve bālā. “Dveme, bhikkhave, paṇḍitā. Yo ca accayaṃ accayato passati, yo ca accayaṃ desentassa yathādhammaṃ paṭiggaṇhā”ti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dve paṇḍitā.

“Monks, there are these two fools: one who does not see a transgression as a transgression, and one who, when another is declaring a transgression, does not accept it in accordance with the Dhamma. These, monks, are the two fools. Monks, there are these two wise ones: one who sees a transgression as a transgression, and one who, when another is declaring a transgression, accepts it in accordance with the Dhamma. These, monks, are the two wise ones.”

“Bhūtapubbaṃ[T 1.0352], bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ deve tāvatiṃse anunayamāno tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

“Once in the past, monks, Sakka, the lord of the devas, while instructing the Tāvatiṃsa devas in the Sudhammā assembly hall, recited this verse at that time:

“Kodho [P 1.0240] vo vasamāyātu, mā ca mittehi vo jarā;

Agarahiyaṃ mā garahittha, mā ca bhāsittha pesuṇaṃ;

Atha pāpajanaṃ kodho, pabbatovābhimaddatī”ti.

“Let anger not come to master you, nor may you fall out with friends; do not blame the blameless, nor speak slander; for anger crushes the evil person, as a mountain does.”

5. Akkodhasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Non-Anger

271. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū…pe… bhagavā etadavoca – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ deve tāvatiṃse anunayamāno tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

271. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the monks… The Blessed One said this: “Once in the past, monks, Sakka, lord of the devas, while exhorting the Tāvatiṃsa devas in the Sudhammā assembly hall, recited this verse on that occasion:

“Mā [M 1.0242] vo kodho ajjhabhavi, mā ca kujjhittha kujjhataṃ;

Akkodho avihiṃsā ca, ariyesu ca paṭipadā vasatī sadā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.);

Atha pāpajanaṃ kodho, pabbatovābhimaddatī”ti.

“Let not anger overcome you, nor be angry toward those who are angry. Non-anger and non-violence is the practice among the noble ones. But anger crushes a foolish person, just as a mountain does.”

Tatiyo vaggo.

The Third Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ [V 1.0278] –

The summary thereof:

Chetvā dubbaṇṇiyamāyā, accayena akodhano;

Desitaṃ buddhaseṭṭhena, idañhi sakkapañcakanti.

Chetvā, Dubbaṇṇiya, Māyā, Accayena, and Akkodha—this is the Pentad on Sakka taught by the best of Buddhas.

Sakkasaṃyuttaṃ samattaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Sakka is concluded.

Sagāthāvaggo paṭhamo.

The First: The Chapter with Verses.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Devatā [T 1.0353] devaputto ca, rājā māro ca bhikkhunī;

Brahmā brāhmaṇa vaṅgīso, vanayakkhena vāsavoti.

Devatā, Devaputta, the King, Māra, Bhikkhunī, Brahmā, Brāhmaṇa, Vaṅgīsa, Vana, Yakkha, and Vāsava.

Sagāthāvaggasaṃyuttapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāḷi of the Connected Discourses with Verses is concluded.
